items.title: Children with developmental language disorder show selective impairments in low-frequency neural tracking of speech
items.summary: by Mahmoud Keshavarzi, Georgia Feltham, Susan Richards, Lyla Parvez, Usha Goswami Neural tracking of slow temporal modulations in speech supports extraction of the prosodic and syllabic structure thought to be critical for language acquisition by Temporal Sampling (TS) theory, yet whether these automatic cortical tracking mechanisms are altered in children with developmental language disorder (DLD) remains unclear. We recorded MEG while children with and without DLD listened to a story, and quantified source-level lagged speech-brain coherence and frequency-specific cortical functional connectivity across bilateral cortical regions. As expected a priori by TS theory, children with DLD showed significantly reduced coherence in the 0.9–2.5 Hz range associated with prosodic information in the story, spanning bilateral auditory and speech-related cortex.
items.author: Mahmoud Keshavarzi, Georgia Feltham, Susan Richards et al.

items.title: Entangled stoichiometric objectives shape microbial catabolism
items.summary: by Maaike Remeijer, Frank J. Bruggeman The understanding of fundamental relationships between energetic and biosynthetic parameters of catabolism and anabolism is a central challenge in microbiology. The large diversity of microbial metabolisms can be compared on the basis of our current definitions of catabolism and anabolism. Catabolism has two functions: synthesising charged energy carriers and carbon precursors. Energy carriers, however, are also involved in precursor synthesis, complicating the analysis. We introduce an unbiased method to quantify stoichiometric relationships between catabolism and anabolism in genome-scale metabolic models. We compare catabolic strategies across diverse (heterotrophic) microbial species and growth conditions, focusing on states of maximal biomass yield per unit of energy source.
items.author: Maaike Remeijer, Frank J. Bruggeman

items.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention
items.summary: by Nurit Haspel Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language model pre-trained on structural data, with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a cross-chain attention mechanism and a contact supervision head. Our method can detect both binding interfaces and pairwise contact matrices.
items.author: Nurit Haspel

items.title: Species-rich and genomically diverse: Comparative genomics reveals how fusions, fissions, and sex chromosomes have shaped beetle evolution
items.summary: by Dwayne G. Tally, Charlie Pittman, Ryan R. Bracewell Chromosome evolution in animals reflects a balance between long-term conservation of ancestral linkage groups and lineage-specific chromosomal rearrangements that reshape genome structure. Beetles (Coleoptera), the most species-rich animal order, exhibit extensive diversity in karyotype, yet the extent to which their chromosomes retain deep ancestral structure remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 190 chromosome-level genome assemblies spanning 39 families and 16 superfamilies to characterize genome diversity, evaluate the conservation of ancestral linkage groups (Stevens elements), identify neo-sex chromosomes, and explore the role of repetitive elements in driving karyotypic change. Our results reveal that beetle genomes are highly diverse, varying substantially in genome size, chromosome number, GC content, and transposable element (TE) composition.
items.author: Dwayne G. Tally, Charlie Pittman, Ryan R. Bracewell

items.title: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides differently affect sleep and plasticity
items.summary: by Rahul Kumar, Gokul Madhav, Priyanka Balasubramanian, Ayur Tadimalla, Rhea Lakhiani, Mugdha Joshi, Vibhu Jaggi, Anushna Pal, Imroze Khan, Krishna Melnattur Molecules implicated in host defense can, independent of their roles as immune mediators, regulate sleep. In mammals, cytokines such as Tumor Necrosis Factor α (TNF α) and Interleukin1β (IL1β) promote sleep. In Drosophila , infection stimulates the systemic release of a battery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). These fly immune effectors have been understudied as sleep modulators. We obtained mutants in different AMPs and characterized their functions in sleep and plasticity. AMP mutants slept less with a longer sleep latency, and lowered arousal thresholds.
items.author: Rahul Kumar, Gokul Madhav, Priyanka Balasubramanian et al.

items.title: DNA uptake and twitching motility are controlled by small RNA Arp through repression of pilin translation in Acinetobacter baumannii
items.summary: by Fergal J. Hamrock, Thomas Guest, Mikaela N. Daum, Orla Connell, Anna S. Ershova, Karsten Hokamp, Alastair B. Fleming, Kristina Schauer, Michael J. Gebhardt, Alexander J. Westermann, Carsten Kröger Acinetobacter baumannii is a major opportunistic pathogen capable of natural transformation. This process is driven by type IV pili (T4P) facilitating horizontal gene transfer and accelerating the spread of antimicrobial resistance. While the transcriptional regulation of T4P is increasingly understood, post-transcriptional mechanisms controlling pilus assembly remain unexplored. Here, we identify and mechanistically characterise a small RNA, Arp ( Acinetobacter repressor of pilin), as a post-transcriptional repressor of T4P-mediated functions in A.
items.author: Fergal J. Hamrock, Thomas Guest, Mikaela N. Daum et al.

items.title: Csi-miR-71a delivered by Clonorchis sinensis extracellular vesicles suppresses liver fibrosis by targeting Scube3 to inhibit the TGF-β/Smad and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways
items.summary: by Meiru Hou, Wei Wei, Ruifeng Mao, Xuewei Liu, Jiawang Zhou, Xue Wang, Hongyu Qiu, Junfeng Gao, Chunren Wang Clonorchis sinensis is a major food-borne parasite that contributes to liver fibrosis in the host by activating hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and promoting extracellular matrix deposition. Recent studies have revealed that miRNAs carried by C. sinensis -derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) have important roles in host–parasite interactions. However, their specific functions and underlying regulatory mechanisms in liver fibrosis remain largely unclear. In this study, EVs were isolated from C. sinensis excretory-secretory products and characterized by electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking, and western blotting.
items.author: Meiru Hou, Wei Wei, Ruifeng Mao et al.

items.title: GM-CSF and M-CSF driven differentiation differentially regulates Chikungunya virus infection and antiviral responses in human monocyte-derived macrophages
items.summary: by Jeury Veloz, Victoria Zyulina, Sara Thannickal, Eva Chebishev, Dabeiba Bernal-Rubio, Maria del Mar Villanueva Guzman, Chenyang Wu, Estefania Valencia, Danielle Novillo, Vrushali Dhamapurkar, Laura Espinar-Barranco, Laurence Gabriel Webb, Rafael Fenutria, Maria G. Noval, Ana Fernandez-Sesma Chikungunya virus is an arthritogenic alphavirus causing debilitating joint pain in infected individuals. The mechanisms driving CHIKV-associated arthralgia is poorly understood, however, macrophages have been implicated as potential reservoirs of persistent viral material and mediators of immunopathology. Granulocyte Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (GM-CSF) and Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (M-CSF) are cytokines that serve as myeloid growth factors that bias macrophages toward pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory phenotypes, respectively.
items.author: Jeury Veloz, Victoria Zyulina, Sara Thannickal et al.

items.title: Hantaviruses: Current insights, lessons from the MV Hondius outbreak, and an urgent call to action
items.summary: by Nikhil Chakravarty, Vrithika Vaithi, Arjit Vijey Jeyachandran, Rakshiah Arunachalam, Anne Zaiss, Anna Bonazzi, Mark Parcells, Gustavo Garcia Jr., Arunachalam Ramaiah, Vaithilingaraja Arumugaswami In May 2026, a cluster of laboratory-confirmed Andes virus (ANDV) infections was reported among passengers aboard the MV Hondius, a cruise ship that originated in Argentina and sailed through the South Atlantic. The exposed population included individuals from 23 countries and resulted in at least 13 cases, including three deaths, representing the first ANDV outbreak with a multi-continental range and providing further evidence consistent with human-to-human transmission of ANDV. There are currently no approved treatments or vaccines for ANDV, necessitating rapid development of drug and prophylactic pipelines.
items.author: Nikhil Chakravarty, Vrithika Vaithi, Arjit Vijey Jeyachandran et al.

items.title: CTCF regulates wild-type and recombinant AAV gene expression by shaping viral chromatin
items.summary: by Clairine I.S. Larsen, Rhiannon R. Abrahams, Rea Guertler, Elliott M. Wilion, Eda Erata, Zachary H. Sykes, Lorelei I. Stoica, Gopishankar Thirumoorthy, Divya Sinha, Richa Rai, Joydeb Majumder, Elizabeth K. Hofer, Eleanor Hart, Eishika Dissanayake, James E. Gern, David M. Gamm, William L. Murphy, Matthew S. Fuller, Kinjal Majumder Adeno-Associated Viruses (AAVs) are powerful platforms for delivering therapeutic transgenes via recombinant AAV (rAAV) vectors. However, a limited understanding of the regulation of AAV gene expression has narrowed the ability to efficiently express therapeutic transgenes from rAAV vectors. Since rAAVs retain only the wtAAV inverted terminal repeats (ITR), we hypothesized that regulatory elements outside the ITR that govern wild-type AAV (wtAAV) gene expression can be used to modify rAAV genomes to enhance vector performance.
items.author: Clairine I.S. Larsen, Rhiannon R. Abrahams, Rea Guertler et al.

items.title: Trends and causes of maternal mortality in Taiyuan, China, 2016–2024: A population-based observational study
items.summary: by Fang Wang, Hailan Yang Background Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016–2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR. Methods We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports . MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests were used for between-group comparisons.
items.author: Fang Wang, Hailan Yang

items.title: Water-induced degradation and small-strain dynamic characteristics of tremella fuciformis polysaccharide treated loess
items.summary: by Shengting Shi, Haokun Tong, Jingxuan Zhou, Zhanpeng Ji, Xinlei Zhang The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The evolution of the maximum shear modulus ( G max ) and reference shear strain ( γ r ) was systematically analyzed under varying applied confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results show that for untreated loess, G max follows a power-law growth with confining pressure and linear attenuation with water content.
items.author: Shengting Shi, Haokun Tong, Jingxuan Zhou et al.

items.title: Development and validation of a real-time PCR assay for the detection of SEA4 clade rabies virus (Philippine strain) in post-mortem non-brain animal samples
items.summary: by Daria L. Manalo, Jude Karlo G. Bolivar, Jeromir G. Bondoc, Blanca J. Nagataki, Karl Ian T. Ermino, Kazunori Kimitsuki, Leilanie B. Nacion, Mark Joseph M. Espino, Chun-Ho Park, Satoshi Inoue Rabies remains a major public health concern in endemic settings, where effective control depends on timely and reliable post-mortem confirmation of infection in animal reservoirs. Although the direct fluorescent antibody test (dFAT) remains the reference standard, its dependence on fresh brain tissue and susceptibility to specimen degradation limits its operational use in decentralized surveillance systems. The present findings demonstrate that the locally optimized RT-qPCR assay targeting the nucleoprotein gene in non-brain tissues exhibits high analytical sensitivity and strong concordance with dFAT results obtained from post-mortem brain specimens of dogs.
items.author: Daria L. Manalo, Jude Karlo G. Bolivar, Jeromir G. Bondoc et al.

items.title: Association between physical activity intensity and self-reported emphysema: A cross-sectional study using NHANES
items.summary: by Qiao Wei, Haiyan Song, Li Jiang, Xiuqin Li, Jihua Zhu Background Emphysema is a significant public health issue. Physical activity (PA) has been suggested to be associated with respiratory health; however, the relationship between PA intensity and emphysema remains insufficiently characterized. Methods This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2016. Emphysema was defined based on self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between different levels of PA and the odds of self-reported emphysema among older adults, adjusting for demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities.
items.author: Qiao Wei, Haiyan Song, Li Jiang et al.

items.title: Feasibility of omitting the unenhanced phase in CT angiography for acute aortic pathologies
items.summary: by Soo Buem Cho, Jieun Byun Objectives To evaluate the feasibility of a contrast-only computed tomography angiography (CTA) protocol versus a conventional multiphase protocol for detecting and characterizing acute aortic pathologies, and reducing radiation dose. Materials & methods This retrospective study included 160 patients who underwent multiphase CTA for evaluating acute aortic syndrome. Two readers independently evaluated 640 predefined aortic segments for the presence of aneurysms, dissections, intramural hematomas (IMH), and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (PAU). Non-inferiority was assessed using generalized estimating equations with a prespecified 5% margin. Inter-protocol and inter-reader agreements were calculated using Cohen’s kappa. Radiation dose also was compared.
items.author: Soo Buem Cho, Jieun Byun

items.title: Mobile radiation shielding device for scatter dose reduction during portable radiography in an orthopedic ward
items.summary: by Jongwat Cheewakul, Natee Ina, Suphalak Khamruang Marshall, Sitthichok Chaichulee Portable radiography in orthopedic wards exposes healthcare professionals and adjacent patients to scatter radiation in open, shared clinical environments. In crowded wards, maintaining an optimal distance or clearing the area during exposure is often impractical. This study designed, constructed, and evaluated a foldable mobile radiation shielding system comprising two three-panel units, each with a chromed steel frame (210 × 180 cm) with 0.6-mm nominal lead sheets covered by a vinyl outer layer (66 × 100 cm) per panel, mounted on wheeled castors for bedside deployment. The two units were deployed together, one along each lateral side of the bed.
items.author: Jongwat Cheewakul, Natee Ina, Suphalak Khamruang Marshall et al.

items.title: Habitual qat chewing and short-term response to conservative management of temporomandibular disorders: A prospective cohort study in conflict-affected Yemen
items.summary: by Raji Mansoor Hajeb, Yousif Osman Yousif, Nader Ahmed Al-Aizari, Essam Ahmed Al-Moraissi Qat (Catha edulis), chewed daily by a substantial proportion of Yemeni adults, contains cathinone, an amphetamine-like alkaloid that augments masticatory muscle activity. Observational evidence links the habit to temporomandibular disorders (TMD), yet none has examined how chewers respond once treated. A prospective cohort of 148 consecutive patients diagnosed by Research Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders Axis I examination was followed at Sana’a University and Al-Kuwait Teaching Hospital between October 2018 and October 2020. Fifty-four (36.5%) were habitual qat chewers, defined as three or more sessions weekly. All received reassurance, education and self-care advice, to which the clinician added an NSAID, diazepam, amitriptyline or a stabilization splint as routine care.
items.author: Raji Mansoor Hajeb, Yousif Osman Yousif, Nader Ahmed Al-Aizari et al.

items.title: Spatio-temporal occurrence of small carnivores in Bagmati-Ratu Complex, Nepal
items.summary: by Bashu Dev Baral, Surya Devkota, Sandeep Regmi, Shivish Bhandari, Bishnu Prasad Bhattarai, Hem Bahadur Katuwal, Jerrold L. Belant, Hari Prasad Sharma Small carnivores are generally more adaptable to human-dominated landscapes compared with large carnivores, but have received comparatively limited attention. We evaluated the single-season multi-species occupancy and temporal overlap of five small carnivores in Bagmati-Ratu Complex (BRC) of Madhesh Province, Nepal using camera-trap surveys during January to February 2023. Camera-trap data were used to evaluate single-season multi-species occupancy using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations to understand the impacts of anthropogenic and environmental variables on community-level occupancy of small carnivores.
items.author: Bashu Dev Baral, Surya Devkota, Sandeep Regmi et al.

items.title: Within-player load-wellness monitoring and lower-limb pain in elite female football: A reproducible secondary analysis of the SoccerMon dataset
items.summary: by Yushuo Liu, Haitao Li Routine athlete-monitoring data can test whether within-player changes in training load and wellness precede health problems, but sparse outcomes and incomplete reporting complicate inference. We conducted a reproducible secondary longitudinal analysis of the public SoccerMon dataset, comprising 50 players from two Norwegian elite women’s football teams monitored in 2020–2021. The outcome was onset on day t (the index player-day) of a self-reported lower-limb pain/injury episode after a 7-day episode washout. The primary risk set contained 42 onset-days from 15 players; the complete-case soreness interaction analysis contained 28 onset-days from nine event players. Under retrospective full-period within-player standardization, the focal acute-load x soreness interaction was estimated below 1.0 by Firth logistic regression (odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.45–0.97), but uncertainty remained substantial.
items.author: Yushuo Liu, Haitao Li

items.title: Sleep duration and cause-specific mortality among US adults with heart disease: A NHIS-NDI linkage cohort study
items.summary: by Tolulope Victoria Adebile, Tobi Oloyede, Emmanuel Azu, Mobolaji Olagunju, Olamide Asifat, Temitayo Mary Paul, Oluwaseun Ipede, Wandoo Abwa, Purbasha Biswas, Lili Yu Background Sleep duration is increasingly recognized as a component of cardiovascular health, yet its prognostic significance among adults with established heart disease remains unclear. We examined associations between sleep duration and mortality among US adults with heart disease. Methods We analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease participating in the 2004 National Health Interview Survey linked to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Sleep duration was categorized as ≤6 hours, 7–8 hours, and ≥9 hours.
items.author: Tolulope Victoria Adebile, Tobi Oloyede, Emmanuel Azu et al.

items.title: Integrated In vitro and in vivo evaluation of anticancer potentials of two clerodane diterpenes isolated from Psidium guajava (L.) through molecular docking approaches
items.summary: by Most Chand Sultana Khatun, Mir Imam Ibne Wahed, Md. Jamal Hossain, Md. Ataur Rahman, Sabbir Ahmed, Md Hasibul Hasan Psidium guajava (L.) is a medicinal plant rich in bioactive phytochemicals with promising therapeutic potential. This study aimed to isolate clerodane-type diterpenes from P. guajava and evaluate their anticancer activity through in vitro and in vivo assays supported by molecular docking.Two clerodane-type diterpenes, borapetoside F (1) and borapetoside B (2), were isolated from the ethyl acetate fraction of P. guajava and identified by 1 H and 13 C NMR spectroscopy. Cytotoxicity was evaluated against Ehrlich Ascites Carcinoma (EAC) cells using the MTT assay and in EAC-bearing Swiss albino mice, with bleomycin as the reference drug.
items.author: Most Chand Sultana Khatun, Mir Imam Ibne Wahed, Md. Jamal Hossain et al.

items.title: Feasibility of patient-reported outcomes measurement information system (PROMIS) computerized adaptive tests in patients receiving physical therapy: A mixed-methods study
items.summary: by Erik-Jan A. Haan, Annet Doomen, Harriët Wittink, Henri Kiers, Remco M. Arensman, Caroline B. Terwee Introduction Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) are widely used in physical therapy, but both clinicians and patients report respondent burden due to the number and the length of existing instruments. PROMIS ® Computerized Adaptive Tests (CATs) may reduce this burden, yet their feasibility in primary care physical therapy is unknown. This study examined the feasibility of Dutch-Flemish PROMIS CATs in patients with musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders of the spine and upper extremity. Methods We conducted a mixed-methods concurrent triangulation study in 14 physical therapy practices where PROMIS CATs were integrated into the electronic health record system and administered during routine care.
items.author: Erik-Jan A. Haan, Annet Doomen, Harriët Wittink et al.

items.title: GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence: Antecedents, perceived usefulness, AI ethics awareness, and career readiness outcomes
items.summary: by Trung Kim Quoc Nguyen, Khanh Phuc Nguyen This study examines GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence (GAISC) among accounting and auditing students and its relationships with GenAI readiness (GAR), perceived ease of use (PEOU), digital learning self-efficacy (DLSE), facilitating conditions (FC), perceived usefulness (PU), AI ethics awareness (AIEA), and career readiness (CR). The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a common latent factor diagnostic and Gaussian copula endogeneity assessment.
items.author: Trung Kim Quoc Nguyen, Khanh Phuc Nguyen

items.title: Trends and outcomes in diabetic ketoacidosis: A 10-year retrospective study at a Norwegian university hospital
items.summary: by Sebastian Breivik Soleim, Kristian Løvås, Eirik Søfteland, Grethe Åstrøm Ueland Aims To describe trends in diabetic ketoacidosis admissions and examine factors associated with repeated admissions and mortality among adults living with type 1 diabetes. Materials and methods Diabetic ketoacidosis admissions among adults at a Norwegian university hospital between 1 August 2012 and 31 August 2022 were retrospectively reviewed using electronic medical records. Results A total of 178 participants with 306 admissions were included. Median [IQR] age at admission was 34 years [22–51]. Median HbA1c was 88 mmol/mol [72–105]. Diabetic ketoacidosis admission frequency decreased by an estimated 6.9% annually (RR 0.931; 95% CI 0.896–0.968; p Conclusions Diabetic ketoacidosis admissions declined substantially over the 10-year study period despite growth in the hospital catchment area population, suggesting that diabetes care has improved.
items.author: Sebastian Breivik Soleim, Kristian Løvås, Eirik Søfteland et al.

items.title: A comparison of soft palate thickness, length, and volume in bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded-flap palatoplasty: A prospective clinical study
items.summary: by Eva A. Ruzics, Cristina Piedrahita Velasquez, Penny J. Regier, Diego A. Portela, Kathleen M. Ham, James Colee, Federico R. Vilaplana Grosso Objectives To compare soft palate (SP) length, thickness, and volume in French bulldogs and English bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded flap palatoplasty (FFP), and to compare the success of procedures in reducing these dimensions. Materials and Methods Dogs diagnosed with brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) underwent staphylectomy (n = 8) or FFP (n = 8). Pre-operative and 4-week post-operative computed tomography was performed to assess SP dimensions and evaluate surgical outcomes.
items.author: Eva A. Ruzics, Cristina Piedrahita Velasquez, Penny J. Regier et al.

items.title: Immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain and efforts to shield it
items.summary: by John V. Dzimianski, Spencer R. Pierce, Sara M. O’Rourke, Ian Kunkel, Kevin Delgado-Cunningham, Aaron D. Gingerich, Jarrod J. Mousa, Ted M. Ross, Rebecca M. DuBois Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines encoding viral glycoprotein antigens fused to the bacteriophage T4 fibritintrimerization domain are increasingly being tested in human clinical trials. AREXVY and ABRYSVO ® , subunit vaccines composed of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F glycoprotein(s) fused to Foldon, are now FDA-approved and regularly administered. However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain.
items.author: John V. Dzimianski, Spencer R. Pierce, Sara M. O’Rourke et al.

items.title: Embedding behavioural and implementation science in a whole school approach to promote physical activity among children and young people with disabilities
items.summary: by Erin Byrd, Jason J. Wilson, Paul McFlynn, Victoria Simms, Laurence Taggart, Áine Boner, Marie H. Murphy Background A whole school approach (WSA) to physical activity is a comprehensive strategy encouraging children's physical activity throughout the school day. However, research on implementing this approach in special educational needs (SEN) school settings is limited. A strategic approach that considers the school context, behaviour change mechanisms and implementation strategies can improve the effectiveness and sustainability of physical activity in a WSA. This study aimed to embed implementation and behavioural science principles to co-develop an implementation research logic model (IRLM) to guide implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings.
items.author: Erin Byrd, Jason J. Wilson, Paul McFlynn et al.

items.title: Online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for people with multiple sclerosis with mild-to-moderate depression– protocol for a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study
items.summary: by Robert Simpson, Jillian Scandiffio, Laura Langer, Sarah Munce, Ashvene Sureshkumar, Anthony Feinstein, Mark Bayley, Caroline Bowman, Tania R. Bruno, Dawn Ehde, Katherine Knox, Nanette Lai, Penelope Smyth, Abhimanyu Sud, Sarah J. Donkers Background Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) is an effective treatment for recurrent depression in the general population and is recommended in clinical guidelines for those with mild-moderate depression. However, the effectiveness of MBCT in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) with mild to moderate depression is unknown. Further, how best to tailor and implement MBCT for PwMS is largely unstudied. This manuscript describes the study protocol for a hybrid-effectiveness study to evaluate online MBCT tailored for PwMS.
items.author: Robert Simpson, Jillian Scandiffio, Laura Langer et al.

items.title: Single-layer low-profile high-gain wideband circularly polarized MIMO antenna for UAV applications
items.summary: by Hung Nguyen-Manh, Giang Nguyen-Hoai, Thai Nguyen-Dinh, Duy-Phong Pham, Nguyen Quoc Dinh This paper presents a single-layer circularly polarized (CP) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with wideband operation and high-gain radiation characteristics. The antenna comprises 16 truncated-corner patches arranged in a 4×4 configuration and capacitively excited by a probe-fed rectangular patch, enabling a low-profile single-layer structure. The final two-port MIMO antenna has a low profile of approximately 0.02λ at the lowest operating frequency. The measured results demonstrate an effective operating bandwidth of 5.16–5.68 GHz, corresponding to 9.6%, with isolation better than 19 dB and a peak gain of 9.4 dBi. In addition, the antenna exhibits good diversity performance in terms of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), channel capacity loss (CCL), and mean effective gain (MEG).
items.author: Hung Nguyen-Manh, Giang Nguyen-Hoai, Thai Nguyen-Dinh et al.

items.title: Clinical applications of reticulocyte hemoglobin indices, including reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (Ret-He) and reticulocyte hemoglobin content (CHr), among pregnant and postpartum women: A scoping review and evidence map
items.summary: by Miki Ohtsuki, Takuma Ohsuga, Kohei Ida, Kaori Tsuyuki, Miho Egawa, Mayumi Toyama, Yoshimitsu Takahashi, Takeo Nakayama, Masaki Mandai Early detection of iron deficiency during pregnancy and the postpartum period, a common condition associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, remains challenging with conventional iron markers. Reticulocyte hemoglobin indices, including reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent and reticulocyte hemoglobin content, may enable earlier detection of iron-restricted erythropoiesis. We conducted a scoping review to map the clinical and research applications of these indices in pregnant and postpartum women. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched PubMed, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Ichushi Web for studies published from January 1, 1990, to May 31, 2025, and performed an updated search on April 21, 2026, for newly added or indexed records.
items.author: Miki Ohtsuki, Takuma Ohsuga, Kohei Ida et al.

items.title: FOXA1 expression and survival outcomes in triple-negative breast cancer: A retrospective cohort study
items.summary: by Angela V. Fonseca-Benitez, David Diaz-Baez, Giulia Capella, Milena Rondón-Lagos, Isabella Castellano, Nelson Rangel Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains the most aggressive breast cancer subtype, with the poorest prognosis among all forms of breast cancer. FOXA1 is a well-known pioneer factor in luminal breast cancer, however, despite its vital role in this tumor subtype, detailed information about FOXA1 expression and function in TNBC is notably lacking. This gap highlights the importance of exploring whether FOXA1 plays different roles across breast cancer subtypes. Accordingly, the present study aimed to assess the independent prognostic value of FOXA1 expression in a well-characterized cohort of 283 women with TNBC, evaluating its association with progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and distant metastasis, and to determine whether this association is independent of the systemic treatment received.
items.author: Angela V. Fonseca-Benitez, David Diaz-Baez, Giulia Capella et al.

items.title: SAE-MOGWO-PRS: A probability ranking strategy-based grey wolf optimizer for spatio-temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization
items.summary: by Yitong Liu, Tianyu Li, Hong Zhang The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogeneity in evaluation times. Instead, they perform high-fidelity evaluations on all objectives for promising population positions identified by their associated surrogate-assisted optimization algorithms in the solution space. While this approach provides complete and error-free solution evaluations, it does not yield the most computationally efficient procedure. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Surrogate-assisted Evolutionary Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer with Probabilistic Ranking Strategy (SAE-MOGWO-PRS). This algorithm is designed to determine which individuals and objective functions within the population should undergo high-fidelity evaluation, thereby enhancing their ability to generate non-dominated solutions with improved convergence and diversity in the Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer.
items.author: Yitong Liu, Tianyu Li, Hong Zhang

items.title: Spatial patterns of plant life-forms along elevation and aridity gradients in temperate deserts of northern Xinjiang, China
items.summary: by Cheng Fei, Yi Qiang Dong, Shazhou An Located in the arid hinterland of Central Asia, the mountain temperate deserts in Xinjiang are jointly shaped by elevational geographic constraints and the east-west-oriented drought stress gradient. Nevertheless, the joint coupling relationships between these two gradient factors and community-level vegetation structural attributes across woody and herbaceous plant functional groups remain unclarified quantitatively at present.
items.author: Cheng Fei, Yi Qiang Dong, Shazhou An

items.title: GB-algebraic class
items.summary: by Miao Liu, Nueraminaimu Maihemuti, Jiayin Peng, Jiangang Tang The purpose of this article is to study the relationships among the BCI-algebraic class, the GB-algebraic class, and the class of algebras of type (2,0). The results indicate that: (1) The BCH-algebraic class and the GB-algebraic class are two distinct algebraic classes, both of which contain the BCI-algebraic class. (2) There exist a proper BCH-algebra and a proper GB-algebra, and necessary and sufficient conditions are provided for BCH-algebras and GB-algebras to be proper BCH-algebras and proper GB-algebras, respectively. (3) All (2,0)-type algebras form a proper class, and the GB-algebraic class is a proper subclass of the class of algebras of type (2,0).
items.author: Miao Liu, Nueraminaimu Maihemuti, Jiayin Peng et al.

items.title: Machine learning approaches for the identification of real-world predictors of mepolizumab response
items.summary: by Koyo Usuba, Lingjiao Zhang, Xinyang Liu, Tim Tian Yu Han, Natalie Nightingale, Ali Tehrani, Peter Howarth, Rafael Alfonso-Cristancho Background Mepolizumab improves control and reduces clinically significant exacerbations in severe asthma patients. Further research is needed to understand factors influencing patient response. Objective Identify predictors of response to mepolizumab using machine learning techniques. Methods Thirty clinically relevant features from the REALITI-A dataset were analyzed. Response to mepolizumab was defined as change in clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1 post-exposure, being free from clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1, and being free from clinically significant exacerbations at both Year 1 and Year 2 post-exposure for primary, secondary, and exploratory analyses, respectively.
items.author: Koyo Usuba, Lingjiao Zhang, Xinyang Liu et al.

items.summary: The large stellar association cataloged as NGC 206 is nestled within the dusty arms of the neighboring Andromeda galaxy along with the galaxy's pinkish star-forming regions. Also known as M31, the spiral galaxy is a mere 2.5 million light-years away. NGC 206 is found at the center of this sharp and detailed close-up of the southwestern extent of Andromeda's disk. The bright, blue stars of NGC 206 indicate its youth. In fact, its youngest massive stars are less than 10 million years old. Much larger than the open or galactic clusters of young stars in the disk of our Milky Way galaxy, NGC 206 spans about 4,000 light-years.
