items.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
items.summary: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation.
items.author: Xian P. Yang, Christopher T. Parzyck, Martin Cross et al.

items.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
items.summary: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute.
items.author: Ellis Brown, Chris Hoang, Shengyi Qian et al.

items.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
items.summary: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.
items.author: Anirban Das, Asmi Haldar, Arnab Das

items.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
items.summary: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. In academia, limited compute and inconsistent baselines often restrict evaluations to small-scale, single-point comparisons, making it difficult to establish whether improvements hold at larger scales or translate into broader impact. ArchSpace addresses both gaps as a public platform for Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing Architecture Researc}: each proposal is recorded with its experiments and reasoning, reviewed by the community, and referenced by later work.
items.author: Jie Wang, Tong Zhu, JiaHao Kuang et al.

items.title: ProtoVis-Nav: Prototypical Visual Imagination for Visual-Spatial Aligned UAV Navigation
items.summary: Vision language navigation (VLN) is very challenging for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) since small errors in 3D motion prediction can lead to navigation errors and collisions. Unable to fathom execution outcomes in 3D environments, existing methods often struggle to predict accurate navigation waypoints from language instructions. To solve this, we introduce the Prototypical Visual Imagination framework, shortened as ProtoVis-Nav, which forces the model to imagine an outcome-associated local visual representation for the intended next UAV movement. Specifically, we predict feature prototypes and use their linear combination to estimate the visual feature of the target region. In this manner, the VLN model first imagines the local visual representation of the next intended location, and then uses predicted prototypes as context for generating the final action, promoting alignment between visual context and waypoint outputs.
items.author: Guangyuan Sui, Yunzhong Hou, Chi Harold Liu

items.title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
items.summary: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. Existing neurosymbolic methods such as Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) offer constraint-satisfying reinforcement learning (RL) via differentiable symbolic supervision but assume a finite, discrete action space. We present a PLPG-inspired continuous allocation method that estimates the probability that the policy's own executed action satisfies the investment mandate, using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling, and adds it to the training objective.
items.author: Zeynep Yıldız, Satchit Chatterji, Ercan Atam et al.

items.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
items.summary: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $ν_τ$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower.
items.author: Dibya S. Chattopadhyay, Carlos A. Argüelles, Vedran Brdar

items.title: Decoupling Dynamics: A Tale of Two Limits
items.summary: The symmetries of a $d$-dimensional QFT are known to be captured by a topological theory in one dimension higher, the Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which is invariant under gauging finite symmetries of the QFT, but not under dynamical gauging of continuous symmetries. We show that the distinct SymTFTs of a $d$-dimensional QFT before and after dynamical gauging of a continuous Abelian symmetry arise as different topological limits of the same dynamical holographic gauge theory in $(d+1)$-dimensions. Gauging changes the boundary condition of this dynamical theory and thereby selects a different topological limit, explaining why the associated SymTFT changes. We give a fully quantum definition of these SymTFTs at the level of Hilbert spaces and operators by combining suitable limits of the bulk holographic theory with photon truncation.
items.author: Andrea Antinucci, Oscar Lewis

items.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
items.summary: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes.
items.author: Sergio Sanjurjo, Themistocles Zikopoulos

items.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
items.summary: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. In this work, we introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL), framing SSL as a program search problem and studying how agents navigate this space under limited supervision. We find that even under weak feedback and matched compute, agents can synthesize code that combines and adapts established SSL techniques, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings by up to +21.8%.
items.author: Ethan Lin, Akanksha Sarkar, Ziang Liu et al.

items.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
items.summary: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements. Specifically, we analyse the statistical properties of two distinct state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble (TE) conditioned on the measurement outcomes of the hybrid circuit, and the projected ensemble (PE) generated by further projective measurements of the system at the final temporal boundary. We find that both ensembles undergo non-analytic changes -- ensemble phase transitions -- at the critical point of the measurement-induced purification transition, despite their first moments remaining completely maximally mixed and blind to the transition.
items.author: Saptarshi Mandal, Sthitadhi Roy

items.title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
items.summary: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case.
items.author: C. S. Shahbazi

items.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
items.summary: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks.
items.author: Peiwen Li, Harshit Verma, Sophia Zhou et al.

items.title: Linking Rapid Learning to Compositional Structure in Neural Networks: Evidence from Additive Analogies in Meta-Learned Parameter Spaces
items.summary: Humans can learn rapidly from limited experience, while neural networks typically require extensive training. In this work, we investigate what properties of a neural network can enable it to learn rapidly. We study neural networks that have been optimized via meta-learning, a technique that exposes a network to many related functions to facilitate its subsequent learning of similar functions. Prior work has shown that these meta-learned networks can learn new functions rapidly, but how they do so remains unclear. To investigate their internal structure, we take inspiration from classic work demonstrating additive relationships among the learned vectors that neural networks use to represent words (e.g., "king" minus "man" plus "woman" approximates "queen").
items.author: Abigail L. Tenenbaum, R. Thomas McCoy

items.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
items.summary: Context attribution asks how removing parts of a prompt changes a language model's output. We study leave-one-out (LOO) attribution for a prompt of $n$ tokens and a fixed measurement function. Computing all LOO values directly requires $n$ model evaluations. Under a stability assumption, our algorithm estimates all LOO values to error proportional to $\varepsilon$ with constant probability using $O(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}/\varepsilon)$ evaluation calls. To complement our upper bound, we prove a matching $Ω(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}/\varepsilon)$ lower bound on the number of evaluation calls in an oracle model. Empirically, we verify coefficient decay consistent with stability and evaluate the performance of our sketching algorithm on a small language-model retrieval task.
items.author: Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas et al.

items.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
items.summary: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence.
items.author: Omar Bachain, Mohamed Amazioug, Rachid Ahl Laamara

items.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
items.summary: Looped models have emerged as a prominent paradigm for reasoning, with successes on simple reasoning puzzles such as Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique. However, these models can be unstable, slow to train, and use many parameters and FLOPs to solve simple puzzles. Descent on an energy not only mitigates these issues but also offers advantages: built-in early stopping, compute that adapts to problem difficulty, fast training without differentiating through a solver, and interpretable weights that learn the constraints of the puzzle. Here we demonstrate this with a learned version of Hopfield & Tank's energy from the 80s, which we term CRAM, solves 99.996% of Sudoku-Extreme and 100% of Maze-Unique test puzzles after 42 ms and 132 ms of training on one GPU, at least 1,000x faster than looped models on these tasks.
items.author: Benjamin Hoover, Hugh Blayney, James C. R. Whittington

items.title: Quantifying structural stability of transparent models for general insurance pricing
items.summary: The short duration of general insurance contracts leads to rapid distributional shifts in the data, warranting regular model updates. This process may yield a post-update model that differs considerably from the pre-update model in both predictions and structure. Structural stability is upstream of predictive stability, yet existing structural stability metrics are mostly restricted to simple decision trees. Thus, we first introduce the notion of functional transparency, characterising models with a prediction function that can be expressed as a sum of univariate functions for main effects and bivariate functions for pairwise interactions. Then, we propose the Mean Squared Shape function distance, a metric to quantify the structural stability of functionally transparent models, which are particularly relevant in actuarial science.
items.author: Félix Côté, Marie-Pier Côté

items.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
items.summary: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours.
items.author: Bibek Saha, David E. Logan, Sthitadhi Roy

items.title: Euclid data release 1 (DR1) - SIR spectroscopic calibration
items.summary: The Euclid space mission is dedicated to probing the nature of dark energy and dark matter, through a comprehensive mapping of the Universe's large-scale structure. Central to these cosmological goals are the spectra produced by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) and reduced by the scientific pipelines of the SIR (Spectral near InfraRed) processing function. Due to the intrinsic complexity of slitless spectroscopic data, scientific observations cannot be self-calibrated by the science pipelines. Consequently, the development of dedicated SIR calibration pipelines, utilising specific pointing sequences and observation fields, is essential. The resulting calibration products are fundamental to ensuring that reduced spectra are characterised within requirements in both wavelength and flux.
items.author: Euclid Collaboration, M. Fumana, Y. Copin et al.

items.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
items.summary: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%.
items.author: Divij Sharma, Roger de Belsunce, Mikhail M. Ivanov

items.title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
items.summary: Interactive video-to-video applications require real-time generation while maintaining long-range temporal consistency. However, recent methods achieve speed by restricting attention to a fixed-length causal window. This limits long-range consistency whenever relevant history falls outside the context window. To address this limitation, we introduce vid2vid-long, a correspondence-based approach grounded in a simple observation. Video-to-video translation provides an explicit cross-frame reference: the regions that match in the input video should match in the output video too. Concretely, we compute patch-level correspondences in the input, guiding retrieval of previously generated outputs in the corresponding regions, and condition the model on these patches through correspondence cross-attention.
items.author: Gaurav Parmar, Zhengqi Li, Richard Zhang et al.

items.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
items.summary: We investigate whether and how LLMs encode goals: internal neural representations that precede and guide action, and that are flexible enough to be realized through many different execution paths. We construct a coding setting with multiple sub-tasks that allows us to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and the selection of sub-goals. In this setting, we localize an encoding of the next sub-goal in the outputs of a sparse set of attention heads. The same heads can be used to decode the LM's future actions in natural language (e.g., "I'm checking if a word is a palindrome"). We verify that this encoding is causal for next action and is plastic: transplanting it into a different environment, e.g., another programming language, triggers the same operation realized with a different sequence of tokens.
items.author: Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht et al.

items.title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
items.summary: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal.
items.author: Paula I. Villar, Federico Guglielmucci Nazar, Elián Urtubey et al.

items.title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
items.summary: On-device inference requires kernels that make effective use of local accelerators. Efficient training and evaluation of models that generate Apple Metal kernels benefit from native macOS tools and concurrent agent sessions. These sessions alternate between model requests, development commands, and GPU execution, leaving GPU capacity idle for much of a rollout. We present Metal Sandbox, infrastructure that combines restricted per-instance file access, native command execution, and command-level scheduling across interconnected Macs. Each agent retains its workspace and private development environment. Parallel commands can run concurrently, while serial commands share one execution slot per node; eligible waiting commands can migrate to available Macs and return results to the original agent.
items.author: Haozhe Wang, Lina Chen, Fanqi Wan et al.

items.title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
items.summary: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit.
items.author: Zhiyao Yang, Bowen Xiao, Huangjun Zhu

items.title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
items.summary: Ceramic materials that maintain structural integrity and resist thermal-shock under extreme conditions are critical for many applications. Here we show that spark plasma sintered composites containing equal weight fractions of hexagonal silicon carbide (6H-SiC) and boron nitride (h-BN) exhibit exceptional stability under extreme high-temperature oxidizing conditions and unusually stable temperature-independent thermal conductivity across a broad temperature range. Under high-velocity oxygen-fuel torch exposure in air, it withstands prolonged heating and thermal-cycling at surface temperatures reaching >1500 °C, whereas pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractures or erodes. Microstructural evaluation shows the formation of a multi-phase surface silica layer that further protects the material from oxidation.
items.author: Abhijit Biswas, Eugenio Garcia-Granados, Saman Zare et al.

items.title: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
items.summary: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary.
items.author: Asaf Kapota, Jake P. Solomon

items.title: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
items.summary: Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility.
items.author: Bowen Xiao, Zhiyao Yang, Huangjun Zhu

items.title: Synthesis Smuggling: Maliciously Hiding Inferred Personal Attributes in LLM Outputs
items.summary: We propose Synthesis Smuggling, a novel threat model in which an adversarial LLM infers sensitive information about a user from routine assistance-seeking interactions and steganographically encodes that into innocuous-looking model-generated content. The user may then unknowingly transmit that information by sharing the generated artifact, say as an email, social-media post, or message, through ordinary communication channels. An adversary monitoring these channels can discover this information. We demonstrate this threat by training two open-weight models to infer gender and age-group labels from conversational cues and encode their predictions using invisible characters or word choices. These results show that user-shared model outputs can become a covert channel for personal inferences, even when the model itself has no direct means of contacting an adversary.
items.author: Gautam Galada, Supreeth Shastri, Sagnik Ray Choudhury

items.title: The $(5,5)$ String
items.summary: We study an $N=(2,1)$ heterotic string with right-movers on $\mathbb R^{2,2}$ and left-movers of signature $(5,5)$, obtained by adjoining the lattice $\mathrm{II}_{3,3}$. Unlike the standard $N=(2,1)$ strings it requires no null current, and its target space remains four-dimensional. All of its states, an infinite tower with sixteen supercharges, are massless. For the neutral bosons, the Kutasov-Martinec determinant action is dual to a cubic action for a self-dual metric coupled to self-dual Maxwell fields, and we complete it with fermions using a single superfield. For the charged states we give evidence that the couplings are the structure constants of a Lie superalgebra formed by the physical states of the left-movers.
items.author: Justin Kaidi

items.title: A precision bound for gravitational transseries
items.summary: We propose that the large $N$ transseries of a holographic observable above the black hole threshold admits a precision bound, a limit on how precisely the transseries can determine the observable at finite $N$, set by the data of its D-brane instanton sectors. In doing so, we develop methods in large $N$ resurgence, based on the work of Écalle, that capture the $e^{-N^2}$ asymptotics of gravitational saddles beyond the $e^{-N}$ instantons. Under an assumption on the growth of the D-brane instanton sums that we expect in the black hole phase, we find an analytic obstruction to the resummation of the large $N$ transseries.
items.author: Ji Hoon Lee

items.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
items.summary: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism.
items.author: Fabian Hahner, Natalie M. Paquette

items.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
items.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014.
items.author: Gilberto Borges, Saeid Salari, Ekta Panwar et al.

items.title: Love numbers for the Myers-Perry geometry
items.summary: We analyze Love numbers for scalar fields in the Myers-Perry geometry in arbitrary dimensions. The tidal responses of black holes are specified by two constants which encode a potential logarithmic running and the Love number. We argue that the parameter specifying the running is not sensitive to the structure of the horizon, and we explicitly compute this parameter for Myers-Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions by utilizing the asymptotic expansion of the wave equation. The Love numbers rely on the details of the boundary conditions at the horizon, and we compute them using several distinct approximations.
items.author: Rhucha Deshpande, Oleg Lunin

items.title: Monopole catalysis with massive fermions: the fate of the twisted sector
items.summary: In the massless limit a fermion scattering on the minimal $SU(5)$ monopole in the lowest partial wave produces an outgoing state with half-integer fermion number in every flavour. This state lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space and is now understood as an ordinary fermion attached to a topological line running back to the monopole. In the Standard Model fermion masses and confinement destroy the line at distances greater than the inverse mass scales, causing the twisted state to decay into physical asymptotic states with integer fermion numbers. We study this decay for an incoming lepton or quark of one generation.
items.author: Valentin V. Khoze

items.title: Implementation of a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD under finite-size parameter estimation
items.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is a promising technology for quantum-secure communications, offering high secret-key rates and straightforward integration with coherent optical communication systems. Conventional Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD encodes information in both optical-field quadratures, increasing requirements for state preparation, modulation, and calibration, while potentially introducing additional preparation imperfections. Unidimensional (1D) Gaussian modulation offers a simpler alternative by encoding information in only one quadrature, while the conjugate quadrature constrains the protocol's security. However, an integrated experimental 1D implementation combining independent-laser coherent reception with practical reconciliation, finite-size parameter estimation, and privacy amplification remains challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD system over 12~km of standard single-mode fiber using a local local oscillator (LLO) architecture with independent lasers and an integrated offline classical post-processing chain.
items.author: Christiano M. S. Nascimento, Maron F. Anka, Gabriel A. V. Menezes et al.

items.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
items.summary: For robots to assist, serve, and collaborate with humans, they must not only interpret human requests conveyed through language and multimodal intentional cues, but also execute long-horizon tasks that interleave navigation and manipulation. In this paper, we introduce HEIR, a resource for studying how to Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interaction. HEIR pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, while each session preserves successive episodes, with each request fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks. The captured data, together with human-authored annotations, support the study of intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion within a unified interaction setting.
items.author: Yichi Zhang, Bo Wang, Zhenghan Zhu et al.

items.title: Circular phonons generate negligible magnetization in insulators
items.summary: The optical excitation of circular phonons has opened up non-equilibrium phenomena with no equilibrium counterparts, ranging from the generation of synthetic magnetic fields to the control of topological order or the manipulation of ferroaxial states. In this area, significant controversy has arisen on whether sizeable "true" magnetizations accompany circular phonons. Several confounding factors cloud the interpretation of the experiments, which are based on probing polarization rotation in the driven material. These range from the interpretation of the Faraday effect in non-equilibrium conditions to spurious nonlinear optical contributions in pump probe experiments. Here we resolve these ambiguities by measuring both polarization rotation inside the driven material and the stray magnetic field generated outside it with a proximate Faraday detector.
items.author: C-C. Wu, M. Buzzi, A. Iudica et al.

items.title: Collaborative Task Allocation for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems Through Iterative Clustering
items.summary: Multi-robot systems face the challenge of efficiently allocating teams of heterogeneous robots to tasks. The task allocation problem is complicated by collaborative interactions between robots where teams of robots develop emergent capabilities that enable them to complete tasks that would be inefficient or impossible for individual robots. To address these challenges, we present an iterative clustering algorithm for collaborative task allocation in heterogeneous multi-robot systems. This approach partitions the computationally intractable global optimization problem into smaller, tractable subproblems by iteratively forming clusters of robots and tasks, then optimizing assignments within each cluster. By ensuring robots remain clustered with their currently assigned tasks, we guarantee monotonic improvement in overall utility with each iteration.
items.author: David R. Martin, Brooks A. Butler, Scott Nivison et al.

items.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
items.summary: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope.
items.author: Praniti Singh, JiJi Fan, Savvas M. Koushiappas et al.

items.title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
items.summary: Automatic differentiation has enabled rapid progress on continuous-variable mechanical design problems, but gradient-based optimization still struggles with discrete variables. The standard approach is to optimize using a continuous relaxation of the choices, then commit to the nearest discrete design at the end. Why this procedure selects unfavorable basins is poorly understood. Here, we introduce a practical, interpretable design problem inspired by origami, in which automatic differentiation is used to design shapes with a target functional behavior. Each origami sheet has a fixed geometry, and a bilevel optimization framework tunes which one of four discrete hinge types to place at each fold.
items.author: Lucy Liu, Leon M. Kamp, Katia Bertoldi et al.

items.title: NASA Ames Stars of the Month: November 2026
items.summary: The NASA Ames Science Directorate recognizes the outstanding contributions of (pictured left to right) Alyssa Villanueva, Steve Howell, and Samuel LeBlanc. Their commitment to the NASA mission represents the entrepreneurial spirit, technical expertise, and collaborative disposition needed to explore this world and beyond. Space Biosciences Star: Alyssa Villanueva Alyssa Villaneuva is an engineer at Blue […]
items.author: Aaron McKinnon

items.title: Two-loop mixed QCD-EW corrections to bottom-pair production in electron-positron collisions
items.summary: We present the two-loop mixed strong-electroweak virtual corrections to the production of a massive bottom-antibottom quark pair in electron-positron collisions. The evaluation of all the relevant Feynman integrals, including those with up to five internal massive lines with three different mass values, has been worked out relying on semi-analytical techniques, using complex-valued masses for the electroweak gauge bosons. The ultraviolet-renormalized and infrared-subtracted finite correction contributes to the NNLO QCD-EW cross section of the inclusive production of a bottom-quark pair. The methodology adopted in this calculation can be extended to the study of fully electroweak second-order corrections to benchmark precision calculations relevant to both the high-luminosity phase of the Large Hadron Collider and prospective future lepton colliders.
items.author: Simone Devoto, Chinmoy Dey, Michele Dradi et al.

items.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
items.summary: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO).
items.author: Donglin Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yantong Zhong et al.

items.title: XBot-Omni: An Omni-Modal Model for Embodied Understanding and Interaction
items.summary: Embodied interaction requires an agent to integrate multimodal perception with verbal and nonverbal behaviors to effectively communicate its intentions, including speech, body motion, and facial expressions. We present XBot-Omni, a Thinker--Talker--Actor architecture that extends the Omni paradigm to robotic modalities, including body motion and facial expressions, with ``X'' representing the extensibility to robotic-specific modalities. The Thinker processes text, images, audio, and video to formulate contextually appropriate responses, which are then realized by the Talker and Actor through speech and coordinated bodily expressions, respectively. In this report, we innovatively introduce the concept of ``Actor'' as a dedicated component for embodied agents: a coordinated, streaming module that leverages the native representations of the Thinker and Talker within an end-to-end pipeline, introducing only modest latency overhead.
items.author: Kerui Gu, Xing Fu, Shuoyang Sun et al.

items.title: Inner Product Regularization for Imitation Learning
items.summary: Robots that learn from demonstrations should extrapolate their policy despite state perturbations such as sensor noise, scene variation, and compounding errors. One approach to this robustness is regularization. Prior regularizers consider each state on its own and limit how sensitive the policy is to any perturbation at that state. By contrast, we explore how the policy's output shifts when given the same perturbation at different states. Our insight is that, locally, the robot should respond to state perturbations in a consistent manner: e.g., if changing an irrelevant object position does not impact the policy at one state, that same change should not shift the policy output at a nearby state.
items.author: Benjamin A. Christie, Tianyu Qiu, Amy H. Choi et al.

items.title: FORGE: Force-Aware Multi-Granularity Control for Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated locomotion, balance regulation, and manipulation under frequent contacts, making teleoperated demonstration collection difficult: a practical controller must simultaneously provide precision, stability, and contact awareness. We propose FORGE, a force-aware multi-granularity control system with a coarse-to-fine command space spanning velocity navigation, planar foot placement, wrist-pose tracking, and optional force-conditioning inputs. Policy training requires no full-body human motion trajectories or joint-angle references; deployment consumes only sparse bilateral wrist poses relative to the pelvis, coarse motion commands, and optional desired wrist-load inputs. For sustained contact, FORGE combines a momentum observer with a learned correction trained using simulator contact-force supervision.
items.author: Liangjun Xing, Ke Fan, Kailin Li et al.

items.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
items.summary: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $ππN$ effects on top of the two-body $πN$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $πΔ(1232)3/2^+$, and $πN(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $πN$ channel automatically.
items.author: Jinzi Wu, Michael Döring, Maxim Mai

items.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts.
items.author: Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Haonan Wang et al.

items.title: High-pressure behavior of the low-frequency mode of water
items.summary: The low-frequency (LF) mode observed in the THz spectrum of liquid water near 10 meV has been known for decades, yet its microscopic origin remains debated. Leading interpretations assign it to a transverse acoustic-like excitation, a transverse optic-like mode, or a mode-mode coupling mechanism. We address this question by probing the collective dynamics of H$_2$O and D$_2$O at room temperature and pressures from 0.1 to 1 GPa using high-resolution (1.6 meV) inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS). The LF mode remains heavily damped, close to critical damping, throughout the explored range, while its frequency hardens markedly with pressure, much more than expected for a transverse acoustic mode.
items.author: Maria Rescigno, Guillaume Radtke, Umbertoluca Ranieri et al.

items.title: Nonperturbative Kinetic Description of the Vacuum QGP Production in the Abelian Projection Method
items.summary: Within the framework of the Abelian projection method in the $SU(N)$ variant of QCD, a system of nonperturbative selfconsistent equations for the back-reaction problem is derived. This system describes the vacuum production of quarks under the influence of strong quasiclassical gluon fields taking into account violating of the electroneutrality condition.
items.author: V. V. Dmitriev, S. V. Churochkina, S. A. Smolyansky et al.

items.title: Asymmetric Frequency Conversion and Violation of Kirchhoff's Law of Thermal Radiation in Phased Floquet Metasurfaces
items.summary: We study a system of three closely spaced conducting sheets, whose thermal emission largely violates Kirchhoff's law through nonreciprocal frequency conversion enabled by Floquet phenomena. We leverage surface mode transitions controlled by temporal modulation of one of the metasurfaces, resulting in largely asymmetric frequency conversion. Our findings broaden the capabilities of Floquet metasurfaces for wave conversion and energy manipulation, paving the way towards magnet-free nonreciprocal photonic devices with opportunities for thermal management and efficient photonic refrigeration.
items.author: Yao-Ting Wang, Emanuele Galiffi, Sander A. Mann et al.

items.title: Pseudovortex-assisted generation of first-order vector modes
items.summary: A practical method of generating first-order vector modes like radially and azimuthally polarized modes is using the so-called vortex waveplates. Shining these plates with Gaussian beams produces parasitic higher-order modes besides the target vector beam. The reason is that there is a mismatch between the incident Gaussian mode and the doughnut-shaped profile required for the vector beam. This imposes a limit on the fidelity of the generated mode with respect to the target vector beam. In this work we demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that this limit can be overcome if the input Gaussian beam is replaced with a pseudovortex beam, which is a doughnut-shaped mode without topological charge.
items.author: L. Marques Fagundes, P. Schneider Lacerda, T. A. Petry Kock et al.

items.title: UV and deep-UV ultrafast harmonic generation enhanced by resonant gold nano-pillar metasurface
items.summary: We report experimental observations and full-vector numerical simulations of second and third-harmonic generation from a two-dimensional periodic gold nano-pillar metasurface, for efficient ultrafast light conversion from near-infrared to the UV and deep-UV spectral ranges. The metasurface is designed to support an angle-tunable plasmonic resonance in the near-infrared spectral range, with its resonance wavelength shifting as a function of the pump angle of incidence. Under resonant conditions, strong electromagnetic-field confinement near the nano-pillar corners enhances the nonlinear light-matter interactions. Compared with a flat gold mirror, the nanostructured metal exhibits enhanced nonlinear frequency conversion, with conversion efficiencies of second and third-harmonic generation increased by two and three orders of magnitude, respectively.
items.author: Shroddha Mukhopadhyay, Yuxuan Chen, Hooman Barati Sedeh et al.

items.title: Proton Spin Fluctuation Decomposition
items.summary: We formulate a fluctuation decomposition of proton spin in terms of the variances and covariances of the spin and orbital angular momentum of quarks and gluons. We derive their representations in terms of single- and double-parton distributions. The definite proton spin imposes sum rules requiring the variances of its spin and orbital contributions to be compensated by their covariances. This framework reveals correlations and fluctuations that are invisible to the conventional proton spin decomposition.
items.author: Tomoya Uji

items.title: Reflection Zeros Set the Scattering Invariant of Finite Majorana Wires
items.summary: Majorana modes, zero-energy excitations of superconducting wires that are their own antiparticles, could store quantum information protected from local noise. In transport experiments, however, ordinary bound states mimic their signature, a conductance peak at zero voltage, and whether Majorana modes have been observed remains debated. A sign, $Q$, of the electron reflection at zero energy marks the topological phase of a long wire, but what $Q$ certifies in a finite device has been unclear. Here we show for the first time that $Q$ counts reflectionless states, waves that enter through one contact and leave entirely through the other: $Q=-1$ when an odd number of them lie in the lower half of the complex energy plane.
items.author: Alex Krasnok

items.title: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
items.summary: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.
items.author: Ashish Pandav, Zhangbu Xu, Bedangadas Mohanty

items.title: Lorentz Boosts and Governing Equations of the Quantum Geometric Tensor in 4D Energy-Momentum Space
items.summary: In solids, the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), $Q_{μν}=g_{μν}-\frac{i}{2} Ω_{μν}$, combines the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Its imaginary part governs anomalous velocity and quantized Hall transport, while its real part determines the quantum weight and geometric contributions to flat-band superfluid stiffness and dielectric response. Here, we extend the QGT to four-dimensional (4D) energy-momentum space ($ω/c,k$), treating frequency and momentum as independent coordinates. Invariance of the real-spacetime plane-wave phase fixes their Lorentz transformation in energy-momentum space. Lorentz boosts of static Dirac and Weyl systems then generate frequency metrics, quadrupolar frequency-momentum shear metrics, and electric-like Berry-Maxwell fields. We identify five Lorentz-invariant contractions and derive the governing field equations and flow conservation laws for both the quantum metric and Berry curvature from static Weyl geometry and Lorentz covariance.
items.author: Yiming Pan

items.title: M 4.5 - 115 km ESE of Bitung, Indonesia
items.summary: A magnitude 4.5 earthquake was recorded 115 km ESE of Bitung, Indonesia. The event happened on 12 November 2026 at 14:58 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 39 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Two Unconventional Hall Effects in the Kagome Magnet TmMn4Cr$_2$Sn$_6$
items.summary: We identify two Hall anomalies in the kagome magnet TmMn$_4$Cr$_2$Sn$_6$. We propose that the high-field anomaly reflects a discontinuous spin reorientation and differing sublattice contributions to Hall transport and magnetization. At low fields, Hall hysteresis persists despite negligible magnetic hysteresis, suggesting a chirality-related contribution, although its microscopic origin remains unresolved. These contrasting regimes show how magnetic transitions can mimic unconventional Hall signals and highlight the limits of magnetization-based Hall decomposition.
items.author: Mohamed El Gazzah, Fehmi Sami Yasin, Bishal Thapa et al.

items.title: The importance of genes does not predict their mutation rate
items.summary: by Sofia Radrizzani, Laurence D. Hurst The convention that mutation is a random process has been challenged by suggestions that selection has acted on between-gene variation in the mutation rate, with claims that more important genes are protected from mutation in part, in prokaryotes, by being on the leading strand, while those required for rapid adaptive evolution have higher mutation rates, in part by being on the lagging strand. The original selectionist claims have proven contentious with several replication failures. However, none of the replication attempts fully allow for covariates and many employ data from mismatch repair (MMR) knockout strains.
items.author: Sofia Radrizzani, Laurence D. Hurst

items.title: Neural integration of acoustic statistics enables mice to detect acoustic targets in noise
items.summary: by Artoghrul Alishbayli, Karol Przewrocki, Paul van Heumen, Bernhard Englitz Sound detection amidst noise presents an important challenge in audition. Many naturally occurring sounds (rain, wind) can be described and predicted only statistically, so-called sound textures. Previous research has demonstrated the human ability to leverage this statistical predictability for sound recognition, but the neural mechanisms remain elusive. We trained mice to detect vocalizations embedded in sound textures with different statistical predictability, while recording and optogenetically modulating the neural activity in the auditory cortex. Mice showed improved performance and neural encoding if they could sample the statistics longer per trial. Textures with more exploitable structure, specifically higher cross-frequency correlations improved behavioral performance as well as neural representation of vocalizations.
items.author: Artoghrul Alishbayli, Karol Przewrocki, Paul van Heumen et al.

items.title: Category learning drives cortical attentional gain to diagnostic dimensions of perceptual information
items.summary: by Sahil Luthra, Raha N. Razin, Adam T. Tierney, Lori L. Holt, Frederic Dick Humans and other animals develop remarkable perceptual and cognitive specializations for identifying, differentiating, and acting on classes of ecologically important signals. This expertise is flexible enough to support diverse perceptual judgments: a voice, for example, simultaneously conveys what a talker says, as well as myriad cues about her identity and state. Expert perception across complex signals thus involves discovering and learning regularities that best inform diverse perceptual judgments, as well as weighting this information flexibly as task demands change. Here, we test whether this process may involve attentional gain.
items.author: Sahil Luthra, Raha N. Razin, Adam T. Tierney et al.

items.title: Life-cycle plasticity enables conditional asexual reproduction in a kelp
items.summary: by Daniel Liesner, Rémy Luthringer, Lineekela Kandjengo, John J. Bolton, Mark D. Rothman, Myriam Valero, Fabian B. Haas, Susana M. Coelho Many organisms alternate between distinct life stages and can reproduce either sexually or asexually, yet the mechanisms coordinating these developmental and reproductive transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the molecular basis of life stage identity and reproductive mode in the kelp Laminaria pallida , a multicellular organism with a complex life cycle. By combining gene expression analyses with developmental experiments and natural population-level approaches, we characterize the transcriptional signatures associated with developmental state transitions in both sexual and asexual contexts.
items.author: Daniel Liesner, Rémy Luthringer, Lineekela Kandjengo et al.

items.title: Decomposition of the S. aureus pangenome reveals evolving genetic repertoire associated with adaptation and virulence
items.summary: by Siddharth M. Chauhan, Bernhard O. Palsson, Jonathan M. Monk Bacterial pangenomes are mosaics of vertically inherited chromosomal backgrounds and horizontally acquired mobile elements, yet existing analysis methods either assign each genome to a single phylogenetic group or treat genes independently, failing to resolve this composite architecture. Here, we show that non-negative matrix factorization decomposes the accessory pangenome of 1,398 curated Staphylococcus aureus genomes into 24 additive gene modules (“phylons”) that cleanly separate lineage-defining components from mobile genetic element repertoires, achieving 90% reconstruction accuracy with 96% precision. The additive representation, where each genome equals a primary lineage phylon plus one or more mobilome phylons, recovers known biology (clonal complex structure, immune evasion cluster types) and reveals previously uncharacterized structure, including multiple horizontal transfer events linking the CC30 and hybrid ST239 pandemic lineages.
items.author: Siddharth M. Chauhan, Bernhard O. Palsson, Jonathan M. Monk

items.title: Novel enzymes for amino acid biosynthesis in diverse bacteria and archaea: GapMind 2026
items.summary: by Morgan N. Price, Valentine V. Trotter, Markus de Raad, Suzanne M. Kosina, Hira P. Lesea, Anthony L. Shiver, Leslie A. Day, Surya Tripathi, Marta Torres, Trenton K. Owens, Audrey Liwen Wang, Anna Lisa Fear, Xuanyu Tao, Jizhong Zhou, Adam M. Deutschbauer, Adam P. Arkin We previously described GapMind, an automated web-based tool for annotating amino acid biosynthesis pathways in bacterial and archaeal genomes. We used GapMind to identify gaps in biosynthetic pathways and systematically used comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics to identify candidate genes to fill these gaps. We confirmed the activity of ten of the proposed enzymes by using cross-species complementation assays.
items.author: Morgan N. Price, Valentine V. Trotter, Markus de Raad et al.

items.title: Singapore grouper iridovirus VP018 exploits FTR86 to promote viral replication through Tollip-mediated degradation of the STING-TBK1 axis
items.summary: by Linyong Zhi, Mengdi Yuan, Guimei Zhang, Dongmiao Xiao, Xinyi Ren, Qiwei Qin, Xiaohong Huang, Youhua Huang Members of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family have been demonstrated to exert crucial roles in immune defense against pathogens. However, functions of the fish-specific TRIM subfamily (FTR), which lacks mammalian orthologues, remains poorly understood. In the current study, we investigated the potential roles of grouper FTR86 (EcFTR86) on innate immune response and its actions during fish virus infection. EcFTR86 was found to localize to lysosomes, and its transcription was significantly up-regulated in grouper spleen cells upon Singapore grouper iridovirus (SGIV) infection. Notably, the exogenous expression of EcFTR86 markedly enhanced SGIV replication, whereas knockdown of endogenous EcFTR86 significantly attenuated viral infection, demonstrating that EcFTR86 functions as a pro-viral factor against virus infection.
items.author: Linyong Zhi, Mengdi Yuan, Guimei Zhang et al.

items.title: Correction: Nucleocapsid-like cryo-EM structure of influenza B virus
items.summary: by Marie Thirion, Alice J. Stelfox, Florian Chenavier, Héléna Chomat, Catherine Isel, Lily-Lorette Freslon, Eleftherios Zarkadas, Rob W. H. Ruigrok, Nadia Naffakh, Thibaut Crépin, Allison Ballandras-Colas
items.author: Marie Thirion, Alice J. Stelfox, Florian Chenavier et al.

items.title: Correction: Lipopolysaccharide-induced alterations in barrier integrity and inflammatory signaling in porcine small intestinal organoids
items.summary: by Sumin Park, Boram Lee, Dahye Kim, Sheet Sunirmal, Min Gook Lee, Haesun Lee, Sun A. Ock, Jae Gyu Yoo
items.author: Sumin Park, Boram Lee, Dahye Kim et al.

items.title: Problem-solving and social support appraisals in the cross-sectional association between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity
items.summary: by Tyrone B. Pretorius, Anita Padmanabhanunni The present study investigated the relationship between social media integration and PTSD-consistent symptomatology among South African university students, with a specific focus on the roles of problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support. Participants were 491 students who completed the Social Media Use Integration Scale, the Problem-Solving Inventory-20, the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, and the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlations, and mediation and moderation analyses with PROCESS. Social media integration was positively associated with overall PTSD-consistent symptomatology and all symptom clusters measured by the PCL-5.
items.author: Tyrone B. Pretorius, Anita Padmanabhanunni

items.title: Paired neutrophil association and ex vivo perturbation sensitivity define a bounded myeloid activation model in ARDS
items.summary: by Wei Wei, Jing Liu, Ying Zhou, Rui Zhao, LinGang Zhang Background Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is biologically heterogeneous, but how myeloid transcriptional programmes relate across blood and lung compartments remains uncertain. We examined whether a pre-specified neutrophil effector/degranulation programme and a separately derived perturbation-response module provide convergent, boundary-aware evidence across public cohorts. Methods Patient-level analyses descriptively localized programmes in a seven-patient peripheral blood mononuclear cell cohort and assessed paired bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and longitudinal alveolar-macrophage profiles. PBMC disease groups were severely confounded with expression-inferred sex. In purified neutrophils, paired ARDS–healthy-volunteer comparisons and healthy-donor granulocyte–macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF)/broad phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) perturbations were analysed separately.
items.author: Wei Wei, Jing Liu, Ying Zhou et al.

items.title: Social media–related dietary behaviors and integrated behavioral model constructs among university students: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Amani Alhazmi, Maha Ali, Manal Mohammed Hawash, Bali Sharma, Ali Mohieldin, Mahmoud Abdelwahab Khedr Background Social media exposes young adults to nutrition information, food marketing, peer norms, and health-related content. However, evidence on social media–related dietary behaviors and their links to Integrated Behavioral Model (IBM) constructs among Saudi university students is limited. This study examined these behaviors, IBM constructs, and factors associated with the Dietary Habits score among King Khalid University (KKU) students. Methods A cross-sectional study included 385 KKU undergraduates, recruited through convenience sampling between February and April 2026. Participants completed the Arabic IBM-based Social Media and Dietary Habits Questionnaire.
items.author: Amani Alhazmi, Maha Ali, Manal Mohammed Hawash et al.

items.title: Evidence for an upper cretaceous strandline deposit in the Lance Formation, Wyoming, USA
items.summary: by Keith Snyder, Nelson Llempen, Caleb Darling, Alessandro Franchini, Matthew McLain, Arthur Chadwick A series of apparently related quarries in the Maastrichtian (uppermost Cretaceous) Lance Formation of Wyoming provided the opportunity to evaluate the taphonomic mode for a suite of vertebrate fossils. Extensive work on the Hanson Ranch over the past three decades has exposed tens of thousands of fossils from dinosaur-bearing bonebeds. All of these bonebeds consist of disarticulated and disassociated remains. However, seven recently discovered quarries have yielded the remains of one or more dinosaur taxa (e.g., Triceratops, Edmontosaurus, Thescelosaurus, Anzu) in a state of association that was hitherto unknown on the ranch.
items.author: Keith Snyder, Nelson Llempen, Caleb Darling et al.

items.title: Analytical performances and field assessment of a multiplex Real-Time PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto in wild canids fecal samples
items.summary: by Graziana Da Rold, Filippo Marzoli, Federica Obber, Roberto Celva, Alessia Franzoso, Giacomo De Conti, Elisa Dalla Libera, Patrizia Danesi, Sofia Sgubin, Rudi Cassini, Erica Marchiori, Dominik Trenkwalder, Piero Bonelli, Giovanna Masala, Chiara Rossi, Heidi Christine Hauffe, Carlo Vittorio Citterio Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato are the causative agents of alveolar and cystic echinococcosis, two important zoonoses with significant public health implications. Several diagnostic approaches are currently available for the detection of these parasites in definitive hosts, including classical parasitological methods and molecular techniques. However, conventional techniques such as intestinal scraping or copromicroscopy are often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and require skilled personnel, while some molecular assays may show limited sensitivity or specificity.
items.author: Graziana Da Rold, Filippo Marzoli, Federica Obber et al.

items.title: Cognitive and physiological responses to prolonged video viewing: Activities of the autonomic nervous system and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis in relation to video interest
items.summary: by Hiroki Matsui, Rina Tanabe, Rikako Mogi, Yuka Sugiura, Hana Yokomachi, Tomoyuki Yokoyama In recent years, online lectures and conferences have become widespread, but prolonged video viewing has been suggested to affect psychological state and physiological regulation. However, few studies have objectively examined how such viewing influences autonomic and endocrine activity. This study aimed to evaluate changes in autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity during the viewing of high- and low-interest videos. Twenty-six university students (10 males, 16 females; aged 21–24 years) watched high-interest (comedy) and low-interest (lecture) videos (90 minutes each). After viewing each video, they recorded subjective ratings of concentration, comprehension, interest, and fatigue.
items.author: Hiroki Matsui, Rina Tanabe, Rikako Mogi et al.

items.title: A Poisson-multinomial model for quantifying gene therapy vector integrity using quadplex digital PCR
items.summary: by Lauren Tereshko, Matthew Ryals, Cullen Mason, Romi Admanit, Jake Gagnon Quantitative characterization of gene therapy vectors is critical for confirming product safety and efficacy. While digital PCR (dPCR) strategies are widely used to estimate sequence integrity, accurate statistical interpretation of multiplexed assays remains a persistent challenge due to limitations of existing analytical models. Here, we describe a quadplex droplet dPCR approach for quantitative characterization of vector integrity across four targets within a single reaction. We adapt a Poisson-multinomial model to enable quantitation of sequence integrity and genetic linkage across all combinations of the four targeted regions. We evaluate both the capabilities and limitations of this approach and provide practical guidance for multiplexed assay design and data interpretation.
items.author: Lauren Tereshko, Matthew Ryals, Cullen Mason et al.

items.title: Network analysis of physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress among Chinese university students
items.summary: by Jingbo Wang, Yuanyuan Ma, Tong Han, Juan Wang Objective Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress may be interconnected among university students, but their dimension-specific associations remain unclear. This study examined their network structure and compared male and female networks. Methods A convenience sample of 1,600 university students from two higher-education institutions in central China was surveyed from 16 March to 29 May 2026. Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales. A 12-node regularized partial correlation network was estimated. Expected influence, bridge expected influence, bootstrap procedures, and network comparison tests were used.
items.author: Jingbo Wang, Yuanyuan Ma, Tong Han et al.

items.title: The true cost of dialysis modalities: A detailed analysis from a UK renal centre
items.summary: by Nitin V. Kolhe, Andrew Muggleton, Lisa Page, Richard J. Fluck, Maarten W. Taal Purpose Dialysis accounts for more than £1 billion of annual NHS expenditure, yet contemporary modality-specific costing studies using real-world operational data remain limited. Accurate cost estimates are essential for service planning, reimbursement, and workforce allocation. We hypothesised that home-based dialysis modalities, particularly home haemodialysis (HHD) and continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD), would be less costly and associated with a more favourable cost–benchmark margin than in-centre haemodialysis (ICHD) when workforce, consumables, infrastructure, and overheads were fully allocated. Materials and methods A comprehensive micro-costing analysis was undertaken at University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust during 2023–24.
items.author: Nitin V. Kolhe, Andrew Muggleton, Lisa Page et al.

items.title: An invariant-guided model for automated detection of anomalous execution regimes from production telemetry
items.summary: by Viacheslav Kovtun, Frederic Huralnyk, Artem Huralnyk, Marta Yankiv, Jamil Abedalrahim Jamil Alsayaydeh Modern cloud-based distributed software systems increasingly exhibit persistent changes in execution behaviour that cannot be adequately characterised by isolated events or threshold violations alone. Although contemporary production environments already provide mature observability infrastructures for collecting logs, metrics, and traces, the formal representation of execution regimes derived from such telemetry remains insufficiently developed. This paper proposes an invariant-guided geometric framework for modelling execution regimes and detecting anomalous regime transitions under weak supervision. The framework applies common principles of invariant-based feature mapping, weighted pseudometrics, and geometric regularisation to log-derived and KPI-derived regime representations.
items.author: Viacheslav Kovtun, Frederic Huralnyk, Artem Huralnyk et al.

items.title: Dose-dependent hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics in BALB/c mice
items.summary: by Samia Iftikhar, Hassien M. Alnashiri, Mehnaz Akhtar, Zuniar Ahsan, Muhammad Latif, A. El-Shabasy, Mohamed Mostafa Soliman Microplastics have emerged as pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing concern regarding their potential adverse effects on mammalian health. However, comprehensive evaluations of the dose-related hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) remain limited. This study investigated the effects of oral exposure to PS-MPs on hepatic and renal function in BALB/c mice. Animals were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 10/group) and orally administered 0 (control), 10, 20, or 30 mg PS-MPs/kg body weight/day for 28 consecutive days. Hepatorenal toxicity was evaluated using serum biochemical biomarkers, histopathological examination, semi-quantitative lesion scoring, and Pearson’s correlation analysis.
items.author: Samia Iftikhar, Hassien M. Alnashiri, Mehnaz Akhtar et al.

items.title: Seasonal dynamics of leaf macro- and micronutrients in three commercial avocado varieties at Mojo and Melkassa, Ethiopia
items.summary: by Zeyede Aregahegn, Edossa Etissa, Israel Bekele, Dejene Abera Seasonal leaf nutrient data needed to guide fertilization are scarce for Ethiopian avocado orchards. We measured total nitrogen (TN), Ca, Cu, Fe, Mn and Zn in leaves of tagged Hass, Fuerte and Ettinger trees at the Melkassa Agricultural Research Center (February–July) and of Hass trees on three farms at Mojo (February–June), and described the soils of both sites. Data were analysed with linear mixed models, Tukey’s test and repeated-measures correlation. Mean leaf TN (1.13–1.41%) was below the sufficiency range in all varieties and did not differ significantly between months, varieties or sites, and leaf Zn was below 20 mg/kg in most samples.
items.author: Zeyede Aregahegn, Edossa Etissa, Israel Bekele et al.

items.title: Patient complaints in dentistry: A qualitative meta-synthesis
items.summary: by Lorraine Snyman, Thomas Corne Postma, Werdie Van Staden Introduction Patient complaints in dentistry concern their dissatisfaction, safety concerns, quality of care, and challenges within the patient-practitioner relationship. Whilst existing research of these complaints has largely focused on quantitative analysis of regulatory complaints and malpractice, these studies capture little of the meaning that patients express in their complaints. This study synthesized a qualitative understanding of patient complaints across various dentistry settings. Method This qualitative meta-synthesis followed the six-step approach of Sandelowski and Barroso, drawing on previously published qualitative findings from various studies that constituted a higher-order case as suggested by Hoon’s design framework.
items.author: Lorraine Snyman, Thomas Corne Postma, Werdie Van Staden

This study aimed to evaluate the impact of implementing the Medi-Span CDSS, a rule-based artificial intelligence, on clinical pharmacy interventions in a tertiary care hospital. Methods This retrospective analysis compared clinical pharmacy interventions before and after CDSS integration with a computerized physician order entry (CPOE) system using data from electronic health records.
