items.title: The effect of self-determination interventions on reading outcomes for middle and high school students with learning disabilities: A systematic review
items.summary: by Mohammed A. Aljufayr, Abdulrahman S. Alsultan, Abdulaziz M. Alasmari Background Students with learning disabilities (LD) often struggle with reading skills, increasing the need for interventions that enhance their reading outcomes. Self-determination (SD) interventions can develop reading skills for students in all grade levels, but previous reviews of SD intervention studies have focused on elementary school students. This systematic review investigated the effects of SD interventions on reading outcomes for middle and high school students with LD. Methods Seventeenth studies published between 1982 and 2025 in scholarly journals were reviewed, examining participant demographics, settings, designs, intervention procedures, dependent variables, interobserver agreement, procedural fidelity, social validity, maintenance, generalization, intervention effects, and quality.
items.author: Mohammed A. Aljufayr, Abdulrahman S. Alsultan, Abdulaziz M. Alasmari

items.title: RPDL-YOLO: An efficient YOLOv8 framework for small bird detection in airport airside environments
items.summary: by Xinling Wen, Liming Liu, Yu Chen, Zhaoyu Liu, Zhengxiang Ma, Yapeng Wu, Kun Liang, Teng Jiang, Heng Yang Bird intrusions into airport security zones pose significant threats to aviation safety. However, the small size, rapid movement, and irregular flight patterns of birds often result in missed detections and false alarms in vision-based surveillance systems, especially in complex open-sky environments with low contrast and significant background interference. Although YOLOv8s achieves strong real-time performance, it remains limited in fine-grained feature representation and small-object detection capability. To address these challenges, we propose an improved detection model termed RPDL-YOLO (Refined Perception with Dual-branch Detection and Localization YOLO).
items.author: Xinling Wen, Liming Liu, Yu Chen et al.

items.title: The effectiveness of compression garments on RRI prevention in half- and full-marathon runners: Emulation of a RCT using data from an observational study
items.summary: by T. P. C. Franke, N. P. A. Zuithoff, F. J. G. Backx, B. M. A. Huisstede Background Runners use compression garments (CGs) to reduce the risk of lower extremity running-related injuries (RRIs). However, studies investigating if using CGs alters the risk of RRIs in runners are scarce. Purpose To study the effect of CGs on the occurrence of lower extremity RRIs in half and full marathon runners. Study design Observational cohort study Method We emulated a hypothetical target trial, an imaginary RCT, using data from the observational SUMMUM-2017 study. Runners who participated in one of the four cohorts of this study during their preparation for the half or full Utrecht Marathon were followed for 16 weeks.
items.author: T. P. C. Franke, N. P. A. Zuithoff, F. J. G. Backx et al.

items.title: Prevalence and factors associated with irregular red blood cell antibodies among blood donors in Eastern Tanzania
items.summary: by Mariam Charles Monah, Vulstan James Shedura, Peter Richard Torokaa, Loveness Urio, Seif Abdul, Rosemary Bulemo, Mariam R. Mbwana, Sephord S. Ntibabara, Oscar Mwashiuya, Beatrice Tingo, Macdonald Mahiti, Upendo Kibwana, Salim Masoud, Joel Manyahi, Mtebe Majigo, Agricola Joachim, Doreen Kamori Background Irregular red blood cell (RBC) antibodies are antibodies other than naturally occurring anti-A and anti-B. Although the global prevalence of these antibodies is relatively low, ranging from 0.2% to 2%, donors who have irregular RBC antibodies can present immunological risk for patients due to hemolytic transfusion reactions. Hence, it is imperative to determine the prevalence of these antibodies in resource-limited settings where laboratory infrastructure for screening is limited.

items.title: The effects of dual task training to improve self-efficacy, functional performance, and quality of life in individuals with Parkinson’s disease: A study protocol
items.summary: by Alvaro Reyes-Ponce, Travis Cruickshank, Andrea Mira, Nuria Pérez-Romero, Josefa Domingos Introduction Dual tasking is impaired in Parkinson’s disease (PD) and adversely impacts activities of daily living and quality of life. The benefits of different dual-task training modalities and the prioritization strategy (directing attention to both tasks versus shifting between them) in individuals with or without cognitive impairment are unclear. It is also unknown whether motor-cognitive benefits from dual-task training are associated with reduced attentional demand. In addition, lower perceived ability to succeed at a specific task (self-efficacy) is associated with worse motor and non-motor symptoms and quality of life.

items.title: Public evaluation of food safety: Changes and influencing factors from the perspective of social governance — Evidence from CSS data (2006–2023)
items.summary: by Han Lin This study used descriptive analysis and multinomial logistic regression on seven‑wave Chinese Social Survey (CSS) data spanning 2006‑2023 to systematically examine long‑term trends and determinants of public food‑safety evaluation. Public food‑safety evaluation exhibited a phased “rise‑fall‑rise” mean score pattern across the study period. Level of social security showed a consistent significant positive correlation with food‑safety evaluation in all seven survey years ( p < 0.001) with fluctuating‑yet‑growing effect sizes; for the “very safe vs. very unsafe” contrast, the odds ratio fell from 2.056 (2006) then rebounded to 2.201 (2023). In year‑stratified models, educational attainment had a stable negative association with food‑safety evaluation, whereas control‑variable effects including gender and age varied across survey waves.
items.author: Han Lin

items.title: The relationship between ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and reactive postural control mechanisms in response to anterior perturbations
items.summary: by Mosa Pashaei, Hadi Ramezanloo, Mohamadreza Hatefi Adequate ankle dorsiflexion range of motion (DF-ROM) is essential for generating sufficient corrective torque during an ankle strategy; however, limitations in dorsiflexion may mechanically constrain this response, potentially leading to earlier reliance on hip or stepping strategies. Although indirect evidence links dorsiflexion capacity to dynamic balance performance, it remains unclear whether restricted dorsiflexion influences the selection of reactive postural control strategies in healthy young adults. Twenty active male participants were recruited for this study. Ankle DF-ROM was measured via the weight-bearing lunge test and categorized as either normal (≥20°) or restricted ( χ 2 (2) = 0.826, p = 0.662).
items.author: Mosa Pashaei, Hadi Ramezanloo, Mohamadreza Hatefi

items.title: SeqBattNet: A discrete-state physics-informed neural network with aging adaptation for battery modeling
items.summary: by Khoa Tran, Hung-Cuong Trinh, Vy-Rin Nguyen, T. Nguyen-Thoi, Vin Nguyen-Thai, Hung Pham, Ho-Si-Hung Nguyen Accurate battery modeling is essential for reliable state estimation in modern applications, such as predicting the remaining discharge time and remaining discharge energy in battery management systems. Existing approaches face several limitations: model-based methods require a large number of physical parameters; data-driven methods rely heavily on labeled datasets; and current physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often lack aging adaptation, still depend on many physical parameters, or require continuous state regeneration. In this work, we propose SeqBattNet, a discrete-state PINN with built-in aging adaptation for battery modeling to predict terminal voltage during the discharge process.
items.author: Khoa Tran, Hung-Cuong Trinh, Vy-Rin Nguyen et al.

items.title: Mobility-state- and handover-direction-aware analytical and machine learning-based HCP optimization in 5G heterogeneous networks
items.summary: by Fozia Panhwer, Muhammad Mujtaba Shaikh, Beenish Ansari, Iqra Ameer, Mohamed A. Elmagzoub, Asadullah Shaikh The use of ultra-dense small cells in 5G heterogeneous networks increases capacity, coverage and spectral efficiency, but it also complicates mobility management. In dense macro-small-cell networks, user devices often cross cells with varying coverage, transmit power, and propagation conditions, which can lead to high risks of radio-link failure, handover failure, ping-pong handover and unnecessary handover. These problems are exacerbated by using fixed handover-control settings, in which a single-value handover margin and time-to-trigger cannot provide a good trade-off across UE velocities and handover directions. In this paper, we propose a mobility-state- and handover-direction-aware HCP optimization for 5G HetNets while retaining the Event A3 handover scheme, state-based handover flow and radio-link-monitoring framework.
items.author: Fozia Panhwer, Muhammad Mujtaba Shaikh, Beenish Ansari et al.

items.title: Generation and in vitro functional characterization of anti-CD22 chimeric antigen receptor T cells derived from newly generated monoclonal antibody clones
items.summary: by Wipawadee Ruengdej, Vichaya Chuthaphakdikun, Sirirut Jewmoung, Nithidol Sakunrangsit, Chatikorn Boonkrai, Trairak Pisitkun, Supannikar Tawinwung, Koramit Suppipat Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies, but relapse after CD19-directed therapy remains a major challenge, often because of loss or downregulation of CD19 expression. CD22 is an attractive alternative target because it is expressed on malignant B cells, including in many cases of CD19-negative disease. In this study, we generated and characterized novel anti-CD22 monoclonal antibody–derived CAR constructs for in vitro evaluation. Four anti-CD22 monoclonal antibody clones were initially screened, and two clones, 24A7G6 and 29H9C8, were selected for CAR development based on their favorable binding and CAR surface expression profiles.
items.author: Wipawadee Ruengdej, Vichaya Chuthaphakdikun, Sirirut Jewmoung et al.

items.title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
items.summary: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties.
items.author: Minh Nghia Nguyen, Beate Paulus, Akhil S. Nair

items.title: Large Pockels Effect in Multiaxial Ferroelectrics Induced by Polarization Reorientation
items.summary: Materials with large linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect have significant potential for fabricating energy-efficient photonic devices. Previous strategies have mostly relied on structural softness---associated with phase boundary, domain wall, or strain induced phase transition---to create large Pockels effect in ferroelectrics. In this Letter, we show that polarization reorientation in multiaxial ferroelectrics may create structural softness and thus induce large Pockels effect. By developing a phenomenological theory, we find that multiaxial ferroelectrics exhibit a hysteretic relationship between the azimuth angles of the polarization and the electric field, and a possible divergence of the linear electro-optic coefficient may occur at an appropriate polarization azimuth angle.

items.title: Discrete anomaly inflow from SymTFT of $U(1)$ global symmetry: the modified Villain resolution
items.summary: We construct a lattice SymTFT for a $U(1)$ global symmetry with anomaly coefficient $k$ using the modified Villain formulation, in which the spin structure required for odd $k$ is realised explicitly by lattice Majorana fermions. We demonstrate that the same Majorana fermions sit at the junctions of the symmetry lines, exactly where the fusion of two $U(1)$ elements wraps around the circle. From the lattice algebra of lines and junctions we derive the $R$- and $F$-symbols in the bulk and on the gapped boundary, and show that for odd $k$ the boundary $F$-symbol obeys the Gu-Wen relation for the $U(1)$ symmetry defect, without passing through a bosonic shadow.

items.title: Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD?
items.summary: Promoting spin to a hydrodynamic variable requires slow relaxation, as mass-suppressed helicity flips in hot QCD suggest. Using the full leading-order collision operator, we show instead that light-quark spin damps at the transport rate $g^4T\ln(1/g)$, nearly as fast as vector currents. Since spatial spin locks to momentum, helicity-conserving soft, small-angle scatterings readily rotate it. Damping involves multiple kinetic modes beyond a single relaxation time, global rotation adds only reversible precession, and stronger coupling further disfavors a slow spin mode in quark-gluon plasma.

items.title: Accelerating solitons in Rindler space
items.summary: Relativistic nonlinear field theories that are integrable in two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime remain integrable in Rindler space. We investigate the properties of classical sine-Gordon (SG) solitons in Rindler space. Accelerating observers in each of the two Rindler wedges can see only a portion of the full soliton in Minkowski spacetime; this portion itself forms a soliton carrying a partial topological charge. The soliton solution admits the following interpretation: a soliton incoming from the horizon decelerates to stop at some point, then falls back and accelerates to the speed of light toward the horizon. Energy can flow into and out of the Rindler horizon.
items.author: Huiquan Li, Jianyong Wang

items.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
items.summary: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $η$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude.

items.title: Affine Vertex Operator Algebras and Correlation Functions on Elliptic Curves
items.summary: Let $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra attached to a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra at arbitrary level, and let $M=\bigoplus_{N=0}^{\infty}M_N$ be a $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ -module. We give an explicit formula for every genus-one trace of affine currents as a finite sum over cycle partitions. We then show the convergence of all fixed zero-mode trace series, hence absolute locally uniform convergence of the current traces and their meromorphic continuation on the elliptic configuration space. The same conclusion is obtained for arbitrary affine-state insertions. Finally, we compute the cases of at most four currents and the nodal limit $q\to 0$, in which the type-1 and type-2 elliptic cycle coefficients degenerate to rational genus-zero cycle coefficients and the module trace reduces to the ground-state space.
items.author: Linfang Hou, Si Li, Yongchang Zhu

items.title: Poles Are Not Enough: Zeros of Dyson-Schwinger Gluon Propagators in Yang-Mills Thermodynamics
items.summary: A normalized two-point function with several poles does not, on its own, fix the source-free thermal partition function. For the Gaussian measure of the original gluon field, a positive-residue rational propagator contributes determinants from its poles and from zeros interlaced between them. The zero factors distinguish this completion from a gas of independent pole fields and restore two ultraviolet polarizations per adjoint eigenvalue at every finite truncation. We apply the construction to a background-covariant completion of the elliptic Dyson-Schwinger gluon kernel. The first-order SU(3) transition is already present with a single pole, and the saturated six-pole result shifts $T_c/M_g$ by only $1.48\%$, where $T_c$ is the coexistence temperature and $M_g$ is the lowest pole mass.
items.author: Marco Frasca, Anish Ghoshal, Stefan Groote

items.title: Thermodynamics within and across AdS Gauss--Bonnet holographic CFTs
items.summary: We study thermal competition within individual holographic conformal field theories (CFTs) and across theories with different anomaly coefficients in five-dimensional AdS Gauss--Bonnet gravity. We derive the work term conjugate to the dimensionless coupling from the boundary first law and use a common boundary clock to compare charged spherical saddles at fixed external source. Varying this source drives a first-order switch between the CFTs at the endpoints of the chosen coupling interval. In the unit-lapse cylinder clock with the zero-type-D vacuum energy, strict concavity at fixed radius reduces the global comparison to these two endpoints. The preferred coupling jumps across the coexistence line, whose slope is related to the entropy difference by a generalized Clapeyron relation.
items.author: Limin Zeng

items.title: Generalized Kosmann derivative and symmetry operators on Dirac structures
items.summary: We develop a spinorial symmetry framework for metric Dirac structures in $H$-twisted exact Courant algebroids. A generalized metric equips a Dirac structure with an intrinsic Riemannian Lie-algebroid geometry and identifies it isometrically with the positive subbundle of the generalized tangent bundle. For sections preserving the generalized metric, we prove an exact intertwining between the positive-spinor Kosmann--Dorfman action and the intrinsic Kosmann derivative. The comparison is independent of the auxiliary compatible generalized connection. Within the intrinsic geometry we derive Killing--Yano (KY) and conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) integrability identities, construct Killing-spinor-preserving operators from odd special KY and even special closed CKY forms, and obtain these forms from Hermitian bilinears of Killing spinors with imaginary Killing number.

items.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
items.summary: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array.

items.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
items.summary: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance.

items.title: Metasurfaces with Anisotropic Electric and Magnetic Conductivities: Parameter Retrieval for Arbitrary Incidence and Polarization
items.summary: Metasurfaces come in a great variety of unit cell geometries and material composition. A common approach for describing them relies on retrieving effective surface parameters (e.g., electric and magnetic conductivities) from plane-wave scattering data. Conventional retrieval methods are often limited to isotropic unit cells, a uniform host material, or lead to increased complexity by requiring reflection and transmission coefficients from both sides of the metasurface. Here, we derive analytical expressions for the equivalent surface conductivities of an electrically- and magnetically-polarizable anisotropic metasurface under oblique plane-wave incidence with arbitrary polarization. The proposed formulation does not require bidirectional scattering information, thus simplifying the process especially in experimental studies.
items.author: Dimitrios Chatzidimitriou, Alexandros Pitilakis, Odysseas Tsilipakos

items.title: Subwavelength registration of skull-compensating acoustic holograms via nonlinear parametric array feedback
items.summary: Realizing the potential of optimized acoustic holograms for applications like transcranial ultrasound requires sub-wavelength alignment accuracy (less than 1.5 mm at 1 MHz), which is difficult to achieve with current non-MRI optical neuro-navigation methods. To address the critical challenge of alignment, we leverage the parametric array (PA) signal as an alignment surrogate, a highly penetrative, low-frequency difference wave generated by the nonlinear mixing of two primary high-frequency beams. Simulations show that a misaligned skull-compensating lens increases the primary acoustic energy within the skull bone (volumetric energy trapping), which strengthens the nonlinear source of the PA signal. We also tested whether shear-mode conversion in bone contributes: 2D elastic simulations showed only a small (3-5%) increase in shear-type motion with misalignment, and the transmitted ex vivo bursts did not lengthen as a shear path would require.
items.author: Pradosh Pritam Dash, Costas D. Arvanitis

items.title: Learning a calibrated decision head from logged bandit feedback
items.summary: A decision head reads a state and a list of options and returns a probability per option in one forward pass. Once deployed, it usually observes only whether the option it chose was right: logged bandit feedback. We adapt such a head, LoRA on Qwen3-0.6B-Base and 1.7B-Base, from that feedback and report three results. First, the Brier or log score of the sampled action's own probability is not a usable REINFORCE reward: every wrong action earns at least gold's reward, with a mean baseline the lowest-probability wrong action gets the largest advantage, and at two options the signal is zero; in one run it cut accuracy on ordered-scale questions from .636 to .111.
items.author: Ye Yuan

items.title: TraceKV: Policy-Preserving Low-Rank KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) impose substantial KV cache demands from both large multimodal contexts and growing reasoning traces. Low-rank KV compression has emerged as a promising paradigm that stores low-dimensional latents of KV states and can be combined with quantization. However, existing low-rank methods often induce growing predictive policy drift from the dense model when compressing reasoning KV states, resulting in reasoning failures. We identify two key causes of this degradation: calibration-state mismatch between static contexts and on-policy reasoning states, and unequal error sensitivity across KV states. To address these challenges, we propose TraceKV, a training-free low-rank KV compression framework that unifies on-policy calibration, sensitivity-aware SVD, and global rank allocation under a single policy-preserving principle, substantially reducing policy-KL divergence during reasoning.
items.author: Ke Li, Zishan Shao, Yiran Chen

items.title: Observations Drift, Structures Remain: Structural Pretraining with Time Alignment for Electromagnetic Signals
items.summary: Electromagnetic signal modeling is increasingly moving toward self-supervised pretraining on heterogeneous I/Q observations. However, an observed waveform is jointly shaped by signal generation, propagation environments, and acquisition processes, which mix reusable structural regularities with observation-specific variations. Existing methods usually pursue unified pretraining with reconstruction objectives on mixed observations. This heterogeneity creates two key mismatches for reconstruction pretraining: (1) appearance mismatch, induced by propagation-dependent waveform variations; and (2) temporal mismatch, induced by acquisition-dependent sampling coordinates. These mismatches make observation-specific appearances and sampling coordinates easier to reconstruct than stable signal structures, inducing observational shortcuts. We identify this failure mode as observation-biased pretraining.
items.author: Wenjin Gui, Junyu Shen, Haibo Xu et al.

items.title: Generalized Inverse Kinematics via Conditional Flow
items.summary: Inverse kinematics (IK) is a foundational primitive in robotics, mapping the task-space objectives expressed by higher-level planners to robot configurations that realize them. Traditional IK methods generally treat each query as an isolated pose-to-configuration problem, but planners often need a distribution over valid realizations that accounts for future reachability and preferences such as collision avoidance and stability. We introduce GenGenIK, a generative modeling approach that supports mobile bases, multiple end-effectors and targets, scene awareness, and preferences over robot behavior within a common interface. Experiments show that GenGenIK outperforms existing methods in both solve rate and runtime across tasks such as bimanual lift and flip-up, while allowing flexible control over the sampled distribution and remaining effective under partial scene observations.
items.author: Kaitlyn Zhang, Tomás Lozano-Pérez, Leslie Pack Kaelbling

items.title: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement
items.summary: Conformal selection promises distribution-free, finite-sample control of the error rate of a decision, and has been proposed as a safety layer for machine-learning CRISPR guide design. We ask whether such a certificate is attainable from the validated off-target data that exist. The constraint is arithmetic: a conformal p-value cannot fall below one divided by the calibration cohort size plus one, so a Benjamini-Hochberg selection certifies a single candidate only when that cohort is at least the candidate pool size divided by the tolerated error rate. Public cohorts supply ten validated guides, whereas a pool of two thousand at a ten percent error rate needs twenty thousand; the accepted set is consequently empty in over ninety-six percent of splits.
items.author: Mohammad Malekpouri, Somayeh Lotfi

items.title: Testing Conversation Preservation Across LLM APIs: A Rule-Based Oracle for Detecting Silent Information Loss
items.summary: LLM applications increasingly rely on translators and compatibility layers to move conversations across APIs. Yet a translated request can be accepted by the target API while silently losing information about instruction roles, tool interactions, error states, or generation controls. We introduce isloss, a deterministic oracle for testing conversation-information preservation across LLM API translations. It maps source and translated requests and replies to a shared intermediate representation, ConvIR, and applies explicit rules to distinguish legitimate representation changes from information loss. Unlike schema validation or reference-based differential testing, isloss requires neither a reference translation nor additional model calls. It also distinguishes avoidable loss from degradation caused by target API limitations.
items.author: Xin Liu, Xu Han, Yuxin Wang et al.

items.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
items.summary: Retrieval-augment generation is a prevalent strategy to mitigate hallucinations of LLMs. The attributable RAG (RAGQ) generates quotes for its answers. The quotes indicate which input contexts support the RAG to derive the answers, enhancing the answer's verifiability and trustworthiness. However, existing RAGQs exhibit significant degradation when dealing with questions that require multi-hop reasoning and multi-modal understanding, suffering from over-citation, implicit entity identification failure, and poor generalization. In this paper, we propose a novel RAGQ framework, namely QDRAG. QDRAG breaks down the input question into atomic subquestions to identify the implicit entities. Then, the reranker prunes context distractors to eliminate the downstream over-citation.
items.author: Yue Liu, Zhongying Ru, Shimin Di et al.

items.title: Analysis choices decide whether untrained networks beat trained ones at V1: a multiverse analysis of model-brain RSA
items.summary: Untrained convolutional networks have been reported to rival trained networks as models of visual cortex, and we had reported an untrained-network advantage over backpropagation at V1 in THINGS fMRI, together with a dependence on evaluation resolution. Under a pre-specified ridge readout, the untrained network scored below the trained one at every pooling grid (median r difference -0.043 at g = 4, 0 of 5 seeds positive), and also in MSE skill and per-fold r. In exploratory analyses, across 36 combinations of unit normalisation, distance measure and voxel normalisation (28 distinct analyses), the sign of the V1 contrast depended on the analysis (intervals above 0 in 5 and below 0 in 9 distinct analyses), and in our networks the resolution dependence of the original convention appeared in only one cell.
items.author: Nils Leutenegger

items.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
items.summary: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statistically significant redistribution of attention mass between visual and textual tokens in hallucinated responses.
items.author: Sachin Acharya, Niyoj Oli, Shishir Adhikari et al.

items.title: One Hierarchy, Many Sports: Hierarchy-Aligned Multi-Task Learning for Next-Shot Prediction
items.summary: Next-shot prediction in racket sports requires learning from event data with different match structures, recorded attributes, and label vocabularies. Table tennis, badminton, and tennis nevertheless share a hierarchy in which shots form rallies and rallies form higher scoring units. We present MT-HTA, a hierarchy-aligned multi-task Transformer that uses this structure to jointly predict the attributes of the next shot. A temporal Transformer captures event progression, a feature-token path models interactions among semantic fields rather than along the time axis, and task-specific attention retrieves information from hierarchical summaries and player context. The architecture supports three- and four-level hierarchies and sport-dependent task sets.
items.author: Chao-Wei Cai, Min-Te Sun, Sheng Kuang Wu et al.

items.title: Reading the Table: Sim-to-Real Game State Detection for the Chef's Hat Card Game
items.summary: Tabletop games offer a compelling scenario to study the interaction between artificial and human agents, combining social interaction with game state tracking and physical manipulation. To assess the game state, a robot needs to precisely detect closely related game objects, such as different card designs, requiring dedicated training data that is costly to annotate in the real world. Instead, we develop a fully automated synthetic data collection pipeline, using re-projection of known 3D coordinates to generate labels automatically and domain randomization to bridge the reality gap. This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state.
items.author: Connor Gäde, Matthias Kerzel, Hauke Bünning et al.

items.title: An Approach to Hinton's Mother-Child Proposal: Neural Networks Learning and Preserving Care in a Finite World
items.summary: Hinton proposed that artificial intelligence should be given "maternal instincts" and relate to us as a mother to her child. We argue that care must first be learned, with the network itself as the child. We construct this upbringing in a finite world and study whether care survives the mother's departure, new situations and further learning. The mechanism combines a vocabulary of harm, a learned measure of future acceptability and an execution veto. A finite role certificate supports transfer within a declared world family. When the hidden representation changes, an update is accepted only if a care readout recovers the required judgements with a prescribed margin and bounded weights.
items.author: Csaba Balogh

items.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories
items.summary: Coding agents are increasingly integrated into GitHub Actions to review pull requests, triage issues and modify code. Identifying these integrations is challenging because agentic workflows often resemble ordinary CI files, with evidence appearing in action references, shell commands and workflow conventions. We present GHAgentCI, a dataset of 15K+ workflow histories from 6K+ of 196K+ mined GitHub repositories, comprising 159K+ revisions and 205K+ agent-evidence records linked to workflow triggers and declared execution constraints. Our open-source extractor, cai-miner, detects agent-related evidence using an extensible catalogue. Manual validation of 576 stratified records confirmed 96.1% of dedicated-action matches and 98.8% of GitHub Agentic Workflow matches, with lower rates for other evidence kinds.
items.author: Daniel Ogenrwot, Jorge Gonzalo Delgado Cervantes, Woojoong Kim et al.

items.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.summary: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. In decentralized environments, global visibility is unavailable. Agents need to proactively discover non-local resources (e.g. tools, skills), and collaborate with other agents to solve tasks. We study decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication, a natural reflection of human structures. Each agent observes only its local state and can interact only with neighboring agents. We introduce a benchmark with synthetic scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Our experiments reveal that recent LLM agents struggle to discover non-local relevant resources and collaborate in decentralized setting.
items.author: Jiali Cheng, Oleg Rokhlenko, Joo-Kyung Kim et al.

items.title: Incentive-Responsive Agents: A Principal-Agent Framework, Metric Suite, and Runtime Architecture for Long-Lived Personal AI Agents
items.summary: Personal AI agents now persist: they hold accounts, mailboxes, long-term memory, and open-ended task streams, yet the dominant way to improve them remains capability-side: prompt engineering, larger models, longer thinking, and retrieval. We argue that long-lived agents are missing an incentive layer. We formalize an incentive not as text in a prompt but as a runtime contract over the agent's operating point (model tier, test-time compute, memory budget, tool authority, task priority, verification, and compensation) that the agent's policy must causally consume. We develop a principal-agent model with hidden effort, a contractible operating point, and costly verification. We derive (i) a non-consumption invariance principle separating genuine incentives from prompt-level persuasion, (ii) a persistence-as-discount theorem making identity continuity a precondition for sustained effort, (iii) an incentive-capability exchange-rate frontier yielding a per-task routing rule, and (iv) a Goodhart bound for multi-channel verification, plus a three-channel decomposition of mechanism gains (allocation, verification, continuation).
items.author: Jipu Su

items.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings
items.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on Shapley-based interpretability, but is typically restricted to low-dimensional state spaces, binary-action settings, and a single class of linear surrogate. We propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability to high-dimensional, multi-action environments. ReShap extracts compact feature representations from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution to characterize how each feature contributes to the policy's decisions, and distills the deep RL policy into an interpretable surrogate trained on the full set of (state, policy-action) pairs along the policy's visited distribution.
items.author: Yiyu Qian, Pengfei Guo, Liyuan Zhao

items.title: Virus-like particles enable highly efficient gene editing across porcine and avian in vitro, ex vivo , and in ovo models
items.summary: by Theresa M. Pauli, Theresa von Heyl, Beate Rieblinger, Sabrina Teresa Schleibinger, Wei Liang, Antonia Schmauser, Mithuoshni Arullmoli, Paul Derrer, Anika Eckstein, Sirradu Jagana, Camila Gatti Corrêa, Krzysztof Flisikowski, Tatiana Flisikowska, Benjamin Schusser Pigs and chickens are not only the most important livestock species for global food production but also serve as key model organisms in various research disciplines. The pig is widely used in translational research due to its anatomical and physiological similarity to humans, providing valuable insights into immunology, metabolism, and disease mechanisms. In contrast, the chicken has become an essential model for studies related to poultry health, animal welfare, and developmental biology.
items.author: Theresa M. Pauli, Theresa von Heyl, Beate Rieblinger et al.

items.title: A new asymmetry, an old toolkit: An emerging developmental enigma in appendage evolution
items.summary: by Caroline Schwaner, Tetsuya Nakamura Dorsoventral polarity is a key feature of paired appendages, yet its evolutionary origin is enigmatic as median fins, which predate paired appendages, are symmetric. A new PLOS Biology study shows lmx1b is dorsal in paired fin mesenchyme but posterior in median fins, implying genetic rewiring of an ancient toolkit. Dorsoventral polarity is a key feature of paired appendages, yet its evolutionary origin is enigmatic as median fins, which predate paired appendages, are symmetric. A new study shows that lmx1b is dorsal in paired fin mesenchyme but posterior in median fins, implying genetic rewiring of an ancient toolkit.
items.author: Caroline Schwaner, Tetsuya Nakamura

items.title: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry sequentially drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation
items.summary: by Allison Cohen, Tim Bergner, Amandine Guérin, Maryse Lebrun, Michael Laue, Christian Klotz, Boris Striepen The apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium is a leading cause of diarrheal disease in young children. Within the intestinal epithelium, Cryptosporidium establishes a unique intracellular niche in the apical brush border of enterocytes. A structurally complex interface between host and parasite acts as a holdfast and enables protein and metabolite transport. How the parasite invades its host cell and builds the interface is poorly understood. Here, we reveal parasite invasion with high temporal and spatial resolution using rigorous molecular markers. We find that sequential discharge of specialized secretory organelles anchors the parasite within the host prior to internalization.
items.author: Allison Cohen, Tim Bergner, Amandine Guérin et al.

items.title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: Multimodal AI-evaluator for functional pharmacokinetics and toxicity of peptides
items.summary: by Elizaveta A. Bogdanova, Timofei F. Lukianov, Artem V. Chernukhin, Alexey K. Shaytan Peptide drugs exhibit exceptional selectivity for biological targets and high functional activity making them among the most promising therapeutic agents. However, unsatisfactory pharmacokinetic characteristics remain a critical barrier to their implementation. They often become the primary reason for the failure of promising candidates in preclinical and clinical trials. To address this issue, we present Pepti-DrugPhAI – a comprehensive algorithm for the precise prediction of the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of a wide range of peptide compounds. Unlike many existing solutions, the proposed algorithm is multimodal and can simultaneously process both SMILES representations of chemical structures and amino acid sequences.
items.author: Elizaveta A. Bogdanova, Timofei F. Lukianov, Artem V. Chernukhin et al.

items.title: Sphinx: An R package for adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling and functional analysis in spatial omics
items.summary: by Mengyi Yan, Xiaoxiu Tan, Zhenhao Liu, Siwen Zhang, Yiwen Du, Hong Li, Lanming Chen, Lu Xie Spatial omics enables analysis of tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, but most spatial tools are optimized for transcriptomics and poorly suited to proteomics data. We developed Sphinx, an R package providing a comprehensive workflow for spatial proteomics, including preprocessing, cell annotation, adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. Importantly, it introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework guided by spatial statistical metrics and incorporates computational optimizations for large-scale datasets, enabling robust neighborhood modeling. Notably, Sphinx offers improved computational efficiency and scalability. Across lung adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and mouse spleen datasets, Sphinx robustly identifies cell types and spatial functional units, including tertiary lymphoid structures.
items.author: Mengyi Yan, Xiaoxiu Tan, Zhenhao Liu et al.

items.title: Burst-to-burst information resetting in sequential rhythmic neural activity
items.summary: by Pablo Sanchez-Martin, Irene Elices, Alicia Garrido-Peña, Carlos Garcia-Saura, Rafael Levi, Francisco B. Rodriguez, Pablo Varona In multiple neural systems, networks of bursting neurons generate and coordinate robust sequential rhythms, such as those observed in central pattern generators (CPGs) that control motor activity. In this paper, we combine electrophysiological experiments and biophysical models of the pyloric CPG to investigate cycle-by-cycle coordination resetting in sequential rhythms. In particular, we focus our analysis on the variability constraints of sequence intervals defined by the burst onset and offset time references, which structure the timing of the rhythmic CPG sequence cycle-by-cycle. We identified the conditions under which sequential dynamical invariants emerge as robust relationships between specific intervals within the same cycle, and when such relations reset at each cycle or extend between intervals of consecutive cycles.
items.author: Pablo Sanchez-Martin, Irene Elices, Alicia Garrido-Peña et al.

items.title: An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design
items.summary: by Faisal Bin Ashraf, Karen Paco, Sanaz Zebardast, Zihao Zhang, Ryan Mooney, Christian J. Dávila Ojeda, Mariana Paco Mendivil, Rashid M. Alam, Eva Chen, Iraneus Ogu, Jordan A. Lay, Tristan Y. Yang, Fernando L. Barroso da Silva, Malkiat Johal, Ilya Tolstorukov, Matthew H. Sazinsky, Animesh Ray, Stefano Lonardi The capacity of an antibody to recognize and bind an antigen with high specificity and strength (i.e., its binding affinity ) is a key determinant in the design and optimization of neutralizing antibodies against pathogenic targets. Here we introduce Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model (PLM) that predicts the binding affinity of an antibody against a target peptide within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
items.author: Faisal Bin Ashraf, Karen Paco, Sanaz Zebardast et al.

items.title: PhysInfer: A physics-constrained neural network for adaptive inference of transcriptional bursting from single-cell RNA-seq
items.summary: by Xiaodong Zeng, Jingwen Zhang, Shan Li, Haohua Wang Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has established that gene expression is driven by stochastic transcriptional bursting. However, inferring burst dynamics from static scRNA-seq snapshots is fundamentally constrained by parameter unidentifiability and model topology mismatch. Here, we propose PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that integrates a physics-constrained neural network with adaptive model selection and parameter decoupling. A physics-informed loss function, combining stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring, reparameterizes the optimization from unidentifiable microscopic rates to an interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representation of burst size and burst frequency, thereby providing an interpretable parameterization for assessing practical recoverability in static data.
items.author: Xiaodong Zeng, Jingwen Zhang, Shan Li et al.

items.title: FDTest: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem as a test for memory effects in brain dynamics
items.summary: by Sebastian Manuel Geli, Juan Manuel Monti, Adrián Ponce-Alvarez, Gustavo Deco, Yonatan Sanz Perl A central challenge in neuroscience is to understand how the brain flexibly balances local and distributed information processing to support diverse cognitive and conscious states. We hypothesize that a key signature of this balance is the presence of memory effects, which arise when a brain region’s future activity depends not only on its current state, but also on past information fed back from the wider network. Here we introduce the FDTest, a method for assessing local memory effects in multidimensional systems by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation–dissipation theorem (FDT).
items.author: Sebastian Manuel Geli, Juan Manuel Monti, Adrián Ponce-Alvarez et al.

items.title: Tachykinin-like NLP-58 signaling through TKR-1 modulates thermotaxis behavior in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.summary: by Moon Sun Jang, Hironori J. Matsuyama, Ryoga Suzuki, King Chuen Law, Yukimasa Shibata, Xiaolin Zhang, Koutarou D. Kimura, Yukihiko Kubota, Masahiro Ito, Kiyoji Nishiwaki, Ikue Mori Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling plays a central role in mammalian thermoregulatory dysfunction associated with menopause, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Caenorhabditis elegans thermotaxis as a genetically tractable system for investigating conserved tachykinin signaling. We demonstrate that overexpression of nlp-58 , the C. elegans ortholog of mammalian NKB, induces abnormal thermotaxis behavior without impairing the temperature response of the thermosensory neurons. NLP-58 is expressed in multiple neurons, including the AIY interneurons, a central integrative node of the thermosensory circuit.
items.author: Moon Sun Jang, Hironori J. Matsuyama, Ryoga Suzuki et al.

items.title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters
items.summary: by Andrea Arroyave, Henintsoa Rabezanahary, Ahmed Sahli, Mariana Baz Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters.
items.author: Andrea Arroyave, Henintsoa Rabezanahary, Ahmed Sahli et al.

items.title: Nuclear egress complex promotes capsid nuclear egress during Kaposi’s Sarcoma-associated herpesvirus reactivation
items.summary: by Ariana C. Calkwood Calderon-Zavala, Olaide A. Adeyemi, Paula García-Valenciano Rodríguez, Alicia de Pablos Fernández, Nathalie R. Lavoie, Allison L. Didychuk, Ekaterina E. Heldwein During herpesvirus replication, newly assembled capsids exit the nucleus by nuclear egress, in which capsids bud at the inner nuclear membrane forming perinuclear enveloped virions that then fuse with the outer nuclear membrane, releasing capsids into the cytoplasm. This process is mediated by the nuclear egress complex (NEC), a conserved viral heterodimer of UL31 and UL34 homologs. Although prior studies demonstrated that overexpression of the NEC from Kaposi’s Sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) induces nuclear membrane vesiculation and proliferation in uninfected cells, its role during lytic replication remained undefined.
items.author: Ariana C. Calkwood Calderon-Zavala, Olaide A. Adeyemi, Paula García-Valenciano Rodríguez et al.

items.title: Swimming motility and type IV pili modulate phagocytosis by shaping physical interactions between Pseudomonas aeruginosa and macrophages
items.summary: by Tania Distler, Chia-Ni Tsai, Han-Yi Huang, Alice Pellegrino, Aaron Weimann, Zainebe Al-Mayyah, Lucas A. Meirelles, R. Andres Floto, Alexandre Persat During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how P. aeruginosa evades phagocytosis under conditions that resemble chronic infection. We use an attenuated mutant lacking a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which reduces macrophage killing, allowing us to isolate determinants of bacterial susceptibility to phagocytosis.
items.author: Tania Distler, Chia-Ni Tsai, Han-Yi Huang et al.

items.title: The pore-forming protein APOL7C ruptures Leishmania major -containing parasitophorous vacuoles in dendritic cells to promote IL-12 production and the induction of T helper type 1 immunity
items.summary: by Gerone Gonzales, Liam Wilkinson, Eymi Cedeño, Song Huang, Cassandra M. Wood, Sidra Ajmal, Armaan Mohan, Neil McKenna, Robin M. Yates, Timothy E. Shutt, Matheus B. Carneiro, Nathan C. Peters, Johnathan Canton Classical dendritic cells (cDCs) are required for the efficient priming of T helper type 1 (Th1) immunity against Leishmania major infections in mice. They do so by producing large quantities of IL-12 in response to L. major infection. IL-12 in turn supports the generation of protective CD4 + Th1 cells. However, the mechanism(s) by which L. major instigates robust IL-12 production by cDCs has not been addressed. Here we show that expression of a pore-forming protein called APOL7C is induced in cDCs by L.
items.author: Gerone Gonzales, Liam Wilkinson, Eymi Cedeño et al.

items.title: Association between TyG‑BMI and repeat percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) risk: exploratory stratification by glucose metabolism status
items.summary: by Weiqiang Fei, Feng Yang, Yongbang Zhu, YiNa Le, Shan Wang, Danxia Sun, XiaoXu Zhang Most patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are diagnosed with coronary heart disease (CHD). The triglyceride glucose‑body mass index (TyG‑BMI) has been reported to be associated with CHD. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with additional exploratory stratification analyses according to glucose‑metabolism status. Data for this study were derived from resident health‑record follow‑up records of Yipeng Community Health Service Center, covering January 2015 to January 2025. Logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) were used to evaluate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with exploratory stratification by glucose‑metabolism status.
items.author: Weiqiang Fei, Feng Yang, Yongbang Zhu et al.

items.title: Emotional synchrony in family networks is linked to adolescent well-being in daily life
items.summary: by Saida Heshmati, Jaymes Paolo Rombaoa, Courtney M. Allred, Alexander P. Christensen, Stacey N. Doan Family emotional processes play a central role in adolescent well-being, yet most research relies on dyadic or static approaches that do not capture the dynamic, system-level nature of family emotional life. In a sample of adolescents (ages 12–17), mothers, and fathers ( N = 120; 2,365 assessments), constituting 40 family triads, we used ecological momentary assessment and a dynamic network approach to estimate how emotions fluctuate over time and co-vary across family members within each system. Emotional synchrony—defined as the extent to which family members’ affective states change together—was modeled at both overall (between-family) and momentary (within-family) levels.
items.author: Saida Heshmati, Jaymes Paolo Rombaoa, Courtney M. Allred et al.

items.title: Intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
items.summary: by Teklehaimanot Gereziher Haile, Negasi Asres, Dawit Gebregziabher, Birhane Fissahaye, Yemane Leake, Girmay Teklay, Haftu Berhe Gebru Introduction Intimate partner violence is a major global public health concern and a serious human rights violation, involving physical, sexual, and psychological abuse within intimate relationships. Worldwide, about one in three women experiences intimate partner violence during their lifetime. Accordingly, this study aims to estimate the overall prevalence and identify the key predictors of intimate partner violence in Ethiopia. Methods A comprehensive systematic search was carried out in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online to identify relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the prevalence and predictors of intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia.
items.author: Teklehaimanot Gereziher Haile, Negasi Asres, Dawit Gebregziabher et al.

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro as an efficient endopeptidase for fusion tag removal in recombinant protein production
items.summary: by Trung-Duc Nguyen, Gia-Bao Do, Phan-Anh Le, Mai-Anh T. Nghiem, Linh T. Ho, Thuy T. Le, Hong-Nhung T. Le, Tuan-Nghia Phan, Hong-Loan T. Nguyen Fusion tags are widely employed to enhance recombinant protein expression, solubility, and purification. However, efficient tag removal is often necessary to obtain proteins in their native form. In this study, SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease (3CLpro) was evaluated as a sequence-specific protease for fusion-tag removal using a recombinant fusion protein substrate under standard protein purification conditions. A substrate containing the canonical recognition sequence AVLQ↓SG was efficiently cleaved by 3CLpro, whereas no detectable cleavage was observed for a variant substrate harboring the sequence TVRLQ↓SG.
items.author: Trung-Duc Nguyen, Gia-Bao Do, Phan-Anh Le et al.

items.title: Sun protection awareness and ultraviolet protection factor product use among pilgrims and nurses during Hajj: A qualitative post-Hajj interview study
items.summary: by Omar Qaladi, Fahda Alrasheedi, Manahil Alhawsawi, Raghad Alluhebi, Abeer Abujalid Background Pilgrims performing Hajj are exposed to extreme heat and ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which pose distinct risks: heat contributes to dehydration and heat-related illness, whereas UV radiation causes sunburn and eye damage and increases long-term skin cancer risk. While heat illness and infectious diseases have been widely studied, awareness and use of UV-protective measures, including sunscreen and ultraviolet protection factor (UPF)-rated clothing and umbrellas, remain underexplored in this context. Understanding both pilgrim and nursing perspectives is essential for developing effective interventions. Methods In this qualitative descriptive study, retrospective semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom between 20 June and 11 July 2025, within approximately one month after the 2025 Hajj season, with 16 Saudi pilgrims and 13 registered nurses who had worked in hospitals in Makkah and Madinah during Hajj.
items.author: Omar Qaladi, Fahda Alrasheedi, Manahil Alhawsawi et al.

items.title: Elevated UHRF1 predicts unfavorable clinical outcomes in adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma: Clinicopathological analysis and preliminary in vitro observations
items.summary: by Ying Lin, Rong-Dong Zhang, Xin-Yu Xu, Huang-zhou Jiang, Ren-Li Chen, Jian-Zhen Shen Background UHRF1 has been established as a susceptibility gene in multiple cancer types; however, its functional role in the pathogenesis of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) remains poorly defined. This study aimed to investigate UHRF1 expression in ATLL and assess its clinical and biological significance. Methods Immunohistochemistry was performed to evaluate UHRF1 protein expression in tumor tissues from 72 ATLL patients and 30 reactive lymphadenopathy controls. Univariate Cox’s proportional hazard regression model was used to screen the factors affecting OS and PFS, and multivariate Cox’s proportional hazard regression model was used to screen independent prognostic factors in ATLL.
items.author: Ying Lin, Rong-Dong Zhang, Xin-Yu Xu et al.

items.title: Feature extraction of static foam images based on U-Net and Hough transform
items.summary: by Deqiang Peng, Daoguang Li, Qingxia Li, Chenyi Wang, Xiaomin Ma In flotation-based mineral processing, froth images contain important visual information that reflects the operating condition of the process and provides a basis for process monitoring and control. However, conventional machine-vision methods still encounter difficulties in extracting static froth features under conditions of bubble adhesion, overlap, weak boundaries, and uneven illumination. To address these problems, a flotation froth image analysis framework is proposed by combining a boundary-aware U-Net segmentation model with a segmentation-guided adaptive Hough transform. In the first stage, the U-Net architecture is enhanced with explicit boundary-oriented supervision to improve the separation of adherent and overlapping bubbles.
items.author: Deqiang Peng, Daoguang Li, Qingxia Li et al.

items.title: Instance causal multiple instance learning for whole slide image classification
items.summary: by Haixing Li, Chao Weng, Wanying Huang, Ming Xu Whole slide images (WSIs) are characterized by extremely high resolution and usually lack fine-grained annotations, making multiple instance learning (MIL) the dominant paradigm for weakly supervised WSI classification. Although existing MIL methods have achieved substantial progress in feature extraction and instance aggregation, most of them overlook the influence of confounding factors, thereby learning spurious associations that impair generalization performance. To address this issue, we develop an Instance Causal Multiple Instance Learning (ICMIL) framework for WSI classification, which aims to reduce the model’s reliance on potentially spurious instance-level associations. Specifically, unlike conventional likelihood-based strategies, the proposed method introduces a backdoor-adjustment-inspired prototype module during instance aggregation, where clustered prototypes are used as proxy contextual patterns to mitigate the influence of potential confounding cues.
items.author: Haixing Li, Chao Weng, Wanying Huang et al.

items.title: Predictive factors for risk of chronic evolution in Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada disease at 1 month after pulse steroid therapy
items.summary: by Tetsuya Muto, Shoichiro Kusuda, Masaaki Sakamoto, Shigeki Machida, Shinichiro Imaizumi, Tetsuju Sekiryu In this study, we aimed to identify factors for risk of chronic evolution in Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada (VKH) disease at 1 month following pulse steroid therapy. This was a retrospective clinical cohort, single center study. A total of 121 eyes from 61 treatment-naïve patients with acute VKH disease, who underwent pulse steroid therapy and had follow-up for over 12 months were evaluated. Patients were categorized into SGF and non-SGF groups according to fundus outcomes at 12 months after treatment. Anterior chamber morphology was assessed using Pentacam ® , while axial length and lens thickness were measured with the IOLMaster 700.

items.title: The spatiotemporal evolution mechanism of enterprise-led organic agriculture: Evidence from Shandong Province
items.summary: by Yueling Yang, Qiang Wang, Shu Wang, Zihong Yang, Thomas Dogot This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of enterprise-led organic agriculture in Shandong Province, China. Using panel data on certified organic enterprise production bases across 16 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023, we combine spatial statistical analysis, Local Moran’s I, two-way fixed-effects regression, and robustness checks. The results show that certified organic bases expanded substantially but became increasingly concentrated, forming a clear core–periphery structure centered on the Jiaodong Peninsula. Transportation infrastructure, e-commerce connectivity, and GI-protected agricultural products are positively associated with base expansion, while fiscal expenditure shows a negative association, possibly reflecting compensatory policy allocation to less-developed areas.
items.author: Yueling Yang, Qiang Wang, Shu Wang et al.

items.title: External validation of a machine learning model for classifying hospitalization outcomes in Asian elephants across three elephant hospitals in Thailand
items.summary: by Worapong Kosaruk, Pichamon Ueangpaibool, Nawapa Hirannithithamrong, Janjeera Kaew-ek, Taweepoke Angkawanish Classification of hospitalization outcomes in wildlife hospitals may support clinical assessment and resource planning, but model performance can vary across institutions with different case profiles and care practices. This study evaluated a previously developed random forest model for classifying hospitalization outcomes in Asian elephants using temporally distinct 2025 data from three elephant hospitals in Thailand. The validation comprised temporal validation at the original development center and institutional validation at two additional hospitals. Because length of stay was included as a predictor, the model was evaluated as a hospitalization-course classification model rather than as an admission-time prognostic tool.
items.author: Worapong Kosaruk, Pichamon Ueangpaibool, Nawapa Hirannithithamrong et al.

items.title: Spatiotemporal patterns and county-level coordination between sports-related intangible cultural heritage and tourism development in the Wuling Mountain Area, China
items.summary: by Jiaxin Zhang, Siqing Zhang, Junrong Lei Sports-related intangible cultural heritage (SRICH) can support culturally grounded tourism, but its county-level alignment with tourism development remains unclear in ethnically diverse mountain regions. This study examined 71 county-level units in China’s Wuling Mountain Area in 2010, 2015, 2019, and 2024. Geographical concentration, kernel density estimation, and standard deviational ellipses traced the administrative distribution of officially recognized SRICH records. Entropy weighting, coupling coordination, relative-balance diagnosis, and Moran’s I assessed their county-level relationship with tourism development. SRICH coverage expanded and geographical concentration declined, while county-represented density peaks increased within a broadly stable regional configuration.
items.author: Jiaxin Zhang, Siqing Zhang, Junrong Lei
