items.title: Comparative connectomics reveals stage-specific gap junction rewiring that reshapes avoidance behavior
items.summary: Environmental stress can remodel neural circuits, yet how such rewiring generates behavioral adaptation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how dauer-specific circuit remodeling alters nociceptive behavior. We discovered that dauers exhibit significantly shorter avoidance durations than adults. Through comparative connectomics, we observed a substantial expansion of gap junctions within the dauer nociceptive circuit and found that dauer neurons exhibit more transient activity dynamics as a result of this rewiring. Modeling neuronal activity demonstrated that removing dauer-specific connectivity constraints failed to reproduce transient characteristics, validating the functional role of dauer-specific gap junctions. Furthermore, introducing synthetic dauer-specific gap junctions into adults was sufficient to recapitulate dauer-like activity patterns and shorten avoidance duration.
items.author: Choe, D. T., Hall, D. H., Nguyen, K. C. Q. et al.

items.title: Repurposing clofarabine against enteric pathogens via metabolic starvation
items.summary: Enteropathogenic and enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EPEC/EHEC) cause severe global diarrhoeal disease, exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance. Pathogenesis relies on attaching and effacing lesions, where bacteria generate actin pedestals to adhere, replicate, and destroy intestinal microvilli. To identify novel anti-virulence candidates targeting this process, we conducted a high-throughput phenotypic screen quantifying pedestal formation via high-content fluorescence microscopy. We identified the anticancer nucleotide analogue clofarabine as a potent inhibitor of EPEC growth and pathogenesis. Distinct from its oncology mechanism - inducing DNA chain termination and apoptosis - clofarabine competes with bacterial ATP-dependent processes to impede gene transcription, protein synthesis, and Type III Secretion System (T3SS) function.
items.author: Deans, N. D., Naylor, K. L., Srour, S. et al.

items.title: The nucleus spatially partitions mechanoprotection and mechanosensing
items.summary: Mechanical forces shape cell behavior, but how the nucleus integrates its roles as genome protector and mechanosensor remains unresolved. Here, we dissect the spatiotemporal control of transcriptional response to forces during epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). By combining genome-wide approaches, in vivo nuclear micromanipulation, and quantitative live imaging, we uncover two key properties of nuclear mechanosensing. First, mechanically induced changes in chromatin accessibility and transcription are spatially patterned within the nucleus: genes closest to deformations appear protected, revealing a local shielding mechanism associated with chromatin closure. Second, relocating a gene between chromatin environments is sufficient to alter its mechanosensitivity, challenging the concept of inherently force-sensitive genes.
items.author: Bouzignac, R., Palandri, A., Fritsch, L. et al.

items.title: Integrating Long-Read Structural Variant Analysis with single-nucleus RNA-seq to Elucidate Gene Expression Effects in Disease
items.summary: Structural variants (SVs) are a major source of genetic diversity, yet how they impact cell types in complex brain diseases remains largely unexplored, partially due to limitations of short-read sequencing. Here, we addressed this fundamental question in Parkinson's disease (PD). generating long-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data for 100 post-mortem brain samples from a PD cohort, constructing a high-confidence catalog of 74,552 SVs. To resolve their functional impact, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from two brain regions from the same samples and focused functional analyses on SVs proximal to genes previously nominated as cis-regulated, potential causal targets of PD-associated GWAS loci.
items.author: Kim, K., Lin, Z., Simmons, S. K. et al.

items.title: Multimodal imaging links molecular identity with nanoscale-resolved 3D cell morphology in opossum cortical cultures
items.summary: In the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), the ability to regenerate after injury drops sharply in the first weeks after birth, but how this change is reflected in cell morphology and organization is still not fully understood. Here we cultivated cortical cell cultures from the gray short-tailed opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and compared cells derived from early postnatal pups (postnatal day 3-6, "Pyoung") with those from older pups (postnatal day 16-18, "Pold"), which differ in their capacity to regenerate after injury. For each culture, we assessed marker-defined cellular composition using fluorescently labeled markers for neurons, glia, and immature/progenitor cells, and characterized their nanoscale-resolved three-dimensional morphology using label-free scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM).
items.author: Ayar, Z., Pongrac, M., Mladinic, M. et al.

items.title: Functional Performance of Electrospun Tissue-Engineered Heart Valve Scaffolds Across Geometries Under Aortic Conditions
items.summary: Electrospun, bioresorbable polymer scaffolds are a promising platform for tissue-engineered heart valves (TEHVs) owing to their fibrous microstructure, tunable mechanics and capacity to support host-cell infiltration and remodeling. Recent in-vitro parametric studies of bioprosthetic heart valve (BHV) geometry have used silicone cast valves to link design parameters to hemodynamic performance and leaflet strain, but the functional behavior of electrospun whole-valve TEHV scaffolds across distinct leaflet geometries and clinically relevant aortic conditions remains poorly characterized. Here, we present an end-to-end workflow in which polycaprolactone (PCL) is electrospun directly onto parametrized, 3D-printed mandrels derived from two established analytical leaflet geometry models, yielding 21 whole-valve scaffolds across four geometries without cutting and assembling flat fiber sheets or suturing of flat fiber sheets.
items.author: Dillinger, H., Saberi, A., Manenti, M. et al.

items.title: A reformulation of the t-test in single-cell transcriptomics dramatically reduces false positives
items.summary: The default differential expression tests in single-cell analysis software provide fast and simple approaches that help practitioners annotate cell populations identified through clustering algorithms. Here, we use theoretical arguments and empirical studies to show that these tests suffer from inflated false positive rates that affect the resulting annotations. We introduce LN's t-test, which tests a novel, asymptotically unbiased log-fold change estimator and avoids these false positives, without compromising speed.
items.author: Kviman, O., Ferreira, P. F., Jun, S.-H. et al.

items.title: Modulating inter-mitochondrial contacts to increase membrane potential for mitigating blue light damage
items.summary: Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) is essential for mitochondrial functions, yet current methods for modulating MMP lack precise spatial and temporal control. Here, we developed an optogenetic mitochondrial tethering system, termed OptoMitoTether, that enables reversible control of inter-mitochondrial proximity with high spatiotemporal precision. Blue light activation induced CRY2PHR oligomerization between adjacent mitochondrial outer membranes, reduced mitochondrial nearest-neighbor distances, and promoted inter-mitochondrial tethering. OptoMitoTether activation was associated with elevated MMP and was associated with lower reactive oxygen species (ROS) and preserved ATP production during prolonged blue light stress. Moreover, OptoMitoTether expression preserved mitochondrial bioenergetic function in human retinal cells and extended lifespan in C.
items.author: Wang, Y., Qiu, K., Zou, W. et al.

items.title: Systematic comparison of gliflozins identifies a selective anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition
items.summary: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide important cardiorenal benefits in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their effects on vascular calcification remain conflicting. Whether potential anti-calcifying effects are shared across gliflozins or involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition is unknown. Methods: We systematically compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a high-phosphate diet-induced mouse model of vascular calcification and complementary ex vivo and in vitro models, including rodent and human vascular tissues and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Aortic transcriptional response was investigated by RNA sequencing. VSMC calcification, proliferation, migration, viability, glucose uptake and bioenergetics were investigated using complementary cellular assays, including OsteoSense staining, Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, radiolabeled 2-deoxyglucose uptake and Seahorse ATP rate analysis.
items.author: Fernandez, L., Brunet, M., Ballongue, E. et al.

items.title: A Double Challenge: Cerebral Blood Flow During Concurrent Breath-Hold and Motor Task
items.summary: Motor activation and breath-holding probe complementary aspects of cerebrovascular function: the response to local neuronal demand and to a global vascular challenge. Combining them tests whether local perfusion responses remain supported when the cerebral circulation must also accommodate a systemic perturbation, potentially revealing constraints that either challenge alone would miss. We used arterial spin labelling (ASL) MRI to investigate whether concurrent breath-holding modifies the regional cerebral blood flow (CBF) response to motor activation. Fourteen healthy volunteers underwent pseudo-continuous ASL at 3T during sequential finger tapping with normal breathing, finger tapping during breath-holding, and breath-holding alone. Each condition included a resting baseline followed by eight 25-second task blocks interleaved with recovery.
items.author: Jakobsen, K., Daiu, M., Critchley, H. et al.

items.title: Higher stomatal density and smaller stomatal size associate with higher grain yield in winter wheat
items.summary: In wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), flag leaf is crucial in determining grain-filling rate and final grain yield. Stomata, microscopic pores on plant surfaces, balance CO2 uptake and evaporative water loss; their numbers and aperture sizes depend on environmental factors. Previous studies have reported associations between stomatal traits and grain yield; mostly under controlled conditions. Our study aimed to investigate flag leaf stomatal anatomical and physiological traits, and their relationships with winter wheat grain yield under field conditions. We measured stomatal density and size, and stomatal conductance on adaxial and abaxial flag leaf surfaces in a three-year field study with twenty-five winter wheat varieties.
items.author: Ivandi, E., Jalakas, P., Tulva, I. et al.

items.title: Time-Resolved Proteomics of a Polyglutamine-Expanded Huntingtin in vitro Cell Model Reveals Early RNA-Regulatory Compensation and Late Respiratory-Chain Remodeling
items.summary: Huntington disease (HD) is caused by a polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin protein that exerts progressive cellular toxicity. However, the temporal order of pathogenic events, and in particular which changes arise early and which emerge late, remains incompletely defined, despite their distinct therapeutic implications. To examine this trajectory, we profiled the proteome of a huntingtin-expressing cell model at early (72 h) and late (144 h) stages. Rather than a linear progression, the proteome changed in two distinct stages. At the early stage, cells showed increased abundance of RNA-processing, splicing, and protein-synthesis proteins, which may reflect an adaptive response to preserve gene-expression fidelity under stress.
items.author: Sonmez, E., Mutlu, P., Ozlevent, C. et al.

items.title: Temporal Dynamics of Multi-Item Working Memory Maintenance in Human Gaze Patterns and EEG
items.summary: Maintaining multiple items in working memory (WM) requires the allocation of limited resources, which may involve prioritizing individual items over others. Previous work has suggested that attentional prioritization can vary rhythmically between WM samples, but direct empirical evidence for such temporal fluctuations remains scarce. Here, we recorded eye-tracking and EEG to track the temporal dynamics of multi-item processing while participants maintained up to three object orientations in WM. Whereas EEG encoding was only short-lived, miniature gaze patterns reflected the orientations of all three items throughout the entire WM delay and showed systematic load and serial position effects. Contrary to rhythmic sampling accounts, however, we found no evidence that eye movements alternated between the concurrently maintained items.
items.author: Broehl, F., Bielefeldt, A. A., Linde-Domingo, J. et al.

items.title: OpenDrive: An Open-Source Microdrive for Large-Scale Neurophysiology
items.summary: Neuropixels-NHP probes have ushered in a new era of high-density neurophysiology recording in large animal models. Here, we present OpenDrive, an open-source microdrive system designed specifically for acute insertion of Neuropixels-NHPs. OpenDrive combines a custom motorized microdrive, six-drive control console, and software platform. Compared with commercially available options, OpenDrive offers (1) low cost, (2) precise, accurate, and stable probe movement, (3) scalability to many-probe recording, and (4) open-source hardware designs and software. In our experiments, OpenDrive has already supported recordings from thousands of neurons across a variety of cortical and subcortical structures. By lowering technical barriers and enabling community-driven development with OpenDrive, we aim to accelerate Neuropixels recording in large animal models.
items.author: Stine, G. M., Gabel, J., Watters, N. et al.

items.title: A nanoscale atlas of extracellular vesicles and particles in Drosophila olfactory sensilla
items.summary: Extracellular particles, including non-vesicular extracellular particles (NVEPs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), are emerging as key contributors to sensory signaling, yet their ultrastructural organization within native tissues remains underexplored. Native tissues preserve extracellular particle organization and heterogeneity that are often lost during dissociation. Using cryofixation-based serial block-face scanning electron microscopy, we generated a nanoscale atlas of NVEPs and EVs across 352 Drosophila antennal olfactory sensilla ([~]70% coverage). Segmentation of more than 7,800 extracellular particles revealed distinct populations differing in morphology, size, electron density, and sensillum-class distribution. Analyses of EV biogenesis identified multivesicular bodies and membrane budding in auxiliary cells. Furthermore, sensilla housing degenerating neurons exhibited marked accumulation of EVs and NVEPs, accompanied by increased auxiliary-cell EV biogenesis.
items.author: Vijayakumar, P., Cauwenberghs, K., Garg, M. et al.

items.title: The MarR-family regulator TilR links biosynthesis of enterotoxin tilimycin with physiologic adaptation in Klebsiella oxytoca
items.summary: Members of the Klebsiella oxytoca species complex (KoSC) are ubiquitous gut colonizers that produce the DNA-damaging enterotoxin tilimycin (TM) as part of their virulence-related program. A MarR-like transcriptional regulator, herein designated TilR, controls expression of the divergently transcribed aroX- and NRPS-operons responsible for TM production. Deletion of tilR resulted in pronounced induction of both operons, elevated toxin production, and increased cytotoxicity - establishing TilR as the key repressor of TM biosynthesis. TilR is encoded downstream of the NRPS operon and binds a 20 bp motif within the aroX-NRPS intergenic region, spatially separated from the predicted promoters driving toxin gene expression.
items.author: Unterhauser, K., Grassmann, A. A., Balachandran, P. et al.

items.title: Detection of bifidobacterial lipoproteins with anti-viral potential in donor human milk
items.summary: Background: Group B coxsackieviruses (CVBs) are involved in triggering type 1 diabetes. Free bifidobacterial lipoproteins (BLps) prevent CVBs cell infection. Our objective is to isolate free BLps potentially released by bifidobacteria in breastmilk and document their bioavailability. Methods: Bifidobacterium breve and B. longum were quantified by qPCR in samples donated to the hospitals biobank (DHM) within two weeks following delivery. BLps were captured onto CV B4, analyzed by SDS-PAGE and competitive ELISA. BLps transport through Caco-2 monolayers was monitored after DHM contact. Titration of anti-CV B IgA was carried out by ELISA. Results: Among the 90 enrolled donors, seven were excluded, 68 donated a unique sample and 15 donated multiple specimens (2 to 12).
items.author: AYARI, S., Sane, F., Piva, F. et al.

items.title: Chemotaxis and motility of Achromatium oxaliferum in response to oxygen, sulfide, and nitrate
items.summary: Bacteria of the genus Achromatium are known for their large cell sizes and intracellular calcium carbonate deposits. Achromatium cells inhabit freshwater, brackish, and marine sediments where they accumulate to high abundances at the oxic-anoxic interface. These bacteria alter their vertical position in the sediment along with daily fluctuations in oxygen concentrations. Yet, the mechanism behind their migration in the sediment remains unknown. In this study, we used chemotaxis assays and time-lapse microphotography to analyze the motility and chemotactic behavior of Achromatium oxaliferum. Microscopic observations revealed that rolling and gliding were the main forms of locomotion exhibited by Achromatium. In absence of any stimulant, the movement appeared to be mostly random and changes in direction frequently occurred.
items.author: Schorn, S., Ionescu, D., grossart, H.-P. et al.

items.title: WHaloForce enables chemigenetic imaging of molecular tension in living cells and animals
items.summary: Piconewton forces borne by individual proteins within complex assemblies underlie cell adhesion, migration, and tissue morphogenesis, yet remain difficult to image in living systems. Here, we introduce WHaloForce, a chemigenetic HaloTag-based tension sensor that converts force-dependent relief of tryptophan-mediated dye quenching into a fluorescence lifetime change. Optical tweezers revealed a switch-like unquenching transition near 5 pN, and cellular measurements demonstrated dynamic responses to actomyosin activity. WHaloForce enabled quantitative tension imaging of diverse force-bearing proteins (vinculin, E-cadherin, -catenin, and laminin) in mammalian cells, mouse tissue, and C. elegans. Bright synthetic dyes made tension measurements possible at endogenous expression levels. In C.
items.author: Wu, D., Morales, E. A., Lee, J. et al.

items.title: Endogenous Mechanical Reporters Encode the Global Mechanical Landscape of Morphogenesis
items.summary: Developmental systems usually comprise multiple genetically programmed morphogenetic events within a mechanically continuous environment, yet how individual processes interact and contribute to the overall mechanical landscape remains unknown. Here, we introduce the concept of mechanical reporter: endogenous tissues function as in situ probes of the embedded mechanical landscape. We exemplified cephalic furrow (CF) migration as a mechanical reporter in gastrulating Drosophila. Using optogenetics and genetics, we revealed that CF displacement reflects the combined effect of both force and tissue mechanical properties. By incorporating condition-specific mechanical landscape into a continuum minimal-response model, we developed a framework to quantitatively predict the reporter dynamics.
items.author: Xu, R., Gao, H., Li, F. et al.

items.title: Shared landscape, divergent genomes: Comparative population genomics of co-occurring flora in an isolated Australian mountain range
items.summary: Understanding how landscape heterogeneity shapes genomic variation is key to conserving biodiversity and evolutionary potential. Yet conservation genomics is typically conducted at the single species level, limiting our ability to identify shared genomic patterns or understand how co-occurring taxa differ in their response to common environmental gradients. We assessed spatial patterns of genomic variation and their associations with geographic and environmental features among populations of nine co-existing plant species with contrasting life-histories and ecological traits across Gariwerd, a threatened biodiversity hotspot in south-eastern Australia. All species exhibited weak overall genetic structure, although the magnitude and spatial distribution of differentiation varied among species.
items.author: Lobos, S. E., Ahrens, C. W., Rymer, P. D. et al.

items.title: Branch-Partitioned Selection Tests Reject Random Labels on Real Genes, Even Against a Null Simulated at the Depth of the Data
items.summary: Comparative genomics often turns a trait into a hypothesis about selection by labelling the branches that carry it and testing them against the rest. We asked how such a test behaves when the labels carry no trait. In three panels of about 50 species, fungi, yeasts and lactobacilli, two of them registered in advance, randomly placed terminal labels on presumed-null single-copy genes were rejected by PAML's two-ratio branch model in 65.9, 68.8 and 88.8% of genes, against a nominal 5%. Referring each real gene to replicates simulated under its own fitted null model did not remove the excess: with a generator matched to the depth of the real alignments, 65.0% (95% CI 53.5-75.3) and 83.8% (73.8-91.1) of 80 genes were still rejected.
items.author: Kim, M., Jae-Ho, S.

items.title: Replicative and chronological epigenetic age track genome instability in opposite directions across cancers
items.summary: Epigenetic clocks are widely applied to tumor tissue, yet clocks trained to predict chronological age and clocks built to count cell divisions measure different quantities, and how either relates to the heterogeneity of methylation change within a tumor remains unclear. Here we compare four mitotic clocks with Horvath pan tissue clock in 506 matched tumor and normal pairs from 13 adult solid cancers and in 1,731 pediatric tumors. We show that mitotic age is higher in the tumor than in matched normal tissue in every adult cancer type, and that this advance is robust to tumor purity and cell type composition.
items.author: Mukherji, A., Chattopadhyay, S.

items.title: Programmable amide bond formation using de novo ligases
items.summary: Amide bond formation is of central importance in the chemical industry, underpinning the synthesis of small bioactive molecules, macrocycles, peptides and their conjugates. Conventional methods of amide synthesis rely on stoichiometric coupling agents and costly protecting group manipulations. While biocatalysis can alleviate some of these challenges, enzymes typically operate across a narrow range of substrates and their adaptation to new coupling partners requires extensive engineering. Here we show that de novo amide ligases featuring a cysteine catalytic triad can be programmed computationally to operate across diverse substrate classes with high selectivity. We first designed complementary peptide ligases to selectively functionalise either the N-terminus or a single lysine residue of a polypeptide sequence containing 36 competing lysines.
items.author: Salike, S., Fluegel, T., Gantz, M. et al.

items.title: SIFT: Syncmer-Informed Selection of Haplotypes for T2T Imputation
items.summary: Genome patching improves the completeness of fragmented assemblies by filling unresolved gaps with sequences from reference genomes. Pangenome panels provide diverse candidate haplotypes for this task, but identifying suitable references efficiently becomes increasingly challenging as these panels grow. We present SIFT, a compressed indexing method for selecting reference haplotypes for genome patching with ImpuT2T. SIFT combines closed-syncmer parsing, phrase-level indexing, and pseudo-maximal exact match (pseudo-MEM) queries. Closed syncmers provide a context-independent parsing rule with bounded distances between consecutive selected positions, enabling consistent parsing of reference and query sequences. We demonstrate that two closed syncmers determine the distance at which they can occur consecutively in any string, so that equal substrings of two parses represent identical sequences and no gap sequence need be stored.
items.author: Ferro, E. A., Varki, R., Lin, M.-J. et al.

items.title: Assessing the Capacity of Genomic Language Models to Generate Informative Embeddings of Viral Genome Fragments
items.summary: Genomic language models (gLMs) trained on large volumes of nucleotide sequences are becoming an alternative to classical methods in metagenomic analysis, particularly for studying genomic "dark matter". In this work, we investigate the ability of four gLMs (DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, ViraLM, and Evo2-7B) to generate taxonomically informative vector representations of short viral genome fragments. We constructed a balanced reference dataset of viruses based on the ICTV Virus Metadata Resource and compared the representations generated by gLMs with conventional k-mer profiles and MinHash sketches using clustering and neighborhood-based metrics (adjusted Rand index (ARI), precision@k, and CROSS precision@k). On the reference dataset, three of the four gLMs outperformed the 4-mer profile in terms of ARI and precision@5 under the same evaluation protocol.
items.author: Kladchenko, A., Manolov, A., Popov, N. S.

items.title: zsasa: a Zig-based engine for high-throughput solvent accessible surface area at proteome scale
items.summary: Advances in structural and computational biology now yield structures by the hundreds of thousands, from predicted-structure databases to molecular-dynamics trajectories. Solvent accessible surface area (SASA), a long-established descriptor of protein stability, binding, and interfaces, remains central to their analysis. Established SASA tools are still widely used, but each covers only part of what such data now demand in input formats, outputs, and speed. We present zsasa, a fast, full-featured, open-source SASA engine for single structures, proteome-scale collections, and trajectories, usable from the command line or Python. It uses the same algorithms as established tools and owes its speed to the implementation, which makes full use of multicore processors and SIMD instructions while keeping memory use low.
items.author: Nagae, T., Tomii, K.

items.title: Enhanced antitumour activity of combined PD-1 blockade and HER2-targeted therapy is associated with reduced epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix-remodelling signatures in gastric cancer
items.summary: Background The combination of PD-1 blockade, HER2-targeted therapy and chemotherapy improves outcomes in HER2-positive advanced gastric and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. However, chemotherapy can independently alter the tumour microenvironment, making the biological effects of PD-1 and HER2 targeting difficult to distinguish. We therefore investigated how PD-1 and HER2 blockade, alone and in combination, affect tumour growth and associated transcriptional programmes. Methods Immunodeficient NOG mice received human PBMCs by tail-vein injection. Three days later, NCI-N87 gastric cancer cells were implanted subcutaneously. Mice were randomised to vehicle, pembrolizumab, trastuzumab, or combination treatment. Tumour growth was assessed, and bulk RNA sequencing was used to identify treatment-associated changes in gene expression, pathway enrichment, and tumour, stromal, and immune cell-associated signatures.
items.author: Wan, P. K.-T., Peng, S., Zhang, X. et al.

items.title: Curvature-based schedule ordering is preserved in homogeneous and heterogeneous tumors
items.summary: During treatment, dosing protocols with identical total dose may favor one schedule over another depending on how exposure is distributed over time. In homogeneous cell populations, Jensen's inequality has been shown to predict whether continuous or intermittent high-dose followed by low-dose is favored, based on the curvature of the concentration-effect function. Scheduling ordering can be performed based on curvature only: concave functions favor continuous dosing while convex functions favor intermittent dosing schedules with a high time-variance. However, tumors exhibit heterogeneous drug sensitivities, and treatment preferentially eliminates drug-sensitive cells, progressively shifting the surviving population toward greater drug resistance. Whether this treatment-induced selection can reverse curvature-based schedule ordering remains unclear.
items.author: Song, A. H., West, J.

items.title: BAF complexes cooperate with lineage-restricted transcription factors to establish cell-state-specific regulatory programs
items.summary: BRG1/BRM-associated factor (BAF) complexes are essential regulators of chromatin organization and cell identity. Genes encoding BAF subunits are among the most frequently mutated in human cancer. Yet, how disruption of a single subunit gives rise to distinct tumor states remains poorly understood. Atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumors (ATRTs) provide a compelling model, as they are uniformly driven by bi-allelic loss of the BAF subunit SMARCB1, yet segregate into distinct molecular subtypes. Using integrated multi-omics profiling of patient-derived ATRT organoids and primary tumor tissues, we show that transcriptional and chromatin accessibility changes upon SMARCB1 reconstitution are directed by subtype- and lineage-specific transcription factor (TF) repertoires.
items.author: He, J., Rios Arceo, C., Anderson, N. et al.

items.title: The Cxcl14 chemokine defines pioneer axon guidance and early circuit assembly in the inner ear.
items.summary: The nervous system wiring requires the precise coordination of axon guidance, neuronal migration, and target cell recognition. Here, we show that inner ear circuit formation relies on pioneer cells extending an axonal scaffold that selectively targets early-born hair cells. High spatiotemporal imaging of pioneer axons reveals how they navigate through the cranial environment, establishing dynamic cell-cell contacts with other axons to finally stabilize in target cells. These pioneer axons are required not only for follower axon growth but also for coordinated migration of follower neurons, revealing a cellular hierarchy underlying circuit assembly. We identify the chemokine Cxcl14 as a novel instructive guidance cue regulating pioneer axon extension, turning, and fasciculation at discrete cellular decision points.
items.author: Rumbo M, Bañón A, Nechiporuk AV, Alsina B.

items.title: Quantitative measurements of kinetochore protein copy numbers via FCS-calibrated molecular counting.
items.summary: The kinetochore is a protein complex for faithful chromosome segregation. While its architecture has been characterized in vitro based on structural studies, the molecular organization of the kinetochore in living cells remains unclear. To understand the molecular organization of kinetochore proteins in cells, we applied fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS), which enables absolute molecular counting based on its theoretical framework. This approach confirmed that CENP-C is present at roughly double the copy number compared with other components of the constitutive centromere-associated network such as CENP-T. We also analyzed the KMN network, specifically the Mis12 complex (Mis12C) and the Ndc80 complex (Ndc80C), and asked whether the recruitment of these outer kinetochore components relies on CENP-T and/or CENP-C.
items.author: Hirano Y, Takenoshita Y, Kitamura A, Hirota T, Fukagawa T.

items.title: Cytokine-Mediated Responses Across Endplate Subregions in Intervertebral Disc Multi-Tissue Explants.
items.summary: Background The endplate (EP) is essential for maintaining intervertebral disc (IVD) homeostasis by regulating nutrient transport to the nucleus pulposus (NP). Structural or biochemical alterations in the EP can impair this function and contribute to disc degeneration and low back pain (LBP). While most studies focus on the NP and annulus fibrosus (AF), increasing evidence suggests that early EP degeneration is a key initiator of disc pathology. Aims This study combined in silico modeling with a novel ex vivo multi-tissue culture system to investigate cytokine-driven degeneration across the intact IVD-vertebral interface. A previously validated signal-transduction network model predicted that degenerative environmental conditions alone, without cytokine stimulation, are limited in inducing chondrocyte degeneration.
items.author: Alminnawi A, Tejero P, Geeroms C, Geris L, Le Maitre CL.

items.title: Ruptured pheochromocytoma during preoperative doxazosin treatment.
items.summary: Rupture of pheochromocytoma is rare but represents a life-threatening complication. A 43-year-old man with episodic hypertension, palpitations, and chest discomfort was incidentally found, during a computed tomography (CT) aortogram performed to rule out aortic dissection, to have a 5.2-cm right adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Biochemical testing confirmed catecholamine excess. He was started on oral doxazosin 1 mg daily, which was titrated to 2 mg daily after 1 week, followed by oral bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily in preparation for surgery. Five weeks later, he presented with severe right-sided abdominal pain and a blood pressure of 215/111 mmHg. Abdominal CT angiography showed interval enlargement of the adrenal mass with posterior rupture and a retroperitoneal hematoma without active bleeding.
items.author: AlMaimoni R, AlFaraj A, AlSaif O, AlWosaibei A, Busbaih A, Hussein S.

items.title: A rare presentation of probable catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.
items.summary: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), a rare thrombotic manifestation of APS, is associated with high mortality. Rarely, it can present with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage (BAH). This case highlights a rare presentation of BAH due to probable catastrophic APS secondary to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). A 57-year-old female with diabetes presented with hypovolemic shock, abdominal pain, and vomiting. Imaging revealed BAH; antiphospholipid antibodies were present in high titers in the blood. Antinuclear antibody and antidouble-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid antibody (anti-dsDNA) were positive in high titers. Catastrophic APS secondary to SLE was diagnosed. Serum morning cortisol was at 9.2 μg/dL (SI: 254 nmol/L) (reference range: 5-25 μg/dL [SI: 138-635 nmol/L]), and adrenocorticotropic hormone was at 180 pg/mL (SI: 39.6 pmol/L) (reference range: 10-60 pg/mL [SI: 1.6-13.9 pmol/L]); which indicated evolving primary adrenal insufficiency.
items.author: Maji J, Roy A.

items.title: Environmental epimutagens, epigenetic memory, and cancer latency.
items.summary: Environmental exposures can cause cancer through DNA damage and mutations, but whether they can also leave durable, cancer-relevant changes in gene regulation is less clear. Chromatin helps maintain cell identity, differentiation state, and plasticity, providing a route by which non-genetic effects of exposure could persist after exposure. We define environmental epimutagens as agents or conditions that perturb chromatin regulation, and examine how such perturbations may influence cancer initiation and latency. Exposures can reach chromatin through altered metabolite or cofactor availability, interference with chromatin-regulating proteins, and direct chemical modification. Most resulting changes are transient, adaptive, or secondary. The central question is which become biologically embedded in long-lived cell populations, remain silent during latency, and alter responses to later genetic, inflammatory, or tissue-level pressures.
items.author: Arimondo P, Coumoul X, Lepeule J, Lopez M, Proudhon C, Sachs LM, Defossez PA.

items.title: Sclerosing mucoepidermoid thyroid carcinoma with eosinophilia treated by thyroidectomy and radiotherapy.
items.summary: Sclerosing mucoepidermoid carcinoma with eosinophilia (SMECE) is a rare thyroid malignancy with fewer than 100 reported cases. We present a 48-year-old male with dysphagia, fatigue, night sweats, and a 43-pound weight loss over 4 months. Evaluation revealed profound hypothyroidism and a thyroid gland entirely replaced by a hypoechoic mass on ultrasound. Core needle biopsy was nondiagnostic, and the patient underwent total thyroidectomy. Pathology confirmed SMECE involving both lobes, measuring 11.1 cm, with extrathyroidal extension into the surrounding adipose tissue. Given the lack of thyroglobulin expression in SMECE, radioactive iodine was not considered effective, and adjuvant external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) was administered at a dose of 60 Gy in 30 fractions.
items.author: Guatemala I, Arguinchona J, Stucky CC, Patel S, Schmitt AC, Doshi K.

items.title: Cilengitide limits syndromic and sporadic thoracic aortic aneurysm by targeting specific αV integrin.
items.summary: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, still lacking an etiologic therapy. Aberrant activation of TGF-β and dysregulation of mechanotransduction signalling in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a key role in the pathology. However, a precise picture of molecular mechanisms in the disease is still unclear. Integrins containing the αV subunit are central in pro-fibrotic pathways mediated by TGF-β and mechanotransduction signalling pathways, but their role as a potential therapeutic target in syndromic and sporadic TAAs still needs investigation. We showed higher expression levels of αV integrin in both types of human TAAs and that the αV integrin inhibitor Cilengitide limits pro-fibrotic events in patient-derived VSMCs.
items.author: Rega S, Bouhuis S, Brusati M, Maverna T, Fanotti N, Casaburo M, Vodret S, Riccitelli F, Celotto F, Lambroia L, Climent M, Elia L, Vescio M, Pattini L, Santoro R, Myasoedova V, Poggio P, Bonalumi G, Udugampolage NS, Taurino J, Pini A, Zacchigna S, Pompilio G, Perrucci GL.

items.title: Siamese banana peel-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles and their broad-spectrum antibacterial activity.
items.summary: Plant-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using agricultural by-products is not only a strategy to develop sustainable nanoparticle synthesis methods but also helps address environmental pollution caused by agricultural waste. In this study, Siamese banana peel (SBP) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for the synthesis of AgNPs. The effects of reaction time, AgNO 3 solution concentration, and the volume ratio between the AgNO 3 solution and banana peel extract on the formation of AgNPs were evaluated using UV-Vis spectroscopy via surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The physicochemical characteristics of AgNPs under optimal conditions were assessed via UV-Vis, FTIR, XRD, and HR-TEM analyses.
items.author: Van Nguyen TT, Nguyen PA, Vu TT, Gia-Thien Ho T, Do BL, Lai CT, Van Nguyen TT, Ta Truong TB, Nguyen-Tran H, Nguyen T.

items.title: Differences in Imaging and Surgical Management of Patellar Instability in Children and Adolescents Between Asia-Pacific and North America: A Systematic Review.
items.summary: Purpose To compare diagnostic imaging practices and surgical interventions for patellofemoral instability in children and adolescents between Asia-Pacific and North America. Methods A systematic review was conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guideline. Inclusion criteria were original surgical studies of patellofemoral instability in children or adolescent patients, with a sample size of more than 5, from either Asia-Pacific or North America. Exclusion criteria included nonoriginal research, cadaveric/biomechanical studies, imaging-only reports, unrelated diagnoses, and adult-only cohorts. Data were synthesized descriptively by region. Results Sixty-eight studies were included, with 15 from Asia-Pacific and 53 from North America.
items.author: Heng WT, Zhang S, Tan SHS, Hui JHP.

items.title: Ultrasound-driven nitrogen oxidation: a sonoelectrochemical pathway to ammonia synthesis boosted by contact-electro-catalysis.
items.summary: Ultrasound activates N 2 , forming reactive NO 2 - and NO 3 - intermediates that are electrochemically reduced to NH 3 . Integrating ultrasound with contact-electro-catalysis significantly enhances N 2 activation and NH 3 yield, offering a simple pathway for sustainable NH 3 synthesis.
items.author: Toghraei A, Guay D.

items.title: Statistically Fragile Evidence Underlies Comparative Trials of Arthroscopic Meniscectomy Versus Nonoperative Management for Degenerative Meniscus Tears.
items.summary: Purpose To assess the statistical robustness of comparative studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing arthroscopic meniscal debridement or meniscectomy with nonoperative or sham interventions. Methods Comparative studies and RCTs of meniscus debridement or meniscectomy versus nonoperative or sham interventions were identified through a comprehensive literature search in June 2025 following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Study characteristics, dichotomous outcomes, and continuous outcomes were extracted. The fragility index and continuous fragility index were calculated as the number of event reversals required to change significance; these metrics were normalized by sample size to calculate the fragility quotient (FQ) and continuous FQ.
items.author: Bosco AP, Rasquinha RD, Voyer E, Rosenberg AE, Quinn M, Marcaccio S.

items.title: Effect of rapid thermal annealing on the optoelectronic figures of merit of a vanadium nitride/porous silicon heterojunction photodetector.
items.summary: Rapid thermal annealing (RTA) is an essential step in the fabrication of photovoltaic devices. It considerably improves crystallinity, dopant activation, electrical conductivity, optical efficiency, and contact formation while minimizing unwanted diffusion. These improvements, in turn, facilitate the fabrication of high-performance devices. In this study, vanadium nitride (VN) thin films and porous silicon (PSi) were prepared using reactive DC sputtering and photoelectrochemical etching (PECE) techniques, respectively. The effects of RTA at 1023 K for 35 s on the structural, morphological, optical, and electrical properties of the VN films and the figures of merit properties of VN/PSi/ n -Si heterojunction photodetectors were systematically studied.
items.author: Kasim ST, Hadi HA, Ismail RA, Hayif ND.

items.title: Competitive ligand exchange of Fe 3+ catecholate complexes with novel biobased chelators: a DFT-metadynamics investigation.
items.summary: The complexation of metal ions by polyphenolic compounds is a ubiquitous phenomenon in both natural and engineered systems, encompassing a vast multidimensional landscape of metal-ligand interactions. An important challenge in a range of applications, including textile care, is the efficient removal of stains formed by polyphenolic compounds coordinated to metal ions at the molecular level. In this study, we investigate the ligand-exchange process between a catecholate ligand coordinated to an Fe 3+ center - a key molecular origin of persistent colored stains - and six candidate chelating ligands using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. The selected ligands were chosen for their potential derivation from bio-based feedstocks, offering promising routes toward sustainable and environmentally benign stain-removal technologies.
items.author: Heshmat M, Kostetskyy P, van Es DS.

items.title: A phosphinic acid bioisostere of hydroxyethylamine as a novel antiplasmodial scaffold: design, synthesis, and in vitro and in silico evaluation.
items.summary: Malaria remains a major global health concern, and the emergence of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains highlights the need for new antimalarial scaffolds. In this study, a phosphinic acid-based analogue 2 was designed and synthesized through bioisosteric replacement of the hydroxyethylamine motif found in plasmepsin inhibitor scaffolds. The target compound was obtained through a multistep synthetic approach and evaluated for its antiplasmodial activity against the drug-resistant P. falciparum W2 strain. Compound 2 showed moderate whole-cell antiplasmodial activity with an IC 50 value of 3.63 ± 0.11 µM. In silico ADMET analysis indicated favorable absorption-related properties and revealed several parameters requiring further experimental investigation.
items.author: Abdou MM, Khodair AI, Qiu D, El-Saeed RA, Bahtati N, Khan FI, Matziari M.

items.title: Modulation of the RNA-sensing RIG/MAVS pathway bypasses resistance to hypomethylating agents in acute myeloid leukemia.
items.summary: DNA hypomethylating agents (HMAs) such as 5-azacytidine (5-AZA) are a cornerstone in the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but development of resistance represents a major clinical challenge. Apart from epigenetic reprogramming of malignant cell clones, therapy with HMA is increasingly recognized to facilitate antineoplastic immunity, yet the relevance of these molecular mechanisms in AML remains poorly defined. Here, we show that AML cell-intrinsic sensing of aberrant RNA via the innate receptor system retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)/mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS) is essential for the therapeutic activity of HMAs. In human and murine AML cell lines, HMA treatment induced robust RIG-I/MAVS pathway activation and subsequent Type I interferon (IFN-I) release.
items.author: El Khawanky N, Nedelko T, Mandracci G, Barth Y, Jiang Y, Wang K, Rosenbaum M, Weiß C, Geisenberger C, Enßle S, Gómez Martínez AM, Göttert S, Hamed N, Fischer JC, Ruland J, Busch DH, Poeck H, Götze KS, Illert AL, Bassermann F, Heidegger SM.

items.title: Wavelength-controlled photothermal reduction of carbon dioxide to produce fuels over Nb 2 AlC/TiO 2 heterostructures in a continuous-flow reactor.
items.summary: A highly conductive Nb 2 AlC MAX phase was coupled with TiO 2 to construct Nb 2 AlC/TiO 2 heterostructures and evaluated for CO 2 photothermal reduction under solar radiations. Incorporation of 10 wt% Nb 2 AlC into TiO 2 significantly improved the photocatalytic performance with 858.8 and 10.5 µmol g -1 h -1 of CO and H 2 respectively with a water-methanol mixture at 150 °C. Using the water-methanol mixture, the CO production rate is 77.7 and 1.7 fold higher than using water and pristine TiO 2 only. Similarly, the corresponding rates were 3.6 and 1.2 fold higher for H 2 production.
items.author: Sharma A, Tahir M, Kumar N.

items.title: Fabrication of guggulsterone-E-integrated chitosan-zinc nanohybrids: surface chemical insights, biointerface interactions and multi-target antidiabetic mechanisms.
items.summary: The research focuses on evaluating the potential anti-diabetic efficacy of encapsulating guggulsterone-E extract within chitosan-ZnO NPs (Gu@ChZn NPs) through a sustainable production method. UV-vis, FT-IR, FE-SEM, HR-TEM, EDX, XPS, and XRD characterizations were used to identify the physicochemical properties of the Gu@ChZn NPs. The UV-visible absorption peak was noted at 320 nm, and morphological analysis revealed that the particles were mainly spherical with uneven surface characteristics and sizes of 5-45 nm. Based on the biological evaluation, it was found that compared with guggulsterone-E alone, Gu@ChZn NPs had a greater inhibitory effect on selected enzymes such as lipase, α-glucosidase, and α-amylase.
items.author: Boomija RV, Kamaraj C, Karthick Rajan D, Thirunavukkarasu S, Al-Ghanim KA.

items.title: Bisspirooxindole synthesis: a comprehensive review of starting material-based strategies (2006-2026).
items.summary: Bisspirooxindole frameworks constitute an important class of heterocyclic compounds because of their unique three-dimensional architectures, the presence of two spiro carbon centers, and widespread presence in biologically active natural products, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials. Owing to their structural complexity and significant pharmacological potential, the development of efficient and selective synthetic methodologies for the construction of bisspirooxindole scaffolds has attracted continuous attention in modern organic synthesis. Despite the remarkable advances achieved over the past two decades, a comprehensive review that systematically categorizes the synthetic strategies toward bisspirooxindole and highlights recent advances has not yet been presented. This review, provides the first extensive and strategy-oriented overview of synthetic methodologies for the synthesis of bisspirooxindole scaffolds reported between 2006 and 2026.
items.author: Ahmadi F, Abdi Z, Javadi M.

items.title: Tracking Temporal Changes in Metal Pollution in Estuarine Sediments: Population Pressure, Pollution Trends, and Policy Responses in India, China, and the USA.
items.summary: This study introduces the Population Normalized Pollution Load (PNPL) as a complementary approach to the Pollution Load Index (PLI) to evaluate sediment metal contamination in relation to population pressure. A global comparative assessment of sediment metal contamination was conducted across major estuarine systems from India, China, and the United States using published data sets. The PLI ranked the investigated estuaries from least to most polluted as: Galveston Bay < Yellow River Estuary < Hudson Estuary < Hooghly (Ganga) Estuary < Mahanadi Estuary < Yangtze Estuary < Chesapeake Bay < Pearl River Estuary < Cochin Estuary < Ulhas Estuary. Temporal PLI trends revealed contrasting contamination trajectories, which reflected differences in historical pollution intensity, population pressure, and pollution control practices.
items.author: Chatterjee S, Chakraborty P, Das A, Roy G, Mohanta S, Chakraborty S.

items.title: Hydrogen peroxide-responsive fluorescent probes based on aromatic imidazole derivatives: design, optimization and biomedical applications.
items.summary: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a key bioactive molecule involved in various physiological processes, including cellular signal transduction, oxidative stress regulation, and immune metabolism. Disruption of H 2 O 2 homeostasis is closely associated with the initiation and progression of multiple diseases, particularly tumors. In this study, we leveraged the ultrahigh brightness of aromatic imidazole carbaldehyde derivatives to design a series of novel H 2 O 2 -responsive fluorescent probes. By integrating two distinct H 2 O 2 -responsive moieties with these highly luminescent fluorophores, we successfully synthesized the probes designated as BTI, BTB, PTI, and PTB, which could be specifically activated by exogenous or endogenous H 2 O 2 in cancer cells.
items.author: Zhu Y.

items.title: Targetoid Eruption With Oral and Ocular Mucositis in a Young Woman.
items.summary: Young adults presenting with fever, targetoid lesions, and severe mucositis pose a diagnostic challenge because drug-induced severe cutaneous adverse reactions and infection-associated mucocutaneous eruptions may appear clinically similar. Correct identification matters because misattributing the eruption to a drug can result in an unnecessary lifelong drug allergy label, and marked ocular involvement may require prompt ophthalmological care to prevent long-term sequelae.
items.author: Jaruvijitrattana P, Tawanwongsri W, Eden C.

items.title: Micropost-integrated acoustofluidic device for enhanced microparticle trapping and release.
items.summary: Acoustofluidics is a powerful tool in the development of devices to focus, trap, or otherwise manipulate microparticles for many uses in materials processing, biomedical analysis, and sample preparation. Most approaches have used the primary acoustic force for positioning and trapping, but this force is dramatically weaker as particles move into the nanoscale. This has driven interest in trapping of particles to surfaces using the acoustic secondary force, which has enabled creation of both acoustically enhanced filters and acoustic trapping via seed particles, effectively trapping particles at the nanoscale. These approaches remain constrained by fluidic drag and limited residence-time control within acoustic fields.
items.author: Senavirathna D, Trujillo RJ, Sellapperumage AF, Oglesby R, Shreve AP, Campen MJ, Graves SW, Piyasena ME.

items.title: Discovery of novel 1,3,4-thiadiazole derivatives as potential dual EGFR/VEGFR inhibitors with activity against breast, colon, and liver cancer cells: biological evaluation and molecular docking investigation.
items.summary: New derivatives of the 1,3,4-thiadiazole scaffold were synthesized and evaluated for their cytotoxic effects on breast (MCF-7), hepatic (HepG-2), and colorectal (HCT-116) carcinomas. The most active compounds (7, 8, 15, and 16) exhibited substantial, broad-spectrum anticancer efficacy, with IC 50 values ranging from 1.58-4.27 µM relative to doxorubicin. To explore their potential modulatory capacity on receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), compounds 7, 8, 15, and 16 were evaluated for enzymatic efficacy against VEGFR-2, and the most active hits, 7 and 15, were further assessed against EGFR. The findings suggest a possible VEGFR/EGFR-mediated inhibition of cancer cell proliferation, with compounds 7 and 15 showing enzymatic inhibitory activity, displaying IC 50 values of 0.42 and 0.23 µM for EGFR and 0.17 and 0.16 µM for VEGFR-2, respectively.
items.author: Belal A, Abourehab MAS, Alsantali RI, Obaidullah AJ, Erfan R, Elwan Y, Gaber AA, Mehany ABM, Sabour R, Elgammal WE.

items.title: Strain-tuned mechanical, ferromagnetic, thermoelectric and pressure-induced thermodynamic properties of the double perovskite Ba 2 InMoO 6 for energy-harvesting purposes.
items.summary: The biaxial strain in oxide-based double perovskites provides significant insight into their electronic and magnetic properties, showing their potential for spintronic applications. A first-principles study of the mechanical, ferromagnetic, thermoelectric and thermodynamic properties of the double perovskite Ba 2 InMoO 6 has been conducted using the WIEN2K simulation package. The structural properties are illustrated via lattice parameters, ground-state energies and optimized curves. The computed values of the elastic constants ( C 11 , C 12 and C 44 ) verify the crystal rigidity, mechanical stability and elastic behaviour, as well as the bonding nature, of the materials. A Pugh's ratio greater than 1.75, a positive Cauchy pressure, and a Poisson's ratio greater than the critical value of 0.26 confirm the ductility of the studied compound.
items.author: Shah STH, Hussain A, Almutairi BS, Khan MN, Nazir S.

items.title: Association of obstetric factors with maternal morbidity and mortality in patients who gave birth preterm.
items.summary: Background Preterm birth is associated with an increased rate of serious maternal complication compared with those who deliver at term. However, data are limited on risk factors for maternal morbidity and mortality specifically in the setting of preterm birth. Improved understanding of risk factors for morbidity in patients with preterm birth can help optimize interventions to best support patients experiencing preterm birth. Objective To assess associations between obstetric factors and maternal morbidities and mortality among patients who gave birth less than 35 weeks' gestation. Study design This is a secondary analysis of a multicenter registry of gravidas carrying singletons or twins who gave birth at 16 0/7 to 34 6/7 weeks' gestation January through August 2019.
items.author: Des Jardin MK, McGee PL, Sibai BM, Clifton RG, Costantine MM, Varner MW, Longo M, Bell EF, Stoll BJ, Allard D, Salazar A, Thorp JM, Reddy UM, Miller ES, Rouse DJ, Simhan HN, Tita ATN, Bailit JL, Dugoff L, Macones GA, Saade GR, Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Units (MFMU) Network.

items.title: Perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended virtual and in-person prenatal care model in integrated healthcare systems.
items.summary: Background Traditional US prenatal care typically includes 12-14 standardized in-person visits. COVID-19-related barriers accelerated adoption of blended virtual/in-person prenatal care, but evidence from large, diverse populations is limited. Objective To compare perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended prenatal care model versus traditional in-person care in a large health maintenance organization. Methods Retrospective cohort study in Kaiser Permanente Northwest and Southern California comparing blended care (cases, July 22, 2022 to December 31, 2024) with traditional in-person care (controls, January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019). Groups were compared using t -tests/Wilcoxon and chi-square tests; multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
items.author: Fassett MJ, West EV, Gibson EC, Tim LSC, Avila CC, Shi JM, Chiu VY, Chung JW, Rudolph EE, Khadka N, Jentz CJ, Mosen DM, Nonog JC, Audelo JW, Getahun D.

items.title: Beyond symptom severity: Prognostic information from subjective person-specific problem networks in young people.
items.summary: Background Person-specific network models are increasingly proposed to support personalized assessment and psychotherapy, but it remains unclear whether the information they contain is prospectively informative in young people. We tested whether characteristics derived from a brief perceived causal network (PECAN), particularly its perceived relational structure, provided prognostic information about subsequent psychopathology beyond baseline symptom severity. Methods Participants were 361 children, adolescents, and young adults assessed by self-report or parent-report. At baseline, participants selected personally relevant problems, rated their severity, and indicated how they perceived these problems to be related. Psychopathology was assessed with the pediatric symptom checklist (PSC-D) at baseline and approximately 4, 8, and 12 weeks later.
items.author: Vogel F, Jungmann S.

items.title: Operant conditioning in Indian free-ranging dogs: effects of positive and threatening cues on sociability.
items.summary: Sociability towards humans is an adaptive trait in free-ranging dogs (FRDs), enabling them to access resources while navigating the risky anthropogenic habitat. We investigated whether operant conditioning shapes sociability in Indian FRDs and whether learned responses generalize to an unfamiliar individual. We exposed 54 dog groups to either a positive or a threatening cue over five consecutive days, followed by tests on day 6 with an unfamiliar and then the familiar experimenter. Using Bayesian GLMMs, we analysed approach proportion, approach latency and demeanour. The threatening cue reduced approach behaviour, increased approach latency and caused a shift towards neutral responses to the familiar experimenter, with the changes occurring earlier compared with the positive cue.
items.author: Nandi S, Roy D, Adak A, Sarkar R, Bhadra A.

items.title: Discovery of new polyacetylenes from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla through activity-directed phytochemical investigation and evaluation of their anti-inflammatory properties.
items.summary: Adenia cardiophylla (Mast.) Engl. Passifloraceae has long been used in traditional medicine throughout Vietnam and Southeast Asia for the treatment of rheumatism, bone pain, and pneumonia. Based on bioassay-guided isolation, seven previously undescribed compounds, including one cyanogenic glycoside (1), four polyacetylenes (2-4, 6), and two cyclopentene carboxylic acid derivatives (20 and 21), together with sixteen known compounds from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla were isolated. The chemical structures were determined by detailed spectroscopic methods (UV, IR, HRMS, NMR), ECD, and computational NMR calculation methods. Anti-inflammatory activity was evaluated by measuring nitric oxide (NO) production in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophage cells.
items.author: Tran DH, Nguyen QPN, Van Thanh Vo N, Truong DDK, Ly TL, Yoon YC, Hoang AV, Kwon SW, Ma CT.

items.title: Uncovering and understanding "transesterification triggers" in aliphatic polyester synthesis with bis-Zn catalysts.
items.summary: On paper, the generation of block copolymers through sequential copolymerisation of two lactones should be straightforward when using a living polymerisation. In practice, this is often not the case, and random copolymer architectures can occur due to transesterification processes. The ability to predict whether certain lactone monomer combinations will deliver block or random copolymers is currently missing. Through a systematic study of monomer features, this work uncovers the impact of monomer substituents, ester functional group density, Lewis basicity, and chelation potential, to identify the key factors that favour or disfavour transesterification. This work uncovers a general trend where the most Lewis basic monomers promote transesterification.
items.author: Tufano F, Hughes JWJ, Neal TJ, Radetzky K, Lamberti M, Garden JA.

items.title: (OTA) 3 FeMo 6 -DES: a liquid catalyst integrating catalytic and extractive functions for room-temperature oxidative desulfurization.
items.summary: To address the intrinsic limitations of up-to-date oxidative desulfurization, this study adopted a synergistic polyoxometalate (POM) - deep eutectic solvent (DES) catalytic strategy to prepare a liquid catalyst (POM-DES) with dual functions of catalysis and extraction through simple stirring. Experimental results demonstrate that the catalyst-composed of an Anderson-type polyoxometalate (OTA) 3 FeMo 6 and a p -toluene sulfonic acid-based ternary DES-achieves complete removal of DBT under mild conditions (30 °C, O/S = 2.8, DES dosage = 0.5 mL, POM loading = 0.02 g mL -1 ) within 30 minutes. Moreover, the catalyst exhibits excellent recyclability, maintaining high activity over five consecutive cycles without significant deactivation.
items.author: Bai Y, Hua Y, Shen Y, Meng X, Yang Y, Zhang H.

items.title: Composition-property correlations of SiO 2 content in CO 2 -based PPC/ionic-liquid composite zinc electrolytes.
items.summary: The performance of multicomponent polymer electrolytes for Zn batteries is governed collectively by the local ionic environment, bulk ion transport, Zn 2+ -associated steady-state response, and electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Here, laboratory-synthesized CO 2 -based poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC) was used as a film-forming matrix, together with PYR 13 TFSI, Zn(TFSI) 2 , and varying contents of SiO 2 , to construct PPC/PYR 13 TFSI/Zn(TFSI) 2 /SiO 2 solid-state composite polymer electrolytes. Systematic composition-property correlations were established between SiO 2 content and multiscale properties in a fixed PPC/PYR 13 TFSI/Zn(TFSI) 2 ternary matrix. Because PPC incorporates CO 2 as a comonomer-derived carbon source, this material platform provides a CO 2 -valorization-oriented electrolyte design.
items.author: Mu G, An S, Ren G, Wang H, Guo L.

items.title: Chitosan- and alginate-based biopolymeric composites for the adsorption of heavy metal ions from wastewater: modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration.
items.summary: Chitosan and alginate offer complementary amino, hydroxyl and carboxylate functionality for the removal of dissolved metal contaminants. Their practical performance depends on chemical modification, network stability, solution composition and sorbent architecture. This narrative review examines modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration, with particular attention to chitosan-alginate hybrids. The review links polymer chemistry and fabrication to reported adsorption performance, distinguishing literature-reported capacities from evidence of mechanism and operational durability. A descriptive compilation identifies study-specific results and gaps in experimental reporting. It is not a normalised benchmark or a systematic meta-analysis. Hybridisation and functionalisation can improve selected properties, but the available cross-study data do not establish universal superiority over single-polymer sorbents or isolate donor chemistry from composition and test conditions.
items.author: Aden M, Elmi A, Idriss S, Idriss AI.

items.title: Chiral amines in the asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral allenes through catalysis and covalent chirality transfer.
items.summary: Axially chiral allenes are useful motifs and intermediates in stereoselective synthesis. Chiral amines provide several routes to these structures, but their operational roles differ. An amine may act as a regenerated organocatalyst, cooperate with a metal catalyst, or serve as a stoichiometric covalent mediator that transfers stereochemical information through a propargylamine. This review compares these roles using amine loading, substrate activation, stereochemical evidence and regeneration as organizing criteria. Noncovalent additions, isomerizations and proton-transfer reactions are considered alongside enamine and dienamine catalysis, stereoselective functionalization of pre-existing allenes, and cooperative palladium-amine and gold-squaramide chemistry. Metal-assisted rearrangements of chiral propargylamines provide complementary access to allenes through covalent chirality transfer.
items.author: Alakonda LM, Nael MA, Elokely KM.

items.title: Current Approaches to the Treatment of Hepatorenal Syndrome.
items.summary: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is a life-threatening complication of advanced cirrhosis that requires early recognition, treatment of precipitating factors, and coordinated transplant assessment. This narrative review examines pharmacological treatment, fluid management, kidney replacement therapy (KRT), transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), and liver transplantation in adults, with emphasis on HRS with acute kidney injury (AKI). Contemporary diagnostic criteria recognize that hepatorenal physiology can coexist with tubular injury or chronic kidney disease (CKD) and discourage a routine 48-hour albumin challenge. Clinical assessment should integrate perfusion, oxygenation, and congestion, with ultrasound used as an adjunct when available. Terlipressin with individualized albumin improves renal reversal in suitable patients, but a consistent overall survival benefit has not been established, and respiratory failure remains a major safety concern.
items.author: Rosales CA.

items.title: Coordination-gated oxovanadium electrolyte for scalable high-temperature vanadium flow batteries.
items.summary: Vanadium flow batteries (VFBs) are promising for grid-scale energy storage, but their thermal operating window is limited by VO 2 + instability. Above 45 °C, VO 2 + undergoes oxo-bridged condensation and causes V 2 O 5 precipitation, leading to system failure. Here we report a heterocationic coordination-gating strategy to regulate V(v) condensation. In the designed electrolyte, Ti(iv) exists as TiO 2+ -like oxophilic units that form VO 2 + through persistent V-O-Ti bridges. These bridges occupy reactive oxo sites of V(v) species, gating V-O-V network formation and delaying V 2 O 5 nucleation. Consequently, a 2 M VO 2 + electrolyte containing TiO 2+ remains stable for 40 days at 50 °C ( vs.
items.author: Long H, Zhao Z, Liu T, Xing F, Jiang J, Hua L, Chen S, Xie C, Li X.

items.title: Peer review of the pesticide risk assessment of the active substance fatty acids from hydrolysed vegetable oils.
items.summary: The conclusions of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) following the peer review of the initial risk assessments carried out by the competent authorities of the rapporteur Member State, Greece, and co-rapporteur Member State, Austria, for the pesticide active substance fatty acids from hydrolysed vegetable oils are reported. The context of the peer review was that required by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 844/2012, as amended by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 2018/1659. The conclusions were reached on the basis of the evaluation of the representative uses of the active substance as an acaricide and insecticide on strawberry, tomato, cucumber, pome fruits and stone fruit, fruiting vegetables, pulses, ornamentals (annual and perennial), brassica vegetable, leafy and stem vegetable, root and tuber vegetable, bulb vegetable and berry fruit.
items.author: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Álvarez F, Arena M, Auteri D, Leite SB, Binaglia M, Castoldi AF, Capilla TC, Chiusolo A, Colagiorgi A, Colas M, Crivellente F, De Lentdecker C, De Magistris I, Fabrega J, Fait G, Ferilli F, Santonja GG, Gouliarmou V, Ippolito A, Istace F, Kardassi D, Kienzler A, Lanzoni A, Lava R, Leuschner R, Linguadoca A, Romano ML, Louisse J, Lythgo C, Mangas I, Mazzega S, Mioč A, Miron I, Molnar T, Padovani L, Padricello V, Panzarea M, Parra Morte JM, Rizzuto S, Santos M, Serafimova R, Sharp R, Szentes C, Theobald A, Tiramani M, Vianello G, Villamar-Bouza L, Becirovic A, Mavriou G.

items.title: Wildfire Drivers, Impacts, and Predictive Modeling: Opportunities in Sensing and Machine Learning.
items.summary: Wildfire prediction and management remain inherently challenging because fire behavior is governed by complex, nonlinear interactions among the atmosphere, biosphere, geosphere, and human influences. Intensified by climate change and anthropogenic activities, wildfires are becoming more severe in portions of the world, degrading air quality, threatening public health, generating substantial economic losses, and producing secondary hazards such as debris flows and water contamination. This review synthesizes recent advances in multi-sensor remote sensing and machine learning approaches for wildfire management, focusing on three key domains: pre-fire risk monitoring, active-fire detection, and post-fire severity assessment. It highlights how emerging sensing technologies and predictive models integrate diverse environmental variables, remotely sensed spectral indices, and geospatial data sets to improve wildfire forecasting, situational awareness, and decision-making.
items.author: Tung JY, Mishra A, Sadegh M, Sabut A, Aghakouchak A, Abatzoglou J, Devineni N, Sankarasubramanian A.

items.title: Metabolic signature combined with changes in proteome and transcriptome shape respiratory syncytial virus infection and response to vaccination in a bovine model.
items.summary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major respiratory disease in infants leading to long-term morbidity. Bovine RSV (bRSV) serves as a clinically translatable large animal model to understand host responses in neonates to vaccination and re-infection enabling straightforward and accessible sample collection not often possible in human infants. This study probes clinically relevant bovine biointerfaces by combining Raman spectroscopy-based metabolic profiling with proteomics and gene expression in nasal fluid, serum, and lung tissues collected from 11 vaccinated (V) and 11 non-vaccinated (NV) neonatal calves following bRSV rechallenge. The analyses showed at Day 7 post-challenge, 16 significant Raman metabolite peaks in nasal fluid, 17 peaks in sera, and 17 peaks in lesioned lung tissue differentiated V from NV calves including features associated with glucose, lipids and fatty acids, and phenylalanine among others.
items.author: Kothadiya S, Mathew AP, Schoofs AD, Nandu RK, Niolo-Velesaca CA, McGill J, Bardhan R.

items.title: High-precision authentication of cigarettes using surface-enhanced Raman scattering spectroscopy combined with machine learning.
items.summary: Rapid and reliable authentication of genuine versus counterfeit cigarettes is challenging because products vary across brands and production batches. Here, we develop a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)-based screening method for cigarette authentication and evaluate it across 17 commercial brands using tobacco water extracts from genuine and confirmed counterfeit products. Method optimization identified citrate-reduced silver nanoparticles (AgC NPs) as the most reproducible SERS substrate, and an extraction temperature of 40 °C provided the best balance of signal stability and class separability. Under these conditions, eight machine-learning classifiers were benchmarked on SERS spectral fingerprints; a quadratic-kernel support vector machine (SVM) achieved the best overall performance, combining high accuracy with strong generalization while limiting overfitting.
items.author: Yang H, Huang Y, Zhou H, Xu Y, Huang N, Su X, Peng J, Kong H, Zhao R, Tang P.

items.title: Preparation, Characterization, and Anti-Fatigue Activity of Clamworm ( Perinereis aibuhitensis ) Hydrolysate and Its Peptide and Polysaccharide Fractions.
items.summary: Fatigue is a prevalent health issue necessitating effective nutritional interventions. Perinereis aibuhitensis (clamworm) is a commercially important marine species traditionally valued for its rich nutritional profile and medicinal properties. This study investigated the preparation, characterization, and anti-fatigue activity of Perinereis aibuhitensis hydrolysate (PAH). Optimized enzymatic hydrolysis yielded PAH rich in small molecular peptides ( p < 0.05). Furthermore, PAH effectively maintained muscle morphology, boosted energy reserves (glycogen and ATP), reduced metabolite accumulation (lactic acid, urea nitrogen, and creatine kinase), and enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase increased by 42.92%-65.34% and 42.51%-52.49%, respectively). These findings reveal that the potent anti-fatigue efficacy of PAH may be associated with the contributions of both its bioactive constituents of BCAAs, putative glycogen-like polysaccharides, and sulfated polysaccharides.
items.author: Qiu D, Fang S, Cui F, Zhou H, Zhang M, Zhao Z, She W, Obadina AO, Wu H, Wang W.

items.title: Push-pull luminescent imidazole derivatives: ICT enables efficient picric acid sensing.
items.summary: Two push-pull fluorophores (3a-b) based on a tri-substituted imidazole core appended with donor-acceptor groups were successfully synthesized by the catalysis of Amberlite IR 120H + and were fully characterized by NMR and mass spectral analyses. The synthesized compounds exhibit strong luminescent properties due to their donor-acceptor (push-pull) electronic structures and possess pronounced excited-state charge transfer characteristics, as evidenced by steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic experiments. Imidazole incorporated with donor groups in the phenyl rings at the 4- and 5-positions (3b) shows a greater extent of charge transfer and emits yellow color in polar solvents like DMSO and acetonitrile. Both the fluorophores were found to act as sensors of picric acid in the solution phase with a very low detection level (nM) by static quenching of the fluorescence emission mechanism.
items.author: Dey M, Bhattacharyya A, Roy S, Majumdar S.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a multimodal deep learning model for screening-level lower-limb alignment using plantar 3D foot scans.
items.summary: Lower-limb alignment is a key determinant of musculoskeletal loading and is associated with biomechanical risk pathways for conditions such as knee osteoarthritis and plantar fasciitis. However, routine alignment assessment still relies on radiography or specialist clinical examination, limiting scalability for early screening. Here, we investigated whether plantar foot morphology captured by weight-bearing 3D scanning can serve as a computational screening feature for proximal lower-limb alignment, and we developed a multimodal deep learning framework to support scalable alignment screening. We established a cross-sectional dataset of 167 participants (adults and children aged 6-60 years) with standardised plantar 3D foot scans and clinical labels for arch type, hindfoot alignment, and frontal-plane knee alignment.
items.author: Ni S, Chen Y, Wang C, Zhou D, Liu J, Zhou M, Leong J, Hu Y, Huang J, Wang J, Liu C.

items.title: Body composition and blood pressure: Haemodynamic links in young men and women
