items.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
items.summary: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
items.author: Gerelle Q. Dodson

items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch.
items.author: Emre Kutlusan, Yongmin Li

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning.
items.author: Sheethal Bhat, Bogdan Georgescu, Awais Mansoor et al.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes.
items.author: Alex Shtoff

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns.
items.author: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Jiangweizhi Peng et al.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation.
items.author: Ziang Liu, James J. Kim, Yijia Dai et al.

items.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
items.summary: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using Lüscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI.
items.author: Kabir Bajaj, Henry W. Lin

items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls.
items.author: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys et al.

items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.summary: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.
items.author: Yeyuan Liu

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for.
items.author: Daniel Lenton

items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly.
items.author: Adi Mashiach

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.summary: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms.
items.author: Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown et al.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.summary: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it.
items.author: Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya et al.

items.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
items.summary: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress.
items.author: Chubin Zhang, Bo An

items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.summary: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which largely decide how the game ends; after that, most models plateau.
items.author: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su et al.

items.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
items.summary: Electric flux strings underpin confinement in gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, their evolution involves competing processes of charge motion, pair creation, and transverse deformation. Accessing these dynamics beyond perturbative limits challenges classical approaches, as entanglement growth restricts the times accessible to tensor-network simulations. Here we use quantum simulation to investigate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction, spanning strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. Using 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, we evolve initially localized strings with static or dynamical endpoint charges. Spatially resolved measurements reveal rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation in the string interior near the pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields.
items.author: Sanziana Stelea, Anthony Gandon, Francesco Tacchino et al.

items.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm
items.summary: Visible and near-ultraviolet light underpins applications from biophotonics to quantum computing, which demand fast control of optical amplitude and phase. Integrated photonics offers scalable control, yet most visible-wavelength platforms lack gigahertz-scale modulation. We demonstrate a thin-film lithium niobate platform at 493 nm integrating grating couplers, beamsplitters, ring resonators, and modulators. Segmented traveling-wave modulators achieve a half-wave voltage--length product of 450 mV$\cdot$cm, $>$20 dB extinction, and bandwidth beyond 50 GHz. Ring resonators show $2.9 \pm 0.2$ dB/cm propagation loss and quantify the platform's photorefractive response. This enables agile visible beam delivery for trapped-ion systems, although photorefraction and substrate uniformity remain key challenges to scaling.
items.author: Nicholas Achuthan, Letícia Magalhães, Xudong Li et al.

items.title: Running out of Field Range: Nonlinear Sourcing of Light Scalars
items.summary: Light scalar fields coupled linearly to the Standard Model are constrained by equivalence-principle tests, fifth-force searches, clock comparison tests, and stellar cooling. These bounds assume that the coupling to ordinary matter can be expanded to linear order for all field values reached. For a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson with decay constant $f$ this fails as soon as the field value reaches $O(f)$. The field around a source then stops growing with the coupling, and in addition the linear coupling of a probe is suppressed depending on its location. We reanalyze all of these bounds for the couplings to photons, electrons and nucleons.
items.author: Abhishek Banerjee, Shourya Mukherjee, Stefan Stelzl

items.title: TanCRAFT: Context-Reasoned Anticipatory Feedback for Assembly Tasks
items.summary: Preventing human error in physical assembly tasks requires assistance systems that can intervene before mistakes are made. This is especially challenging in settings where users are free to choose the construction order and correctness depends on the evolving assembly rather than a fixed next step. We present TanCRAFT, a four-stage real-time predictive assistance system that tracks the scene state, reasons about the current partial assembly, forecasts the near-future motion of manipulated pieces, and intervenes when the predicted placement is incompatible with the target. We instantiate our framework and confirm its effectiveness in a controlled tangram assembly task through offline benchmarks and a within-subject user study.
items.author: Sassan Mokhtar, Lars Doorenbos, Marius Bock et al.

items.title: Finite-Key Readiness and Authentication-Key Replenishment in QKD-Assisted UAV Edge Computing
items.summary: A service that needs fresh quantum keys must wait for key release, and may be denied it, before protected computation starts. We quantify this cost for a trusted stationary UAV serving two ground gateways, each obtaining its keys from one finite-key decoy-state BB84 attempt with parameters fixed in advance. A count-level Monte Carlo model, reproduced by a semi-analytic model, links key acceptance to protected upload, computation, and download, including failed attempts and hover energy. At 26~dB effective optical loss, with authentication hashing at its proxy-benchmarked, near-zero cost, fresh keys raise the 95th-percentile completion time of both tasks from 10.37 to 28.65~s; hover energy grows in proportion.
items.author: Dang H. Le, Ban Q. Tran, Susan Mengel

items.title: Structure of correlations for the single-$j$ model using quantum information theory
items.summary: We say that a system undergoes a quantum phase transition when the mean-field ground state of a given Hamiltonian spontaneously breaks its symmetries depending on the Hamiltonian parameters. It is a widely accepted view that this phenomenon enables the mean-field state to absorb the maximum amount of correlations without losing its mean-field structure. However, it is still uncertain how those correlations are incorporated within the mean-field state and how the correlation structure changes when we get closer to the exact ground state by restoring the symmetries. In this work, we answer these questions by studying the single-$j$ model, which is a realistic fermionic nuclear model with abelian and non-abelian broken symmetries.
items.author: Javier Faba, Vicente Martín, Luis Robledo

items.title: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling
items.summary: Thermal amplification enables sensitive control of heat currents, providing a basis for heat management and thermal signal processing in quantum devices. For a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, we recover the absence of thermal amplification when system-reservoir interactions permit only single-quantum exchange. A controlled weak-nonlinearity expansion, supported by numerical stationary solutions, shows that two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification and predicts its onset. When two-quantum exchange dominates at the emitter and collector, varying the base temperature redistributes populations between even and odd oscillator sectors. This changes the emitter and collector heat currents far more than the base current, enabling large thermal amplification.
items.author: Laiba Hayat, M. Tahir Naseem

items.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
items.summary: Precise measurements of galaxy bias parameters are essential for extracting cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Field-level analyses infer bias coefficients at a finite cutoff $Λ$, typically related to the lattice resolution, while $n$-point function analyses typically adopt renormalization conditions defined in the low-$k$ limit. In this work, we use the renormalization group (RG) to relate field-level measurements at different cutoffs and connect them to $n$-point function measurements. We generate mock galaxy fields with a Lagrangian perturbation theory forward model and a galaxy bias expansion, and then measure the bias parameters across a range of cutoffs. We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $Λ\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_δ$ and second-order $b_{δ^2}, b_{{G}_2}$.
items.author: Hsiang-Ming Huang, Henrique Rubira, Fabian Schmidt

items.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
items.summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit.
items.author: Shauvik Biswas, Sayan Chakrabarti

items.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
items.summary: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths.
items.author: H. Amar, J. Álvarez, X. Arrue et al.

items.title: Dimensional Crossover and Correlated Spin Dynamics in the Chain-Like van der Waals Antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$
items.summary: We report a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of the chain-like van der Waals antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ using magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The magnetic susceptibility exhibits a broad maximum near 250 K, characteristic of strong short-range antiferromagnetic correlations in a low-dimensional system. A classical Fisher-chain analysis gives an effective intrachain exchange scale $J/k_B\approx 140$ K, while a quantum $S=3/2$ nearest-neighbor-chain calculation yields $J/k_B\approx 114$ K. A constrained AF-FM zig-zag-chain calculation is also compatible with the susceptibility, supporting a dominant quasi one dimensional antiferromagnetic exchange scale of order 100 K. $^{31}$P NMR measurements provide microscopic insight into both static and dynamic spin correlations.
items.author: C. S. Saramgi, Y. Shemerliuk, S. Selter et al.

items.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
items.summary: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations.
items.author: Amani Kiruga, Zhiyi Li, Ruojin Cai et al.

items.title: NASA to Welcome Expedition 74 Astronauts Home at Space Center Houston
items.summary: NASA will welcome home the Expedition 74 crew during a public event at Space Center Houston following their return from a long-duration mission aboard the International Space Station. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams; ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot; and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud‑Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev will share mission […]
items.author: Wendy K. Avedisian

items.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.summary: We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $π_{0.5}$. On the 50 tasks shared with 2025, its Q rises from 0.260 to 0.371; across all 100 tasks it scores 0.392.
items.author: Ilia Larchenko, Gleb Zarin, Atindra Nair et al.

items.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
items.summary: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers.
items.author: Izack Cohen, Dominik Kress, Lara Nehrke et al.

items.title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors. We analyze the linear-depth multiplexer and the noise-resilient bucket-brigade architectures, adapting the latter to a native superconducting gate set and refining its fidelity analysis using the fully decomposed gate schedule.
items.author: Joao F. Doriguello, Alessandro Luongo, Harshit Verma

items.title: SIGMO: Sigmoid Gated Interaction-Aware Motion Planning
items.summary: Despite the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicle technologies, reliable navigation within cluttered environments remains arduous due to the necessity of interaction-aware strategies; example scenarios include: narrow passages with multiple agents, lane changing in dense traffic, and crossing unsignalized intersections. These scenarios often require highly proactive strategies, simultaneously demanding interpretability and quick adaptability, which challenge end-to-end and data-driven methods. An effective strategy requires: scalability to multiple agents, adaptability to changes in other agents' behavior, and harmony with surrounding traffic without freezing or becoming overly conservative. To meet these requirements, we present SIGMO, a sigmoid-gated interaction-aware motion planner, with two main contributions.
items.author: Avinash Singh, Manish Saroya, Fatemeh Cheraghi Pouria et al.

items.title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes
items.summary: The theory of turbo iterative decoding was brought into the quantum coding framework through the development of quantum serial turbo codes and quantum block turbo codes. In this paper, we present a theory for multidimensional quantum block turbo codes, a turbo decoding technique for multi layer product codes. We describe its algorithm and simulate the performance for the 3D case on a depolarizing channel.
items.author: Khaled Jebari, Luiz Anet Neto, Ramesh Pyndiah et al.

items.title: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers
items.summary: Tavis--Cummings lattices couple cavities containing several emitters and host polaritonic many-body dynamics whose real-time correlations are costly to compute classically in two dimensions, especially when unequal emitter relaxation or dephasing rates break permutation symmetry. We analyze logical resources for fault-tolerant closed- and open-system simulation of an atom-resolved lattice with $L$ cavities, $N$ emitters per cavity, and photon cutoff $n\_{\max}$, including target observable estimation. Building on ladder-operator block encoding, we construct circuits for photon hopping and local light--matter exchange and combine them to encode the lattice Hamiltonian. By updating source and destination photon occupations in place, the hopping circuit eliminates the auxiliary $L\lceil\log_2(n\_{\max}+1)\rceil$-qubit photon register used by two-register implementations.
items.author: Soumya Sarkar, Rakshit Gharat, Nam Nguyen et al.

items.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
items.summary: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK.
items.author: Feiyu Li, Yang Liu, Zhen Yang et al.

items.title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
items.summary: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969. Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) still show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD.
items.author: Ondrej Chvala

items.title: M 5.2 - 21 km WNW of Popondetta, Papua New Guinea

About 2 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.

items.title: M 5.2 - Mid-Indian Ridge
items.summary: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake was recorded Mid-Indian Ridge. The event happened on 10 November 2026 at 17:36 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV
items.summary: Small, holonomic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) enable close-range inspection of underwater structures from arbitrary viewpoints, requiring accurate position and attitude tracking under state and input constraints. Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) naturally handles these requirements, but relies on an accurate dynamics model, which is difficult to obtain underwater. In this paper, we present a nonlinear MPCC in all six Degrees of Freedom (DoF) for a holonomic AUV and alleviate the inaccuracies in the dynamics by augmenting the nominal model employed with residual dynamics learned via Gaussian Process (GP) regression. The learned residual is embedded in the optimal control problem through a zero-order robust optimization scheme, which keeps the controller real-time capable at 25 Hz.
items.author: David Dörner, Giancarlo Troni, Ignacio Torroba et al.

items.title: The Higgs boson, naturalness, and the Universe
items.summary: The Higgs boson -- the only known fundamental scalar particle -- may have profound implications for both particle physics and cosmology. This review examines how the Higgs field may have influenced the Universe from its earliest moments to its present state. We first discuss particle-physics puzzles, including the naturalness and hierarchy problems, as well as the possible metastability of the electroweak vacuum. We then turn to cosmological scenarios where the Higgs boson could be a driving force, including Higgs inflation, reheating and the onset of the hot Big Bang, the electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis via electroweak processes.
items.author: Mikhail Shaposhnikov

items.title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models
items.summary: Pretrained video diffusion models (VDMs) offer a powerful foundation for World Action Models (WAMs), which jointly predict robot actions and future observations. Building such models requires injecting low-dimensional robot signals (e.g. proprioception, actions, and values) into a latent space shaped by natural videos, and a key design choice is the interface through which these signals enter: existing schemes treat it as a formatting detail, spending a separate latent frame on each signal or bolting on dedicated encoders and decoders. We argue that signal injection is instead a distribution-alignment problem: how well a representation matches the prior of the pretrained VDMs during denoising.
items.author: Guoqiang Liang, Yiqi Lin, Yanzhe Chen et al.

items.title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$
items.summary: We report direction-selective anomalous quantum transport in epitaxial YbSb$_{2}$ thin films associated with an interplay between anisotropic topological surface states and an electronic instability. Quantum oscillations reveal a quasi-two-dimensional orbit with a non-trivial Berry phase and Dirac-like dispersion, observable for current along the $a$-axis but absent along the orthogonal in-plane $c$-axis. Together with first-principles calculations, these observations support its assignment to a saddle-like topological surface state. Its oscillation amplitude exhibits a field-dependent, non-monotonic temperature evolution that departs from conventional Lifshitz-Kosevich behavior. Raman and coherent phonon spectroscopy reveal additional low-temperature modes consistent with a density-wave instability. Their pronounced polarization anisotropy and colossal field-induced Raman enhancement suggest a strongly anisotropic, field-enhanced electronic susceptibility associated with the density-wave modes.
items.author: Rudra Dhara, Pritesh Srivastava, Jack Tregidga et al.

items.title: Multiloop Unitarity from Airy Zeros
items.summary: Hidden zeros are non-trivial cancellations that make amplitudes or integrands vanish on specific kinematic loci away from propagator poles. They have been shown to uniquely determine tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands in $\Tr(φ^3)$ theory, without assuming factorization. Here we extend both the zeros and the uniqueness results to two, three and four loops at arbitrary multiplicity. We show that two types of zeros naturally enter the all-loop problem. First, tree-level zeros extend to all loop orders and fix relative weights within families of subgraphs attached to vacuum ``loop cores.'' We then show that Kontsevich's matrix Airy function can be used to generate a rich structure of loop level zeros that fix the relative weights of the loop cores themselves.
items.author: Laurentiu Rodina

items.title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
items.summary: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity.
items.author: Manuel Del Piano, Stefan Hohenegger, Francesco Sannino

items.title: Renormalization-group flow of nucleon--$Δ$ contact interactions with an explicit $Δ$: decoupling and the scale dependence of large-$N_c$ relations
items.summary: We study the leading-order (LO) contact interactions among nucleons and $Δ$ isobars under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp momentum cutoff, keeping the $Δ$ as an explicit coupled channel, and determine which large-$N_c$ relations among the couplings are invariant under the flow. The two-channel flow with the $ΔΔ$ threshold inside the cutoff range is solved exactly, and the closed channels decouple with relative corrections of order $Λ^2/κ_{ΔΔ}^2$, where $κ_{ΔΔ}=\sqrt{2M_Δ(M_Δ-M_N)}$ is the closed-channel momentum. Applying the $1/N_c$ expansion of the Hartree Hamiltonian to the $N$--$Δ$ system, we find that a generalized time reversal removes all corrections of relative order $1/N_c$, that the LO fixes eleven of the 18 S-wave couplings in terms of seven, and that the exact-SU(4) two-parameter form used in the literature differs from the LO by an operator of relative order $1/N_c^2$ with matrix elements of order one in the $Δ$ channels.
items.author: Dominador F. Vaso,, Daris Samart, Jingle B. Magallanes

items.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
items.summary: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families.
items.author: Tyler Gorda, Aleksi Kurkela, Tuhin Malik

items.title: Resolved $Q_1^q$-$Q_{7γ}$ interference in $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ at NLO: Hard matching and radiative charm-loop jet function for $m_c \to 0$
items.summary: We study next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the subleading-power resolved-photon contribution to $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ arising from the interference of the current-current operator $Q_1^q$ and the electromagnetic dipole operator $Q_{7γ}$. This contribution is among the main sources of theoretical uncertainty in Standard Model predictions for the decay rate. Using a factorisation theorem in soft-collinear effective theory for the kinematic endpoint region, $m_b-2E_γ=\mathcal{O}(Λ_{\rm QCD})$, we determine all previously unknown perturbative ingredients at NLO in the limit of a vanishing charm-quark mass, $m_c\to0$. Specifically, we compute the $m_c$-independent one-loop hard-matching coefficients, derive their renormalisation-group equations, and obtain accurate analytic approximations to their solutions by retaining the first two terms in a $1/N_c$ expansion.
items.author: Riccardo Bartocci, Philipp Böer, Kevin Brune et al.

items.title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
items.summary: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve.
items.author: Yuxuan Shi, Hao Wei

items.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
items.summary: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.
items.author: Lei Hou, Xiang Zhang, Qiang Zhu et al.

items.title: Nanostructuring Semiconductor Surfaces Using Self-Assembled Metal Nanoparticles for Optoelectronic Applications
items.summary: Semiconductor nanostructures are key light-management elements because their geometry can strengthen light-matter interaction, suppress reflection, and enhance optical coupling. Yet their adoption across material platforms is constrained by lithography, multistep pattern transfer, persistent masks, and material-specific etching. Here, we introduce a lithography-free two-step strategy in which thermally evaporated self-assembled Ga nanoparticles act as self-consuming masks during Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching. Correlated transmission electron microscopy on GaAs reveals the formation mechanism. Comparable erosion of the Ga nanoparticles and exposed substrate progressively converts Ga-capped pedestals into pure semiconductor nanocones while preserving crystalline order. Nanocone dimensions extend from tens to hundreds of nanometres, and surface coverage is tunable through Ga deposition and plasma power.
items.author: S. Catalán-Gomez, M. Ibáñez, P. Guo et al.

items.title: ForeseeDrive: Future-Token Conditioning for Anticipatory Generative Driving
items.summary: Generative driving planners can represent diverse ego futures, but a downstream scorer can choose only among sampled candidates; it cannot recover an absent maneuver. We present ForeseeDrive, which turns future scene evolution into a deployable interface for shaping candidate generation. Rather than reconstructing dense future states or scoring a fixed menu, ForeseeDrive derives query-indexed tokens from logged actor motion, occupancy evolution, route interactions, and TTC margins, and predicts the same token space from present context at deployment. The tokens condition trajectory geometry before candidates materialize. A zero-token-gated residual path and candidate-preservation loss limit unnecessary drift, while a TTC-margin guard targets brittle safe-to-unsafe boundary crossings.
items.author: Shaokai Wu, Xunchu Zhou, Pinzhi Wang et al.

items.title: Reducing Massive Scattering Amplitudes to Normal Form
items.summary: Local amplitude reduction is a crucial tool in effective field theory (EFT) calculations. While polynomial normal forms reproduce the massless y-basis, massive amplitudes require reduction rules that preserve little-group tensor contractions. We generalize Gröbner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities, determining leading monomials in their contraction contexts and generating the higher-degree rules induced by mass determinants. Using three-, four-, and five-point replacement catalogs, we demonstrate symbolic-mass amplitude reductions and reproduce the independent three- and four-vector operator bases, providing traceable normal-form reductions for local EFT matching and syzygy analysis.
items.author: Ming-Lei Xiao

items.title: Memory-gated transient anomalous transport of quasiparticles out of equilibrium
items.summary: Anomalous transport is ubiquitous across condensed matter, materials science, and biophysics. Yet, in far-from-equilibrium settings, what determines when, how much, and in which direction transport departs from diffusion remains a fundamental open question. By adopting the dispersive Holstein model of small polarons as representative of a wide class of dissipative systems, we show that a signed bath memory time governs the direction and the strength of the transient departure, and that when it vanishes, diffusion emerges without an asymptotic delay. Tuning the dissipative environment from resonant to off-resonant with the carrier density of states, transport turns from subdiffusion to superdiffusion as the memory time changes sign.
items.author: Pranay Venkatesh, Tianchu Li, Srijan Bhattacharyya et al.

items.title: The $χ_{c1}(3872)$ Multiplet in the Diabatic Dynamical Diquark Model
items.summary: We apply a minimal form of the diabatic dynamical diquark model, which uses only dimeson thresholds augmented by constraints obtained from heavy-quark spin symmetry, to the hidden-charm tetraquark spectrum. We find that this model is insufficient to simultaneously reproduce the experimentally established states \(χ_{c1}(3872)\), \(T_{c\bar c1}(3900)\), and \(T_{c\bar c1}(4020)\). We therefore extend the model to its complete form, by restoring the spin- and isospin-dependent diquark-antidiquark interactions from the original adiabatic dynamical diquark model into the full diabatic potential. Aligning the resulting framework to these three states allows the remaining members of the \(Σ_g^+(1S)\) multiplet to be predicted through coupled-channel scattering simulations.
items.author: Richard F. Lebed, Ethan H. Pham

items.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
items.summary: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy. […]

items.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
items.summary: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $ω_α$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $λ_α$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_α$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission.

items.title: Yang-Lee edge singularity at $\mathcal{O}(\partial^4)$ from the functional renormalization group: revised analysis
items.summary: We determine the critical exponents of the Yang-Lee edge singularity as continuous functions of dimension using the functional renormalization group, retaining all operators at second and fourth order in the derivative expansion. At fourth order, we obtain $η=-0.153(7)$, $-0.352(9)$ and $-0.575(9)$ in $d=5$, $4$ and $3$, respectively, in agreement with the six-loop $ε$ expansion. In three dimensions, these results give $σ=0.076$ and $ν_c=0.359$. We locate the zero of the edge exponent at $d_σ=2.65(1)$, also consistent with the six-loop estimate. Continuing the fixed point through $d_σ$, we obtain $η=-0.795(21)$ and $ω=1.90(6)$ in $d=2$, compared with the exact values $-4/5$ and $2$.
items.author: Konrad Kockler, Jan M. Pawlowski, Vladimir V. Skokov

items.title: Intracycle Interference in Strong-Field Photoemission from a Tungsten Needle Tip
items.summary: Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been observed. We present carrier-envelope phase-resolved photoemission spectra from a nanometric tungsten needle tip driven at 1570 nm revealing such interference, supported by quantum orbit and TDSE simulations that elucidate attosecond-scale electron dynamics.

items.summary: A magnitude 5.5 earthquake was recorded 40 km S of Puerto San José, Guatemala. The event happened on 10 November 2026 at 14:54 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 60 km. items.title: Universal Multichannel Coherence-Mediated Thermal Transport in Carbon Allotropes: Experimental Evidence and Scaling Laws
items.summary: Understanding thermal transport in structurally disordered carbon materials remains a fundamental challenge because conventional models based on a single coherence contribution cannot accurately describe heat conduction over a broad temperature range. In this work, the thermal conductivity of graphene oxide (GO), thermally reduced graphene oxide (trGO), GO-hydrated fullerene composites (GO-HyFn), expanded graphite (EG), and EG-multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) composites was measured between 4.5 and 300 K. Despite substantial differences in density, porosity, graphitic ordering, and microstructure, all materials exhibit glass-like temperature dependence of thermal conductivity. The experimental results demonstrate that the conventional two-channel model, comprising a Peierls contribution and a single thermally activated coherence term, systematically fails to reproduce the observed temperature dependence.
items.author: A. Jeżowski, A. I. Krivchikov, O. A. Korolyuk et al.

items.title: Exponential Control of Adiabatic Time Reflection by Complex-Time Singularities
items.summary: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. A perturbation bounded by $0.6\%$ of the total inverse-permittivity change raises the reflected mode amplitude from $8.02\times10^{-10}$ to $1.28\times10^{-3}$. The complex action and pole residue predict this amplitude to within $0.32\%$. Within this waveform family, deviation and monotonicity constraints select three design regimes. At fixed deviation bound, reoptimization keeps the central feature's time scale comparable to the inverse incident angular frequency.
items.author: Shiyue Deng, Qian Niu

items.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases
items.summary: Optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases is essential for attosecond science. Improving conversion efficiency from the infrared driving laser to the extreme-ultraviolet high-order harmonic radiation requires balancing microscopic single-atom dipole responses with macroscopic phase matching. The resulting conversion-efficiency landscape exhibits complex structures, such as the hyperbolic ridge in the pressure-length space, which can be difficult to accurately reconstruct using conventional Bayesian optimization. Here, we introduce a physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates known physical scaling relations through nonlinear transformations of the search space. We first demonstrate the approach in the two-dimensional pressure-length space, where a direct grid scan enables detailed validation of the reconstructed landscape, before extending it to four dimensions, where exhaustive scanning becomes computationally impractical.
items.author: Dominika Maslarova, Mattys Pouyez, Patrik Jansson et al.

items.title: SGAA: Independent active alignment of optical subgroups with uncompensated aberrations
items.summary: Uncompensated subgroup aberrations complicate subgroup-level active alignment (AA), as local image-quality extrema do not directly indicate the target alignment state. We propose SGAA, an image-learning-based method for independent active alignment of optical subgroups. Multi-field point spread functions (PSFs) from a dedicated test configuration characterize misalignment, while golden-sample reference calibration and unified regression predict adjustments toward a common optical target across toleranced specimens. In simulations with tolerances, one step reduced the mean differential wavefront RMS from $0.0592λ$ to $0.0086λ$, an 85.4% reduction. In alignment experiments on 100 production subgroups, SGAA increased the mean full-lens weighted modulation transfer function (WMTF) at 30, 50, and 80 lp/mm by 0.073, 0.065, and 0.040, respectively, relative to industrial MTF-based scanning.
items.author: Le Dai, Zhenyao Zheng, Wenyong Li et al.

items.title: PhagoCyt enables isolation of Salmonella -containing phagosomes and mapping of host and bacteria remodelling of the intracellular niche
items.summary: by Ritika Chatterjee, José Luis Marin-Rubio, Francesca Romana Cianfanelli, Andrew Michael Frey, Benjamin Bernard Armando Raymond, Abeer Dannoura, Camila Valenzuela, Meihan Meng, Tiaan Heunis, Mengchun Li, Frances Sidgwick, Jost Enninga, Andrew Filby, Matthias Trost Macrophages engulf pathogens into dynamic phagosomes, which many bacteria manipulate for survival. However, isolating pure pathogen-containing phagosomes remains challenging. Here, we developed a novel flow cytometry-based isolation and ultrasensitive proteomics approach to analyse phagosomal and bacterial proteomes from macrophages infected with wild-type (WT) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (STM) or a ΔphoP mutant at 30 min and 4 hours post-infection. Our approach provides higher throughput, requires lower cell numbers and quantifies more proteins than previous techniques.
items.author: Ritika Chatterjee, José Luis Marin-Rubio, Francesca Romana Cianfanelli et al.

items.title: Vertebrate paired fins are specified by an ancient dorso-ventral patterning system
items.summary: by Rebecca E. Dale, Silke Berger, Sara Alaei, Marcus C. Davis, Frank J. Tulenko, Peter D. Currie The origin of paired fins was a major event in early vertebrate history that fueled the adaptive radiation of the gnathostome clade. Evidence for the conservation of ancient regulatory systems between paired and median fins supports a model in which appendage-patterning mechanisms first evolved in the midline and were later redeployed to a new embryonic context, the flank. However, while paired fins and limbs are asymmetric along the dorsoventral (DV) axis, the equivalent axis does not exist in median fins, which are symmetric across the midline, raising questions of how DV patterning evolved.
items.author: Rebecca E. Dale, Silke Berger, Sara Alaei et al.

items.title: Beyond unseen entities: Auditable cold-start evaluation for drug interaction prediction
items.summary: by Xiaoqing Ru, Yansu Wang, Quan Zou, Mengting Niu Reliable generalization is essential for deploying drug–drug interaction (DDI) and drug–target interaction (DTI) models in drug discovery, pharmacovigilance, and clinical decision support. However, strong performance on random splits or weakly constrained evaluations may not reflect how well a model generalizes to new drugs, targets, or deployment conditions. In pairwise prediction, test instances may still resemble training examples in molecular structure, sequence, or network context. Such overlap can inflate performance estimates and make interpolation appear to be extrapolation. In this Perspective, we argue that cold-start evaluation should be treated as an auditable deployment claim.
items.author: Xiaoqing Ru, Yansu Wang, Quan Zou et al.

items.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data
items.summary: by Emma E. Goldberg, Michael D. Kupperman, Ruian Ke The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid population growth.
items.author: Emma E. Goldberg, Michael D. Kupperman, Ruian Ke

items.title: Paralogous guanine deaminases acquired from bacteria by horizontal gene transfer promote purine homeostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.summary: by Sushila Bhattacharya, Lisa Fischer, Evrim Fer, Jennifer Snoozy, Grace N. Hagedorn, Marco Herde, Betül Kaçar, Claus-Peter Witte, Kurt Warnhoff Disruptions in purine metabolism contribute to a range of human diseases, from rare genetic disorders such as Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and xanthinuria to common conditions including gout and cancer. To better understand the metabolic networks that regulate purine homeostasis, we developed a Caenorhabditis elegans model of xanthine dehydrogenase ( xdh-1 ) deficiency. Remarkably, xdh-1 mutant animals form rare xanthine stones, recapitulating a hallmark of human xanthinuria. To uncover genetic regulators of purine homeostasis, we performed a forward genetic screen for mutations that exacerbate xanthine stone formation in xdh-1 mutants.
items.author: Sushila Bhattacharya, Lisa Fischer, Evrim Fer et al.

items.title: Modulation of Fe 3+ homeostasis by African Swine Fever virus facilitates its efficient replication in Ornithodoros lahorensis and pigs
items.summary: by Hua-Lin Sun, Ying Liu, Rong-Zeng Hao, Zi-Min Zhao, Ji-Fei Yang, Xin-Ting Lan, Zhan-Cheng Tian, Bell-Sakyi Lesley, Gui-Quan Guan, Hong Yin, Qing-Li Niu African swine fever virus (ASFV) can be transmitted through direct contact and, in specific ecological settings, by Ornithodoros spp . soft ticks. However, the cellular mechanisms that support ASFV replication in both porcine host and tick vector remain poorly understood. Iron is essential for cellular metabolism and viral replication, but excessive labile iron can induce oxidative stress and ferroptosis-like morphological changes in mitochondria. Whether and how ASFV exploits intracellular Fe 3+ homeostasis to sustain its replication has not been fully defined.
items.author: Hua-Lin Sun, Ying Liu, Rong-Zeng Hao et al.

items.title: Heterogeneous transfusion risk linked to variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in a non-human primate model
items.summary: by Jessica Rontard, Jacqueline Mikol, Florian Almela, Daisy Bougard, Christelle Jas-Duval, Olivier Andreoletti, Jérôme Delmotte, Mohammed-Amin Madoui, Jean-Philippe Deslys, Emmanuel E. Comoy Among the 178 cases of variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (v-CJD) in the UK, three were reported between 2003 and 2007 to be linked to a probable transmission through blood transfusion. With no further primary or iatrogenic cases observed worldwide since 2016, several countries are lifting – or have already lifted - deferrals for blood donors who have lived in the UK or, more broadly, Europe, to reduce the threat of supply shortages. However, the high prevalence of silent infection according to abnormal PrP in lymphoid tissues (potentially 100 times higher than for clinical cases in the UK) remains a concern in assessing the potential iatrogenic risk associated with long-term silent carriers for a disease whose incubation periods can extend over decades.
items.author: Jessica Rontard, Jacqueline Mikol, Florian Almela et al.

items.title: County-level spatial heterogeneity and environmental correlates of human echinococcosis in Xizang, China
items.summary: by Jiajia Ai, Lamu Ciren, Quzhen Gongsang, Lamu Suolang, Xiaoyao Ji, Jiakun Wang, Yangjin Baima, Zhaohui Luo, Zhuoma Bianba Background Human echinococcosis remains a major zoonosis in Xizang, China, where marked climatic, topographic and landscape gradients may be associated with spatial variation in disease prevalence. We investigated county-level spatial patterns of overall human echinococcosis, cystic echinococcosis (CE) and alveolar echinococcosis (AE), and their environmental associations. Methods Surveillance data from 74 counties during 2019–2023 were analysed. Because usable surveillance data were unavailable for 32 counties in 2022, that year was excluded from the spatial and generalized additive mixed model (GAMM) analyses.
items.author: Jiajia Ai, Lamu Ciren, Quzhen Gongsang et al.

items.title: Effectiveness of a participatory educational intervention on menstrual health and hygiene knowledge, attitudes, and practices among nursing and midwifery students in Bangladesh
items.summary: by Md Nahid Uz Zaman, Akira Sai, Taro Yamauchi Background Menstrual Health and Hygiene (MHH) is fundamental to women’s well-being but remains underprioritized in professional health education. In Bangladesh, nursing and midwifery students, future frontline health workers, rarely receive structured menstrual health curricula. This study assessed the effectiveness of a Participatory Educational (PE) intervention in improving menstrual Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) among nursing students. Methods A quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test study was conducted among 384 female nursing and midwifery students in Rajshahi, Bangladesh, with 192 students each in the intervention and control groups. The four-week PE intervention, adapted from WaterAid’s Menstrual Hygiene Matters guide, covered menstrual physiology, hygiene practices, stigma reduction, and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) management.
items.author: Md Nahid Uz Zaman, Akira Sai, Taro Yamauchi

items.title: Psychosocial influences on hypertension in Southeastern Nigeria: A mixed-methods study protocol
items.summary: by Awele Rosemary Ebigwei Omeda, Marcus Chilaka, Masoud Mohammadnezhad, Eleftheria Vaportzis Introduction The Southeastern region of Nigeria faces a severe public health challenge from hypertension due to its high prevalence. Psychosocial factors including perceived stress, anxiety, depression, coping mechanisms, and social support play essential roles in hypertension development and health behaviour, yet there has been limited scholarly attention to these determinants in Nigerian and international qualitative research. This study addresses this evidence gap by investigating the psychosocial determinants of hypertension-related health behaviour outcomes in adults living in Southeastern Nigeria. Materials and methods The sequential explanatory mixed methods study includes validated psychometric instruments assessing perceived stress, anxiety, depression, coping mechanisms, and social support.
items.author: Awele Rosemary Ebigwei Omeda, Marcus Chilaka, Masoud Mohammadnezhad et al.

items.title: MFMNet: Adaptive tri-layer graph pyramid with cross-scale attention router for synergistic drug prediction
items.summary: by Lei Wang, Liping Sun, Jingwen Pan, Guangming Shao, Guokun Shi, Guanyu Zhang, Yucheng Shi, Li Jin Background and objective Experimental screening of synergistic anticancer drug pairs is time-consuming, while effectively integrating complementary molecular graph representations with cell-line-specific information remains challenging for computational drug-synergy prediction. Methods We developed MFMNet with a Tri-Layer Graph Pyramid (TGP) comprising GCN, GIN, and GAT branches for extracting complementary molecular graph representations. A Cross-Scale Attention Router (CSAR), implemented as an adaptive feature-wise gating mechanism, integrates the graph representations before they are combined with drug embeddings and cell-line transcriptomic features for synergistic drug-pair prediction. Results In the initial five-fold cross-validation analysis, MFMNet achieved a mean five-fold AUROC of 0.9301 ± 0.0036.
items.author: Lei Wang, Liping Sun, Jingwen Pan et al.

items.title: Study protocol for a non-randomized trial of community participation support for people with Acquired Brain Injury who have ceased driving in Japan
items.summary: by Satonori Nasu, Yu Ishibashi, Tsutomu Sasaki, Ryuji Kobayashi Introduction Driving cessation after acquired brain injury (ABI) represents a major life transition that can restrict community participation and negatively affect quality of life. Although many individuals are unable to resume driving after illness or injury, structured support programs addressing life after driving cessation remain limited, and prospective evaluations are scarce. This study protocol describes a theoretically grounded community life support program for individuals with ABI who have ceased driving. Methods This is a single-center, non-randomized controlled trial with ward-level cluster allocation conducted in a convalescent rehabilitation hospital in Japan. Participants with ABI who were determined to be unable to resume driving will be allocated at the ward level to either an intervention group receiving the Community Life Support Program for Individuals with Acquired Brain Injury after Driving Cessation (CLASP-AID) or a control group receiving usual care.
items.author: Satonori Nasu, Yu Ishibashi, Tsutomu Sasaki et al.

items.title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid
items.summary: by Zun Wang, Chen Yang, Wencai Wang, Zijian Zhang, Zhonghua Sun, Zhiyong Diao Background Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear. Methods We integrated network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, virtual gene perturbation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, external transcriptomic validation, and qRT-PCR to investigate candidate molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid. Results A total of 127 shared candidate targets between pyrethroid insecticides and keloid were identified, mainly enriched in MAPK, PI3K–Akt, and FoxO signaling pathways. Three machine-learning algorithms prioritized VCAM1 and FGFR1.
items.author: Zun Wang, Chen Yang, Wencai Wang et al.

items.title: Multi-modal multi-task internet sentiment recognition model based on mid-to-back fusion strategy
items.summary: by Sichen Wu, Ruina Lin Previous studies of multimodal sentiment recognition have paid limited attention to the discrepancy between unimodal expression and multimodal perception in sentiment labeling, and to the question of where in the network the modalities should be fused. This paper proposes a multimodal multi-task sentiment recognition model based on a mid-to-back fusion strategy. Text, audio and visual inputs are encoded with the pre-trained BERT, Wav2Vec 2.0 and CLIP models, respectively, and refined by convolutional, recurrent and self-attention layers. Each unimodal branch is trained with its own unimodal sentiment label, so that modality-specific representations are optimized before fusion; the three high-level unimodal representations are then integrated by a residual multi-head self-attention module supervised by the multimodal label, and the four tasks are optimized jointly.
items.author: Sichen Wu, Ruina Lin

items.title: Glycyrrhizinic Acid and Isatidis folium extracts combined with Bacillus subtilis protect against dextran sulfate sodi-um-induced colitis in Hu sheep
items.summary: by Dianzhong Zheng, Xiao Fu, Manyu Li, Yufeng Liu, Di Liu Weaning stress caused by maternal separation and dietary changes often leads to intestinal disorders such as diarrhea and enteritis in young animals, and the development of antibiotic-free, safe preparations to manage these conditions is therefore a promising strategy. The optimal proportion of each component in the formulation was determined in our preliminary study using orthogonal experimental design and range analysis. This study first evaluated the effects of glycyrrhizic acid and Isatidis folium extract on the growth of Bacillus subtilis ( B. subtilis ), and then examined the effects of the compound preparation (CP) composed of glycyrrhizic acid, Isatidis folium extract, and B.
items.author: Dianzhong Zheng, Xiao Fu, Manyu Li et al.

items.title: Associations of palmar surface lactic acid with hand scaling and in vitro pathogen inactivation: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Kenichi Nagano, Kenji Manabe, Ichiro Mori, Yasuhiro Okada, Eri Shimizu, Satoru Naito The relationship between palmar surface lactic acid and hand scaling is not well understood. This cross-sectional study examined associations between palmar surface lactic acid, hand scaling, and in vitro anti-pathogenic activity, to generate hypotheses relevant to hand skin condition and pathogen inactivation. In 49 healthy adults, after standardized hand washing and acclimation (20°C, 40% RH), we assessed scaling (visual score), surface lactic acid and stratum corneum ceramides (LC–MS), stratum corneum amino acids (ion-exchange chromatography), skin pH and temperature, and sweat rate. Anti-pathogenic activity of palmar extracts was quantified as log 10 reduction against influenza A/H3N2, Escherichia coli NBRC3301, and Staphylococcus aureus NBRC13276.
items.author: Kenichi Nagano, Kenji Manabe, Ichiro Mori et al.
