items.title: Comparative assessment of ensemble and machine learning models for susceptibility mapping of 2024 Wushi earthquake-triggered landslides
items.summary: by Yutong Wu, Junpeng Huang, Wenqian Li, Xiangfeng Jia, Yaning Li, Zhiyi Wang Coseismic landslide susceptibility mapping plays a critical role in disaster risk mitigation, infrastructure protection, and territorial spatial planning, particularly in tectonically active mountain belts such as the Tianshan Mountains. Conventional machine learning models often suffer from overfitting and inadequate generalization capability due to their homogeneous structures and inflexible modeling strategies. In this study, targeting the coseismic landslides triggered by the 2024 Ms 7.1 Wushi earthquake in the Biedieli River basin, a landslide inventory comprising 904 events was compiled and randomly partitioned into training (70%) and validation (30%) datasets.
items.author: Yutong Wu, Junpeng Huang, Wenqian Li et al.

items.title: Perceived occupational physical fitness priorities and a preliminary conceptual framework for information technology students at selected vocational colleges in Shanxi Province, China: An exploratory cross-sectional mixed-methods study
items.summary: by Xiaobin Jin, Xiaoying Cui, Yi Zhao, Yu Hou Students majoring in information technology are frequently exposed to prolonged sitting, continuous screen use, sustained static postures, repetitive fine motor operations, and high cognitive load during their academic training and future work. These conditions may increase the risk of visual fatigue, neck and lower-back discomfort, physical fatigue, and psychological stress. This study adopted an exploratory cross-sectional mixed-methods design, using questionnaire surveys as the primary method and semi-structured interviews as a supplementary method. Participants included information technology students from selected vocational colleges, teachers whose teaching or research activities were related to vocational education or information technology student training, and personnel from information technology-related enterprises in Shanxi Province, China.
items.author: Xiaobin Jin, Xiaoying Cui, Yi Zhao et al.

items.title: A unified progressive fusion network with adaptive degradation prompts for multi-weather thermal infrared image restoration
items.summary: by Yinxuan Xia, Shaoshuo Mu Thermal infrared (TIR) image restoration aims to recover clearer and more informative images from inputs degraded by unfavorable weather conditions. Current TIR restoration approaches, however, mainly focus on individual degradation categories, such as rain, snow, or haze, which limits their ability to address different weather degradation categories within a unified framework. To address this challenge, we introduce a TIR unified prompt-guided fusion network, an adaptive degradation-prompting framework designed for unified TIR image restoration under individually occurring rain, snow, or haze degradations. A weather-adaptive dynamic prompt module is first constructed, where a lightweight degradation predictor estimates the probability distribution over predefined degradation categories in TIR images and produces dynamic degradation prompts from a learnable prompt bank.
items.author: Yinxuan Xia, Shaoshuo Mu

items.title: N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia
items.summary: by Cong Zhao, Jie Liu, Chao Tong, Chunyan Chen, Yalan Liu, Yan Chen, Lin Wang, Hua Peng Background Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a prevalent chronic lung disease in preterm infants, characterized by arrested alveolarization. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and receptor signaling are critical for alveolarization and are strictly regulated by protein N-glycosylation. However, the specific role of the vital post-translational modification in BPD pathogenesis remains unexplored. The present research aims to delineate a N-glycoproteomic landscape and elucidate the glycosylation-associated pathogenic mechanisms in a murine BPD model. Methods To establish BPD models, newborn mice were exposed to continuous hyperoxia (85% O 2 ) for 14 days.
items.author: Cong Zhao, Jie Liu, Chao Tong et al.

items.title: Laboratory-based assessment of quantitative PCR to describe Arctic fish assemblages in surface water affected by acid rock drainage
items.summary: by Laura C. Scott, Andrew M. Ramey, Ann E. Riddle-Berntsen, Brett A. Poulin, Joshua C. Koch, Jonathan A. O’Donnell, Michael P. Carey Permafrost thaw has been identified as a cause of metal mobilization from acid rock drainage and transport to Arctic rivers. Elevated metal concentrations and precipitation of Fe(III) minerals (i.e., rusting) in surface waters deteriorates water quality and raises questions about ecosystem effects, especially to the health of fish species. Environmental DNA (eDNA) analyses could be used for assessing impacts of acid rock drainage to fish assemblages but may be prone to biases like polymerase chain reaction (PCR) inhibition.
items.author: Laura C. Scott, Andrew M. Ramey, Ann E. Riddle-Berntsen et al.

items.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of extrarenal manifestations in patients with lupus nephritis: A retrospective cohort study
items.summary: by Young-Eun Kim, Soo Min Ahn, Ji Seon Oh, Yong‑Gil Kim, Chang‑Keun Lee, Bin Yoo, Seokchan Hong Objectives To evaluate the prevalence and prognostic implications of extrarenal involvement in lupus nephritis (LN), with emphasis on treatment response and the risk of future renal and extrarenal flares. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients newly diagnosed with LN between January 2006 and December 2022 and categorized them according to the presence of extrarenal involvement at diagnosis. Renal response and remission at 12 months, defined according to the Definition of Remission in SLE (DORIS), as well as the incidence of renal and extrarenal flares during follow-up, were compared between groups.
items.author: Young-Eun Kim, Soo Min Ahn, Ji Seon Oh et al.

items.title: Age-specific Epstein-Barr virus seroprevalence in Costa Rica
items.summary: by Sabrina Acosta-Egea, Elexandra Barboza Arguedas, Eva Villalobos Chacón, Romain Fantin, Carolina Porras, Viviana Loria, Juan Carlos Venegas, Connie M. Weston, Sarah S. Jackson, Arturo Abdelnour, Amada Aparicio, Alejandro Calderón, Daniela Mora, Rebeca Ocampo, Roy Wong-McClure, Melvin Morera, Roberto Castro, Henry H. Balfour, Jr, Rolando Herrero, Allan Hildesheim Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) is a common herpesvirus linked to cancers and autoimmune diseases. The age, socioeconomic status and geographic distribution of EBV infection are varied. This study evaluated age-specific EBV antibody prevalence in Costa Rica among 2,990 participants in a population-based cohort that enrolled in 2020/1. Seropositivity prevalence was age-dependent, with rates over 80% in adolescents, and higher than 90% in adults 20 + .
items.author: Sabrina Acosta-Egea, Elexandra Barboza Arguedas, Eva Villalobos Chacón et al.

items.title: Time-dependent efficacy of seven pharmacological regimens for ulcer healing and delayed bleeding prevention after gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection: A frequentist network meta-analysis
items.summary: by Linqiang Li, Xiaowei Zhu, Hengda Hu Background Gastric ESD induces large mucosal defects with potential delayed complications, including bleeding and perforation. The comparative efficacy of pharmacological regimens—PPI, P-CAB, H2RA, MP, and their combinations—remains unclear. Methods We conducted a frequentist network meta-analysis of 31 randomized controlled trials evaluating seven pharmacological strategies for post-ESD ulcer healing and delayed bleeding prevention. Outcomes were assessed at 4 and 8 weeks for mucosal healing and ulcer reduction, and across the treatment course for delayed bleeding/perforation. Odds ratios (ORs), mean differences (MDs), and P-scores were calculated. Heterogeneity, inconsistency, sensitivity, and publication bias were assessed. Transitivity was evaluated qualitatively, and certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE framework.
items.author: Linqiang Li, Xiaowei Zhu, Hengda Hu

items.title: Effects of crude oil on the somatic and immune development of juvenile threespine stickleback
items.summary: by Kelly S. Ireland, Kathryn CA. Milligan-McClellan Aquatic oil spills have profound effects on surrounding ecosystems, prompting significant investments in oil spill response efforts to remove oil from the environment as quickly as possible. Oil has immunotoxic effects and may be particularly harmful to larval and juvenile fish as it can cause a number of developmental defects and stunted growth. In spite of significant efforts to clean up oil, it is unclear whether larval and juvenile fish can recover from the effects of oil, and no work has been published on the effect crude oil has on developing threespine stickleback ( Gasterosteus aculeatus ) fish.
items.author: Kelly S. Ireland, Kathryn CA. Milligan-McClellan

items.title: A PPE detection method based on the advanced YOLOv11 architecture with a lightweight refinement block system
items.summary: by Alibek Barlybayev, Nurzada Amangeldy, Bijeesh Kozhikkodan Veettil, Bekbolat Kurmetbek, Akmaral Kassymova, Ramazan Sadvakassov Automated monitoring of personal protective equipment usage is crucial due to the high incidence of accidents in the construction industry, with over half attributed to the improper use of protective equipment. Existing deep learning models show limited performance in detecting small-scale objects and reduced accuracy under challenging visual conditions. To address these limitations, this study introduces YOLOv11s-R 3 , an enhanced version of the YOLOv11s architecture with a P2-focused refinement block. The proposed model extends the standard feature pyramid network to stride-4 resolution and applies a single lightweight C2f block on the P2 feature map, targeting fine-scale objects.
items.author: Alibek Barlybayev, Nurzada Amangeldy, Bijeesh Kozhikkodan Veettil et al.

items.title: Acute doses of 3 and 6 mg/kg caffeine produce outcome- and phase-specific improvements in male 100-m sprinters: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial
items.summary: by Tao Mei, Jianing Li, Xiangang Yang Evidence is limited on whether commonly used caffeine doses provide uniform benefits across sprint phases and performance outcomes in trained sprinters. We compared the acute effects of 3 and 6 mg/kg caffeine in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-condition crossover trial. Twenty-one male 100-m sprinters completed placebo, 3 mg/kg caffeine, and 6 mg/kg caffeine trials separated by at least 7 days. Sixty minutes after ingestion, participants completed two maximal 60-m sprints, followed by countermovement jump, squat jump, and 10-s Wingate tests. Sprint times, derived split times, start reaction time, starting-block rate of force development, stride variables, and perceived exertion were also assessed.

items.title: Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moiré rhombohedral graphene
items.summary: An anomalous Hall crystal (AHC) is a quantum state of matter, in which spontaneous electron crystallization leads to a quantized Hall effect without a magnetic field. The state can emerge in materials with strong Coulomb interaction and large Berry curvatures, such as few-layer rhombohedral graphene. Although the idea of AHCs has been invoked to explain some of the observed Chern insulators in moiré rhombohedral graphene (mRG), direct experimental evidence of AHCs has been missing so far. Here, we report experimental evidence of AHCs in hole-doped mRG through combined electrical transport and noise measurements. We identify a series of distinct Chern insulators spanning a broad and continuous range of doping densities incommensurate with the underlying moiré lattice; the states exhibit current-induced broadband noise and memory effects as well as pronounced gate hysteresis.
items.author: Hongyuan Li, Zuhan Geng, Annika Weber et al.

items.title: Generalizing Causal Decision-Making: Markov Equivalence, Transportability and Counterfactuals
items.summary: Structural causal bandits use causal knowledge to guide exploration when reward mechanisms are unknown. This paper extends the approach to partially known causal structure, information from other environments, and realizable counterfactual actions. First, we develop graphical criteria for minimal intervention sets under Markov equivalence and characterize possibly-optimal minimal intervention sets for maximal ancestral graphs. A search algorithm finds sets that are possibly optimal in at least one graph represented by a partial ancestral graph. Second, we derive target reward bounds from source distributions through partial transportability, accounting for non-manipulable variables. Dominance relations provide further bounds for action pruning and restricted exploration, with a regret guarantee under valid prior bounds.
items.author: Min Woo Park, Sanghack Lee

items.title: A human-in-the-loop Control Paradigm for Construction Robotics: From VR-Guided Teleoperation to Semi-Autonomous Dual-Arm Operation
items.summary: Construction tasks in hazardous and unstructured environments require both human adaptability and robotic precision, yet existing approaches often treat teleoperation and autonomy as separate control modes. This paper presents a human-in-the-loop control paradigm that enables structured transitions among VR-guided teleoperation, semi-autonomous shared control, and rule-based autonomous execution for contact-rich dual-arm construction tasks. The proposed system combines immersive VR guidance, a manually defined library of reusable skill primitives, and a shared-autonomy framework with explicit human-robot role allocation and command-priority rules. This integration allows operators to retain supervisory and corrective authority while delegating repetitive and precision-critical actions to the robot. The paradigm is validated on a dual-arm platform through representative facade-installation tasks.
items.author: Jinhua Chen, Xiaoji Xu, Zhongyuan Liao et al.

items.title: Where Do Vision-Language Models Get Left and Right? Position-Code Counterfactuals in Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3
items.summary: A vision-language model may take left-right direction from the orientation of image content within patches, its vision transformer's (ViT) position code, or token positions and order in its language model (LLM). Ablations show the ViT code is necessary; we test sufficiency by mirroring only a position code. In Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-4B and InternVL3-2B, mirroring ViT width positions reproduces the flipped-image answer on 84.3-93.2% of CV-Bench left-right questions (Qwen2.5-VL-3B: 87.5%, partly a left fallback). With two options, this also counts disruption; a half-grid shift flips most answers too. With the ViT code intact, LLM-side id and token-order mirrors change few left-right answers in all three series (a weak id test in Qwen2.5-VL).
items.author: Enhao Cui, Junzhi Yang, Yaoshun Lin et al.

items.title: HandsOnAid: Building and Evaluating an Offline First-Aid Assistant for Emergency Response Scenarios
items.summary: Emergencies can occur where there is no phone signal and no ambulance nearby. A small language model on a phone can be helpful in such situations, but its advice needs to be safe and accurate. We built HandsOnAid, a 4-bit Gemma 2B model fine-tuned with QLoRA on FirstAidQA dataset, a corpus of 5,550 first-aid question-answer pairs. We compared seven configurations, including the base, 4-bit and 8-bit fine-tuned models, and versions with a length floor, safety gate, or retrieval. We used a 41-pair question-answer bank with medically reviewed references that followed ANZCOR guidelines, and a strict 0-5 score rubric, with twelve safety overrides.
items.author: Rezwan Islam Salvi, Saiyma Sittul Muna, Mushfiqur Rahman Mushfique

items.title: RedirectMimic: Local Motion Content Redaction for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
items.summary: Humanoid motion interfaces should accommodate application-specific movement constraints while retaining useful reference behavior. Local content redaction requires a controller to replace selected movements even when it continues to receive the original reference. Removing the tracking incentive for those movements leaves their replacement unspecified. We introduce RedirectMimic, which separates the reference observed by the actor from the target used to train its execution. A rule-generated edited reference guides tracking rewards during proximal policy optimization, while the deployed observation and action interfaces remain unchanged. We evaluate pose- and speed-defined arm editing in Unitree G1 simulation using a tracker pretrained on 7,509 motion clips.
items.author: Zepeng Wang, Xiaochuan Shi

items.title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning
items.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. Existing WAMs, encompassing both video-first action prediction and joint video-action modeling, directly transfer global physical representations from world models to action generation. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. Specifically, LaST0.5 learns a compact interaction-centric latent space under the supervision of visual interaction cues between the robot and the environment.
items.author: Xuheng Zhang, Yiming Zhang, Jialin Gao et al.

items.title: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training
items.summary: Adversarial training is often plagued by "pseudo-attacks", perturbations that significantly increase the loss value but fail to truly alter the model's confidence structure. To address this, we propose two complementary approaches to directly attack and defend against confidence structure deformation. First, building upon the traditional loss maximization perspective, we introduce a hybrid objective that integrates cross-entropy and KL divergence, encouraging adversarial examples to simultaneously disrupt prediction accuracy and distribution consistency. Second, we geometrically reconstruct adversarial training by generating perturbations that maximize the distribution distance on the confidence manifold. Theoretical analysis shows that the optimal perturbation direction aligns with the principal eigenvectors of the Fisher information matrix.
items.author: Chenlong Wei, Hanling Wang, Chong Zhang et al.

items.title: CV-TF-QKD
items.summary: We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. At fixed weak input-referred excess noise per arm, both rates per relay use scale as $\sqrtη$, where $η$ is the end-to-end transmissivity. For phase disclosure, we establish composable security against general coherent attacks using a bounded test of preparation intensities and sign-parity complementarity. For specified apparatus parameters, finite-key calculations incorporating detector inefficiency, dark counts, phase fluctuations, and reference overhead predict rates exceeding the pure-loss and matched thermal-loss repeaterless bounds.
items.author: Stefano Pirandola

items.title: ScaleBrain: A Scale-Consistent Framework for EEG Foundation Models
items.summary: Foundation models pre-trained on large unlabeled electroencephalography (EEG) corpora have emerged as a transformative paradigm for Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications. Recent EEG foundation models have shown that multi-scale representations derived from fixed-length patches can improve EEG representation learning. Existing frameworks commonly construct temporal scales through feature-level operations. However, these operations leave the correspondence between learned features and scale-specific characteristics of the original EEG signals implicit. Moreover, when the self-supervised objective is not aligned with the multi-scale input representations, information at some temporal scales may receive insufficient supervision during pre-training. In light of this, we propose ScaleBrain, a scale-consistent pre-training framework that explicitly coordinates multi-scale representations of EEG from both the model input and optimization objective sides.
items.author: Minyu Zhou, Yajing Wu, Yongqiang Tang et al.

items.title: HiPFuse: Real-Time LiDAR Semantic Segmentation for Robotic Perception on Edge Devices
items.summary: Real-time robotic perception requires accurate LiDAR semantics under limited resources. Bird's-eye-view (BEV) aggregation is efficient but can mix differently labeled surfaces in columns. We present HiPFuse, a point-BEV fusion framework that exchanges point and height-partitioned BEV features across horizontal scales, combining point-wise detail with 2D spatial context from one LiDAR scan. Fixed height assignments preserve separate vertical aggregation groups, with auxiliary supervision of initial BEV features using targets from the same 3D cells. A dual-scale BEV context module adds broader context from a coarser grid. On SemanticKITTI and MCD, HiPFuse achieves 63.7% and 62.5% mIoU at 14.2 and 22.4 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin, respectively, exceeding the 10 Hz scan rate.
items.author: Haiyang Wu, George Vosselman, Ville Lehtola

items.title: Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: In reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, a language model is rewarded for a correct final answer, and GRPO passes that reward to every token of the solution in equal measure. We instead place the credit where the model hesitated, in a method we call MCPO (Margin-Credit Policy Optimization). We measure hesitation by the top-2 margin $M=p_1-p_2$ of the policy's next-token distribution, map it to a score with two fixed thresholds, and spread each solution's advantage over its tokens so that the mean stays unchanged. The margin is read from a forward pass the trainer already performs, so the method needs no extra model evaluation and no batch statistics.
items.author: Chi Liu, Xin Chen, Yuchuan Weng et al.

items.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Language-model agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks whose interaction histories exceed the model's active context. They must therefore decide what to write down and what to read back, and when to do either. Recent work has begun to use on-policy distillation (OPD) to make memory control part of the policy, relying on memory tools and compaction protocols that lie outside either model's pre-training. However, this weakens the distillation on both sides: the teacher cannot give useful guidance on an interface it has never used, and the student samples too few meaningful memory actions for that guidance to take effect. To study this problem, we introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym II (CAMG-II), a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shop, Coding, AutoResearch, General, and Visual.
items.author: Lirui Luo, Kelong Mao, Xinwei Yang et al.

items.title: Normalizing Flows for Classical Simulation of Quantum Circuits in Phase Space
items.summary: We present a novel framework to learn a representation of quantum circuits based on the phase space formulation of many-body systems. Given that $N$-qubit states can be represented as probability distributions on a smooth $2N$-dimensional manifold, we show how unitary gates can be parameterized as normalizing flows between these distributions, opening a new avenue for quantum circuit simulation using generative models. We evaluate our method on three common families of quantum circuits, and show that its accuracy exceeds that of current state-of-the-art neural network methods for large system sizes.
items.author: Edward Jiang, Timothy Heightman, Marcin Płodzień

items.title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
items.summary: Robotic additive manufacturing requires joint paths that reconcile robot feasibility with process-specific geometry. We develop an offline optimization-based path planner that combines joint-path regularity and self-collision penalties with process costs and constraints, so that a new process enters through its own reference, residuals, and tolerances. Full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization handle references of different lengths. Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) determines the cost weights from the gaps between Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their targets. In carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing, the planned paths meet the geometric tolerances and all KPI targets, and both paths are executed on a UR10e, without extrusion for printing, with joint-level tracking recorded during execution.
items.author: Shiva Ganesh Murali, Valentin Bhend, Deepak Ingole et al.

items.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
items.summary: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions.
items.author: Niran Nataraj, Maina Sogabe, Masamichi Yamashita et al.

items.title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
items.summary: Minimally invasive brain implants require compact deployment geometries and controlled shape transformation for delivery through confined vessels. Origami-inspired structures enable large shape changes from compact to tailored deployed configurations, but implementation at microscale dimensions remains challenging, as conventional designs rely on predefined mountain and valley folds that become increasingly difficult to fabricate and assemble as unit-cell size is reduced to meet clinical requirements. To address this, we propose a self-folding methodology based on thermally induced stresses in thin-film bimetallic composites. Pairing the shape memory alloy Nitinol (NiTi) with molybdenum or stainless steel (SS316L) exploits their differing thermal expansion coefficients to generate localized hinge bending, enabling deterministic, autonomous folding into prescribed mountain and valley configurations.
items.author: Suhas Chandrashekar, Thomas Stieglitz, Prasanth Velvaluri

items.title: Chiral magnon Kerr interaction from linear and nonlinear Meissner screening in ferromagnet--superconductor bilayers
items.summary: Magnon Kerr interaction showing a dependence of magnon dispersion frequency on its population is a useful functionality for nonlinear and quantum magnonics; its strength and sign depend on magnetic anisotropy, bias, and mode geometry. We here propose to use a superconducting gate to tune the Kerr interaction of magnons in ferromagnetic insulators. Even when the superconductor responds linearly, the frequency shift induced by its reflected dipolar field depends on the longitudinal magnetization. The decrease of this magnetization with increasing precession amplitude therefore produces a Kerr contribution. We go beyond this linear Meissner-screening regime by showing that at finite excitation amplitude, the significant Meissner screening currents reduce the superfluid stiffness, thus enhancing the effective magnetic-field penetration and rendering the Meissner backaction amplitude dependent.
items.author: Hanchen Wang, Tao Yu

items.title: ReACT: Reflection-Consistent Modulation and Cross-Load Consistency for Humanoid Velocity Tracking Under Asymmetric Loads
items.summary: In recent years, humanoid loco-manipulation has progressed to whole-body grasping, lifting, and transport. A basic requirement underlying these tasks is carrying the object to its destination, which depends on the locomotion controller accurately executing velocity commands from the navigation policy. However, carrying an object in one hand introduces a persistent asymmetric upper-body load that can degrade velocity tracking. Persistent tracking biases can accumulate into position and heading deviations, increasing the risk of collisions and navigation failure. To address this problem, we present ReACT, a framework for accurate velocity tracking under asymmetric upper-body loads. Reflection-consistent disturbance modulation uses the estimated wrench to modulate actor features for load compensation while preserving action correspondence under reflected observations.
items.author: Xianghui Wang, Aoran Fu, Liyou Luo et al.

items.title: Persistent Metric-Semantic Maritime Scene Memory from Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs
items.summary: Three-dimensional scene graphs (3DSGs) can provide robots with persistent metric-semantic representations for spatial reasoning, but the existing methods have primarily been developed for indoor and terrestrial environments. In this paper we investigate how a representative outdoor open-vocabulary method transfers to maritime environments and which adaptations are needed. Our experiments show that zero-shot representative outdoor 3DSG descriptions agree with our labeled ground truth for a majority of geometry-supported objects on our data, but the resulting map exhibits considerable physical-entity fragmentation, and its terrestrial higher-level assumptions don't capture maritime spatial organization needs. We therefore keep the underlying mapping method and post-process its accumulated evidence.
items.author: Kim Alexander Christensen, Dina Zimmermann, Martin Steinert et al.

items.title: Orchestr.AI: A Unified Workflow for Training and Benchmarking of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Machine-learning force fields enable atomistic simulations at near-reference accuracy and substantially reduced computational cost, but their development remains fragmented across software frameworks with incompatible data formats, configuration schemes, dependencies, and execution procedures. Orchestr.AI addresses this limitation through a unified workflow that coordinates different MLIP software frameworks, referred to as engines, for data preparation, model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment. A common YAML interface defines each experiment, while engine-specific environment profiles preserve compatible software stacks and avoid dependency conflicts. The platform currently supports five MLIP model architectures, namely SchNet, PaiNN, NequIP, Allegro, and MACE, through their corresponding software implementations, providing automated configuration mapping and standardized dataset handling across these frameworks.
items.author: Zain Ul Abideen, Mario Fernández-Pendás, Muhammad Usman et al.

items.title: Additively manufactured ceramic platforms for miniaturized optical frequency references and robust atomic sensor systems
items.summary: Transferring atomic quantum sensors from laboratory-scale physics packages to compact, alignment-free sensor heads suitable for field and space deployment requires a structural platform that combines mechanical, thermal, and optical functionality within a single, manufacturable component. We present such a platform based on additively manufactured technical ceramics: lithography-based ceramic manufacturing is used to fabricate monolithic micro-optical benches with application-specific mounting geometries, while high-precision active alignment and adhesive bonding realize long-term stable optical assemblies through micro-integration. As a first system-level demonstrator, we present a micro-integrated optical frequency reference based on Doppler-free spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 line, integrated within a 6 mL Al2O3 module.

items.title: Associations of fibroblast growth factor 21 with renal parameter changes during pemafibrate treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes.
items.summary: Background Experimental studies suggest that fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is involved in pathways related to peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) activation, whereas elevated circulating FGF21 has also been associated with metabolic stress and kidney dysfunction. We examined the associations of FGF21 with renal parameter changes following the initiation of pemafibrate, a selective PPARα modulator, in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Methods In this retrospective study using prospectively collected blood samples, 81 patients with T2DM who initiated pemafibrate and continued treatment for ≥ 2 years were analyzed. Clinical data and serum high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and FGF21 levels were assessed at baseline and two years.
items.author: Okuma H.

items.title: Evidence generation for diabetes prevention and treatment through the integration of clinical medicine, nutritional epidemiology, and behavioral science.
items.summary: Diet and other lifestyle factors are central to diabetes prevention and management. Effective dietary and lifestyle support requires consideration of differences in pathophysiology, food culture, and living circumstances. This narrative review summarizes our research integrating clinical medicine, nutritional epidemiology, and behavioral science, with a particular focus on diet quality. Analyses of large US cohorts showed that higher-quality plant-based diets were associated with lower risks of stroke and mortality. In longitudinal biomarker analyses, increases in healthful plant-based diet scores were associated with favorable changes in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, whereas increases in unhealthful plant-based diet scores were associated with unfavorable changes in inflammatory biomarkers.
items.author: Baden MY.

items.title: GLP-1 based therapy of obesity and type 2 diabetes.
items.summary: GLP-1 is 30-amino acid peptide that is secreted from the intestine in response to food intake. The release mechanism involves luminal exposure to as well as absorption and metabolism of the major nutrients. It functions mainly as a part of the ileal brake mechanism whereby nutrient entry in distal segments of the small intestine inhibit gastrointestinal secretion and motility as well as appetite and food intake, signalling nutritional abundance. It also functions as a second line incretin hormone. It acts on the brain via sensory vagal afferents, but also interacts with exposed neurons expressing the GLP-1 receptor in the circumventricular organs, in turn activating brain nuclei involved in appetite regulation and reward.
items.author: Holst JJ.

items.title: LLM tool use in manuscript review: Toward guidance and transparency.
items.summary: The peer review system is straining under rising submissions, growing manuscript complexity, and a shrinking reviewer pool. Meanwhile an increasing number of researchers now use tools based on large language models (LLMs) when performing peer review, often without disclosure and against journal policies. This erodes trust in peer review and risks deteriorating the quality and integrity of research publications. We argue for professionalization and transparency rather than prohibition, and propose guidelines built on three aspects: model selection and data protection, human guidance and accountability, and publication integrity. These principles offer a sustainable path forward, leaving scientific judgment where it belongs; that is, with human experts.
items.author: Day CP, Xhabija B, Gopalan V.

items.title: Mitochondrial protein import stress augments α-synuclein aggregation and neural damage.
items.summary: Genetic and environmental factors are known to converge on mitochondria to cause Parkinson's disease. The underlying mechanism is incompletely understood. In addition to bioenergetic defects, nonbioenergetic pathways have been largely unexplored. Validating the nonbioenergetic mitochondrial stressors as independent pathogenic factors is challenging because most mouse models of mitochondrial stress are confounded by bioenergetic defects. Here, we show that expression of Ant1 P.A114P,A123D , previously shown to cause mitochondrial protein import clogging in cultured human cells, does not affect the overall bioenergetic capacity, yet it induces proteostatic stress responses in the cytosol that suggests accumulation of unimported precursor proteins. In a Parkinson's disease model expressing α-synuclein (A53T), Ant1 P.A114P,A123D increased the size of α-synuclein aggregates, increased aggregation of mitochondrial preproteins, heightened neuroinflammation, and worsened motor coordination defects.
items.author: Coyne LP, Rana A, Wang X, Mauro J, Bhagwagar S, Umino Y, Solessio EC, Middleton F, Chen XJ.

items.title: TRIM37 recognizes a bipartite degron to ubiquitinate centrosome substrates.
items.summary: Dysregulation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM37 is associated with tumor formation and Mulibrey nanism, a recessive developmental syndrome. TRIM37 regulates steady-state levels of centrosome proteins and limits their ectopic assembly, but how it recognizes and ubiquitinates its substrates is poorly understood. We found that TRIM37 directly ubiquitinates the centrosome-forming protein Cep192 at 7 lysines clustered near its C terminus. TRIM37 binds Cep192 at a C-terminal intrinsically disordered region followed by an ASH domain (IDR+ASH8). Mutation of the 7 lysines or the IDR+ASH8 domain increased Cep192 levels and stability in cells, indicating loss of TRIM37-based regulation. Fusing IDR+ASH8 to unrelated proteins was sufficient to enable their degradation via TRIM37.
items.author: Stachera WE, Tafur J, Yaguchi K, Familiari NE, Rios MU, Woodruff JB.

items.title: Novel pathogenic FOXP3 variant in two unrelated families with IPEX syndrome.
items.summary: The authors describe three patients with IPEX due to a novel pathogenic variant, two of which have been successfully treated with stem cell transplant. Confidence about variant pathogenicity is difficult in IPEX, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) outcomes are variable; reporting classical IPEX due to novel variants, in this case with an elevated TSDR, remains essential.
items.author: Schim van der Loeff ICD, Johnson MB, Campbell DI, Williams E, Hambleton S.

items.title: Truncating variants reveal functional divergence of the SAMD9 and SAMD9L paralogues.
items.summary: Germline gain-of-function (GoF) variants in the paralogous sterile alpha motif domain containing 9 (SAMD9) and SAMD9-like (SAMD9L) genes cause myelodysplasia, primary immunodeficiencies, and neurological disorders. Predicting the functional consequences of individual variants, however, remains challenging, owing partly to the complexity of these large, multidomain proteins. Here, we functionally characterized several rare patient-derived SAMD9/9L variants, identifying multiple novel GoF and loss-of-function (LoF) variants, including SAMD9L p.C883X-the shortest documented SAMD9L GoF truncation within the NTPase domain. SAMD9L NTPase domain truncations are associated with severe, early-onset pathology, yet despite the high structural and sequence similarity between the two proteins, analogous truncating variants have not been reported in SAMD9 patients.
items.author: Mitev P, Khurana A, Eriksson C, Saccon E, Eshtad S, Vonlanthen S, Tesi B, Dadfar E, Horne A, Mellström E, Paucar M, Sundin M, Bryceson YT.

items.title: Familial TLR8 gain-of-function presenting as HLH with response to IFN-γ blockade.
items.summary: Gain-of-function variants in TLR8 cause X-linked immune dysregulation characterized by cytopenias, bone marrow failure, and lymphoproliferation. We report an 8-year-old male in whom TLR8-GOF manifested as hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, an association not previously described. Treatment with emapalumab was associated with clinical improvement.
items.author: Barber JS, Saucier N, Murphy M, Schmitz EG, McDaniels K, Cook C, Venturi G, Sleasman JW, Mahadeo KM, Cooper MA, Mousallem T.

items.title: Drivers and Impacts of Postharvest Losses in Mango Production for Poverty Reduction Among Smallholder Farmers in Kintampo North Municipality, Ghana.
items.summary: Mango is a key export crop that contributes to Ghana's economic growth. However, postharvest losses threaten the industry and the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and traders. Moreover, limited empirical studies assess the extent, constraints, and impact of these losses. The aim of this study was to quantify the amount of mango fruit wasted at the farm level, identify the causes of these losses, and assess their impact on farm income. Using a structured questionnaire, data was solicited from 297 mango producers from Kintampo North municipality in the transitional agroecological zone of Ghana. Disaggregating mango postharvest losses into quantitative and qualitative losses, the data show that approximately 137 kg (2.74 of 50 kg boxes) and 85 kg (1.7 of 50 kg boxes) are wasted per hectare respectively.
items.author: Adams F, Mensah A, Ullah A, Laryea MAM, Donkor E.

items.title: Modulation of Physiological Responses in Damask Rose to Combined Salinity and Botrytis cinerea Stress by Chitosan and Nano-Chelated Copper.
items.summary: Salinity exacerbates Botrytis cinerea damage, posing a major constraint to Rosa × damascena greenhouse cultivation. This study investigated the physio-biochemical responses of R. × damascena to individual and combined salinity (50 and 100 mM NaCl/CaCl 2 ) and B. cinerea stress, evaluating the mitigating potential of foliar-applied chitosan (0.4% w/v) and nano-chelated copper (NCC; 1000 and 2000 mg L -1 ). Using a four-way factorial design (36 treatments; N = 108), we assessed morphological traits, photosynthetic pigments, proline content, antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, catalase), and membrane integrity via electrolyte leakage (EC). Combined stress resulted in nonadditive physiological deterioration, characterized by significantly elevated EC and disease indices alongside suppressed antioxidant capacity and pigment retention compared to individual stressors.
items.author: Khorrami Moghaddam M, Akbari Oghaz N.

items.title: Differentiating language-specific from language-related network dynamics using dynamic functional connectivity analysis.
items.summary: Language processing is a highly complex dynamic neural activity that requires the recruitment of both regions critical for language processing and large-scale cognitive networks. Because language networks are interconnected and dynamically reconfigure their connections depending on task demand and complexity, it is challenging to differentiate language-specific networks form language-related cognitive networks during both resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and task-based fMRI (tb-fMRI). Prior evidence demonstrated state-dependent differences in dynamic functional connectivity (FC) within identical networks across rest- and task-conditions. Based on this evidence, we hypothesized that examining dynamic FC patterns could help differentiate the functional specialization of large-scale neural networks in the human brain.
items.author: Kurosu A, Liang J, Sinaii N, Thaploo D, Sobitan A, Wingert K, Rajan S, Biassou N.

items.title: Beyond the Primary-Secondary Dichotomy: Toward a Unified Metabolic Perspective.
items.summary: The distinction between primary and secondary metabolism has long provided a useful conceptual and pedagogical framework in biochemistry, particularly in plant sciences, but it increasingly fails as a literal description of how metabolites are produced and function. Pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulatory mechanisms, transport systems, and recycling routes, while metabolites conventionally assigned to different categories can contribute to growth, signaling, defense, nutrient acquisition, structure, or stress responses depending on context. Here, we review the historical origins of the primary-secondary dichotomy and synthesize biochemical, genetic, ecological, metabolomic, and systems-level evidence for a more integrated interpretation of plant metabolism. We do not argue that established terms must be abolished: they remain useful descriptors of broad tendencies in conservation, distribution, and pathway organization.
items.author: de Lima Moreira D, Ramos YJ, Pereira RC.

items.title: Mechanical nociceptive thresholds of the foot do not change following anaesthesia of the digital flexor tendon sheath in horses.
items.summary: Background The selectivity of diagnostic analgesia of the digital flexor tendon sheath (DFTS) in horses remains debated. This study aimed to determine whether intrasynovial administration of 2% lidocaine into the DFTS increases the mechanical nociceptive threshold (MNT) of the dorsal lamellar stratum, sole, coronary band and heel bulbs, with correct placement confirmed by contrast tenography. Methods Six healthy horses with no clinical or radiographic distal limb abnormalities were used. Forelimbs were randomly assigned, with one limb receiving 2% lidocaine and the contralateral limb receiving lactated Ringer's solution via the palmar pastern approach to the DFTS; both solutions were mixed with radiographic contrast to confirm accurate placement.
items.author: Cota LO, Malacarne BD, Dias LA, Pinho Neto AC, Correa MG, Cavalcante MA, de Da Cunha MSL, Silva CFRE, Paz CFR, Carvalho AM, Silveira AB.

items.title: Interstitial Molar Ectopic Pregnancy Despite Euploid Embryo Transfer: A Case Report.
items.summary: Background Even with modern in vitro fertilization (IVF) techniques, unexpected pregnancy outcomes can occur. Molar pregnancy after IVF and embryo transfer can be the result of true abnormal fertilization in the embryology lab. Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies (PGT-A) has advanced and is widely used, but unless additional testing of single-nucleotide polymorphisms is performed, the rare case of partial molar pregnancy (defined as triploidy of paternal origin) after IVF may be missed. Unexpected pregnancy outcomes may also be a result of spontaneous fertilization during assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment. Case The patient is a 36-year-old G1P100 who initially underwent IVF and intracytoplasmic sperm injection with PGT-A and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders for galactosemia carrier status in both partners.
items.author: Patel K, Sakkas D, Groszmann Y, Murphy L, Penzias A, Dottino J.

items.title: Correction to: Abstracts of the ECTS 2026 Congress.
