items.title: CLIPittyClip: a single-command framework for CLIP sequencing data analysis.
items.summary: Crosslinking immunoprecipitation (CLIP) sequencing is the standard method for mapping RNA-binding protein (RBP) binding sites transcriptome wide, yet most analysis pipelines are either modular toolkits requiring manual assembly or large-scale workflows built for consortium infrastructure. Here, we present CLIPittyClip, a single-command pipeline that processes CLIP data from raw FASTQ files to a peak matrix and crosslink site outputs, supports five major CLIP read architectures and runs entirely locally on standard laptop hardware. The pipeline introduces CLink, a Python reimplementation of CLIP Tool Kit crosslink-induced truncation and mutation site analyses that is up to 27-fold faster while recovering equivalent binding motifs and crosslink site resolution.
items.author: Yi S, Luna JM.

items.title: Genome-wide analysis of TMD-associated local ribosome accumulation reveals stress- and eS7-associated remodeling in Saccharomyces cerevisiae .
items.summary: Local ribosome accumulation near transmembrane domains (TMDs) may report cotranslational events in membrane-protein biogenesis, but its spatial organization and stress responsiveness remain unclear. Saccharomyces cerevisiae ribosome-profiling data were reanalyzed using a replicate-aware, TMD-centered workflow. Two untreated wild-type baseline samples showed maximal accumulation approximately 75 nucleotides downstream of annotated TMD starts. At this position, 2896 TMDs met strict eight-sample coverage criteria; 2892 were testable using quasi-likelihood negative-binomial models of target-window counts relative to gene-wide non-TMD coding background. Forty-one TMDs showed an ER-stress effect in wild-type cells, six in eS7-4KR cells, and 22 showed a genotype-by-stress interaction at false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05.
items.author: Li M.

items.title: Self-disgust and the body as a target in self-harm and suicidal behavior: A narrative review.
items.summary: Self-harm and suicidal behavior are commonly framed as failures of emotion regulation, yet the emotions that make the body the target of harm remain under-specified. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on self-disgust as a candidate mechanism in non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and in suicidal ideation and behavior. Self-disgust is an aversive self-directed emotion organized around the appraisal of the self, and often the body, as revolting or contaminated. Cross-sectional studies consistently link self-disgust with NSSI, suicidal ideation, and suicide-risk scores, and qualitative accounts place it at the center of some suicidal crises. Longitudinal studies from China suggest it mediates reciprocal links between emotional abuse and suicidal ideation and a path from body-image concerns to NSSI.
items.author: Jelaga D, Belous M.

items.title: Aphasic status epilepticus presenting with prominent psychiatric symptoms: A case report.
items.summary: Background Aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) is a subtype of nonconvulsive status epilepticus characterized by aphasia as its primary ictal manifestation. Although psychiatric symptoms are uncommon in ASE, they may obscure the diagnosis when present. We report an atypical case, presenting predominantly with agitation and irritability, which was rapidly diagnosed as ASE by electroencephalography (EEG) based on the abrupt symptom onset and neurological history. Case presentation A 49-year-old right-handed woman with alcohol use disorder was referred to our psychiatric hospital because of agitation, irritability, and disorganized thinking. Approximately 2 months before presentation to our hospital, she developed a generalized tonic-clonic seizure 3 days after sustaining a head injury.
items.author: Yamada Y, Takahashi S, Fujiwara M.

items.title: scMINA: an interpretable workflow for paired scRNA-scATAC multiome integration and regulatory prioritization.
items.summary: Single-cell multiomic technologies that jointly profile transcriptomic and epigenomic states provide unprecedented opportunities to investigate cellular heterogeneity and gene regulatory mechanisms in complex diseases. However, analysis of paired single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) data remains computationally challenging due to modality-specific technical variation, integration complexity, and limited interpretability of downstream regulatory inference. Here, we present scMINA (single-cell Multimodal Integration and Network Attribution), a modular and interpretable analytical workflow for the analysis of paired single-cell multiome datasets. scMINA comprises coordinated modules for multimodal integration, technical covariate correction, and regulatory feature prioritization, enabling systematic characterization of cellular states across transcriptomic and epigenomic modalities.
items.author: Zhang S, Hu H, Wang X, Xiong C, Kanekiyo T, Asmann YW, Ren Y.

items.title: Identification of valepotriate as a novel antimycobacterial agent against drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis through screening of a natural terpenoid compound library.
items.summary: Background The continued emergence of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( M. tb ) has substantially limited treatment options and highlights the need for new antimycobacterial agents. Although terpenoids comprise one of the largest classes of natural products with diverse biological activities, their antimycobacterial potential has not been systematically investigated. Methods A library comprising 354 natural terpenoid compounds were screened against M. tb . Lead compounds were subsequently characterized by determining minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs), minimum bactericidal concentrations (MBCs), time-kill kinetics, activity against clinical drug-sensitive and drug-resistant isolates, cytotoxicity in THP-1-derived macrophages and intracellular antimycobacterial activity using colony-forming unit assays. Results Primary screening identified 10 compounds with strong antimycobacterial activity, among which valepotriate showed as a novel antimycobacterial agent.
items.author: Zhu C, Wang X, Zhang X, Jia H, Zhang L, Zhang Z, Pan L.

items.title: Tiny molecules, mighty impacts: MicroRNAs in muscular dystrophies and myopathies.
items.summary: Abstract Microribonucleic acids (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNA molecules that regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and play essential roles in muscle differentiation, regeneration, and metabolism. A specific subset, known as myomiRs, is predominantly expressed in muscle tissue and has been implicated in key molecular pathways underlying muscular dystrophies and myopathies. Due to their stability in biological fluids, myomiRs have emerged as non-invasive biomarkers. The present narrative review summarizes selected studies addressing myomiR expression patterns, functional roles, and translational implications in muscular dystrophies and myopathies, particularly Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1), limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD), McArdle disease, and myofibrillar myopathy (MFM), highlighting their biological relevance and clinical potential.
items.author: Fabris-Moraes AL, Fratini P, Pellacani E, Feder D, Carvalho AAS.

items.title: Ultrasound Evaluation of Varicoceles: A Closed-Loop Audit of Compliance With European Society of Urogenital Radiology Guidelines.
items.summary: Objective To evaluate ultrasound reporting practices for varicoceles at a district general hospital in London against the European Society of Urogenital Radiology Scrotal and Penile Imaging Working Group (ESUR-SPIWG) standards and measure the impact of a structured reporting intervention. Background Varicoceles are common and may cause infertility and chronic scrotal discomfort. Ultrasound is the gold standard imaging modality for investigation. The ESUR-SPIWG guidelines, based on the Sarteschi grading system, mandate documentation of testicular volume, vein location and diameter (supine and erect), and duration of venous reflux. Previous audit data suggested poor compliance with these standards. Methods Retrospective closed-loop audit of ultrasound reports for 40 patients per cycle, investigated for varicoceles (Cycle 1: July 2023; Cycle 2: October 2024).
items.author: Khan HA, Paramesparan K.

items.title: Combined Arthroscopic Anterior Cruciate Ligament and Oblique Popliteal Ligament Reconstruction of the Knee.
items.summary: The oblique popliteal ligament is the largest ligamentous structure of the posterior knee capsule and serves as a primary restraint to genu recurvatum and a contributor to rotatory stability. This technical note describes an arthroscopic-assisted method for oblique popliteal ligament reconstruction, performed as an isolated procedure or in combination with anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, or multiligament knee reconstructions. Indications include symptomatic post-traumatic genu recurvatum, posterior capsular laxity, recurrent or high-risk anterior cruciate ligament failure associated with hyperextension, persistent posterior or rotational instability, and complex multiligament injuries. The technique uses standardized femoral and tibial tunnels; controlled posterior graft passage through posteromedial, trans-septal, and posterolateral portals; and fixation in slight knee flexion to optimize posterior capsular tension in full extension.
items.author: Amouzadeh Omrani F, Sarzaeem MM, Manafi Rasi A, Omidian MM, Alahgholiei A, Dolikhani M, Pourmojarab A.

items.title: A Cuproptosis Nanoparticle Reverses Lung Adenocarcinoma Drug Resistance.
items.summary: Residual tumors that received targeted therapy often evolve into drug resistance, with an increasing risk of recurrence and metastasis. By analyzing patient data, it is found that KRAS -mutated lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) exhibits a worse survival rate than wild-type LUAD. Although the clinical drug AMG-510 has been approved to treat KRAS(G12C) -mutated LUAD, its effectiveness is still limited by drug resistance. Cuproptosis, a newly identified mode of cellular death, shows promise in cancer treatment and in reversing drug resistance. By comparing cell lines with different sensitivities to AMG-510, we discovered that ATP7B , a key regulator of cuproptosis, was up-regulated in AMG-510-resistant cell lines to decrease their sensitivity to cuproptosis.
items.author: Wu L, Li K, Wang H, Ma S, Wang R, Fan Y, Qin X, Li M, Gonzalez-Rivas D, Ji X, Ni D, Xie D.

items.title: Enhanced Third-Harmonic Generation in a Bound State in the Continuum Assisted Multiband All-Dielectric Metasurface.
items.summary: Multiband Fano resonances are demonstrated in the near-infrared (near-IR) using an all-dielectric metasurface whose unit cell consists of four silicon nanoblocks on a glass substrate. An in-plane asymmetry triggers symmetry-protected quasi-bound states in the continuum (QBICs), producing multiple high- Q resonances. Their origin is identified through multipolar decomposition of the scattering cross section and field distributions at the resonances. The strong field localization at these resonances enables efficient multiband third-harmonic (TH) generation in the ultraviolet (UV), with a maximum simulated conversion efficiency of 8.5×10-3 at a peak pump intensity of 1.6GW/cm2 . The metasurface is fabricated in symmetric and asymmetric configurations, and its linear and nonlinear responses are measured under normal incidence.
items.author: Mondal P, Alamoudi H, Sanchez RP, Al Ibrahim RH, Ooi BS, Roqan I, Bagci H.

items.title: Spontaneous Rupture of an Infected Pelvic Mesenteric Cyst With Features Suggestive of a Pseudocyst Presenting With Peritonitis.
items.summary: Suspect rupture of a previously documented pelvic mesenteric cyst when acute abdominal pain and new free fluid develop, even if CT no longer clearly shows the cyst. Prompt surgical source control is essential; residual cyst wall warrants clinical and radiological surveillance.
items.author: Al Shaaibi R, Al Aufi N, Elsayed A, Elghadban H.

items.title: Exploring Predictive Modeling Algorithms for Good Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Secondary Analysis of a Cluster Randomized Trial Cohort Further Explored by Sex.
items.summary: Background and aims Predictive modeling algorithms show promise in identifying risk factors influencing clinical outcomes. This study aims to evaluate different machine learning algorithms to identify an accurate predictive model of glycemic control at 18-months follow-up in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients and explore sex-specific risk factors. Methods Data of T2DM patients from the INTEGRATE dataset (2016-2019) were used. Baseline demographic, anthropometric, clinical biomarkers, and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) were included to develop predictive models using LASSO logistic regression, CART, XGBoost, and Random Forest. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration using calibration intercept, slope, and Brier score, clinical utility using decision-curve analysis (DCA), and model interpretability using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).
items.author: Shan S, Michell A, Chen AX, Devaux A, Arnott C, Billot L, Campain A, Adavi U, Myton R, INTEGRATE team, Lee VYJ.

items.title: Missed Nursing Care and its Influencing Factors Among Nurses in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis, 2025.
items.summary: Background and aims Missed nursing care, defined as the omission or delay of required nursing activities such as patient assessment and medication administration, is an important indicator of the quality and safety of healthcare services. In Ethiopia, where healthcare systems often face workforce shortages and resource constraints, the magnitude and determinants of missed nursing care remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of missed nursing care and identify its associated factors among nurses in Ethiopia. Methods This study followed PRISMA guidelines and focused on research conducted in Ethiopia. A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, identifying eight eligible studies.
items.author: Kitil GW, Hirpo AH, Butta FW, Chereka AA.

items.title: A Comparison of Owl Pellet Analysis and Conventional Trapping: A Review of Central European Cases for the Study of Small Mammal Communities and More Efficient Paleoenvironmental Reconstructions.
items.summary: Due to their rapid reproductive cycles and short generation times, small mammals-particularly rodents and shrews-are widely used as bioindicators in ecological studies. While traditional live trapping provides detailed demographic data for such monitoring, it is labour-intensive and subject to sampling bias. In contrast, owl pellet analysis presents a non-invasive and cost-effective alternative for evaluating small mammal community structure over broad spatial and temporal scales, though potential prey preferences should be considered. This study evaluates the effectiveness of owl pellet analysis in comparison to conventional trapping methods for monitoring small mammal communities. We synthesised data from 26 published studies and additional unpublished field reports, comprising a uniquely robust dataset of 40 systematically processed case studies across seven countries in Central Europe, a biogeographically coherent region.
items.author: Szalai D, Kiss C, Cserkész T, Virág A, Németh A.

items.title: Implant-Preserving Guided Bone Regeneration for Peri-Implant Bone Loss Associated With Early Peri-Implantitis: A Case Report.
items.summary: A 60-year-old man developed localized peri-implant bone loss 2.5 months after implant placement. Surgical debridement was followed by guided bone regeneration using autogenous retromolar bone and a resorbable collagen membrane. At follow-up, satisfactory hard-tissue healing and implant stability were observed, permitting successful prosthetic rehabilitation and maintenance of function.
items.author: Samantaray RK, Sinha P, Agarwal SK, Sharan J, Devi LB, Basynat SK.

items.title: Metabolic Nanomedicine Reprograms Mesenchymal Stem Cells for Durable Exosome-Mediated Immunomodulation.
items.summary: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are widely recognized for their immunomodulatory potential, yet their clinical efficacy remains inconsistent due to poor persistence and functional instability under prolonged inflammatory stress. Here we identify NAD + depletion as a central driver of MSCs exhaustion, leading to metabolic collapse, programmed cell death, and loss of immunoregulatory activity. Direct restoration is nontrivial, because NAD + is membrane impermeable and extracellularly unstable. To overcome this barrier, we developed a nanoparticle system for efficient intracellular delivery of NAD + , enabling sustained metabolic support even under hostile inflammatory conditions. NAD + restoration markedly improved MSCs survival, preserved their ability to suppress T cell proliferation, and enhanced therapeutic efficacy in murine colitis.
items.author: Chen J, Zeng K, Chao J, Zhang X, Zhou Z, Li X, Liu W, Xie X, Wang L, Ye M.

items.title: From Static Records to Virtual Digital Patients: An Artificial Intelligence‐Driven Framework for Medical Data Assetization and Governance
items.author: Lian Y, Zhao Y, Liu Y, Gao H, Li M, Wang G, Zhang Z.

items.title: Subcutaneous Basal Cell Carcinoma of the Cheek: A Diagnostic Pitfall Le carcinome basocellulaire sous-cutané de la joue : un piège diagnostique
items.author: Madede B, Kotze Engelbrecht J, Kairinos N.

items.title: Beyond enteral feedings: Teduglutide and its role in gut resiliency
items.author: Grabow H, Duffy M, Seto D, Tizzard P.

items.title: High-throughput light-sheet 3D microscopy of whole rodent brain microstructure for integration with MRI
items.summary: Whole-brain cellular mapping is essential for understanding how differences in cellular architecture shape brain organisation and function. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides whole-brain coverage in humans and animal models but is only indirectly sensitive to cellular features. Integrating MRI with whole-brain microscopy is therefore critical for interpreting existing microstructural MRI measures and developing more specific ones. Here, we present a scalable cross-resolution framework integrating 3D light-sheet microscopy (LSM) of intact rodent brains with diffusion MRI (dMRI). By combining active tissue clearing and immunolabelling with accelerated LSM acquisitions, we achieve multiplexed whole-brain mapping of neuronal and glial populations on timescales comparable to conventional histology and 2D microscopy.
items.author: Hanmer, J. M., D'Antonio, F., Assimopoulos, S. et al.

items.title: Interconnected reservoirs of multidrug-resistant bacteria and plasmids within hospital plumbing infrastructure
items.summary: Hospital sinks and wastewater streams are hotspots for contamination and colonization with multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR-GNB). While hospital water systems may facilitate MDR-GNB transmission during outbreaks, longitudinal population dynamics of environmental MDR-GNB and their long-term relationship with patient isolates remain unclear. Here we aimed to characterize the diversity and abundance of MDR-GNB within the hospital built environment and evaluate their relationship with clinical isolates. We performed nanopore sequencing on MDR-GNB cultured from sink drains (n=523) and wastewater (n=146) at a New York City hospital between March-August 2023. We assessed spatial and longitudinal genomic strain and plasmid dynamics and quantified relatedness to historical clinical isolates from the same hospital (n=602).
items.author: Annavajhala, M. K., Hokunson, T. W., Terzoglou, K. et al.

items.title: Molecular Modulation of the SAM-I Riboswitch Drives Global Dynamical Shifts
items.summary: A surge in antimicrobial resistance in recent years has made protein-targeting antibiotics less effective against key pathogens. It is possible to expand the range of therapeutic targets by using RNA-based therapies, but it remains necessary to improve the molecular-level understanding of interactions between RNA and known and potential binders. The SAM-I riboswitch, which controls the transcriptional termination of gene expression involved in sulfur metabolism in most bacteria, is an excellent ligand target. Thus, understanding its behavior with and without ligand complexes would be helpful for drug design. Here, we studied the interactions between the SAM-I riboswitch and its natural ligand, SAM, which controls riboswitch function, and compared those to its interactions with the similar small molecule SAH, which does not control riboswitch function, and to its interactions with a potential binder JS4, identified via virtual screening.
items.author: Nair, V., Niknam Hamidabad, M., Erol, D. et al.

items.title: Hybrid RY-mers increase aDNA alignment sensitivity
items.summary: One of the key steps in ancient DNA data analysis is the accurate identification of endogenous short reads that originate from the ancient genome. Currently, this step is performed using general-purpose sequence aligners, such as BWA-aln, with parameter settings optimized for sensitivity. This approach results in increased runtime, even relative to standard DNA alignment workflows, and is not sufficient for aligning samples that are highly divergent from a reference database. We introduce hybrid RY-mers, a seed construct designed to incorporate aDNA-specific sequence damage. We adapt hybrid RY-mers to the existing concept of multi-context seeds and implement them in the read aligner strobealign.
items.author: Tolstoganov, I., Sahlin, K.

items.title: Implicit Hierarchical Tensor Decomposition of Single-Cell Four-Omics Data Reveals Cell-Type-Linked Candidate Enhancer--Promoter-Associated Programs
items.summary: Single-cell multi-omics provides complementary views of gene regulation, but integrating modalities with natural features comprising enhancers, genes, and three-dimensional (3D) genomic loci remains challenging. This study developed an implicit hierarchical tensor decomposition framework and applied it to the CHARM single-cell four-omics mouse brain data (GSE303006) by jointly analyzing ATAC, H3K27ac, RNA, and reconstructed 3D enhancer--promoter (E--P) distances. After quality control, 730,969 E--P pairs, 42,669 enhancers, 16,239 genes, 391,435 20-kb bin pairs, and 4,258 cells were retained. Each modality was independently reduced to 20 components and mapped to an implicit 730,969x4{,}258x20x4 tensor, which was decomposed without materializing the full array. In a joint model, cell type explained more variance than biological replicate for all 12 distinct cell components represented among the 100 largest Tucker core elements.
items.author: Taguchi, Y.-h., Turki, T.

items.title: Simple models outperform single-cell foundation models on downstream benchmarks
items.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data exhibit strong and reproducible statistical structure. This has motivated the development of large-scale foundation models, such as TranscriptFormer, that use transformer-based architectures to learn a generative model for gene expression by embedding genes into a latent vector space. These embeddings have been used to obtain state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on downstream tasks such as cell-type classification, disease-state prediction, and cross-species learning. Here, we ask whether similar performance can be achieved without utilizing computationally intensive deep learning-based representations. Using simple, interpretable pipelines that rely on careful normalization and linear methods, we obtain SOTA or near SOTA performance across multiple benchmarks commonly used to evaluate single-cell foundation models, including outperforming foundation models on out-of-distribution tasks involving novel cell types and organisms absent from the training data.
items.author: Souza, H., Mehta, P.

items.title: Large seed size accompanying GmSDP1 suppression is linked to cellular remodeling and phytohormone regulation
items.summary: Soybean (Glycine max) seeds contain approximately 20% oil and 40% protein and are important for food, feed, and biofuel. Improving soybean productivity and seed quality requires optimizing carbon partitioning during seed development. Previously, seed-specific suppression of the lipase-encoding gene Sugar-Dependent 1 (SDP1) increased seed oil content by approximately 5% while slightly reducing raffinose family oligosaccharides without compromising protein content. Seed-specific SDP1 suppression also increased seed size by 18-25% without affecting seed number, resulting in greater seed biomass per plant. To determine the developmental basis of the increased seed size, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying this phenotype. Microscopy and biochemical analyses showed that larger seeds were associated with increased seed cell size and enhanced lignocellulosic cell wall accumulation.
items.author: Mukherjee, T., Crowley, S., Lingwan, M. et al.

items.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
items.summary: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling.
items.author: Jo, K. B., Alruwaili, M. M., Kim, D.-E. et al.

items.title: Shared experimental materials inflate and reorder cross-participant decoding benchmarks
items.summary: Decoding mental states from brain activity underpins brain-computer interfaces and cognitive neuroscience. Decoders are judged by how well they generalize to people left out of training, taken as evidence that they capture what transfers between brains. However, most benchmarks present the same experimental materials to every participant, so held-out participants are tested on materials the model has already seen. Here we show, across 15 EEG, fMRI and eye-tracking datasets and 318 matched comparisons, that shared materials inflate cross-participant accuracy by up to 46 percentage points. They also reorder methods, reversing the advantage of foundation models over handcrafted features on the largest emotion EEG benchmark.
items.author: Cui, H., Zhu, Y., Huang, S. et al.

items.title: Widespread oscillatory suppression in autism persists in the absence of psychotropic medication.
items.summary: Purpose: Investigate the neural oscillatory activity associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) using electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings in children and adolescents. Compare the corresponding oscillatory power between ASD patients taking psychotropic medication with a drug-naive group. Methods: ASD diagnosis was done using DSM-IV and CARS (Childhood Autism Rating Scale). EEG recordings employed 22 scalp electrodes (10/20 system). ASD vs. neurotypical groups were matched for sex and age (5 females; average age: ~10 years old). We analyzed the resting state (eyes open) EEG power spectrum during ~2-minute recordings. The multitaper FFT method was used to estimate spectral power for the delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma frequency bands.
items.author: Amorim, A. K. J., Alves, G. M., Pontes, G. C. L. et al.

items.title: Accessing Mesoscale Functional Organization from Standard Functional MRI Leveraging AI-Based Super-Resolution
items.summary: Access to the fine-scale functional organization of the human brain is essential for understanding cognition and neurological disorders yet remains beyond the reach of conventional functional MRI (fMRI) because of its limited spatial resolution and contrast-to-noise ratio. To overcome this limitation, we developed f-LENNS (functional Localization Enhancement via Neural-Net-Sharpening), an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework that enhances the effective spatial resolution of reconstructed fMRI magnitude images. The model was trained exclusively on high-resolution synthetic MRI data using extensive domain randomization and no adversarial or generative components. This approach enables robust out-of-the-box generalization (without retraining) to experimental datasets obtained with diverse acquisitions, while effectively curbing hallucination.
items.author: Nasr, S., Li, H. B., Zemlyanker, D. et al.

items.title: Rab10 and Arhgef7 interact to promote axon extension by linking vesicle supply and exocytosis
items.summary: The formation of functional neural circuits begins with the extension of a single axon by immature neurons. Axon elongation requires an expansion of the plasma membrane that depends on the polarization of vesicle trafficking and exocytosis. It is not completely understood how the increased transport of vesicles into the growing axon is linked to their subsequent insertion into the plasma membrane. An analysis of early stages of neuronal differentiation indicates that an asymmetry in neurite length precedes axon specification and the accumulation of PPVs in the nascent axon. We show that increasing the transport of vesicles in unpolarized neurons is sufficient to promote the extension of additional axons.
items.author: Olocco, F., Bekker, E., Ravindran, P. et al.

items.title: Geometric Kinematics of Human Eyes
items.summary: In previous studies by the author on binocular vision with the asymmetric eye (AE), which models a healthy human eye with misaligned optical components, the results were primarily presented in the Rodrigues' vector (RV) framework and supported by simulations and 3D visualizations in GeoGebra's dynamic geometry environment. In this paper, the novel geometric kinematics of the human eye, that is, the eye with misaligned optics, and simplified assumptions about the eye rotations (the eye's translational movements are disregarded), are developed within the framework of rigid-body rotations. The originality of the analysis lies in a precise geometric decomposition of a full rotation of the eye's posture into a torsion-free rotation (the geodesic part) and a torsional rotation (the non-geodesic extension of the geodesic part).
items.author: Turski, J.

items.title: SPOUT: An open-source hardware and software platform to study decision making while manipulating and recording from neural activity
items.summary: Recording and manipulating brain activity during behavior is critical to understanding the underlying mechanisms of decision-making. Linking neural activity to behavior requires behavioral hardware and software tightly integrated with recording and perturbation systems on a shared clock. We built SPOUT (State-machine Platform for Operant Uni/dual-spout Tasks), an open-source, Teensy-driven state-machine platform with a MATLAB interface that runs 10 unique decision-making tasks (with dozens of variations available through user-friendly settings) to study behavior in head-restrained mice. The platform is built on several custom hardware devices: a dual-lick detector, headplate designs for optogenetics and two-photon calcium imaging, a three-axis motorized spout manipulator, and an optogenetics power modulator.
items.author: van den Boom, B. J. G., Dash, D., Rutherford, M. et al.

items.title: Sex differences in astrocytic reactivity and its association with cognitive decline in cognitively unimpaired older adults
items.summary: INTRODUCTION: Astrocyte reactivity may contribute to increased Alzheimers disease (AD) risk in women. Although plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels have been reported to be higher in women than in men, few studies have examined sex-specific associations with other plasma AD biomarkers and cognition. METHODS: Participants were enrolled in the Memory Education and Research Initiative, a longitudinal community-based cohort, and underwent evaluation including blood biomarker sampling. The Alzheimers Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) was included as a replication cohort. RESULTS: Females had higher plasma GFAP levels than males in MERI (N{equiv}584), a finding that was replicated in ADNI. In MERI, higher baseline GFAP was associated with lower A{beta}42/40 and higher p-Tau231 and NfL levels.
items.author: Reichert Plaska, C., Jacobs, T., Bruno, D. et al.

items.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence
items.summary: Adolescence is a period of distinct maturational changes in sleep physiology. Age-related trends in sleep physiology have been captured using laboratory-based polysomnography, a method limited by logistical burden and high cost. We tested the ability of the Dreem3 sleep EEG headband to replicate established age effects in sleep physiology from late childhood through early adulthood. Typically developing youth (N=100, 9-26 years) completed 3-4 consecutive nights of at-home sleep recording. We estimated age-related trends across eight macro-architecture and 15 micro-architecture variables with known age effects and conducted exploratory analyses of 24 additional variables. The Dreem3 replicated some established age trends, including increases in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) stage 2%, and decreases in N3%, time in bed, NREM delta and theta power with increasing age.
items.author: Lokhandwala, S., Cooper, R. E., Hayes, R. et al.

items.title: BenchRep-T: A Systematic Evaluation of T-Cell Repertoire-Based Disease Diagnostics
items.summary: Adaptive immune receptor repertoire sequencing data has emerged as a promising potential modality for disease diagnosis, relying on computational methods to analyze T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences from an individual's blood sample. Published methods rely on different cohorts, data preprocessing pipelines, and evaluation metrics, making direct comparison across methods challenging. We present BenchRep-T, a unified benchmark that standardizes multiple publicly available TCR repertoire datasets and evaluates nine computational approaches, spanning statistical enrichment of shared sequences, feature-engineered ensembles, deep learning, and sequence clustering. BenchRep-T evaluates methods on four tasks: disease classification across conditions, performance scaling under restricted sequence-sampling depth, recovery of known antigen-specific driver sequences, and evaluation of sensitivity to demographic confounding.
items.author: Buendia, A., Im, C., Kundaje, A. et al.

items.title: Systemic TLR7 agonism moderates disease severity in acute DSS-induced colitis in mice
items.summary: Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is an endosomal sensor of single-stranded RNA, studied for its antiviral and pro-inflammatory functions. Its role in intestinal inflammation is undefined, and no approved or clinical-stage therapy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) engages this pathway. Here we report that systemic administration of the reference TLR7 agonist GS-9620 (vesatolimod) moderates disease severity in acute dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. GS-9620-treated mice lost less weight, had lower Disease Activity Index scores, and were protected from DSS-induced colon shortening. Immunophenotyping of the spleen showed reduced Th17 and Tr17 populations and an increased proportion of regulatory T cells.
items.author: Kazimierczyk, D., Seed, B., Jain, N.

items.title: Metagenomic Insights into the Fecal Microbiome, Resistome, and Mobilome of Beef Cattle in Cow-Calf Operations in Florida, United States
items.summary: Food-producing animals are a focus of One Health approaches to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) as reservoirs of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). We hypothesized that microbial composition, ARGs profiles, and mobile genetic element (MGE) profiles would differ by operation size and animal age group. Fecal samples from 162 cows and calves were combined into 54 composite samples, each comprising three animals of the same age group. Across operation sizes, Bacillota (51.4-64.9%), Bacteroidota (12.0-17.3%), Pseudomonadota (10.3-16.5%), and Actinomycetota (3.3-10.9%) were predominant phyla. Alpha diversity did not differ among operation sizes; however, cows exhibited greater observed richness, Shannon diversity, and Simpson diversity than calves (all P < 0.001).
items.author: Ali, A., K. Edison, L., Bittar, J. H. J. et al.

items.title: Structural basis of virion assembly in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis-infecting mycobacteriophage SWU1
items.summary: The rising threat of drug-resistant tuberculosis has renewed interest in bacteriophage therapy as an urgently needed alternative. Rational engineering of these viruses, however, requires an atomic-level understanding of virion architecture. Mycobacteriophage SWU1 belongs to subcluster A2, one of the few mycobacteriophage lineages known to infect Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis). Using single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), we resolved essentially the entire SWU1 virion architecture by localized reconstruction of four modules, the capsid, portal vertex, tail and baseplate, at resolutions of 3.62 [A], 3.51 [A], 3.70 [A] and 3.22 [A], respectively. The T=7 capsid comprises 415 copies of an HK97-fold major capsid protein and lacks any decoration protein in density.
items.author: Bian, Q., Huang, Y., Feng, T. et al.

items.title: Novel viral diversity and geographic structuring in the New Zealand West Coast blackfly (Austrosimulium ungulatum)
items.summary: Background Vector-borne diseases represent a major global public health burden, with climate change, land-use change and increasing human activity altering arthropod vector distributions and creating opportunities for infectious disease emergence. In Aotearoa New Zealand, insects commonly referred to as "sandflies" are blackflies belonging to the family Simuliidae. The West Coast blackfly, Austrosimulium ungulatum, is an endemic, human-biting species abundant throughout the South Island, yet its associated viral diversity remains largely unexplored. Methods Here, we used metatranscriptomic sequencing to characterise the virome of the West Coast blackfly and investigate patterns of viral diversity and community composition across geographical and environmental gradients.
items.author: Byrne, K., Darnley, J. A., Waller, S. J. et al.

items.title: Metabolism of bilirubin to urobilinogen by human gut bacteria occurs by a branched, multi-enzyme pathway
items.summary: Bilirubin, the predominant product of heme catabolism in mammals, enters the intestine via the hepatobiliary system and subsequently is metabolized by the gut microbiome into multiple downstream derivatives, such as urobilinogen and stercobilinogen. Variation in levels of bilirubin and its derivatives are associated with inflammatory and metabolic disorders, but the microbial species and enzymes that metabolize bilirubin have remained largely unknown, which has precluded causal and mechanistic studies. Here, we demonstrate that metabolism of bilirubin to urobilinogen requires multiple distinct reactions carried out by separate enzymes. We find that bilirubin reductase (BilR), an enzyme that was recently discovered and proposed to convert bilirubin to urobilinogen, is specific for reducing the methine bridges of bilinoids, converting bilirubin to the previously uncharacterized intermediate divinylurobilinogen and mesobilirubin to urobilinogen.
items.author: Russell, B. J., Hasenoehrl, E., Marando, V. M. et al.

items.title: Characterization of Lactobacillus rhamnosus-Derived Extracellular Vesicles and Their Cellular Cytoprotective Effects Against Trimethylamine-Induced Oxidative Stress in Caco-2 Cells
items.summary: Dietary trimethylamine (TMA) underwent gut microbiota-mediated catabolism and subsequent hepatic oxidation to generate trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a key metabolic factor linked to vascular and colorectal diseases. While the systemic effects of circulating TMAO were heavily investigated, the direct localized cellular interactions of its precursor, TMA, at the intestinal epithelial level required further elucidation. This study characterized extracellular vesicles isolated from Lactobacillus rhamnosus (Lr-EVs) and evaluated their cytoprotective potential in an in vitro human intestinal Caco-2 cell model under TMA-induced stress. Exposure to a high concentration of TMA (20 mM) significantly reduced Caco-2 viability to 78.8%, triggered intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and compromised tight junction integrity as observed via the disruption of Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) alignment.
items.author: Wang, L.-M., Kin, T. C., Hung, W.-C. et al.

items.title: Viral replication and host response in airway epithelial cells predicts coronavirus pathogenicity and identifies HCoV-229E as an atypical seasonal coronavirus
items.summary: Human coronaviruses (HCoVs) range from mild seasonal strains to pathogenic viruses that cause severe pneumonia. The virological and host determinants that distinguish pathogenic coronaviruses (MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2) from seasonal strains (HCoV-229E, HCoV-NL63 and HCoV-OC43) remain poorly defined. To identify determinants of pathogenicity, we systematically compared replication, cellular tropism, innate responses and cytopathogenicity of pathogenic compared with seasonal HCoVs across nasal, bronchial, small airway and embryonic stem cell derived alveolar type II (AT2) epithelial cell cultures. All HCoVs preferentially infected ciliated cells in the upper airway, but only pathogenic viruses replicated to high titres in AT2 cells. Pathogenic HCoVs reprogrammed AT2 function and suppressed key innate immune signatures, consistent with distal lung epithelial dysfunction.
items.author: Gartner, M. J., Hirankitti, A., Mohenska, M. et al.

items.title: Chromosome-scale CRISPR screening reveals secretory pathway genes as drivers of aneuploidy-mediated antifungal tolerance
items.summary: The gain or loss of chromosomes in eukaryotes often drives aberrant phenotypes by altering the expression levels of hundreds or thousands of genes. In the case of beneficial aneuploidies, the genetic basis of fitness improvement has rarely been pinpointed, and identifying the causal genes remains a major challenge in engineering biology. The leading cause of human fungal infections, Candida albicans, frequently acquires extra copies of chromosome R (ChrR) following exposure to azole antifungal drugs, resulting in heightened antifungal tolerance. Despite this, why this aneuploidy frequently emerges following azole exposure and how it promotes antifungal tolerance remain unknown. Here, we combine RNA-seq with parallel chromosome-wide CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screens to systematically profile the ChrR genes contributing to azole tolerance.
items.author: Gervais, N. C., Esquivel, B. D., Wensing, L. F. et al.

items.title: Nuclear retention and RNA editing safeguard self-tolerance to immunogenic intron lariats
items.summary: Introns are excised as lariats and rapidly degraded upon linearization, leaving their post-splicing role unclear. Here, we investigate their immunoregulatory potential by analyzing the intron lariat landscape upon inhibition of the debranching enzyme DBR1. We find that lariats harboring transposable elements (TEs), especially inverted Alu repeats (IRAlus), elicit cell cycle-dependent activation of protein kinase R (PKR), but only in cells harboring a high burden, such as breast cancer. These immunogenic lariats are initially retained in the nucleus, but upon cytosolic release, they drive PKR activation and apoptosis. Exploiting this, we combine DBR1 depletion with anti-mitotic chemotherapy to enhance lariat-PKR interactions and promote cancer cell death in vitro and in vivo.
items.author: Lee, K., Ku, J., Park, S. Y. et al.

items.title: LOca-1: A minimal calcium-activated arginyl-specific orthocaspase from the Loki's Castle hydrothermal vent field
items.summary: Orthocaspases are prokaryotic homologs of metacaspases within the C14 family of cysteine proteases, yet their biochemical properties and cellular roles remain poorly understood. Here, we report the discovery and comprehensive characterization of LOca-1, a metagenome-derived orthocaspase from the Loki's Castle hydrothermal vent field. LOca-1 consists primarily of a single, conserved p20 catalytic domain and undergoes calcium-dependent activation through cleavage at a conserved arginine residue. Once activated, LOca-1 displays strict arginyl-specific proteolytic activity and strong selectivity for residues surrounding the cleavage site. The enzyme is both thermoactive and thermostable, exhibiting maximal activity at 65 {degrees}C and a melting temperature of approximately 72 {degrees}C.
items.author: Arsın, H., Hribovsek, P., Urich, L. et al.

items.title: A TMEM175 Mutation Disrupts the Lysosomal-Mitochondrial Axis Causing Short QT Syndrome and Sudden Cardiac Death
items.summary: Short QT Syndrome (SQTS) is a rare cardiac channelopathy characterized by abnormally short QTc intervals and increased sudden cardiac death (SCD) risk. Only 20-30% of SQTS cases have been linked to genetic mutations, typi-cally in surface membrane ion channels. We identified a novel lysosomal TMEM175 gene mutation (p.Arg377His) in 7 patients in a family with SQTS and SCD. Genetic analyses, including whole exome sequencing in the family and rare-variant burden testing in [~]118,000 UK Biobank participants, sug-gested an association between TMEM175 rare variants and QT interval short-ening. Functional studies in CRISPR-engineered mice and patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) revealed that TMEM175R377H causes shortened QT intervals and hastened repolariza-tion, respectively, as well an increased arrhythmia susceptibility.
items.author: Cruz, F. M., Ruiz-Robles, J. M., Martinez-Carrascoso, I. m. et al.

items.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis-primed neutrophils reshape the brain microenvironment to promote brain metastasis
items.summary: Brain metastasis (BrM) is a devastating complication of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet how host macroenvironmental conditions influence brain metastatic susceptibility remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a common complication in patients with cancer, on TNBC brain metastasis. Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer. Using two syngeneic TNBC models, we demonstrated that DVT selectively enhanced brain metastasis without significantly affecting primary tumor growth or lung metastasis. Mechanistically, DVT increased neutrophil accumulation in the brain metastatic microenvironment, and neutrophil depletion completely abrogated the metastasis-promoting effect of DVT.
items.author: Endo, S., Rujchanarong, D., Keeran, K. et al.

items.title: A LOV-domain photoreceptor mediates phototaxis in brown algae
items.summary: Phototaxis enables motile cells to navigate light environments and plays a critical role in survival and reproduction across diverse eukaryotic lineages. This ability has evolved independently through distinct photoreceptor systems. Yet, the molecular mechanisms underlying phototaxis remain poorly understood in many major eukaryotic lineages, including stramenopiles. Here, combining functional genetics, cell biology and evolutionary analyses, we identify Helmchrome (HELM), a LOV-domain protein required for phototaxis in the brown alga Ectocarpus. HELM localizes to the posterior flagellum and is responsible for the characteristic flavin-associated fluorescence of brown algal gametes. Loss of HELM abolishes phototactic accumulation and directional orientation without affecting basal motility or fertilization, demonstrating its specific requirement for light-directed movement.

items.title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure

A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $μ$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $μ$V.

items.title: Molecular Gas Optics Using Vibrational Population Density Refraction
items.summary: Gas optics holds promise for development of advanced optical elements with 2-3 orders of magnitude higher damage threshold than any solid-state optics. Here, we demonstrate a new concept for refracting the laser beam using vibrationally excited molecules as gas optics instead of traditional control of thermodynamic gas temperature. The transient, vibrational population density grating is formed in a CO2 gas by interfering two mid-IR lasers to imprint spatial modulation in the linear refractive index (Delta n0 >=2x10-5) of the neutral gas via enhancement of the molecular polarizability. It is increased by pumping the asymmetric stretching mode of CO2 at optimal wavelengths to resonantly produce a highly nonequilibrium state that increases the effective vibrational mode temperature to greater than 2000 K in a room temperature gas.

items.title: Dephasing-Induced Melting of Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
items.summary: Long-range spectral order can be probed using spectral form factors, where it manifests itself as sharp Bragg peaks at integer multiples of the Heisenberg time in nearly crystalline spectra. We examine how energy dephasing in open systems affects this spectral order and how to control it. We find that Bragg peaks fade algebraically with revival order and dephasing strength, $K_{\rm Bragg}(p)\propto(γp)^{-1/2}$, within an extensive intermediate regime, and persist up to the lifetime of nearest-neighbor coherences despite an extreme decoherence rate. Our results establish the spectral form factor as a probe of spectral order in open quantum systems and identify temporal correlations in spectral fluctuations as a means of controlling it.
items.author: Preethi Gopalakrishnan, Adolfo del Campo

items.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights.
items.author: Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang et al.

items.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
items.summary: Machine learning models often achieve high average accuracy in the training data while performing poorly on test data due to subpopulation shift. A common data-centric solution is to enforce balanced subgroup proportions, but full balance can be costly, infeasible, and not always necessary. In this work, we study whether balanced training data is the unique optimal configuration for robust subpopulation generalization. We extend a Gaussian feature-model framework to theoretically characterize the performance landscape across general training subgroup distributions. We show that multiple configurations, including substantially imbalanced ones, can perform comparably to the balanced one. We further derive gradient-based directions for adjusting subgroup proportions to improve adjusted accuracy and worst-group accuracy more efficiently.
items.author: Zhaoying Pan, Yipei Wang, Shenyu Lu et al.

items.title: Chiral waveguide model for error-correctable quantum computation
items.summary: We develop a first-principles framework connecting microscopic waveguide scattering to quantum error correction and algorithmic performance. For polarization-encoded single photons interacting with an ensemble of two-level atoms in a chiral waveguide, we derive an effective polarization quantum channel by tracing out the frequency degree of freedom. Using this channel as the physical noise model for a rotated planar code, we observe threshold behavior as the number of atoms $N$ and the atom-waveguide coupling strength $Γ$ are varied. An asymptotic analysis of the microscopic scattering model explains the threshold scaling with $NΓ/σ$, where $σ$ is the photon spectral bandwidth. For identical, lossless atoms with symmetric real coupling and a photon spectrum centered at resonance, the effective noise is strongly biased toward $X$ errors.
items.author: Zixiang Hong

items.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
items.summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients.
items.author: Majdi Hassan, Marta Skreta, Dominique Beaini et al.

items.title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
items.summary: Motivated by reinforcement learning subject to communication constraints, we study a policy evaluation problem with linear function approximation over a rate-limited channel. In our setup, an agent interacting with an unknown environment (modeled as a Markov Decision Process) transmits quantized estimates of a temporal-difference (TD) learning update direction to a server over a finite-capacity channel. Our goal is to investigate to what extent one can preserve the statistical convergence rates achievable when the channel has infinite capacity. To that end, we propose a new algorithm called Batched Adaptively Quantized TD (BAQ-TD), which uses batching to reduce the variance of the transmitted information, and adaptive quantization to encode innovations.
items.author: Sreejeet Maity, Aritra Mitra

items.title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
items.summary: Estimates of when photonic devices outgrow classical simulation are hard to compare: even for single-photon boson sampling, quoted thresholds range from 50 to 98 photons, as they rest on different tasks and assumptions. We propose as a common unit the time a classical computer needs to draw one sample from the device's exact output distribution, up to floating-point rounding. Only exactness applies equally to every kind of light, since the cost of approximate sampling depends on the accuracy required. The simulability frontier is the device size at which our fastest exact sampler produces one sample per second on a fixed machine; this device size increases with better hardware and algorithms.
items.author: Jean Senellart, Benjamin Stott, Stephen Wein et al.

items.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history.
items.author: Haozhen Zhang, Bohan Liu, Jianzhu Bao et al.

items.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
items.summary: Anomaly detection (AD) is a critical for trustworthy machine learning and scientific discovery. Existing methods typically define anomalies through local density, isolation heuristics, or distance from a fitted distribution, making them sensitive to neighborhood scale, partitioning choices, or restrictive distributional assumptions. In this work, we introduce a new paradigm by formulating anomaly detection from a diversity perspective. We propose the $\textit{Vendi Anomaly Score}$ (VAS), which detects anomalies by quantifying how much a sample changes the diversity of the dataset, as measured by the Vendi score, when removed. VAS captures both local redundancy and global data structure without relying on density estimation or partitioning heuristics.
items.author: Amey Pasarkar, Adji Bousso Dieng

items.title: NASA’s Chandra Finds Source of Star’s Mysterious Outbursts

A new study, published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit […]

items.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
items.summary: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling.
items.author: Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang et al.

items.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
items.summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that neural networks are converging toward similar representation spaces. As language models become more capable, their representations are aligning with those of vision models. However, recent work has questioned whether this trend continues to hold for newer language models. Moreover, it has been shown that representation similarity metrics can be confounded by model depth and width, requiring appropriate baselines for interpretation. In this work, we first investigate where alignment emerges between unimodal models across model layers and representation dimensions. Next, we find that the PRH capability-alignment trend persists for newer models as long as the captions are sufficiently clean and informative.
items.author: Julia Herbst, Simon Roschmann, Quentin Bouniot et al.

items.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve an agent's task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements. We study this reward-driven misalignment, including reward hacking, through verifiable reward--context conflicts, where compliant task completion remains feasible while some executable shortcuts earn more reward than every compliant strategy. Encoding these conflicts in task dynamics lets us generate diverse interactive environments at scale and derive compliance feedback from execution histories. In resource and reporting workflows, task optimization increases real productivity through unauthorized resource use or raises reported scores while actual work declines. Controlled changes in the training distribution show that minority conflict exposure can still lead to widespread shortcut acquisition, reaching 97.9\% certified profitable violations on an API task under a 25\% conflict mixture after 128 updates.
items.author: Xinjie Shen
