items.title: Risk Benefit Analysis of Restarting Antithrombotic Medications After Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization in Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
items.summary: Background and objectives Middle meningeal artery (MMA) embolization is used in chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH). The safety of resuming antithrombotic (AT) therapy after MMA embolization remains unclear. This study evaluates the impact of AT resumption on hematoma resolution, recurrence, and reoperation rates, while assessing thromboembolic risks associated with interrupting AT therapy. Methods A retrospective review was conducted of patients undergoing MMA embolization for cSDH at a Level I trauma center from 2020 to 2023. Cases were stratified based on postprocedural AT resumption. Primary outcomes included >50% reduction in cSDH size and reoperation rate. Secondary outcomes included recurrence, functional outcomes measured by the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), and rate of thromboembolic complications in patients who withheld AT medications.
items.author: Gong AD, Kareddy A, Stuebe C, Pham D, Brewer C, Diekemper N, Awan O, Dang DD, Chaudhry S, McEachern J, Greenberg E, Chitale A.

items.title: Immediate Femoral Closure Without Mobility Restrictions: Using the CELT ACD ® for Neuroendovascular Interventions.
items.summary: Background and objectives A vascular closure device that provides rapid hemostasis is useful for neuroendovascular patients, especially for those with altered mental status or high intracranial pressure that limits compliance with bedrest. CELT ACD ® (arterial closure device) has demonstrated effectiveness and safety in non-neurological cohorts, and thus, the aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of CELT in neuroendovascular interventions. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study at our institution, enrolling consecutive patients undergoing neuroendovascular intervention with femoral access and subsequent CELT closure. We used a CELT-first approach for femoral closure during the study period, with all patients undergoing immediate head-of-bed (HOB) elevation postprocedurally.
items.author: Sorrentino ZA, Yang W, Saini N, Dagra A, Sarathy D, Lucke-Wold B, Robinson CP, Koch MJ, Hoh BL, Chalouhi N.

items.title: A Novel Method for the Temporary Treatment of Sunken Flap Syndrome: A Presentation of 3 Cases.
items.summary: Background and importance Sunken flap syndrome (SFS) is a neurological decline that results from paradoxical brain shift following decompressive hemicraniectomy. It is thought to arise from a gradient between atmospheric and intracranial pressure and can cause neurological morbidity if not surgically corrected. In most cases, this involves autologous or synthetic cranioplasty. However, in select patient populations, this is not possible-either because of recent infection, availability of cranioplasty implant, anticoagulant use, or other patient-specific factors. Clinical presentation In this case report, we present 3 patients with SFS who could not undergo cranioplasty due to a recent surgical site infection. Instead, their SFS was managed nonoperatively with a makeshift "external cranioplasty" that resulted in significant improvement in their midline shift and mental status.
items.author: Rodrigues A, Jha R, Prochilo G, Stapleton C.

items.title: Preventive Linear Ablation Strategy for Intra-Atrial Reentrant Tachycardia Following Cardiac Surgery.
items.summary: Aims Intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia (IART) frequently occurs following cardiac surgery due to scar-related conduction abnormalities. While advances in mapping technologies have improved the acute success rate of catheter ablation, arrhythmia recurrence remains a significant clinical concern. This study aimed to evaluate whether a preventive linear ablation strategy guided by voltage mapping improves the long-term success rate of catheter ablation in patients with IART post-cardiac surgery. Methods and results A total of 46 consecutive patients following cardiac surgery who underwent atrial tachycardia ablation between 2022 and 2024 were enrolled in the study group. After activation mapping-guided ablation for ongoing IART, preventive linear ablation was performed based on voltage mapping.
items.author: Chen J, Pan T, Liu Y, Chen Z, Zhao Y, Bai J, Shen W, Xu W.

items.title: Combined Transnasal and Transcranial Approach for a Complex Type IV Nasal Dermoid Sinus Cyst.
items.summary: Background and importance Nasal dermoid sinus cysts (NDSCs) are rare congenital midline anomalies caused by incomplete separation of ectoderm and neuroectoderm during embryogenesis. Intracranial extension, although uncommon, increases the risk of infection, recurrence, and neurological complications. Hartley type IV lesions involve the intradural compartment and represent the most complex subtype. Clinical presentation A 13-year-old boy presented with a congenital nasal tip pit associated with recurrent swelling and serous discharge since age 9. MRI and computed tomography revealed a midline fistulous tract extending through the foramen cecum, with extradural intrafalcine and intradural frontobasal components, consistent with a type IV NDSC. Complete excision was achieved through a combined transnasal interalar and transcranial transfrontal approach.
items.author: Peron S, Palopoli A, Scalise M, Sicuri M, Campione A, Rusconi A, Colombo S, Bianchini E, Stefini R.

items.title: Presence of Human Papillomaviruses in the Normal-Appearing Hypopharyngeal Mucosa: A Prospective Study.
items.summary: Objective Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a well-established etiological factor in oropharyngeal cancer, whereas its role in the hypopharynx is less well understood. This prospective study investigated the prevalence of HPV in normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based HPV detection. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing hypopharyngoscopy, laryngomicroscopy, or transnasal esophagogastroscopy for benign indications were prospectively recruited. Biopsies were obtained from normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa and analyzed for HPV DNA by PCR-based genotyping. Participants completed a questionnaire addressing HPV-related risk factors. Results Tissue samples were collected from 53 patients (median age, 51 years; range, 18-85 years), of whom 32 (60.4%) were female.
items.author: Järvenpää P, Auvinen E, Silling S, Akgül B, Aaltonen LM.

items.title: A rare cause of acute bilateral visual loss in pregnancy: seronegative inflammatory optic neuritis.
items.summary: Optic neuritis is an inflammatory disorder of the optic nerve and a common cause of acute visual loss in young adults. Although frequently associated with multiple sclerosis, a substantial proportion of cases remain seronegative for aquaporin-4 (AQP4-IgG) and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG-IgG) antibodies. Seronegative inflammatory optic neuritis, defined in this context as negative testing for AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG, remains a heterogeneous and incompletely understood entity. Severe bilateral involvement is uncommon and poses diagnostic challenges, particularly during pregnancy. We report a 29-year-old woman at 29 weeks of gestation who presented with acute bilateral visual loss evolving over several days, severe ocular pain, headache, and vomiting.
items.author: Rodríguez Sánchez MA, Morales Flores OE, Olguin Guizado CA, Corrales Sarabia YG, Angulo Lapizco EA, Flores Gutiérrez SM, Figueroa Zaldívar JM.

items.title: Kikuchi-Fujimoto Disease Presenting as Necrotic Cervical Lymphadenopathy Mimicking Tuberculous Lymphadenitis in a Young Woman With Strong Familial Autoimmunity: A Case Report.
items.summary: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD), also known as histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis, is a rare and usually self-limiting condition that predominantly affects young adults, particularly women. It commonly presents with fever and cervical lymphadenopathy and may be accompanied by weight loss, night sweats, and fatigue. Due to its nonspecific presentation, KFD can mimic infectious, malignant, and autoimmune conditions, making diagnosis challenging. We report the case of a 20-year-old woman with a significant family history of autoimmune disease who presented with a two-week history of intermittent fever, progressively painful left-sided cervical lymphadenopathy, weight loss, night sweats, and lethargy. Initial investigations revealed leukopenia and raised inflammatory markers, while computed tomography demonstrated bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy with a necrotic left cervical lymph node.
items.author: David R, Khan Basheer J.

items.title: Effects of Overripe Banana Processing Techniques on the Chemical Composition and Attractancy to Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
items.summary: The rising incidence of vector-borne diseases transmitted by mosquitoes has become a significant public health concern. The increasing resistance of mosquitoes to conventional insecticides has prompted the need for alternative control strategies such as Attractive Targeted Sugar Baits (ATSBs). While fruit-based attractants have shown promise, the impact of different production methods on their attractiveness remains underexplored. This study investigates the effect of three production techniques of overripe banana (Musa acuminata) extracts: liquid extraction, syrup concentration, and freeze-drying, on the chemical composition and their attractiveness to Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Extracts were infused into hydrogel beads and tested in dual-choice olfactometer assays to mosquito vectors Ae.
items.author: Abuelmaali, S. A., Hui, L. W., Sabar, S. A. et al.

items.title: Engineered microvessel networks -- Longitudinal transcriptomic profiling validates chip-grown tissues as a robust model for studying vasculature
items.summary: Vascularised Organ-on-Chip (OoC) models are promising New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), but their translation requires validation for defined Contexts of Use (CoU). Here, we combine microfluidic microvessel networks (MVNs) with longitudinal bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to determine how cell provenance influences engineered vascular phenotype. Stromal cell identity produced distinct network architectures and transcriptional trajectories, demonstrating that support cells, commonly treated as interchangeable, represent an important CoU variable. Primary human pancreatic microvascular endothelial cells failed to form stable perfusable networks, but supplementation with 10% Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells (HUVECs) or Blood Outgrowth Endothelial Cells (BOECs) rescued self-assembly. Single-cell transcriptomics identified specialised endothelial populations associated with vascular morphogenesis, including tip, stalk, phalanx, endothelial to mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and pericyte-like endothelial cells.
items.author: Osorio, L. A., Hansen, B., Suba, K. et al.

items.title: PROST: An Open Toolbox, Harmonised Multi-Lab Dataset, and Meta-Analysis of Ankle-Foot Roll-Over Shape
items.summary: The ankle-foot roll-over shape (ROS) is the sagittal-plane path of the centre of pressure (CoP) during the stance phase of walking, expressed in a shank-based coordinate system. It describes the effective rocker geometry that emerges from both the shape and the elastic deformation of the ankle-foot system during walking, and informs prosthetic and orthotic design. Previous studies characterised ROS in small samples with differing laboratory protocols, so they have not systematically assessed inter-individual variability or its relation to anthropometrics. We developed the open-source Public ROS Toolbox (PROST) for standardised ROS computation, and used it to harmonise marker trajectories, ground reaction forces and CoP data from four public gait datasets collected in independent laboratories.
items.author: Reichsbouscher, C., Solav, D.

items.title: MorphoANOVA: Dissecting Histology-Gene Expression Relationships in Spatial Transcriptomics
items.summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures the expression of hundreds to thousands of genes within tissue architecture, often accompanied by histology images. However, it remains challenging to systematically characterize which genes exhibit associations with tissue morphology, whether these associations vary spatially, and which genes show additional spatial expression patterns beyond those captured by morphology. Here we introduce MorphoANOVA, a gene-wise statistical framework for characterizing morphology--expression relationships across genes measured by ST. Using nested spatially varying coefficient models and sequential ANOVA, MorphoANOVA assesses slide-wide associations with an H\&E-derived morphology feature, location-specific changes in these associations, and additional spatial variation after accounting for the selected feature.
items.author: Chen, P.-W., Yan, G., Yu, S. et al.

items.title: Synthetic chromatin engineering for STAT1 reactivation toward restoring cisplatin sensitivity in breast cancer
items.summary: Chemoresistant cancers acquire transcriptomic and epigenetic alterations through changes in transcription factor activity and chromatin accessibility. Integrative in silico analyses identified STAT1 as a recurrently suppressed transcription factor in cisplatin-resistant breast cancer. Using cisplatin-resistant triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) MDA-MB-231 cells, we further confirmed reduced STAT1 expression and activity, accompanied by defective nuclear translocation, indicating that suppression of STAT1 signaling contributes to cisplatin resistance in breast cancer. To restore STAT1 activity, we sought to promote its nuclear localization and transcriptional activation through chromatin engineering. Based on the identification of PHF6 as a direct STAT1-binding protein through in silico and in vitro analyses, we engineered Dual Reader 3 (DR3), a PHF6-derived synthetic chromatin regulator designed to enhance both STAT1 interaction and chromatin engagement through histone H2B ubiquitination.
items.author: Park, I.-G., Kwon, M., Yoo, T. h. et al.

items.title: Programmable interphyla communication for Staphylococcus aureus by transferability of homoserine lactone sensors between Bacillales bacteria
items.summary: Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive opportunistic pathogen of the order Bacillales and a frequent member of human-associated microbiomes. Despite its clinical relevance, engineering S. aureus and the communities it inhabits remains limited by a shortage of well-characterized genetic tools for precise control of gene expression and intercellular signaling. Biosensors for homoserine lactones (HSLs) are widely used in Gram-negative bacteria, as HSLs are small, passively diffusible signaling molecules for and their sensors are tightly regulated. Here, we show that synthetically designed HSL sensors using LuxR-family regulators are highly functional in S. aureus. Notably, synthetic designs previously built for the Gram-positive model Bacillus subtilis, a distantly related Bacillales, transferred functionally and establish repurposing the genetic toolbox as an effective strategy for importing these functions into S.
items.author: Sarker, B., Rondthaler, S. N., Zeng, M. et al.

items.title: Early visual cortex is not functionally necessary for temporal attention: A TMS study
items.summary: Temporal attention enhances the selective processing of information at a specific point in time and improves perception. Previous neuroimaging studies investigating its neural mechanisms have either conflated temporal attention with temporal expectation or provided correlational evidence. Thus, whether early visual cortex is functionally necessary for temporal attention remains unknown. Here, we combined psychophysics with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to examine whether V1/V2 are functionally necessary and play a causal role in temporal attention. Observers performed an orientation-discrimination task in which two consecutive stimuli, T1 and T2, were presented in the periphery, preceded by a precue providing either valid or neutral temporal information.
items.author: Lee, H.-H., Carrasco, M.

items.title: Novel Tau Interaction Partners as Potential Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets in Neurodegenerative Diseases
items.summary: Alzheimers disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder leading to cognitive decline and ultimately death. One of the main hallmarks of this disease is the accumulation of pathological tau protein into neurofibrillary tangles. To better understand these pathological mechanisms, it is essential to characterize the tau protein interactome in health and disease. In this study, we performed a yeast two-hybrid screening using a human brain cDNA library, from which we identified 15 novel tau-interacting proteins that bind to full-length human tau, or its fragments: the N-terminus, microtubule-binding domain, or C-terminus. We subsequently validated these novel interactions using in vitro co-immunoprecipitation and colocalization assays with both physiological and pathological tau isoforms.
items.author: Pichlerova, K., Sinsky, J., Njemoga, S. et al.

items.title: Polyphyletic origins and lineage-specific expansion of chemosensory systems in phylum Actinomycetota
items.summary: Phylum Actinomycetota (syn. Actinobacteriota or Actinobacteria), one of the largest well-studied bacterial phyla, is renowned for complex morphology, non-motility, ecological versatility, and secondary metabolite production. Chemosensory systems (CSS) are among the most sophisticated prokaryotic signal transduction architectures, yet their evolutionary distribution in this phylum remains poorly understood. Here, a comparative genomic analysis of 693 high-quality genomes spanning the phylum resolves the diversity, distribution, and evolutionary trajectories of CSS. Despite extensive genomic complexity and ecological versatility, only 6.9% of genomes encode complete CSS clusters, confined to a subset of lineages within a few classes, indicating lineage-specific retention or loss. In contrast, two-component systems (TCS) are ubiquitously abundant, with hybrid kinases enriched in CSS-deficient classes, suggesting functional compensation for the absence of dedicated chemosensory pathways.
items.author: S, S. N., Brighty, S., Sharma, G.

items.title: Hypoxic Stress Induces LARP1-Driven Stress Granules That Protect mRNAs from Decay to Sustain Mitotic Cell Cycle Progression
items.summary: Hypoxia is a defining feature of solid tumours that elicits extensive transcriptional and post-transcriptional adaptations. Stress granules (SGs) are frequently observed under hypoxia, yet how they assemble and whether they contribute to hypoxic gene regulation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that hypoxia induces SGs through an assembly mechanism distinct from that of classical acute stresses. Hypoxia SG formation occurs independently of the integrated stress response and instead requires the HIF1-REDD1-mTORCC1-4EBP1 axis. Remarkably, hypoxia SGs assemble despite robust ongoing translation, suggesting that additional mechanisms lower the threshold for RNA condensation. We identify LARP1 as a potential determinant of this process, where it promotes G3BP-dependent SG assembly specifically during hypoxia.
items.author: Lim, T., Ramanathan, J., Gao, H. et al.

items.title: A Standalone PD-1 Chimeric Switch Receptor T-Cell Platform Expands the Therapeutic Window of PD-L1 Targeting in Solid Tumors
items.summary: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a promising therapeutic target owing to its broad expression on tumor cells and immunosuppressive myeloid cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), providing an opportunity to target both cellular compartments. However, physiological PD-L1 expression in normal tissues poses a substantial risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity, limiting the therapeutic window and clinical translation of PD-L1-targeted cellular therapies. Here, we developed a standalone programmed death-1 (PD-1) chimeric switch receptor (CSR) T-cell platform designed to preserve the therapeutic advantages of PD-L1 targeting while improving tumor-normal discrimination. Iterative receptor engineering, with antitumor activity and normal-cell reactivity evaluated as parallel selection criteria, identified two lead PD-1 CSR T-cell candidates.
items.author: Luo, Y., Guo, S., Qie, Y. et al.

items.title: A Human Tumor Virus Recruits HSP70 Chaperone to Remodel Its Replisome on DNA
items.summary: Human Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCV) large T (LT) protein functions as a replication helicase analogous to the cellular MCM complex but requires a second MCV protein, small T (sT), for efficient LT-initiated replication. Both LT and sT encode highly-conserved DnaJ domains that bind to the cellular refolding molecule, heat shock protein 70 (HSP70). Using single-molecule imaging and FRET, we find that sT recruits dimeric HSP70 to serve as a molecular bridge between sT and LT on DNA and that this complex facilitates remodeling LT into a functional double-hexameric helicase. Disruption of LT-HSP70-HSP70-sT interaction with HSP70 inhibitors or by mutations to the LT-sT DnaJ domains collapse the LT-HSP70-HSP70-sT complex, abolishing sT-enhanced LT dodecamerization and ATP-dependent DNA unwinding.
items.author: Wan, L., Li, X., Vittot, P. et al.

items.title: Palindrome Presence, Location, and Structural Context Are Predictive of RNA Self-Association
items.summary: RNA self-association is a key elementary event behind many cellular processes from ribosome assembly, to regulation of gene expression, to assembly of biomolecular condensates. While RNAs self-interact in many ways, one direct and unambiguous sequence-encoded pattern for RNA self-recognition is a palindrome, or palindromic motif. In isolation palindromic motifs tend to fold back on themselves, favoring stable stem-loop secondary structures. However, palindromes have been implicated in some cases of RNA self-recognition, segregation and phase separation, raising the question of which palindromes in a given RNA are actually available for intermolecular engagement. Toward answering this question, we define three classes of palindromic regions based on local secondary-structure context, and degree of availability for interactions via their nucleobases, sorting into three classes.
items.author: Ahn, C., Park, H., Rodrigues, V. L. et al.

items.title: Age-associated repression of HNF4α is a driver and potential therapeutic target in liver metabolic dysfunction
items.summary: Aging is a major risk factors for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, the mechanisms by which aging disrupts hepatocyte transcriptional networks to drive metabolic dysfunction remain poorly understood. Hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha (HNF4) is a master regulator of hepatocyte identity and metabolic homeostasis, but its role in liver aging has not been defined. Here, we perform a comprehensive multi-omic profiling of young and aged mouse livers combined with targeted HNF4 functional studies to define how aging remodels HNF4-dependent gene regulation and whether HNF4 can be a target to reverse age-associated liver dysfunction. Despite preserved HNF4 expression with age, aging was associated with reduced HNF4 chromatin occupancy and transcriptional activity, accompanied by epigenetic remodeling, including changes in histone acetylation, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation.
items.author: Proulx, J., Lande, K. A., Lei, X. et al.

items.title: Inference of cell division parameters in bacteria under transient growth conditions
items.summary: Most quantitative models of bacterial cell division assume steady-state growth, yet natural environments are highly dynamic. Here, we infer division control parameters of E. coli from single-cell size trajectories under nonsteady growth. We describe growth as a continuous process interrupted by stochastic divisions, whose propensity depends on cell size and on the size added since birth. Combining an estimation of time-dependent single-cell growth rates with a maximum-likelihood estimator that we previously validated on synthetic data, we obtain time-resolved estimates of the mean added size at division, its noise, and a strategy parameter that measures how added size depends on birth size.
items.author: Nieto Acuna, C. A., Rezaee, S., Vargas-Garcia, C. A. et al.

items.title: Quantitative Head-to-Tail Analysis Reveals Heterogeneous Cellular Organization and Connexin Expression in the Porcine Sinoatrial Node
items.summary: Background: The sinoatrial node (SAN) is an integral component of the cardiac conduction system that dictates heart rhythm. Optical mapping studies have demonstrated functional differences between the superior and inferior leading pacemaking sites in the human SAN; however, the mechanistic connections between structure and function in the SAN through intra-tissue and inter-tissue current source-sink relationships have not been fully resolved. Methods: Porcine SAN longitudinal cryosections along the head-to-tail axis were immunostained and analyzed for regional cell organization and connexin (CX) isoform expression. Results: Quantification of pacemaking cardiomyocyte (PCM) density revealed >9-fold more PCMs within a SAN volume than suggested by a widely cited estimate, assuming comparable PCM densities across species.
items.author: Kao, H. K. J., Smithers, R. L., Ramos-Rodriguez, D. H. et al.

items.title: Unbiased lineage tracing across the adipose organ decouples developmental origin from anatomical and transcriptomic identities
items.summary: The developmental origins of individual adipose depots and whether embryonic lineage dictates adult function remain unresolved. Here, we apply in utero CRISPR-mediated barcoding lineage tracing to construct the first unbiased clonal map of adipose organ development in mice. The developmental hierarchy we uncover challenges several conventions. Remarkably, interscapular brown fat, used as the prototypical brown fat, is the most developmentally isolated brown fat; depots sharing Myf5/Pax3 lineage markers fail to cluster together; mesenteric white fat shares unexpected high clonal ancestry with brown fats despite a radically divergent transcriptome; and subcutaneous white adipose tissues converge transcriptomically despite distant developmental origins. These findings call for a reinterpretation of single-marker lineage tracing data across the adipose organ and propose that adipose depot identity is not solely encoded by embryonic lineage but is substantially shaped by the anatomical niche.
items.author: Inoue, O., Singh, A., Ginugu, M. et al.

items.title: Age-dependent mechanical stress underlies unexpected vestibular differentiation and regeneration patterns
items.summary: Loss of inner-ear sensory hair cells (HCs) is a major cause of hearing and balance disorders. Promoting HC regeneration offers a potential therapeutic strategy, but regenerative capacity is limited in adult mammals and declines rapidly during early postnatal development in mice. HCs can regenerate through trans-differentiation of neighboring supporting cells in a process controlled by Notch mediated lateral inhibition. However, the factors underlying the decrease in regeneration capacity are poorly understood. Here, we combine live imaging with single-HC ablation in mouse vestibular explants to track the dynamics of HC development and regeneration. We reveal unexpected age-dependent deviations from the classical lateral inhibition model, in which new HCs differentiate adjacent to existing HCs.
items.author: Inbar Kasirer, S., Shraga, M., Dullweber, T. et al.

items.title: Signals beneath the ectoderm: Mesodermal FGF signaling keeps the dorsally closing epithelium in shape
items.summary: Morphogenesis requires coordinated biochemical signaling, actomyosin contractility and dynamic adhesion within and between tissues. During Drosophila development, ectodermal fibroblast growth factor (FGF) ligands regulate mesoderm morphogenesis through the FGF receptor (FGFR) Heartless. We find that the mesoderm reciprocally influences ectodermal morphogenesis. We show that loss of the FGF ligands Pyramus or Thisbe, Heartless, or its adaptor Stumps transforms normally straight dorsal seams and the formed dorsal epidermis into highly distorted, dynamically changing zigzags during dorsal closure. In these mutants, mesoderm is specified but defective. Mesodermal expression of Heartless restores epithelial stability in heartless mutants, whereas ectodermal expression does not. Genetic ablation of mesoderm produces more extensive seam distortions that persist beyond the end of closure, thereby displacing the dorsal midline.
items.author: Amini, M., Mortensen, R. D., Fogerson, S. M. et al.

items.title: Dynamic mechanical sorting biases niche occupancy and lineage outcome during development of bilayered glandular epithelia
items.summary: Tissue compartmentalization into basal and luminal domains is a hallmark of glandular epithelia, yet how fate boundaries are established and stabilized during dynamic morphogenesis remains a major unresolved question. Here, using mouse embryonic explants, organoids, quantitative live imaging and genetic perturbations, we show that basal-luminal compartmentalization is not maintained by fixed boundaries, but through continuous positional corrections. We show that differences in cellular adhesion and actomyosin contractility drive these positional corrections by promoting active cell sorting. We further find that these mechanical differences influence lineage specification by controlling cell positioning rather than directly instructing cell fate. Before commitment, mosaic, but not uniform, perturbation of cell mechanics alters niche occupancy and biases lineage outcome, indicating that relative mechanical properties determine access to fate-instructive niches.
items.author: Journot, R. P., Deshayes, T., Harari, L. et al.

items.title: Tree cavities as attractors: an experimental test of the effects of woodpecker legacy on local bird activity and species richness
items.summary: Tree cavities, whether excavated by birds or formed through wood decay, are key structural features of forest ecosystems. They are critical resources for secondary cavity users and influence breeding bird assemblages by affecting the occurrence and abundance of certain species. However, the effect of an individual cavity on fine-scale bird activity, independently of the surrounding habitat context, remains poorly understood. Here, we experimentally tested the effect of cavity presence on bird activity in a coniferous forest in southern Poland. We installed pairs of standardized, debarked snags, each consisting of one snag with an artificial entrance resembling a woodpecker-excavated cavity and one control snag without a cavity entrance.
items.author: Wolska, A., Trybala, M., Ciach, M.

items.title: Gregariousness can promote invasion success of pest insects while higher environmental heterogeneity decreases it
items.summary: Climate change and environmental homogenization are expected to facilitate the expansion of many forest pest insect species and increase the vulnerability of forest ecosystems to insect outbreaks. At present, we lack empirical data on how the antipredator defence traits of pest insects interact with the local environmental conditions and shape outbreak risk. Here we study this and ask 1) how the antipredator defence strategy of pest insects shapes survival under naturally varying predator community, and 2) how is predation risk shaped by the diversity and structure of forests? We tested these questions by conducting a field predation experiment with artificial prey system (prey items made from edible dough) where we manipulated the gregariousness, unpalatability and defensive colouration of prey and tested their effects on prey survival.
items.author: Jonsson, M., Korhonen, V., Guilbault, E. et al.

items.title: Two decades of EU pesticide substitution have not reduced impacts on stream invertebrates
items.summary: Chemical regulation assumes that withdrawing hazardous substances and replacing them with alternatives reduces environmental harm. We tested this premise within the EU pesticide regulatory framework using a 23-year record of event-driven pesticide exposure and stream-invertebrate communities from 152 German agricultural streams sampled between 1998 and 2021. Neither pesticide toxic pressure nor pesticide-related invertebrate impairment showed a detectable decline over time, and an improvement equivalent to one ecological status class can be excluded. Dominant toxicity drivers shifted from organophosphates to neonicotinoids and subsequently to pyrethroids, yet the relationship between toxic pressure and community effects remained consistent despite their distinct modes of action.
items.author: Gröning, J., Liess, M.

items.title: The tiger shark, Galeocerdo cuvier (Peron & Lesueur, 1822), genome reveals genomic and epigenomic signatures of shark evolution and demographic history
items.summary: Cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) represent one of the oldest extant vertebrate lineages, persisting for over 450 million years, yet genomic resources remain limited for many species despite widespread conservation concern. The tiger shark, Galeocerdo cuvier (Peron & Lesueur, 1822), the sole surviving member of the family Galeocerdonidae, is a circumglobally cosmopolitan predator vital in ecosystem regulation but is experiencing population declines. Here, we generated the first chromosome-scale haplotype-phased reference genome for the tiger shark and integrated comparative and population genomics with methylomics to characterise its genome architecture and evolutionary history. This assembly presented the first evidence of male heterogamety in this species.
items.author: Pearce, J. R., Doran, A., De Jong, E. et al.

items.title: Phosphorylation-dependent conformational change in the Keratin 19 head domain: Implications for filament assembly and binding to GSK3β and 14-3-3
items.summary: Keratins are intermediate filament (IF) proteins expressed in various cell types, playing a crucial role in mechanical support and signaling pathways. Keratin 19 (K19) is predominantly found in gut epithelia and early embryonic ectoderm. K19 interacts with signaling proteins such as GSK3{beta} and 14-3-3 to participate in cell signaling pathways. However, details on the binding sites of these proteins on K19, and specific molecular mechanisms governing these interactions, are lacking. Additionally, the N-terminal head domains of IFs including K19 are considered intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), and their atomic-resolution structures are unavailable. Using NMR spectroscopy, we obtained the first solution structures of K19 head domain peptides.
items.author: Ji, Y., Jeong, M., Kim, J. et al.

items.title: The ganglioside profile of mouse brain does not respond to changes in dietary n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid supply
items.summary: Long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LC-PUFAs) of the n-3 and n-6 families are major components of brain lipids, both in terms of levels and biological significance. They play crucial roles in various neurological processes. The brain is largely dependent on food supply of LC-PUFAs and its lipid composition can be modulated by changes in dietary intake. Sufficient dietary supply of the n-3 LC-PUFAs as well as a balanced n-6/n-3 ratio are required for proper brain development and function. As dietary intervention using n-3 LC-PUFAs is considered a promising therapeutic approach to prevent or treat brain disorders, it is important to understand the associated biochemical changes as well as the mechanisms underlying the biological effects.
items.author: MASSON, E. A. Y., MARTINE, L., CABARET, S. et al.

items.title: Vasopressin V2 receptor phosphopeptide reshapes the conformational landscape of arrestin-2 beyond C-tail detachment
items.summary: Binding of phosphorylated GPCR tails influences arrestin conformation, but the contribution of this interaction to the interdomain rotation associated with activation remains incompletely characterised. In particular, it remains unclear whether displacement of the arrestin C-tail is sufficient to favor larger interdomain rotations or whether the bound phosphotail exerts an additional effect on the conformational landscape. Here, we used enhanced-sampling simulations to characterise the conformational free-energy landscapes of basal (unbound) and V2Rpp-bound arrestin-2. We find that V2Rpp binding broadened the range of energetically accessible interdomain rotation angles relative to basal arrestin-2. However, the pronounced rotation observed in the experimental structures, while accessible, was not strongly favored.
items.author: Bzowka, M., Feser, R., Aureli, S. et al.

items.title: Modular assembly of mitochondrial complex III from a dynamic matrix domain pool
items.summary: Mitochondrial complex III is a central component of the cellular energy metabolism. It is an obligate dimer of catalytic and accessory subunits that are encoded by two genomes. How its large matrix domain, formed by the core proteins Qcr1 and Qcr2, is built and joined to the membrane part and during assembly is not known. Here we show that Qcr1 and Qcr2 preassemble independently of complex III into matrix domain modules. Cryo-EM structures from a cardiolipin-deficient yeast strain and of recombinant protein resolved single, double and triple matrix domains, which are linked by the C-terminal tail of Qcr1. In the mature complex III, the same tail binds cytochrome b and cardiolipin.
items.author: Jimenez-Niebla, J., Jha, R., Wirth, C. et al.

items.title: Distinct mechanical signatures of dairy and plant-based cheeses
items.summary: Plant-based cheeses account for about 1% of U.S. retail cheese sales and often fail to match the texture and flavor of dairy cheese. Here we compare three commercial dairy and plant-based pairs, cheddar, feta, and mozzarella, with texture profile analysis (n = 60), tension, compression, and shear tests (n = 219), constitutive artificial neural networks, and a consumer panel (n = 306). Plant mozzarella is at least five times stiffer than dairy mozzarella at small strain, yet softer and less cohesive under 50% compression. Plant feta matches the initial stiffness of dairy feta but shows a peak in its shear response.
items.author: Koosis, A. O., Darwin, E. C., Ellingsen, V. et al.

items.title: Benchmarking foundation models for resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging time series in cognitive aging research
items.summary: Foundation models trained on large neuroimaging datasets could help smaller studies investigate cognition from brain recordings. However, whether the foundation model-derived representations improve assessment of current cognition, prediction of follow-up cognition, or characterization of cognitive change remains unclear. We evaluated nine configurations from five model families that process regional resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging time series, using 3,103 scans from 1,653 participants across two observational and five intervention aging cohorts. Primary frozen representations showed no consistent superiority over conventional functional connectivity for concurrent cognitive associations or diagnostic classification. Changing the readout improved selected concurrent cognitive associations without updating model weights, indicating that performance depended partly on how representations were extracted.
items.author: Liu, Y. M., Ai, M., Zhao, K. et al.

items.title: He spent a year on ‘Mars’: NASA science officer emerges from mock mission
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03588-w Engineer Matthew Montgomery, who just finished a 378-day simulated Mars mission, talks about what it was like to be out of contact with the rest of humanity for…
items.author: Kaia Glickman

items.title: The super El Niño is more than a climate shock – it’s a health one, too
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03628-5 Food shortages and disease outbreaks are to be expected and need to be addressed together.

items.title: How to make failure your friend and teacher in science
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03654-3 Apprentices develop expertise after doing monotonous tasks repeatedly and learning from their mistakes. Scientists are no different, argues Ruth Morgan.
items.author: Dom Byrne

items.title: Carlo Rovelli says fundamental physics is overrated
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03626-7 The theoretical physicist unpacks the need for more humility in science and whether artificial intelligence could ever become conscious.
items.author: Chris Stokel-Walker

items.summary: Nature, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03631-w Scientists say governments must commit to carbon dioxide removal if world is to bring temperatures back down to safer limits.

items.title: How academic freedom is changing around the world — by the numbers
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02998-0 Nature reports on five countries where academic freedom has either plummeted or soared in recent years.

items.title: Nanohertz gravitational waves and asymmetric dark matter from a supercooled dark sector phase transition
items.summary: We study the connection between asymmetric dark matter and nanohertz gravitational waves from a supercooled first-order phase transition in a classically conformal dark sector. The dark sector contains a real scalar, a complex scalar and a Dirac fermion, whose mass arises from radiative symmetry breaking. An additional Affleck--Dine condensate generates a fermion asymmetry and heats the dark bath before nucleation. The conserved dark charge fixes the asymmetry between fermions and antifermions, while entropy production during delayed visible-sector reheating dilutes the relic and determines the redshift of the gravitational-wave spectrum. We calculate the thermal nucleation rate in a three-dimensional effective theory with finite-density corrections, next-to-leading-order contributions and fluctuation determinants (NLOdet).

items.title: The $φ$-$η$ Puzzle and the Five-Layer Effective-Temperature Hierarchy in $pp$ Collisions at 2.76 and 7 TeV
items.summary: Sequential kinetic freeze-out in high-energy collisions probes the dynamics governing the final stages of strongly interacting matter. Inspired by the recently established quadruple freeze-out scenario, we present a thermodynamic analysis of transverse momentum spectra for a set of identified particles produced in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 2.76$ and $7$ TeV. Using a modified Tsallis-Pareto function, we extract the effective temperature and the non-extensivity parameter for each species. We observe a robust five-layer hierarchy in the effective temperature. At both energies, the layers are: non-strange hadrons, singly-strange hadrons, multi-strange hadrons, light nuclei, and the $φ(1020)$ meson. At $7$~TeV, the $η$ meson joins the $φ(1020)$ meson in the highest-temperature layer.

items.title: Regret without Optimal-Arm Feedback under Reward-Dependent Delays
items.summary: We study stochastic bandits with reward-dependent delays, possibly infinite, whose reports omit the originating round. For each $c\in[0,1)$, Balanced Historical Optimism (BHO) has a delay term controlled by the largest suboptimal-arm quantile at level $1-cΔ_i$, without requiring optimal-arm reports. Lower bounds give an inverse-square slack cost in the logarithmic statistical regime and linear minimax regret at $c=1$. A family with growing $K$ forces worst-case regret $Ω(G\log K)$ for every learner, where $G=\max_iΔ_i h_i$ is the largest gap-weighted suboptimal cutoff. Pending-triggered balance preserves BHO's weighted-cutoff bound for $c<1$ and attains the historical-greedy exploration coefficient with deterministic rewards, a unique optimum and fixed bounded delays.
items.author: Zhong Han

items.title: Learning through Capacity Awareness to Minimize Hospital Readmissions
items.summary: Predictive algorithms are increasingly used to guide hospital discharge decisions, yet these models can exhibit censoring bias for vulnerable patients due to insufficient historical data or past discharge decisions. When biased readmission risk predictors are used to inform discharges, the training data generated by discharge decisions may perpetuate similar biases when predictors are re-trained, leading to a vicious cycle. We extend a queueing-based Markov decision process for hospital discharge to incorporate periodically retrained readmission risk predictors. Our key insight is that cost-optimal, "capacity-aware" operational decision policies can naturally diversify the lengths of stay at which patient outcomes are observed, enabling consistent estimation of readmission risk without explicit fairness constraints.
items.author: Lydia T. Liu, Kara Schechtman, Pengyi Shi et al.

items.title: CallCleaner: Lightweight Bioacoustic Denoising from an Audio Foundation Model
items.summary: Many studies of animal vocalizations require clean recordings, but animals are usually recorded in the field, with background noise from weather, vehicles, and other animals. Animal vocalization denoising is challenged by the scarcity of clean training data and the extreme diversity of animal vocalizations. Classical spectral gates leave residual noise, especially without voice activity detection (VAD), while detector-free neural denoisers designed for bioacoustics remove less noise. We show that a general-purpose source separation foundation model, SAM-Audio, removes more noise than either of these types of methods, when used without training and prompted with time spans from a simple animal VAD.
items.author: Michael Xie, Gašper Beguš, Morris Alper

items.title: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration
items.summary: Autonomous UAV exploration is increasingly used for large-scale surveying and inspection in inaccessible or disaster-affected environments, where onboard memory and computational resources are often severely constrained. Most existing UAV exploration systems maintain globally queryable geometric map representations for motion planning and exploration decision-making, causing memory consumption and spatial-query costs to increase with the explored area. Robot-centric local mapping bounds dense-map memory and computation but discards global task context needed for long-horizon exploration.We present FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context. At the observation level, lightweight LiDAR-keyframe visibility records preserve ray-wise evidence for frontier reasoning.
items.author: Yizhe Zhang, Jianping Li, Yilun Gao et al.

items.title: MicroSim: Contrastive Graph Neural Networks for Binary Code Similarity Detection
items.summary: We present MicroSim, a system for binary code similarity detection that represents each function as a graph built from IDA Pro Hex-Rays microcode and compares such graphs with a contrastive Siamese graph neural network (GNN). We evaluate on the TREX cross-optimization benchmark, a corpus of 849,072 function-level microcode graphs spanning optimization levels -O0 through -O3, under a strict class-disjoint split in which no function key is shared between train and test. Under this protocol, MicroSim reaches 0.9972 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) and 0.9762 Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), outperforming Gemini (0.9332 ROC-AUC), SAFE (0.9752), and jTrans (0.9740) retrained on the same split, as well as a structure-free Bag-of-Words (BoW) baseline (0.9484).
items.author: Moussa Moussaoui, Tarik Houichime, Abdelghani Souhar et al.

items.title: One-Shot Hierarchical Federated Clustering for Distributed Non-IID Biomedical Data Analysis
items.summary: In multi-institutional biomedical data analysis, comprehensive disease profiles are often fragmented across different data silos. Furthermore, local data distributions typically exhibit varying levels of granularity or even complex nested structures. Although Hierarchical Clustering (HC) is a powerful tool for exploring such data topologies, its cumbersome recursive process incurs prohibitive computational overhead and renders it highly susceptible to privacy leakage. This paper, therefore, introduces an efficient one-shot hierarchical FC framework that performs client-end (institutions) distribution exploration and server-end distribution aggregation through one-way prototype-level communication from clients to the server. Although the designed one-shot prototype transmission guarantees minimal computational overhead and mitigates privacy risks, it inevitably incurs information loss.
items.author: Shenghong Cai, Yiqun Zhang

items.title: Robust and Private Swarm Learning via Zero-Knowledge Validator Admission and Consensus Aggregation
items.summary: Swarm Learning improves resilience and removes the need for a single trusted coordinator by distributing model aggregation and validation across participating nodes. However, it also delegates the validation of model updates to peers whose private data may be biased, unrepresentative, or adversarial, and existing Swarm Learning protocols generally do not attest that data, leaving decentralized validation as an attack surface. We present a robust, privacy-preserving Swarm Learning framework that makes verifiable data quality the condition for admission to the learning task. A validator joins only after a zero-knowledge attestation proves, without revealing any raw sample, that a reference model ran correctly on its private data.
items.author: Marco Arazzi, Mert Cihangiroglu, Antonino Nocera

items.title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
items.summary: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model.
items.author: Yitian Pang, Yifan Li, Xiaowei Yue et al.

items.title: RealEmbedBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Real-World Application-Layer Embedded Software Tasks
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) perform well on general coding tasks, but their capabilities in application-layer embedded software development remain underexplored. Existing embedded benchmarks primarily focus on hardware-in-the-loop validation in simulated environments. We introduce RealEmbedBench, a benchmark of 5,142 samples covering three application-layer tasks: code generation and completion, state machine modeling and implementation, and cross-OS code translation. We evaluate six representative LLMs and find substantial performance differences across tasks and models. Project context, especially the local code window, significantly affects code generation and completion. Models perform reasonably well at state machine modeling but struggle to translate these models into executable code.
items.author: Yujun Huang, Yuwei Zhang, Yi Zhou et al.

items.title: When Normality Shifts: Multi-Level WavLM Modeling for Open-World Audio Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Audio deepfake detectors trained with known synthesis attacks can learn generator-specific shortcuts that fail as synthesis systems and acoustic conditions evolve. We investigate an attack-free alternative: a normality model trained exclusively on bona fide speech, which scores synthetic audio by its deviation from authentic representations. We propose MLN-WavLM, a method that applies shrinkage-Mahalanobis modeling to pooled hidden states from a frozen large-scale, pre-trained speech processing WavLM Base+ architecture. Evaluated on ASVspoof 2019 LA, our best attack-free variant achieves an 8.45\% Equal Error Rate (EER), closely tracking a fully supervised WavLM-HM-Conformer baseline (7.86%). However, when subjected to the ASVspoof 2021 DF domain shift, performance drops to 22.12% EER, exposing vulnerabilities in the bona-fide-calibrated operating point.
items.author: Daniel Niekurzak, Daniel Kozuch, Weronika Folwarska et al.

items.title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: My Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge
items.summary: The CoRL 2026 RoboEval challenge has eight bimanual tasks, and it ranks a policy not only on whether it succeeds but on how: every stage of the task, done safely, efficiently and with both arms in coordination, scored against human demonstrations. My solution has two parts. The generic part, carried over from my LeHome challenge solution, is off-policy RL on a $π_{0.5}$-based policy that is also its own value function. It is trained with AWR and RECAP on advantages of the exact official score, in a loop where every rollout is at the same time a Thompson-sampling trial of about 20 inference parameters.
items.author: Ilia Larchenko

items.title: Identifiable alignment of unpaired representations
items.summary: Aligning two models without paired data requires a distance that both share, yet existing methods use Euclidean or spherical geometry. This is either an arbitrary choice or imposed by their loss function. We show that, under a precise form of the manifold hypothesis, the pullback of the data metric gives such a distance for any two models of one data-generating process. This holds whether the models are encoders, decoders or both, and whatever their architecture, loss, prior or training data. The alignment map preserves this distance and the distribution of representations, and is identifiable if and only if the data distribution breaks every symmetry of the data manifold.
items.author: Stas Syrota, Albert Lopez I Serrano, Johanne Franck et al.

items.title: MOMENT-DP: Momentum Aware Evaluation of Correlated Noise for Differentially Private Training
items.summary: Temporally correlated noise can substantially improve the utility of differentially private optimization, yet candidate mechanisms are commonly designed or evaluated using only partial information about the optimization process, such as workload structure, learning-rate schedules, or local curvature. We study whether persistent optimizer state provides additional information that can change the relative utility of privacy-valid correlated-noise mechanisms. We introduce MOMENT-DP, an optimizer-state-aware framework that models how temporally correlated privacy noise propagates through momentum-based optimization. For locally quadratic objectives, MOMENT-DP expresses privacy-induced final loss through an optimizer transfer operator that jointly captures curvature, learning-rate scheduling, momentum, and temporal noise covariance. NoiseCurve's curvature-aware quadratic criterion is recovered exactly as the zero-momentum, constant-learning-rate special case.
items.author: Sunny Gupta, Raja Viswanadha

items.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model on its own responses, guided by a fixed teacher. Generating these responses is expensive, so systems use quantized inference and asynchronous rollouts to reduce the cost. Both, however, introduce training-inference mismatch between the rollout engine and the model being trained. Such mismatch can destabilize reinforcement learning (RL), but its effects on OPD remain unclear. This paper investigates how much mismatch OPD tolerates, where its effects arise, and how training systems can use this tolerance. Measuring all mismatch sources on one scale, we examine quantization across three student-teacher pairs, with additional tests of weight staleness and injected noise on one pair.
items.author: Cong Yu, Ziting Wang, Songlin Jiang et al.

items.title: Learning to Rank Propagators in Constraint Programming
items.summary: The order in which propagators are executed can substantially affect the performance of constraint programming solvers, yet propagator priorities are typically determined by fixed, manually designed heuristics. In this work, we explore learning instance-dependent propagator priorities from static problem features. We formulate the task as a learning-to-rank problem, addressing the challenge that the quality of a priority assignment can be measured through solver runtime, while the desired priorities of individual propagators are not directly observable. A self-attention-based model jointly scores the propagators present in an instance and is trained using pairwise preferences derived from solver runtimes measured under randomized propagator priority assignments, with a Plackett-Luce-based ranking objective.
items.author: Matija Lojović, Mladen Nikolić

items.title: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary
items.summary: Advances in spatial understanding have enabled frontier models to power coding agents that control a real robot arm zero-shot and end-to-end, without task-specific demonstrations or retraining. This brings two new safety challenges. First, the extensive knowledge of frontier models lets these agents perform tasks that earlier VLA and WAM paradigms could not, opening the door to new forms of capability misuse. Second, coding agents can access digital resources such as web pages and emails. Threats in these resources, such as indirect prompt injection, can carry over into the physical world when the agent controls a robot. We therefore introduce ArmedAgent, the first systematic benchmark to evaluate both risks for coding agents performing zero-shot robot control.
items.author: Yiming Sun, Mi Zhang

items.title: Single-Radar Bilateral 3D Near-Field Imaging for Mobile Robots
items.summary: Mobile robots operating in homes need reliable 3D perception of nearby furniture and surrounding structures, yet recovering this information on both sides of the robot's path with a single forward-mounted millimeter-wave radar remains challenging because of near-field wavefront curvature, viewpoint-dependent target visibility, and limited elevation diversity. This paper presents a motion-assisted framework for reconstructing structures on both sides of a robot's trajectory. Our near-field model relates scene reflectivity to stepped-frequency multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) observations across frequencies and robot positions using spherical paths from transmitter (Tx) to scatterer to receiver (Rx). Bilateral Tx combining provides wideband directional weighting, while sliding-aperture back-projection coherently focuses the measurements using near-field propagation distances.
items.author: Yingqi Wang, Tingwei Chen, Zhongqin Wang et al.

items.title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow
items.summary: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. We perform large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth cylinder and four stranded cables at four inclinations from $22.5^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, all stationary, with $Re \approx 1.0 \times 10^4$. Aerodynamic differences are governed mainly by cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth. Force-source decomposition shows that surface pressure contributes 94.9%--98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, whereas deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and a persistent lateral pressure imbalance.
items.author: Tielin Ma, Junlin Zhang, Jingcheng Fu et al.

items.title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics
items.summary: Estimating the motion of deformable bodies in soft robotics from proprioceptive sensing is challenging due to partial observability, as internal observations provide only indirect access to global motion, contact, and shape evolution. In such settings, instantaneous observations are insufficient, and accurate estimation requires temporally consistent latent representations. This paper studies deformable motion estimation under proprioceptive partial observability from a latent dynamics perspective. We argue that a key requirement for long-horizon estimation is latent temporal consistency, where latent states remain predictive of future observations. To this end, we present DeepSoMo, a learning-based framework that enforces predictive structure in latent dynamics through a self-supervised latent prediction constraint.
items.author: Hanwen Zhao, Weicheng Dai, Luoyao Chen et al.

items.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
items.summary: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. The world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing both articulated hand dynamics and scene changes under demonstrated actions, including the motion of fingers occluded from the cameras.
items.author: Zhongxi Chen, Yi Yang, Xinyi Chen et al.

items.title: Tutorial: Vision-Based Formation Control with Differential-Drive Robots
items.summary: This tutorial presents a step-by-step introduction to multi-robot formation control using differential- drive robots, an overhead camera, and Python. ArUco markers are used to estimate robot positions and orientations, while desired pairwise displacement vectors define a circular formation. By comparing measured and desired relative positions, the controller computes movement vectors that are converted into differential-drive wheel commands, with basic proximity-sensor-based obstacle avoidance. The tutorial guides readers through hardware and software setup, robot pose estimation, formation geometry, feedback control, system integration, and formation-error evaluation. Motivated by the need to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding and practical implementation in robotics education, we emphasize how mathematical concepts are translated into coordinated behaviors on physical robots.
items.author: Christian Marowski, Byung-Cheol Min

items.title: A Blueprint for National and International Healthcare Data Ecosystems: Learning From Building STRONG-AYA.
items.summary: Introduction Healthcare systems aim for continuous improvement to ensure excellent clinical outcomes, including optimized quality of life. This relies on accurate data and evaluation patient-centered as well as biomedical outcomes. This data increasingly arises from real-world data (RWD). We are using this data across a multi-national European consortium, to create a Learning Healthcare System, improve care, policy, and ultimately patients' outcomes. Methods STRONG-AYA is an interdisciplinary community, led from the Netherlands Cancer Institute, working across frequent consensus meetings, surveys, questionnaire design, data collection, synthesis and privacy-preserving federated analysis (in Vantage6), to ethically study and apply clinical and patient-centered outcomes data to learn about healthcare systems for Adolescents and Young Adults (AYAs) diagnosed with cancer when aged 15-39.

items.title: Development of a Multimodal Model Combining Imaging and Clinical Data to Predict Bone Cement Leakage During Vertebroplasty for Fresh Thoracolumbar Compression Fractures.
items.summary: Background Bone cement leakage is a common complication of percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP), but perioperative risk stratification remains challenging. Existing models based on single-source clinical or imaging features have limited performance. This study aimed to develop and validate multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) models integrating clinical, imaging, and radiomics features to predict bone cement leakage during PVP. Methods This multicenter study included 486 treated vertebrae from 378 patients at the North, South, and Shenshan campuses of our hospital. The treated vertebra was the prediction unit, while all vertebrae from the same patient were retained in the same dataset partition and cross-validation fold.
items.author: Choi W, Chen J, Qiu J, Xie T, Li Y, Pan Z, Zhang Z, Huang G, Liao N, Lin Y, Deng Z, Qiu X, Gao B, Huang D, Zhou H, Wu Z, Gao W.

items.title: Impedance-Based Contact Visualization for PulseSelect Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Single-Center Feasibility Study.
items.summary: Background PulseSelect pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) lacks a dedicated contact indicator. Methods We retrospectively compared 63 patients undergoing PVI before and after EnSite Contact Index (CI) implementation. Because electrical isolation does not confirm lesion transmurality, post-procedural unipolar electrograms (u-EGMs) were assessed as acute surrogate markers. Results CI guidance was associated with more applications, shorter fluoroscopy, and in an exploratory analysis of analyzable patients, fewer residual high-voltage u-EGMs (1/20 vs. 8/24; p = 0.027). No complications occurred. Conclusions CI-guided PVI was feasible; these procedural and acute electrophysiological associations require prospective validation.
items.author: Mizobuchi M, Matsumoto J, Oka K, Takemura H, Yamashita T, Nakamura S.

items.title: Three-dimensional mapping of human lung fibrosis identifies spatial coupling between tissue microarchitecture and maladaptive repair states
items.summary: Human lung fibrosis progressively destroys three-dimensional tissue architecture, yet how the structural microenvironment shapes cellular states remains unclear. Integrating 3D X-ray histology with spatial omics, we generate a volumetric multimodal atlas of human lung fibrosis that enables direct interrogation of relationships between tissue microarchitecture and spatial molecular programmes. We identify collapse of the alveolar-capillary unit - the coupled loss of alveolar type 1 epithelial cells, capillary endothelial cells, and basement membrane integrity - as a structural transition associated with early fibrogenesis. Surrounding transitional zones exhibit aberrant epithelial differentiation and proteolytic matrix remodelling, with epithelium shifting toward bronchiolised, airway-like states. Stromal activation converges on spatially restricted fibrogenic cores, sites of maximal collagen maturation and matrix stabilisation that function as signalling hubs within surrounding perifocal and vascular microenvironments.
items.author: Bell, J. A., Robinson, S. K., Pedley, R. et al.

items.title: Proliferation and mutation as humoral immune response
items.summary: The affinity maturation process, through which antibodies acquire relatively high affinity for an invading pathogen, involves complex mechanisms whose relative importance is not yet fully understood. This study proposes an analytical model of this process, to investigate the main factors governing proliferation and mutation and assess their respective roles. The model suggests that the immune system should not be expected to follow a single, rigid evolutionary pattern, as a wide range of proliferation and mutation strategies can yield nearly optimal outcomes. Keywords: Antibody, antigen, affinity, B-cell, mutation, proliferation
items.author: Meilijson, I., Sacerdote, L. L.

items.title: StableProt: Structure-Aware Deep Learning for Protein Thermostability (Tm) and Environmental Adaptation (OGT) Prediction
items.summary: Predicting protein melting temperature (Tm) and organismal optimal growth temperature (OGT) is essential for enzyme engineering, biocatalyst design, and metagenomic bioprospecting, yet computational prediction faces several fundamental bottlenecks: sequence-only representations miss tertiary packing; dual-task coupling induces destructive gradient conflict; natural database skew (>87% mesophiles) drives mesophilic collapse; and existing tools produce uncalibrated point predictions. To address these challenges, we present StableProt, a structure-aware framework that couples amino acid sequences with Foldseek 3Di structural tokens via a frozen SaProt backbone to capture 3D contacts. Disjoint heads condition thermodynamic stability on ecological context without gradient conflict, while targeted 14% mesophilic subsampling expands thermophile representation to eliminate mesophilic collapse.
items.author: Behera, B. P., Dixit, A.
