items.title: Can qualia be geometric? A geometro-diffusion framework for the relational structure of color experience.
items.summary: Within the Geometro-Diffusion Theory (GDT) of consciousness, we formulate a candidate geometry for the relational organization of color experience. We distinguish a diffusion-induced scaffold, the color content encoded on it, and its neuronal realization. Elementary network examples establish these distinctions and show how consensus-directed nonlinear activity preserves the diffusion scaffold. On a 76-region human structural connectome, a distributed encoding is learned from 16 controlled colors and then frozen. Evaluation on 256 new colors gives a Spearman correspondence of 0.919 with the CIEDE2000 perceptual reference, compared with 0.923 for direct CIELAB distances. Nonlinear Izhikevich encoding followed by the same anatomical propagation gives analytic-neuronal correspondence of 0.924.
items.author: Estrada E.

items.title: Cold-Inducible RNA-Binding Protein Alleviates Hypertensive Renal Injury Through the KEAP1-NRF2 Pathway.
items.summary: Angiotensin II (Ang II) plays crucial roles in renal dysfunction, fibrotic changes, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. CIRBP, a cold-inducible RNA-binding protein, functions to maintain cellular homeostasis. However, its role in renal damage elicited by Ang II remains unclear. Here, we investigated the mechanisms through which Cirbp overexpression alleviates renal damage caused by Ang II, and Cirbp deletion induces basal renal injury. Transcriptomic analysis identified the involvement of Cirbp in hypertension-related renal injury. Across the animal and cell models, Cirbp overexpression attenuated Ang II-induced renal dysfunction, fibrosis, apoptosis, and inflammation, whereas Cirbp deficiency aggravated basal injury and increased renal susceptibility to injury.
items.author: Zhang Y, Li Q, Luo M, Hua D, Sheng Y, Wang L, Li P.

items.title: Craniofacial Load Modifies the Interaction of Obesity and Apnea Hypopnea Index Severity in Adult Males.
items.summary: Objectives Multiple physiological, skeletal structural, and BMI variables determine obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity. To better understand how craniofacial, hyoid, and obesity measures interact, data from a population-based study was re-evaluated. Methods Lateral facial cephalometric and polysomnographic data (2% desaturation criteria for hypopnea) were reanalyzed from a population-based study and enhanced clinic population (Wisconsin Cohort Study). Cephalometric x-rays were performed awake, upright, at end expiration. Data on craniofacial structure (45 craniofacial, 10 hyoid related), age, and obesity were re-evaluated using linear and non-linear logarithmic methods. Residual variance was assessed with hierarchical cluster analysis and classified with linear discriminant analysis. Results 203 male patients (141 population based and 62 clinic) were included (female numbers were inadequate and were excluded from analysis).
items.author: Woodson BT, Hanson PR.

items.title: Multi-Analytical Characterization and Taxonomic Distinction of Australian Plant Exudates.
items.summary: Plant exudates have been used worldwide for millennia in broad applications due to their unique physicochemical properties. Indigenous Australians have used exudates in long-standing cultural and technical practices, including hafting adhesives and paint binders. Chemical characterization and botanical identification can provide important insight into the origin, properties, and usage of exudate materials from the archaeological past to the present. However, Australian exudates and cultural heritage materials have been far less examined compared to European, Asian, and North African counterparts. Here, we report combined Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, X-ray Raman scattering (XRS) spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and pyrolysis gas chromatography mass spectrometry (py-GC-MS) analyses for atomic- to molecular-level characterization of over 20 genera of Australian exudates.
items.author: Vogelsang SA, Paredes-Mellone O, Georgiou R, Gardezi SM, McDonald J, Sokaras D, Popelka-Filcoff RS, Bergmann U.

items.title: Fortuitous Discovery of Asymptomatic Homozygous Antithrombin Deficiency: A Rare p.Leu131Phe Heparin-Binding Site Mutation: A Case Report.
items.summary: Homozygous Type II heparin-binding site antithrombin deficiency is a rare inherited thrombophilia associated with a high risk of early thrombotic events. We report a 6-week-old infant homozygous for the SERPINC1 c.391C>T (p.Leu131Phe) variant (Antithrombin Budapest III), with markedly reduced antithrombin activity (12%). Despite this high-risk genotype, the patient remains asymptomatic without thrombotic or vascular abnormalities and has not required anticoagulant treatment to date. This case highlights the phenotypic heterogeneity of homozygous antithrombin Budapest III deficiency and the importance of genetic diagnosis, family screening, and careful long-term follow-up. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.
items.author: Cherkaoui S, Dedeken L, Demulder A, Simar J, Orlando C, Rozen L.

items.title: Peripheral Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Changes and Clinical Response to Electroconvulsive Therapy and Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review.
items.summary: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading contributor to the global burden of disease, and a substantial proportion of patients experience inadequate responses to conventional treatments. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a key regulator of neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, has been investigated as a potential biomarker of antidepressant response. However, its clinical relevance following brain stimulation remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated changes in peripheral BDNF concentrations and their association with clinical outcomes following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adults with MDD. The review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, and searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), PsycINFO, and LILACS (Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences).
items.author: Galindo CD, Jemar G, Osorio IC, Lopez A, Uribe Zapata M, Gonzalez Perez L, Villamil Montejo SD, Carvajal Angarita LA.

items.title: Chest Pain in Vain: Spontaneous Portal Vein Thrombosis.
items.summary: A 53-year-old man with a patient-reported history of ultrasound-diagnosed fatty liver disease presented with sudden-onset severe chest pain and a brief loss of consciousness, followed by progressive abdominal pain and a single episode of bloody diarrhoea. Admission investigations approximately 24 hours after the chest pain episode showed a D-dimer of 14,502 µg/L and high-sensitivity troponin I below 3 ng/L. An arterial-phase computed tomography (CT) aortogram showed no aortic dissection but did not establish portal venous patency. Following specialist thoracic radiology review, the aortogram was considered satisfactory to exclude pulmonary embolism down to the segmental level, and dedicated pulmonary angiography was not performed.
items.author: Makstutis S, Collins S.

items.title: Factors Associated With Extended Resection (Cecal Resection or Right Hemicolectomy) in Patients With Acute Appendicitis at a Tertiary Private Hospital: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: Introduction Acute appendicitis may require surgical procedures beyond conventional appendectomy, including cecal resection and right hemicolectomy. This study aimed to identify clinical factors associated with extended resection in adults undergoing surgery for acute appendicitis. Methods This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 360 adults treated surgically for acute appendicitis at a tertiary care hospital between 2018 and 2023. Extended resection was defined as cecal resection or right hemicolectomy. Associations were assessed using univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, symptom duration, previous abdominal surgery, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. Appendicitis severity was evaluated in a secondary model using grouped phases.
items.author: Silva-Ramos CS, Leal-Hidalgo JL, Arechavala-Lopez SF, Ramos-Griera MF, Fuentes-Calvo KJ, Alfaro-Goldaracena A, Díaz Girón-Gidi A, Villegas-Tovar E, Montalvo-Jave EE.

items.title: Diagnostic Pitfall: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension Presenting With Postpartum Right-Sided Heart Failure in a 21-Year-Old-Case Report.
items.summary: Mixed connective tissue disease is a multisystem autoimmune condition characterized by overlapping clinical and serological features related to anti-U1-RNP antibodies of at least two connective tissue diseases. It may present with myocarditis, pericarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and, less commonly, heart failure. We present a 21-year-old female with bilateral foot swelling, cough, and shortness of breath 3 months after a vaginal delivery. On examination, she was hypotensive (90/70 mmHg), with an elevated jugular venous pressure, a pulmonary systolic murmur with loud P2, and a tricuspid regurgitation murmur. Bronchial breath sounds and fine crepitations were present in both lower lung fields. She was evaluated initially for suspected postpartum cardiomyopathy.
items.author: Alla SSM, Khetan MS, Alla D, Ganguru SL, Appala S, Sree K, Shah RJ, Seth A, Rawtani NA, Aamir MR, Emmanuel NW.

items.title: AIM-Photonics Visible-to-Near-Infrared Silicon-Nitride-Based Silicon-Photonics Platform and Component Library.
items.summary: Silicon-photonics platforms operating at visible and near-infrared wavelengths are essential for a growing range of applications, including biosensing, chemical detection, Raman spectroscopy, quantum, optogenetics, and displays. However, unlike their infrared counterparts, visible-wavelength platforms have lacked comprehensive component libraries with pre-characterized devices, limiting the ability to rapidly design photonic integrated circuits for these applications. In this work, we present the design, fabrication, and broadband experimental characterization of a comprehensive visible-to-near-infrared-spanning component library for the AIM-Photonics 300-mm-wafer silicon-nitride-based platform, which features two silicon-nitride waveguiding layers, a sensing trench, thermo-optic phase shifters for modulation, and a dicing trench for fiber-to-chip edge coupling. We design and characterize components for both the fundamental quasi-transverse-electric and quasi-transverse-magnetic modes for wavelengths spanning from 450 to 1000 nm.
items.author: Garcia Coleto A, Crawford-Eng H, Dahl TJ, Shapiro M, Schnuck M, Walsh KJ, Lipkowitz ST, Pruessner MW, Tyndall NF, Bouchard JN, Antohe A, Kar S, O'Mullan PJ, Hurley C, Hedlesky P, Sundaram VSS, Preble S, McComber K, Eakin J, Petkie DT, Carpenter LG, Stievater TH, Notaros J.

items.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Laterality Disorder Associated With NME7 Variants.
items.summary: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital laterality disorder characterized by a mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal organs. Although isolated SIT is generally associated with a favorable prognosis, prenatal diagnosis requires careful evaluation to exclude associated structural malformations and syndromic presentations, as well as genetic investigation to identify a possible underlying etiology and improve prognostic assessment. The genetic basis of SIT is complex and remains incompletely understood. To date, genotype-phenotype correlations for SIT-associated genetic variants remain poorly established. We report the prenatal and postnatal clinical course of a fetus with isolated SIT carrying a homozygous intragenic deletion of the NME7 gene, identified by whole-exome sequencing.
items.author: Hardy V, Ortegat M, De Clippel K, Sznajer Y, Wuyts W, Blaumeiser B, Steenhaut P.

items.title: Outside-In Inverted L-Shaped Capsulotomy in Hip Arthroscopy.
items.summary: Hip arthroscopy has become the mainstream surgical treatment for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, with approximately 88.75% of patients returning to sports postoperatively. Capsulotomy is a critical step in arthroscopic labral repair; however, various reported techniques possess inherent limitations. This technique employs an outside-in longitudinal capsulotomy along the femoral neck, followed by a transverse capsular release from its acetabular attachment along the path of the labral tear, creating an inverted "L"-shaped opening. On completion of the repair, the hip capsule is closed and retensioned using the remaining sutures from the labral repair anchors. This article summarizes the advantages, disadvantages, pearls, and pitfalls of this technique.
items.author: Feng Y, Ni J, Tian Z, Chen Z, Wei W, Wang D, Shi Z.

items.title: Symmetric Off-Axis Spectral Encoding Enables High-Throughput Six-Color Optical Sectioning Imaging.
items.summary: Multicolor fluorescence microscopy is central to biological imaging, but simultaneous detection of additional colors typically reduces throughput, increases spectral crosstalk, or lowers signal-to-noise ratio. We developed symmetric off-axis spectral encoding microscopy (sym-OSEM), which uses paired spatial encoding and differential decoding to separate fluorescence channels and suppress common-mode out-of-focus background. The differential decoding requires no specimen-specific reference spectrum, point spread function, or training data. All fluorophores are excited and detected simultaneously, so acquisition time is largely independent of channel count within the demonstrated two- to six-color configurations. Simulations and experiments using cell preparations, a serially imaged 300 μm-thick mouse-brain volume, and lymph node sections validated the approach.
items.author: Zhao J, Ding Z, Zhang Z, Zhang J, Qi S, Yuan J.

items.title: Asthma Exacerbations Following Wildfire Smoke PM 2.5 Exposure Among U.S. Adults.
items.summary: Asthma exacerbation can be triggered by various forms of air pollution, including PM 2.5 from wildfire smoke. This study aims to investigate the association between wildfire smoke PM 2.5 exposure and asthma exacerbations in adults during the warm months (April-August) between 2006 and 2019. Using a case-crossover design, we analyzed 18,935 asthma exacerbation events and four matched control periods per event from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) All of Us research program. We used the conditional logistic regression to estimate the association (odds ratios [ORs]) between wildfire smoke PM 2.5 exposure and asthma exacerbation, considering lag periods of 0-7 days and adjusting for temperature, precipitation, and humidity.
items.author: Huang Y, Luo L, Leng S, Zhang S, Lavin RP, Buenemann M, Lin Y, Campen M, Gong X.

items.title: Epidemiological Profile and Temporal Trends of Exogenous Poisoning in the State of São Paulo and Brazil From 2010 to 2020.
items.summary: Background Exogenous poisoning is a compulsorily notifiable condition in Brazil, but analyses of its temporal trends in the state of São Paulo remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological profile of exogenous poisoning in the state of São Paulo from 2010 to 2020 and its distribution across Regional Health Care Networks (Redes Regionais de Atenção à Saúde (RRAS)) and to analyze temporal trends in incidence, mortality, and case fatality compared with Brazil. Methods An observational time-series study was conducted using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)), obtained through the TabNet platform of the Brazilian Ministry of Health, and population estimates from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics.
items.author: Dos Santos PHSC, Wolff LF, Camurça VD, Martins FL, Sugino RG.

items.title: Hybrid Osteosynthesis for Septic Humeral Shaft Nonunion in a Patient with Obesity: A Case Report.
items.summary: Septic humeral shaft nonunion represents a complex reconstructive challenge in orthopedic surgery, particularly in patients with obesity, in whom increased lever arms and greater mechanical loading of the upper extremity substantially compromise fixation stability. Recurrent failure of isolated fixation constructs, including intramedullary nails or compression plates, necessitates hybrid strategies that combine enhanced biomechanical stability with effective eradication of microbial infection. This article presents the case of a middle-aged man with obesity and a history of a left humeral shaft fracture initially treated with intramedullary nailing in December 2020 who developed persistent nonunion. Following revision surgery with dynamic compression plating, fixation failure occurred secondary to implant fatigue.
items.author: Chiquini-Ramírez P, Villamues-Moreno NL, Ponce-de-Léon-Dominguez J, Moreno-Degante L, Pettet-Ruiz B, Torres-Casado E, Reyes-García HM, Garduza-Leyva N.

items.title: Bridging the Gap in Headache Care: Insights From the International Headache Society Survey in Nepal.
items.summary: Background Headache disorders impose a substantial public health burden worldwide, with low- and middle-income countries like Nepal facing pronounced challenges due to limited healthcare infrastructure, inadequate provider training, and restricted access to essential treatments. Objective This study aimed to assess the current state of headache care in Nepal, focusing on the distribution and training of healthcare providers, access to medications, and socioeconomic factors that affect treatment adherence. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted as part of a multinational joint initiative by the International Headache Society and Middle East, North Africa and Asia Headache Group. Data were collected from 232 healthcare providers across Nepal using a survey questionnaire.
items.author: Ojha R, Ma J, Chapagain A, Timasina RR, Gajurel BP, Karn R, Rajbhandari R, Gautam N, Uludüz D, Özge A, Taşdelen S, Amirguliyev S, Şaşmaz T, Burstein R.

items.title: Self-Powered Photodetection and Optical Information Recognition in a Mixed-Dimensional WSe 2 /CdSe Heterojunction.
items.summary: Mixed-dimensional van der Waals heterojunctions offer opportunities for self-powered optical sensing and information processing, yet identifying the spatial origin of zero-bias photoresponse remains important for understanding device operation. Here, a vertical WSe 2 /CdSe heterojunction composed of a WSe 2 nanosheet and a CdSe nanobelt is investigated for visible photodetection. Under 610 nm illumination, the device exhibits a photovoltaic response with an open-circuit voltage of 0.403 V and a short-circuit current of 4.77 × 10 -10 A. Quantitative photocurrent mapping reveals a mean response of 5.94 nA in the heterojunction overlap region, approximately 50 times that near the metal contacts.
items.author: Liu L, Dou H, Huang H, Mu F, Yang Y, Zhang H, Song F, Liu Y.

items.title: Genetic Structure of Harbour Seals Phoca vitulina vitulina Along the Coast of Norwegian Mainland: Implications for Management.
items.summary: Alignment between biologically meaningful units and stock boundaries is one or the requirements for sustainable resource management. In Norway, harbour seals ( Phoca vitulina vitulina ) are managed at the county level and, when local populations are deemed sufficiently large to support harvesting, hunting is permitted under a quota corresponding to 5% of the counted individuals. An assessment of population structure along the entire Norwegian coastline based upon 16 microsatellites revealed significant overall differentiation ( F ST = 0.036, p < 0.001) consistent with a pattern of Isolation by Distance, in agreement with the estimated effective migration surface (EEMS). Pairwise differentiation among sampling sites challenged the current stock outline.
items.author: Quintela M, Frie AK, Lille-Langøy R, Tiedemann R, Nilssen KT.

items.title: Unusual Presentation of Left-Sided Bilothorax Following Spleen Laceration: A Case Without Biliary Tree Injury.
items.summary: A 46-year-old pedestrian sustained blunt injury to abdomen when he was struck from behind by a motorcycle, causing him to fall flat onto the roadway. Ultrasound abdomen showed splenic injury and hemoperitoneum. Chest x-ray showed left mild pleural effusion. He was managed conservatively by multiple blood transfusions for anemia and referred to our center after 3 weeks. A triphasic CT scan of abdomen revealed a splenic laceration with multiple pseudoaneurysms, moderate hemoperitoneum, and trace bilateral pleural effusions. No biliary tree injury or fistula was identified. On fifth postoperative day after splenectomy, he developed progressive breathlessness and ultrasound showed increased effusion on left side.
items.author: Reddipilli T, Gandra RR, Gella V, Ithepalli D.

items.title: Correction: Dupilumab in children with eosinophilic esophagitis: a retrospective multicenter study.
items.author: Hasosah M, Sukkar G, AlSahafi A, Zaidan A, Ghous N, Alshahrani A, Al Zahrani Z, Hasosah N, Qurashi M, Goronfolah L, Alsharief A, Kamal NM.

items.title: Prevalence and symptom severity of thrower's shoulder in elite youth handball players.
items.summary: Objective To identify the prevalence and severity of overuse shoulder symptoms in elite youth handball players. Methods Six-hundred and sixty (52.3% boys) elite youth handball players were followed prospectively for one season during the seasons 2016-17, 2017-18, 2018-19, and 2019-20. Players completed standardized questionnaires throughout the season and reported any overuse shoulder symptoms. The Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index (WOSI) questionnaire was distributed five times per season. Latent class analysis (LCA) was carried out to identify different symptom patterns. Results Of 660 athletes, 148 (22.4%) (50% boys, age: 14.1 ± 0.7 years) reported shoulder problems in at least one WOSI questionnaire.
items.author: Achenbach L, Benning A, Zeman F, Kaiser M, Limmer J.

items.title: Correction: Erythrocyte membrane with CLIPPKF as biomimetic nanodecoy traps merozoites and attaches to infected red blood cells to prevent Plasmodium infection.
items.author: He Z, Yu C, Pan Z, Li X, Zhang X, Huang Q, Liao X, Hu J, Zeng F, Ru L, Yu W, Xu Q, Song J, Liang J.

items.title: Mechanistic Population Pharmacokinetic Modeling of Extended-Release Metformin in Obese South African Women Living with HIV on Dolutegravir.
items.summary: Regulatory limits on metformin co-administered with dolutegravir (DTG) derive from healthy-volunteer studies in which DTG increased metformin exposure by 79% through organic cation transporter 2 inhibition, prompting a 1,000 mg/day metformin dose restriction. Whether this applies to women with HIV and severe obesity, a clinically important and understudied population for metformin-DTG coadministration, is unknown. In a secondary analysis of a reported cohort, we developed a population pharmacokinetic model of extended-release (XR) metformin with a zero-order-release, first-order-absorption structure scaled by lean body mass (LBM). Estimated glomerular filtration rate and DTG exposure were evaluated as clearance covariates, including DTG as a time-varying competitive inhibitor.
items.author: Benecke RM, Pillay-Fuentes Lorente V, Decloedt E, van Rensburg R.

items.title: Implementation of Pharmacogenomics in Pediatric-Focused Institutions Within the Pharmacogenomics Global Research Network.
items.summary: Descriptions of how pediatric-focused institutions implement pharmacogenomic testing are scarce, and often not differentiated from adult-focused institutions. We aimed to provide a detailed description of how pediatric-focused institutions across the world implemented pharmacogenomic testing in clinical practice. A survey was distributed to members of the Pharmacogenomics Global Research Network to assess program infrastructure, implementation efforts, genes tested, method of testing, and clinical decision support. The survey was completed by 43 institutions that have implemented pharmacogenomics: 12 pediatric-focused, 10 adult-focused, and 21 institutions serving all ages. All pediatric-focused institutions provide testing for CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP3A5, NUDT15, and TPMT. Psychiatry and hematology/oncology were the specialties most commonly reported as implementing pharmacogenomics at pediatric-focused institutions.
items.author: Ramsey LB, Bousman C, Brand R, Cook K, Gregornik DB, Haidar CE, Hakooz N, Keuler N, Lamb N, Nagy M, Nguyen JQ, Paetznick C, Schultz A, Smith DM, Tsermpini EE, Elchynski AL.

items.title: A subtype-specific gene regulatory program controls differential circuit integration of deep CA3 pyramidal neurons
items.summary: How closely related neuronal subtypes integrate into different circuits remains poorly understood. Deep and superficial hippocampal CA3 pyramidal neurons (PNs) differ in intrinsic firing and mossy fiber (MF) input at specialized postsynaptic structures termed thorny excrescences (TEs). Combining developmental single-nucleus multiomics with genetic targeting, morphological analysis and electrophysiology, we identify the transcription factor ST18 as a regulator of deep CA3 subtype identity. ST18 marks sparsely thorny and burst-firing neurons, and gene regulatory analyses predict that it represses a superficial-associated program involved in dendritic spine development, synaptic organization, and electrophysiological properties. Postnatal ST18 loss shifts the transcriptional and chromatin landscape of deep CA3 PNs toward a superficial-like state.
items.author: Daaboul, D., Vandensteen, J., Dascenco, D. et al.

items.title: Learning to play with spikes: characterizing, predicting, and engineering unsupervised plasticity rules for spiking reservoir computing
items.summary: Spiking reservoir computing, and reservoir computing more generally, is a powerful and efficient framework for neuromorphic and biological applications, in which a fixed random reservoir drives a trained readout. Its performance depends critically on the reservoir initialization, so that enriching the reservoir with adaptive, unsupervised plasticity rules offers a natural solution to this limitation. However, it is unclear which rules work, or why, and how to find the best-suited rules for specific tasks without exhaustive and expensive search. Here, we learn how to play the Atari game Pong in a plastic spiking reservoir network. We systematically characterize a large family of local plasticity rules that were meta-learned in prior work.
items.author: Kania, M., Confavreux, B., Vogels, T. P.

items.title: FMRP safeguards long mRNA expression by opposing repressive RNP states
items.summary: Fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP) is widely viewed as a translational repressor, yet its loss paradoxically compromises expression of exceptionally long, dosage-sensitive neurodevelopmental mRNAs. First shown in Drosophila oocytes, this selective loss extends to mouse cortex and hippocampus, but its mechanism remains unknown. Here, we uncover a protective function for FMRP: shielding long mRNAs from repression by Me31B/DDX6, a conserved RNA helicase that organizes repressive RNP complexes. In Drosophila oocytes, FMRP loss redirects target mRNAs into Me31B-marked P-bodies. Transcriptome-wide binding maps reveal extensive FMRP-Me31B co-occupancy, preferentially concentrated on long coding sequences whose translation depends on FMRP. Strikingly, disrupting Me31B-dependent repression preferentially enhances translation of FMRP targets in FMRP-deficient oocytes.
items.author: Ma, K., Hossain, A. R., Judson, K. L. et al.

items.title: Integrated genomics and transcriptomics reveal molecular insights into extreme dietary adaptation in vampire bats
items.summary: Vampire bats are the only tetrapods that feed exclusively on blood. To uncover the molecular changes associated with this extreme dietary specialization, we generated six new reference genomes, including genomes of all three vampire bat species, and integrated comparative analyses of gene sequence evolution (selection signatures, duplications, and losses) with transcriptomic data from six major organs to identify shifts in gene expression. Our integrative analyses reveal sequence or expression changes in 150 genes that provide insights into the molecular biology of sanguivory. Through comparative analyses and experiments, we show that the enlarged vampire bat stomach has increased connective tissue content, likely facilitating extreme expansion, is pH-neutral, and exhibits reduced mucus production, together providing molecular insights into its shift from a digestive to an absorptive organ for water, electrolytes, and vitamins.
items.author: Liu, S., Freitas, M. B., Sartori, S. S. R. et al.

items.title: Open-source benchmarking of dairy and dairy-free products
items.summary: Dairy-free products offer opportunities to reduce the environmental impact of food. However, they must reproduce the diverse sensory and functional properties of conventional dairy, from foam stabilization in a latte to acid-gel structure in yogurt and melt--stretch behavior in mozzarella. Yet, large-scale, open-source sensory benchmarks across dairy product categories remain scarce. Here we show that the sensory gap between dairy and dairy-free products varies substantially across ten categories: barista milk, butter, cheddar, cream cheese, creamer, ice cream, fluid milk, mozzarella, sour cream, and Greek-style yogurt. We analyze the NECTAR Taste of the Industry 2026 dataset, which includes 1,437 respondents, 3,220 overall-liking ratings, and 79,027 recorded survey responses, including 35,762 product-linked responses.
items.author: Koosis, A. O., Cotto, C., Kuhl, E.

items.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES
items.summary: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-stage sequence-based modeling suite designed to study these regimes. Stage 1 trains ligand-specific predictors using a pretrained protein language model (PLM). Stage 2 introduces ligand conditioning through learned embeddings, enabling a single multi-ligand model.
items.author: Pourmirzaei, M., Alqarghuli, S., Chen, K. et al.

items.title: CryoSHIELDs: tunable amphipathic peptide additives for cryo-EM
items.summary: While cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has transformed structural biology, sample preparation remains a major determinant of success. Specifically, the air-water interface (AWI) can damage complexes, impose preferred orientation, and reduce particle density. Here, we introduce cryoSHIELDs, a library of peptide additives designed to modulate the AWI and improve cryo-EM grid preparation. Across 24 diverse protein systems, cryoSHIELDs improved particle distribution, angular sampling, complex integrity, and, in selected cases, map quality and resolution. CryoSHIELDs enabled structure determination of the OSMR{beta}-Vixarelimab complex, the multi-subunit CCAN kinetochore complex without chemical cross-linking, and membrane proteins including ABCC6 and the -opioid receptor-Gi complex, the latter resolved at 2.3 A using tenfold lower protein concentration without compromising map quality.
items.author: Azumaya, C. M., Dutka, P., Johnson, M. C. et al.

items.title: The methionine cycle sustains the mesenchymal phenotype of tumor cells and drives PDA progression
items.summary: Mesenchymal traits are associated with poor prognosis in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDA), but direct targeting of mesenchymal tumor cells remains a challenge. Metabolic profiling of tumor cells isolated from murine PDA and liver metastases (LM) revealed that LM rely more on the methionine cycle than does primary PDA. This metabolic shift was specifically associated with increased activation of the methionine cycle in mesenchymal tumor cells compared to differentiated tumor cells. We show that the targeting of the key enzyme of the methionine cycle S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase (SAHH) in mesenchymal cells lowers the levels of homocysteine (Hcy) and glutathione, resulting in reduced antioxidant capacity, deregulated intracellular calcium homeostasis, and ultimately loss of mesenchymal markers.
items.author: Vasseur, S., Guillaumond, F., Elodie, M. et al.

items.title: Extending the least-cost theory of stomatal regulation to include soil moisture stress
items.summary: Terrestrial biosphere models commonly use empirical scaling factors to represent soil moisture constraints on carbon and water fluxes, but these lack mechanistic grounding and produce inconsistent estimates of soil moisture limitations on primary production and transpiration across models. Here we extended the least-cost hypothesis for optimal stomatal conductance to account for soil moisture limitations by allowing soil water availability to modulate the carbon cost of water transport, drawing on the observed temperature dependence of stem respiration, and derived a simple empirical approximation to the theory using global {delta}13C and eddy covariance data. The empirical analysis shows moderated thermal acclimation of stem respiration and a weak increase in water transport costs with aridity, supporting the interpretation that the decline in light-use efficiency (LUE) under arid conditions is primarily attributable to non-stomatal limitations.
items.author: Sandoval, D., Flo, V., Zhang, H. et al.

items.title: Hierarchical organization in sparse gene regulatory networks shapes structural coherence and emergent regulatory coordination
items.summary: A fundamental challenge in systems biology is understanding how regulatory coordination is maintained within extremely sparse gene regulatory networks (GRNs). While traditional unsigned network metrics can quantify the overall magnitude of influence a specific node or edge exerts over the network, they cannot predict the functional direction and consistency of these regulatory changes. To address this gap, we introduce the coherence matrix. This topology-based framework for signed, directed GRNs computes a strictly bounded, interpretable measure of directional regulatory coordination between gene pairs. Using synthetic network ensembles, we demonstrate that architectures with low intrinsic structural coherence suffer severe density-driven scaling penalties.
items.author: Harlapur, P., Jagadeesan, R., Ribeiro, A. S. et al.

items.title: Uncovering the latent structure of interwoven population and temporal codes
items.summary: Population analysis methods have become standard for navigating the complexity of neural data. However, these methods often assume a rate code, neglecting information encoded in the precise timing of spikes. Critically, additional information encoded in bursts of action potentials may be missed. Here, we develop a probabilistic latent-variable framework that disentangles the factors associated with bursts and individual spikes. This enables burst codes to be investigated directly from the structure of the data, without requiring external covariates. We demonstrate that analyzing firing rates alone obscures the latent structure and factors underlying bursts. Applying our method to simulated and experimental data, we show that it can infer the correct latent structure and be used to test for the presence of burst coding.
items.author: Friedenberger, Z., Cao, Y., Naud, R.

items.title: Proteome-wide discovery of novel diagnostic antigens for coccidioidomycosis
items.summary: Coccidioidomycosis, commonly called Valley Fever (VF), caused by Coccidioides spp., is an understudied fungal disease that accounts for a substantial fraction of pneumonias in endemic areas. Diagnosis remains challenging because the mainstay of diagnosis is serology, and current assays have modest sensitivity in early infection. Discovery of new antigens could improve serologic detection early in disease. Here, we use PepSeq, a DNA-programmable serology platform, to represent the complete proteome of Coccidioides within a library of 244,000 DNA-barcoded peptides. By profiling antibody reactivity at the protein and epitope levels in VF patients, naturally infected pigtail macaques, and healthy controls, we identify numerous previously-unrecognized antigens and epitopes, including some shared between humans and macaque responses.
items.author: Elko, E., Ryle, L., Nelson, G. A. et al.

items.title: Near real-time data on the human neutralizing antibody landscape to influenza virus in summer of 2026 shows antigenic advance of H3N2 subclade K region D mutants and H1N1 D.3.1.1 Sa mutants
items.summary: Human seasonal influenza evolves rapidly, necessitating twice yearly decisions about whether to update the strains in the vaccine. To help inform this decision, we have been using high-throughput sequencing-based neutralization assays to make twice yearly measurements of how recent human sera neutralize current human H3N2 and H1N1 strains. Here we provide the third installment in this series of measurements by reporting 52,268 titers representing neutralization of 148 viral strains by 355 human sera collected between April and August of 2026. Our measurements show that new H3N2 subclade K strains with mutations in antigenic region D and new H1N1 subclade D.3.1.1 strains with mutations in antigenic region Sa (such as G155E) have reduced neutralization by human sera, with notable heterogeneity in the impact of some of these mutations across sera from different individuals.
items.author: Kikawa, C., Butler, A., Huddleston, J. et al.

items.title: Integrated omics analysis reveals reorganization of nitrogen and lipid metabolism in a toluene-degrading bacterium in the gas phase
items.summary: Gas-phase bioprocesses, in which microbial cells are immobilized on solid carriers exposed to the gas phase, enable efficient conversion of poorly water-soluble compounds for biodegradation and bioproduction. However, operation without a surrounding bulk aqueous medium can constrain the replenishment of water and nonvolatile nutrients. The metabolic mechanisms that sustain cellular activity in these low-water environments remain largely unknown. Here, we elucidated the metabolic alterations in the highly adhesive bacterium Acinetobacter sp. Tol 5 degrading toluene in the gas and aqueous phases. Polyurethane carriers bearing cells from independent cultures were assigned to the gas phase or to two aqueous media, nitrogen-depleted basal salt medium and phosphate-buffered saline, so that the conditions differed only in phase and nutrient availability.
items.author: Inoue, S., Naobayashi, T., Tokiyoshi, K. et al.

items.title: R-pyocin-mediated selection restores aminoglycoside sensitivity in a pan-drug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate
items.summary: The global escalation of antibiotic resistance is a critical threat necessitating innovative strategies to provide new therapeutic options and restore the efficacy of conventional drugs. Pseudomonas aeruginosa exemplifies this challenge by utilizing a robust genomic resistome to persist in clinical settings. Here, we demonstrate that R-pyocins (phage-like bactericidal particles) can be leveraged not as conventional biocides but as precise selective forces to drive an evolutionary trap. We subjected the laboratory strains PAO1 and PAK and the clinical pan-drug-resistant (PDR) wound isolate MRSN 6220 to R-pyocin selective pressure. Under sustained R-pyocin pressure, every pyomelanogenic variant we recovered evaded R-pyocin killing through large-scale chromosomal deletions spanning 250-388 kbp.
items.author: Estrada, I., Campbell, D., Welch, G. S. et al.

items.title: SF3b inhibitors suppress proliferation of nonsmall cell lung cancer cells irrespective of EGFR mutation status
items.summary: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) are standard care for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance limits their durability, and alternatives that do not depend on EGFR kinase activity are needed. We asked whether inhibitors of SF3b, a core component of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particle, act on NSCLC cells regardless of EGFR genotype. Three lung adenocarcinoma lines were treated with pladienolide B or herboxidiene at 0.01, 0.1 and 1 uM: PC9 and HCC827, both carrying an EGFR exon 19 deletion and both inhibited by gefitinib at nanomolar concentrations, and A549, which is EGFR wild type and gefitinibin sensitive.
items.author: Fukagawa, W., Horita, Y., Harada, H. et al.

items.title: LplA-mediated rescue of lethal myopathy and cardiomyopathy in mitochondrial lipoylation-deficient mammalian caused by Lipt1
items.summary: Inherited mitochondrial metabolic disorders impair cellular energy generation and often lead to fatal metabolic crises. Mitochondrial lipoylation defects represent a severe case of such disorders that can lead to lethality but lacks effective treatment so far. In this study, we generated a viable mouse model with muscle-specific deficiency of the lipoyltransferase coded by Lipt1 to provide an in vivo preclinical model that overcomes embryonic lethality. Using this model, we examined a bacterial lipoate protein ligase A (LplA)-mediated gene therapy via adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery. By introducing LplA alongside lipoic acid supplementation, we reconstituted a salvage pathway that bypasses the mammalian endogenous lipoylation pathway.
items.author: Yu, J., Hu, Z., Liu, Z. et al.

items.title: Glycolytic enzymes form membrane-less condensates in the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum by sensing glucose levels
items.summary: Recent studies have shown that liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) in cells can regulate essential cellular events, including metabolic processes. Glycolytic bodies (G-bodies) are biomolecular condensates formed through the LLPS of glycolytic enzymes, and they accelerate glycolysis to overcome hypoxic stress in several organisms. Although the asexual blood stage (ABS) of the human malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum highly depends on glycolysis for energy production, there have been no reports of the formation of such G-bodies throughout the parasite's lifecycle. Using fluorescence tagging and live imaging, we found that G-body-like condensates containing phosphofructokinase 9 (PFK9) and phosphoglycerate kinase (PGK) were formed in the parasite cells after long-term culture under conditions of low glucose.
items.author: Ishii, R., Sakura, T., Inaoka, D. K. et al.

items.title: Global failure to track international biodiversity targets on islands
items.summary: Islands harbour exceptional biodiversity but face severe threats, making their conservation crucial to achieving the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. To evaluate progress toward its 23 targets across islands worldwide, we screened 504 biodiversity and socioeconomic indicators, and retained 47. We modelled historical time series from 1950, then projected to 2030. Progress was uneven: nine targets improved across all available indicators, while nine displayed conflicting trends. Critically, 15 of 23 targets (65%) lacked a suitable headline indicator, and five had none. Furthermore, 29 of 47 indicators (62%) were reported nationally, potentially obscuring island conditions. Most targets also lacked quantitative objectives, limiting evaluation of whether change rates suffice for 2030.
items.author: Mologni, F., Essl, F., Ah-Peng, C. et al.

items.title: Body size and fruit handling ability explain frugivory patterns among Asian mammals
items.summary: Aim Frugivore traits influence the diversity of fruits that frugivores consume. While well studied in birds, trait-based drivers of frugivory remain less understood in mammals despite their considerable morphological, physiological, and ecological diversity. We compiled a comprehensive dataset of mammalian frugivory across Asia, and compared the species diversity and morphological traits of fruits consumed across major mammal guilds. We examine the importance of traits such as body size and fruit handling ability in explaining observed frugivory patterns among Asian mammals. Location Asia. Time period 1964 to 2023. Major taxa studied Herbivores (Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla, Proboscidea), Primates, Carnivora Methods We compiled frugivory data for three major non-volant, terrestrial Asian mammals from 518 sources, comprising 5276 unique plant mammal interactions between 142 mammal species and 2,234 plant species.
items.author: Basu, B., McConkey, K. R., Pulla, S. et al.

items.title: High-throughput identification of chromatin-opening transcription factors
items.summary: Cell fate transitions involve major changes to the chromatin landscape, some of which are thought to deepen the basin around a newly adopted cell state, stabilizing gene expression programs that might otherwise be transient. Transcription factors (TFs) are central to this process, binding only a subset of the genome-wide occurrences of their cognate motifs to create accessible regions that can act as cell type-specific enhancers. However, apart from a few well-studied cases, it is not clear which of the ~1,600 mammalian TFs can directly or indirectly initiate newly accessible sites, nor why only some motif occurrences gain accessibility. Here, we performed pooled CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) screens to upregulate endogenous developmental TFs in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) and assess their impact on the chromatin landscape.
items.author: Keith, A., Jain, S., Daza, R. M. et al.

items.title: Molecular Characterization of T-Lineage Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia by an Optimal-Transport Based Multi-Omics Integration Framework
items.summary: T-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) is an aggressive pediatric malignancy characterized by complex heterogeneity across multiple molecular layers. Accurate subtyping is essential for understanding disease mechanisms, risk stratification, and guiding targeted therapeutic strategies. However, current diagnostic approaches are labor-intensive and time-consuming, and existing computational methods are limited by reliance on single-modality data or simple integration strategies. Effective integration of heterogeneous multi-omics data remains a major computational challenge. We present OTTER (Optimal Transport-based Transcriptomics and gEnomics Representation), a novel multi-modal deep learning framework that jointly models transcriptomic and genomic data for T-ALL molecular characterization. OTTER encodes each omics modality through a modality-specific encoder and aligns the resulting latent representations using Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport (GW-OT), which preserves the internal geometric structure of each modality without requiring a shared feature space.
items.author: Li, L., Wang, J., Wan, S.

items.title: Global Proteomic Analysis of Colorectal Cancers Stratified by Microsatellite Instability Subtype Reveals Protein Differences
items.summary: Lynch syndrome, historically known as hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer, is caused by germline mutations in the DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, MLH1, MSH2 (EPCAM), MSH6, and PMS2. While the genetic changes associated with Lynch syndrome have previously been characterized, there have not been studies of the associated proteomic alterations, in part because of the limited availability of primary samples and the absence of in vitro model systems. In this study, the first large-scale tissue proteomic assessment of Lynch syndrome samples as well as three other subtypes of colorectal cancer was completed with specimens from the Ohio Colorectal Cancer Prevention Initiative.
items.author: Tobias, F., Sekera, E. R., Xiong, X. et al.

items.title: Dual kinase inhibition provides early clues to restoration of neuroimmune homeostasis in an AAV-haSyn model of Parkinsons disease
items.summary: Background Previous studies of drugs targeting mixed linage kinase type 3 (MLK3) and/or leucine rich repeat kinase type 2 (LRRK2) in sporadic Parkinsons disease (PD) have failed to meet clinical endpoints despite multiple lines of evidence implicating these kinases in pathogenesis. This has reduced enthusiasm for MLK3 and LRRK2 as druggable targets. Largely overlooked is the evidence that these targets remain valid but must be considered in combination to achieve a therapeutic outcome. This provides the rationale for this study. Methods We conducted a pilot study modeling early, pre-symptomatic PD with subsequent evaluation of therapeutic potential of a multi-kinase inhibitor (URMC-099) in alleviating disease pathology.
items.author: Chiang, W., Sandoval, I. M., Li, H. et al.

items.title: Shikonin alleviates bone cancer pain through suppression of spinal IGF2-associated p38 MAPK signaling
items.summary: Background Bone cancer pain (BCP) is a debilitating complication of advanced cancer that substantially impairs physical function and emotional wellbeing. Current pharmacological treatments often provide incomplete analgesia and may be limited by adverse effects. Shikonin, a bioactive naphthoquinone derived from Lithospermum erythrorhizon, exhibits analgesic and anti inflammatory activities, but its effects and underlying mechanisms in BCP remain unclear. Methods A rat model of BCP was established by intratibial inoculation of luciferase labeled MADB106 cells. The analgesic and behavioral effects of intrathecal Shikonin were evaluated using mechanical and thermal nociceptive assays, CatWalk gait analysis, the open field test (OFT), elevated plus maze (EPM), light/dark box (LDB) test, and rotarod testing.
items.author: Ma, z., Jia, J., Lu, D. et al.

items.title: Feasible closed-loop stimulation for neural latent dynamics control
items.summary: Modern neuroscience benefits from powerful computational and experimental methods for studying neural populations, including latent dynamics models that predict behavior with few dimensions. But despite their explanatory utility, latent factors are seldom targeted explicitly with experimental perturbations, leaving causal relationships to behavior and inferred dynamical landscapes untested. A promising solution is closed-loop, multi-channel optogenetic control, which, when paired with model predictions, could steer neural trajectories in real time--a feat impossible for traditional, hand-designed stimulation. However, because closed-loop latent control has not been demonstrated in vivo, the hardware and software requirements remain unclear--particularly the necessary stimulation dimensionality and how limited resources such as implant volume and bandwidth should be allocated between stimulation and recording capabilities.
items.author: Johnsen, K. A., Lai, Y., Vivekanandasarma, L. et al.

items.title: Identification of Kinome Biomarkers and Therapeutic Rescue in cGMP-Linked Retinal Degeneration
items.summary: Inherited retinal degenerations, such as Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) and Leber's congenital amaurosis (LCA), are major causes of progressive and irreversible vision loss. The large number of genes associated with these disorders makes their clinical and molecular characterization difficult, while systemic biomarkers for disease progression or treatment response remain limited. These challenges were addressed by targeting cGMP-associated mechanisms shared by RP and LCA and integrating systemic biomarker profiling with retinal outcomes. Kinase activity analysis (kinome analysis) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells distinguished healthy and diseased states and captured therapy-associated signatures in rd10 mice treated with LP-CN03, a liposomal formulation of the cGMP analog CN03.
items.author: Topcu Okan, I. C., Ahmadian, M., Altay, H. Y. et al.

items.title: Epidermal Langerhans Cells Act as Neuroimmune Regulators of Pain and Itch
items.summary: Neuroimmune interactions in the skin coordinate immune defense and somatosensory perception, yet how immune cells shape sensory signaling remains poorly defined. Here, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), epidermal antigen-presenting cells, function as local immune-derived amplifiers of cutaneous sensory signaling. Anatomical and transcriptomic analyses reveal preferential LC association with non-peptidergic sensory neurons. LC activation increases neuronal and behavioral responses to thermal, mechanical, and pruritic stimuli without directly exciting sensory neurons, whereas LC inhibition or ablation selectively reduces pruritogen-evoked itch. We identified semaphorin 7A as a candidate LC-expressed mediator. Semaphorin 7A sensitized cultured sensory neurons to chloroquine and histamine, and neutralizing semaphorin 7A abolished the increase in chloroquine-evoked scratching produced by LC activation.
items.author: Sakai, K., Ishida, H., Pavlenko, D. et al.

items.title: Sequential pathways preserve kinetochore integrity in meiosis
items.summary: Kinetochores connect chromosomes to spindle microtubules, but how their integrity is maintained as they are remodelled during meiosis remains poorly understood. Here, we identify three distinct pathways linking centromeric chromatin to the outer kinetochore in budding yeast, mediated by the Ctf19 complex (Ctf19cCCAN), Mif2CENP-C and binding of Okp1CENP-Q-Ame1CENP-U to the Cse4CENP-A essential N-terminal domain (END). Although partially redundant during mitosis, all three connections are required during meiosis, with distinct temporal requirements. The assembled Ctf19cCCAN and Mif2CENP-C-dependent pathways maintain kinetochore integrity from meiotic entry, while Cse4CENP-A-Okp1CENP-Q-Ame1CENP-U binding becomes critical during prophase and the meiotic divisions. We further show that Ipl1Aurora B maintains kinetochore integrity independently of Ctf19cCCAN and provide evidence for an outer kinetochore-associated Ipl1Aurora B pool.
items.author: Hamaia, M. C., Spanos, C., Borek, W. E. et al.

items.title: SPACE-Tag Enables High-Throughput Spatial Chromatin Profiling With CUT&Tag
items.summary: Spatial epigenomics maps chromatin states within intact tissues, yet current methods remain limited by accessibility and scale. We developed SPACE-Tag, a spatial CUT&Tag framework that converts epigenetic marks-associated DNA into polyadenylated RNA through T7 based linear amplification, enabling direct integration with standard spatial transcriptomic workflows. Applied to the mouse brain, SPACETag resolved activating and repressive chromatin landscapes, recovered region-specific gene regulatory programs across anatomical domains, and showed strong correlation with existing bulk and single cell reference data. We generated an integrated multimodal atlas of the aging mouse brain, profiling five histone modifications and the transcriptome in parallel across the adult lifespan to establish the largest spatial multimodal dataset to date.

items.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
items.summary: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $φ$ couples via the effective operator $φ\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $φ$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.
items.author: Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia

items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.summary: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies.
items.author: Chen Chen, Omid Bagherieh, Naveen Nikamanth Appiah Balaji et al.

items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.summary: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for constructing robust CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces. ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable, robust to input perturbations, and 16-291x cheaper to invoke than the source model.
items.author: Peter Belcak, Greg Heinrich, Saurav Muralidharan et al.

items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Scenario-based simulation is central to evaluating autonomous-driving policies, but a scenario scripted before execution (i.e., with predetermined, fixed actor routes and speeds) may not preserve its intended interaction once the tested ego policy responds in closed loop. Scripted scenarios cannot adapt to unanticipated ego behavior, while learned traffic actors may remain reactive without reliably realizing a particular scenario intent. We introduce a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the joint traffic state and adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment for creating a specific scenario intent. At each step, the orchestrator solves a constrained optimization problem that preserves the intended interaction while limiting interventions and maintaining traffic feasibility.
items.author: Frieda Rong, Zhaoyue Wang, Veer Kapadia et al.

items.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
items.summary: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$.
items.author: Eloi Martinet, Leon Bungert

items.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
items.summary: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context. Yet the dominant paradigm in multi-person 3D motion prediction remains deterministic, with existing methods producing a fixed number of outputs per agent. In contrast, we present a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse future motions for multiple agents, modeling both global trajectories and root-relative poses. A B-spline reparameterization compresses the generative state space while enforcing temporal smoothness, and a dual-stream transformer conditions each agent's predictions on observed neighbor motion for interaction-aware forecasting. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on CMU-Mocap (UMPM) and 3DPW, outperforming deterministic baselines on joint position error, pose error, and final displacement error despite producing a full predictive distribution.
items.author: Aadya Agrawal, Ho Kei Cheng, Alexander Schwing

items.title: Graded convolutional networks: scale invariance without the scale and robustness to unknown blur
items.summary: The Gaussian jet of an image is a graded vector space: a dilation by $λ$ multiplies derivatives of order $k$ by $λ^{-k}$. Local graded convolutions are exactly homogeneous differential operators, and a local feature is dilation-invariant if and only if it factors through the scale-normalized jet or, without the scale, through the retraction onto the weighted sphere of the grading. Under unknown Gaussian blur the retraction changes only by a change of scale, whereas the scale-normalized jet acquires a grading factor that no radial normalization removes. At the zero jet the retraction separates image families that radial normalizations and continuous classifiers cannot.
items.author: Tanush Shaska

items.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
items.summary: Tendon-driven continuum robots can reach through constrained spaces, but contact along their bodies is invisible to the sensors at their motors. We show that this is a structural limitation rather than a tuning problem: the map from contact forces to tendon measurements has a null space of dimension at least seven, so no estimator that leaves the contact support free can locate contact. When the obstacle geometry is known, however, non-penetration and complementarity make the contact force locally identifiable, and we prove that the resulting system with unknown contact inputs is locally exponentially strongly detectable. We present a constrained moving horizon estimator (MHE) that encodes these conditions and runs in real time as one quadratic program per sample, and we give a local, mode-wise robust stability result for it.
items.author: Haitham El-Hussieny

items.title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
items.summary: We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited $1/f$ noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations.
items.author: Nada Khogeer, Jerison Parra, Caroline Desgranges et al.

items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.summary: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors.
items.author: Yu-Ning Zhang, Aleksandr S. Mokeev, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ et al.

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. Because population-majority bias is generally unidentifiable without external supervision, we focus on mitigating the downstream effects of finite-rollout variation. We propose \emph{Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO)}, which conditions within-prompt robust reweighting on observed vote reliability to make updates from sampling-sensitive prompts more conservative. We further introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce self-supervised forgetting during online adaptation. Across six mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and five model backbones, PC-Dr.DPO matches or outperforms the strongest TTRL baseline in 24 of 30 settings.
items.author: Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Yuanyuan Wang et al.

items.title: Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
items.summary: Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. While they have fundamental theoretical implications, their existence has not been rigorously established. This is particularly subtle in the setting of the full infinite-dimensional bootstrap, i.e. the limit of zero numerical truncation. In this article, we prove that extremal solutions exist for OPE maximisation problems in 1d CFT. These are a large class of generically interacting, unitary, exact solutions of the crossing equation that maximise an OPE coefficient. We also prove that these problems have 'zero duality gap', meaning there exist functionals arbitrarily close to extremality.
items.author: Filip Herček, Nat Levine

items.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
items.summary: Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise. Automated surgical scene descriptions could reduce this burden by leveraging recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge. Methods: We propose GRAC (Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning), a framework that represents surgical scenes as graphs capturing relationships among instruments, actions, and anatomical structures. Given an input scene graph, GRAC learns to retrieve relevant graph-caption pairs from training data. It compares instrument-tissue interactions between retrieved examples and the input scene, using comparison features to condition retrieved-caption representations during generation.
items.author: Rochak Dhakal, Chen Zhao, Soup Cobb et al.

items.title: Emergence and polymer physics of the center-vortex network: Confronting SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory
items.summary: The geometric organization and statistical properties of center-vortex networks provide a window into the infrared dynamics underlying confinement in Yang-Mills theory. Motivated by this connection, we investigate new consequences of a previously proposed confinement mechanism based on physically equivalent elementary Cartan fluxes. We show that, in the percolating phase, these fluxes dynamically reorganize into center-charge sectors whose dominant vortex tensions satisfy a Casimir scaling law, similar to that observed for confining string tensions. We then confront this result with the first nontrivial Yang-Mills case: the doubly charged vortex chains recently observed in SU(4) lattice simulations. To extract the parameters needed to connect the lattice ensemble with the effective description, we characterize how center-vortex chains grow and bend in SU(3) and SU(4) using polymer-inspired techniques not previously applied to center vortices.
items.author: Luis E. Oxman, Jackson A. Mickley, Derek B. Leinweber

items.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. Existing approaches address this challenge either through model-based methods, which often require accurate dynamics models, or through learning-based methods, which reduce this requirement but typically assume a fixed or predefined initial grasp. However, different geometrically stable grasps can lead to substantially different downstream manipulation performance. Therefore, we propose Grasp-TAGS, a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement.
items.author: Xun Tu, Minghao Zou, Karthik Desingh

items.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
items.summary: Many multimodal alignment problems require mapping a source modality into a fixed space defined by a target modality, where the target space is not merely an intermediate embedding but is used directly for downstream analysis. In this setting, successful alignment should preserve both the global structure of the target distribution and the instance-level correspondence observed in paired source--target training data. Existing objectives typically address only part of this goal: contrastive losses encourage relative similarity, distribution-matching losses improve marginal agreement, and pointwise regression fits each source sample to its paired target without explicitly modeling target-space path geometry. We propose FlowAlign, a flow-guided target-space alignment method that repurposes conditional flow matching as a training-time alignment signal rather than an inference-time transport model.
items.author: Ruizhi Yuan, Zeqiu Yu, Wei Gao et al.

items.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
items.summary: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions.
items.author: Ghansham Chandel, Siddhartha Das

items.title: Particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole
items.summary: By considering a massless Klein-Gordon field and the moving mirror model, we calculate particle production for a noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole sourced by smeared distributions of mass and charge. We show that noncommutative truncated trajectories diminish the emission spectrum at large frequencies, due to noncommutative effects on the external surface gravity of the black hole, in sharp contrast with the spectrum of a classical Reissner-Nordström black hole.
items.author: Alberto Maya, Marco Maceda

items.title: Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
items.summary: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor.
items.author: Henry Amir, Jack Zwettler, Ka Ho Wong et al.

items.title: Lessons from double-plane lenses for galaxy profiles, the Hubble tension, and the mass-sheet degeneracy
items.summary: Double-plane lenses, like single-plane lenses, are subject to the mass-sheet degeneracy, a fundamental limit to our knowledge of the deflector mass profiles from lensing. However, with a prior on the relative expansion history, unlike in the single-plane case, this degeneracy can be constrained with the modelling of lens images, without the need for time delays, velocity dispersion measurements or a prior on the Hubble constant $H_0$. We show that double-plane lenses are sensitive to a specific combination of the mass-sheet components of the two lens planes. Using literature values of the cosmological scaling factor from the double-plane lenses J0946 and AGEL0353, a measurement from the point-source images of J1721 (the ``Einstein zig-zag'' lens), and a reference value of $Ω_\mathrm{m}$, we show the constraints that can be placed on the mass-sheet component of each of these systems.
items.author: Daniel P. Johnson, Martin Millon, Pierre Fleury et al.

items.title: Beyond trial and error: A framework for AI-driven solid-electrolyte discovery
items.summary: A battery material can look perfect in the lab and still fail in a real battery. That is the puzzle facing researchers working on solid electrolytes, the materials seen as key to safer, longer-lasting batteries.

items.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
items.summary: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions.
items.author: Josep Cabedo, Claudio Iacovelli, Leticia Tarruell et al.

items.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
items.summary: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H$_2$ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H$_2$ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H$_2$ and para-H$_2$ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO$_2$ and N$_2$O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H$_2$ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H$_2$ loading.
items.author: Nathan McLane, Richard C. Remsing, Leah G. Dodson

items.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
items.summary: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning.
items.author: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck

items.title: Player-coach rift report will only galvanise England - George
