items.title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
items.summary: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics. We operationalise this intuition with (i) controlled summary generation from diverse models; (ii) a LLM evaluator that compares pairs of summaries and emits structured judgments; and (iii) a calibrated aggregation rule that combines supportive evidence while penalising only corroborated contradictions.

items.title: Scotland come full circle for another crack at All Blacks

items.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
items.summary: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical? In the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the de facto benchmark for Time Series Classification (TSC), the same recordings ask a different question: "which of 52 pigs produced this trace?". We find that several datasets are repurposed from their original task, built from toy setups, or have flawed test splits. items.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
items.summary: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.
items.author: Elias R. Koch, Albert Gallemí, Clàudia López et al.

items.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
items.summary: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants.
items.author: Gabriel Rabelo-Soares, Yevgeniy Kovchegov, Giorgio Torrieri

items.title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
items.summary: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$. We show that this operator agrees with the Hamiltonian on the ground-state subspace and has a spectral gap. For SU(2) specifically, the representation theory of the singlet sector gives an astronomical reduction in the number of degrees of freedom. This allows us to construct an efficient variational basis whose inner products we compute exactly. We demonstrate the method by computing a state that satisfies rigorous bounds on its energy $E\,g_{\mathrm{YM}}^{-2/3}\leq 4.18\times10^{-8}$ and ground-subspace overlap $\|P_{\ker H}ψ\|^2\geq 0.999997$. We compute ground-state moments with high precision, finding values consistent with the bounds from our matrix bootstrap.
items.author: Alexander Michel, Jaroslav Scheinpflug, Xi Yin

items.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
items.summary: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality or body part. We describe a radiology agentic framework that standardizes how an orchestrator calls modular tools to produce a structured report, and use it to measure what such a system can do with the tools from FDA-cleared radiology AI devices.

items.title: Deterministic Quantum Search for NP Problems Through Verifier-Based Oracle Construction
items.summary: Problems in the class NP are important in computational science, where a given candidate solution can be verified in polynomial time, while finding a solution may require evaluating the entire search space in the worst case. Classical exhaustive approaches generally solve such problems by evaluating the verifier function over all possible inputs, resulting in a worst-case query complexity of O(N), where N = d^n represents the size of the search space, d is the number of possible values for each variable, and n is the number of variables. Quantum search algorithms can solve unstructured search problems more efficiently by reducing the query complexity to O(sqrt (N)), providing a quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search.
items.author: Soumyajyoti Chatterjee, Harishankar Mishra, Asvija Balasubramanyam et al.

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost.
items.author: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova et al.

items.title: On Superconformal Index Degenerations and Half-Indices in S-Confining Gauge Theories
items.summary: We study the $p \rightarrow 0$ limit of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal indices and its relation to half-indices of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories. At the level of special functions, this limit reduces elliptic hypergeometric integrals to basic hypergeometric integrals. The scaling of the flavor fugacities determines the Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions of the chiral multiplets. The gauge multiplet has Neumann boundary conditions. We apply this prescription to s-confining theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$, $USp(2N)$, $G_2$, and $SU(N)$, and recover the half-index identities of several boundary confining dualities, expressed through the Nassrallah-Rahman and Gustafson integrals. For $SU(N)$ with a rank-two antisymmetric chiral, four fundamentals and $N$ antifundamentals, we obtain an analytic proof of the half-index identities proposed by Okazaki and Smith for all $N \geq 5$.

items.title: The Double Copy of the Doubly Spinning Black Ring
items.summary: We establish an exact curved-background Weyl double copy for the doubly spinning Pomeransky--Sen'kov black ring. Its full Weyl tensor is a quadratic form in two source-free Maxwell fields: one generated by the stationary Killing vector, the other a flux-carrying magnetic field obtained by linearizing the dipole-ring gauge potential about its vacuum limit. The mixed Maxwell bilinear is essential: no spacetime-independent real or complex change of field basis removes it. We identify the inverse $S_{IJ}$ of the Weyl coefficient matrix as a matrix zeroth copy. The same matrix arises independently from a weighted limit of the inner products of two Killing vectors in a six-dimensional Ricci-flat parent and satisfies $\Box_g S_{IJ}=-\tfrac12 F_{I\,ab}F_J{}^{ab}$.

items.title: Reversible Interchain Associations Dominate Plateau Elasticity in Conjugated Polymers
items.summary: The modulus plateau is widely regarded as a hallmark of topological entanglement in homopolymer melts and has been used to identify entanglement in semiflexible conjugated polymers. Using regiorandom poly(3-alkylthiophenes) as a model system, we show that their plateau elasticity relaxes through an Arrhenius process decoupled from segmental and terminal dynamics, reorganizes persistently under mechanical perturbation, and varies systematically with side-chain length. These behaviors are hard to reconcile with a purely topological-entanglement picture and instead support a transient network dominated by reversible interchain associations, consistent with π-π interactions between conjugated backbone segments. The results thus demonstrate that plateau elasticity alone does not uniquely identify topological entanglement in conjugated polymers.
items.author: Juncheng Zheng, Xiaobing Zuo, Xiaodan Gu et al.

items.title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_2$ S-folds and Seiberg--Witten curves
items.summary: We compute the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ S-folds of five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ rank-1 superconformal field theories. Two complementary constructions are presented. First, we implement the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ action by identifying pairs of points on the original curve, thereby mapping them to a single point on the S-folded curve. Second, motivated by arXiv:2112.14550, we tune mass parameters to special values, corresponding to the insertion of $D_4$ 7-branes. As a nontrivial consistency check, we show that the two Seiberg--Witten curves agree with each other when expressed in the Weierstrass normal form.
items.author: Sung-Soo Kim, Song Liu, Mudassar Sabir et al.

items.title: Exciton design via topological spin textures
items.summary: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys.
items.author: Karim Rezouali, Selcuk Sözeri, Samir Lounis

items.title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
items.summary: The reconstruction of the top-quark-pair ($t\bar{t}$) kinematics in the dilepton $t\bar{t}$ decay channel is challenging due to the presence of two undetected neutrinos. In this work, existing kinematic reconstruction methods used by the CMS Collaboration are studied using a Monte Carlo sample with $t\bar{t}$ events from CMS Open Data at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. An improved version of the loose kinematic reconstruction, LKRv2, is developed by imposing more stringent requirements on the jet-lepton pairing entering the reconstruction. A further modification, LKRv3, exploits the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems and improves the resolution of the reconstructed $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass relative to the baseline LKR by $7\%$, with smaller improvements for the transverse momentum and rapidity of $t\bar{t}$.

items.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation
items.summary: When should a robot look at the cup, and when at the portafilter? Spatial-reasoning benchmarks evaluate whether a model can describe a scene, but manipulation needs something more specific: the ability to acquire the particular evidence that makes the current command executable. A view that is informative for one task can be useless for another, even at the same workstation. We introduce Seeing What Matters, a benchmark for task-conditioned actionable spatial belief in simulated tabletop manipulation. Across three domains--coffee workstation, drawer/cabinet, and microwave/appliance--the benchmark provides 860 frozen evaluation cases; expanding across methods, budgets, and inference repeats yields more than 115,000 evaluator episodes under two protocols: closed-loop actionability and same-object functional out-of-distribution generalization.
items.author: Yina Jian, Mingkun Xu

items.title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
items.summary: The gallium anomaly, a 20% deficit in the measured $ν_e$ captures on $^{71}$Ga, remains unexplained. A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805 (2026), arXiv:2512.20560] has proposed a solution based on the breakdown of the factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions that underlies the prediction of the cross section, combined with ad hoc Gamow-Teller nuclear transition densities. We test this proposed solution with transition densities calculated within the nuclear shell model (NSM), normalized to the $^{71}$Ge electron-capture half-life and convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions. We explore several NSM interactions, bare and effective Gamow-Teller operators, as well as the impact of the valence space.
items.author: D. Castillo, D. Frycz, J. Menéndez

items.title: Edge dynamics of covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons
items.summary: We study the covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons in 2+1 dimensions in the presence of a planar boundary. The differential generator associated with the scalar gauge symmetry singles out a single scalar Ward combination of the functional field equations. Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes the normal-tangential field $w_i=h_{2i}$ explicit and yields an ordinarily conserved vector current with a standard $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra. Functional differentiation also produces a mixed equal-time bulk-boundary commutator between $w_1$ and $h_{11}$: it is non-vanishing at finite normal distance and vanishes in the intrinsic boundary limit.
items.author: Erica Bertolini, Matteo Carrega, Nicola Maggiore et al.

items.title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
items.summary: Infrared spectroscopy is a key tool to study complex structural dynamics in molecular systems. However, resolving weak or broad vibrational modes is challenging due to their rapid decay. Here, we demonstrate a technique to significantly extend the detectable lifetime - and thereby spectral resolution - of molecular signatures by employing synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. Utilizing a Cr:ZnS laser system and a nonlinear ZnGeP2 crystal, we achieve a 10-fold increase in the electric field strength of the infrared molecular signal, yielding a two-orders of magnitude enhancement in dynamic range and a 2-fold increase in the signal-to-noise ratio.

items.title: Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot
items.summary: Snake robots can leverage their hyper-redundant morphology for both locomotion and manipulation through distributed body contact but whole-body loco-manipulation is particularly challenging since the entire body serves simultaneously as propulsive mechanism and manipulation tool Prior work on wheeled legged and snake robot platforms has decoupled these functions through dedicated appendages body segmentation or grippers We present closed-loop loco-manipulation with our snake robot COBRA without this distinction such that any part of the body may make contact We develop a contact-implicit dynamic model unifying robot-ground robot-object and object-ground interactions within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulate a trajectory optimization over the full-order dynamics guided by a geometric planner and nominal proportional controller to autonomously push an object to a goal location during sidewinding We validate the planner and controller on hardware across varied configurations and present simulation results for a simplified trajectory optimization that resolves robot-object and object-ground contacts
items.author: Adarsh Salagame, Henry Noyes, Haroon Hublikar et al.

items.title: Uncovering TeV-scale dark matter with Z-fusion at a muon collider
items.summary: We demonstrate the advantage of the $Z$-boson fusion channel at a high-energy, high-luminosity muon collider in eliciting signals of a TeV-scale scalar dark matter (DM) particle. The utility of such a set-up lies in (a)the attainability of high centre-of-mass energy ($\approx 10 ~\rm TeV$), (b)the likely availability of large integrated luminosity ($\gtrsim 10~ab^{-1}$), and (c)the facility for efficient detection of very forward tagged muons. Our analysis is based on the process $μ^+ μ^- \rightarrow μ^+ μ^-$ + missing energy, driven by $Z$-fusion. We present the results in the context of (i) a scenario characterised by dimension-6 effective couplings, and (ii) an inert doublet model.
items.author: Anindya Datta, Jayita Lahiri, Biswarup Mukhopadhyaya

items.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
items.summary: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.

items.title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
items.summary: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62.

items.title: A wearable input/output interface learns personalized models of haptic perception
items.summary: Wearable haptic interfaces deliver physical stimuli to the skin, yet perceived locations vary widely across users and diverge from actuator locations, particularly for emergent tactile-feedback techniques. We developed a wearable haptic input/output (I/O) device integrating a 36-channel electrotactile array with capacitive touch sensing, enabling stimulation and user-reported percept locations to be registered within the same body-referenced coordinate frame. In 24 participants, the device revealed electrotactile and referred-thermal perceptual maps with notable interparticipant variability. Despite this variability, both modalities retained electrode-pair-specific spatial structure across participants. Tactile and thermal percepts also showed spatial correspondence, whose strength varied across participants. These findings motivated our human-in-the-loop calibration framework, which adapts a forward-prediction strategy to individual users and generates personalized perceptual models.
items.author: Wen Li, E. Magnus Adams, Zijie Xu et al.

items.title: Cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation from Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O
items.summary: Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O provide a solid-state setting for creating giant optical nonlinearities. Here, we use second-harmonic generation (SHG) to study Rydberg excitons in a doubly resonant optical microcavity designed to enhance both the pump and second-harmonic fields. We observe even-parity exciton states in an optical cavity and extend cavity-based measurements of Rydberg excitons up to $n=10$. The SHG intensity depends strongly on pump cavity detuning, showing the dominant role of the microcavity is the enhancement of the intra-cavity pump field. Analysis reveals an additional enhancement from the resonant second-harmonic cavity giving an overall SHG enhancement factor of $21 \pm 2$ inside the microcavity.
items.author: Horatio Q. X Wong, Krzysztof Sawicki, Madeleine Fisher et al.

items.title: Theory of Optical and Magneto-Optical Properties of [111]-Oriented Site-Controlled Quantum Dots
items.summary: Site-controlled [111]-oriented quantum dots (QDs) are promising sources of non-classical light, yet their optical spectra exhibit apparently conflicting symmetry signatures. At zero magnetic field, excitonic spectra are commonly interpreted as $C_{2v}$-like, whereas measurements in Faraday geometry display selection rules characteristic of $C_{3v}$-like symmetry. Here, we show that both regimes can be described consistently without invoking any change in the underlying structural symmetry. Combining 8-band $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ theory, a self-consistent Hartree-informed configuration interaction scheme, and group theoretical analysis, we introduce a controlled symmetry reducing perturbation that lowers the QD symmetry to $C_s$. At zero field, the optical response remains predominantly $C_{2v}$-like because the additional low-symmetry transitions carry only weak oscillator strengths.

items.title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
items.summary: We demonstrate simultaneous optical injection locking of an integrated pair of photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide. Due to fabrication-induced disorder, the two nanolasers exhibit distinct emission wavelengths, allowing their individual locking ranges to be resolved as a function of the injection-laser detuning and power. We identify a region where both nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the master laser. To probe this collective locked state, the two nanolasers are independently pump-modulated at distinct radio frequencies. A beat note at the difference frequency appears only within the overlap region, providing a direct RF signature of simultaneous locking. These results establish RF beating as a compact diagnostic of common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.

items.title: Vertically-coupled microring resonators for lithium niobate on insulator integrated photonics
items.summary: We propose and demonstrate lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) microring resonators that are verticallycoupled to index-matched silicon-rich silicon nitride (SiN x ) access waveguides as an alternative to conventional lateral coupling schemes for integrated photonics applications. The wafer-scalable fabrication process involves a planarization step exploiting a single-step and reproducible spin-coating of a SU-8 epoxy spacer layer which allows a controlled separation to be established between the resonator and its access waveguide. The resulting multimode and single-mode microring resonators exhibit, for their fundamental TE 0 mode, intrinsic quality factors of 4.0 x 10 5 and 3.4 x 10 5 , respectively.

items.title: Spin to Orbital Angular Momentum Conversion in the Neutron Nucleus Weak Interaction
items.summary: The neutron nucleus weak interaction generates a small parity non conserving rotation of the neutron spin as the neutron moves through matter. This parity-odd neutron rotary power can reach up to 2.2e-3 rad * cm-1 for slow neutrons in 139La, which possesses a p-wave resonance at 0.7 eV where the parity-odd asymmetry is greatly amplified. This spin rotation must conserve total angular momentum. Here we show that this conservation occurs through neutron orbital angular momentum generation. We experimentally demonstrate that a neutron prepared initially in a longitudinal spin-orbit state experiences no change in total angular momentum.

items.title: Experimental Evaluation of High-Throughput Structure Predictions
items.summary: High throughput computational databases such as Materials Project, the Open Quantum Materials Database, and Alexandria now each list on the order of 10^5 predicted stable compounds. However, the overall reliability of these predictions in terms of actual experimental synthesizability remains poorly understood. In this work we attempt to synthesize, via arc melting, 34 different predicted ternary compounds. The majority of these materials did not form in the predicted structure, instead resulting in disordered variants or multiphase mixtures. Four formed ordered structures not reported before, one of them at a composition reported earlier without a structure. We discuss both the failures and the successes, and identify simple filtering criteria that can help researchers avoid hypothetical materials that are unlikely to form.

items.title: Inversion symmetry breaking by interlayer hybridization in a tetralayer van der Waals heterostructure
items.summary: Inversion symmetry breaking unlocks a broad range of physical phenomena fundamental for modern technologies, motivating efforts to engineer noncentrosymmetric materials. In this context, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, which naturally lack inversion symmetry, have emerged as a versatile platform for valley physics, strong excitonic effects, and nonlinear optics. However, in their hexagonal stacking phase, inversion symmetry is restored in even-layer stacks and bulk form, suppressing these effects and limiting applications. In this work, inversion symmetry breaking is demonstrated in a vertically stacked tetralayer heterostructure assembled from two intrinsically centrosymmetric bilayer flakes, as evidenced by second harmonic generation measurements with an intensity comparable to that of their constituent monolayer.

items.title: Interference effects in MSSM Higgs boson searches at low $tanβ$: the $gg\to H\to WW, ZZ, hh$ and $gg \to A \to Zh$ channels
items.summary: The LHC limits on the heavy neutral Higgs bosons of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model, which are particularly relevant at low values of the ratio of vacuum expectation values $\tanβ$, have been obtained in the narrow-width approximation, without including the interference between the pure Higgs signal and the QCD background. We study the interference of the resonant heavy neutral CP-even $H$ and CP-odd $A$ boson contributions with the non-resonant gluon-fusion amplitudes in the processes $gg\to VV$ with $V=W,Z$, $gg \to hh$ and $gg\to Zh$ at low $\tanβ$, $1\le \tanβ\le 6$. We work at leading order but with the exact top-quark mass dependence, and with the longitudinal $VV$ and $Zh$ amplitudes obtained from the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem that lead to loop form factors similar to those appearing in $gg\to hh$.
items.author: Abdelhak Djouadi, John Ellis

items.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
items.summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. However, the origin of these structures remains unclear. We develop a mathematical model in which a modulator phase-locked to the QPO acts multiplicatively on the underlying variability. The resulting frequency mixing naturally produces both the ridge and hypotenuse associated with the fundamental QPO, as two parts of the same modulation-induced bispectral structure, and the same mechanism extends to the second harmonic. The model further predicts opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. We test these predictions using NICER observations of Swift~J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI~J1820$+$070.
items.author: Pei Jin, Mariano Méndez, Federico García et al.

items.title: Dynamical gluon mass generation, the Schwinger mechanism, spontaneous symmetry breaking, and color confinement in the linear covariant gauges of QCD
items.summary: We critically re-examine the Kugo-Ojima (KO) scenario for color confinement and identify several inconsistencies and a crucial error in its derivation. Within the KO framework, under customary assumptions, we show that the BRST quartet structure incorporates a unique mechanism for dynamical gluon mass generation -- namely, the Schwinger mechanism, in the formulation developed by Aguilar, Binosi, Ferreira, and Papavassiliou (ABFP). We show that the Schwinger mechanism is a Higgs mechanism, in that it occurs together with the spontaneous breaking of the global gauge charge, as it should. The ABFP bound state is the associated (unphysical) composite Goldstone boson. The zero-momentum value of the gluon propagator evaluated in the Pinch Technique--Background-Field Method (PT-BFM) naturally emerges in the derivation, setting a Renormalization-Group invariant scale for mass generation and suggesting a new nonperturbative interpretation of the PT-BFM.
items.author: Giorgio Comitini

items.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
items.summary: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.
items.author: Ohad Silbiger, Yakir Hadad

items.title: Scanning Probe Control, Quantum Dynamics, and Dispersive Readout of Suspended Carbon Nanotube Resonators
items.summary: Suspended carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer promising opportunities for quantum nanomechanics owing to their small effective mass, strong electrostatic tunability, and mechanical nonlinearity. We develop a unified theoretical framework for coherent control and readout of a suspended CNT driven by an atomic force microscope (AFM) tip and capacitively coupled to a Cooper-pair box (CPB). We first derive the linear and nonlinear Duffing response of the CNT and quantify the effects of AFM force gradients, tip-position fluctuations, and voltage noise on mechanical stability, dephasing, and heating. These results establish operating conditions for coherent actuation with limited backaction. We then quantize the Duffing oscillator, derive its Kerr anharmonicity, and identify the requirements for selective control of individual vibrational transitions.
items.author: Cristian Staii

items.title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
items.summary: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. In a search for phonon-mediated superconductors, density-functional perturbation theory on 45 structurally novel designs gives isotropic Allen-Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39; the highest is 24.0 K for ZrTiNb2CN3, and H4LiPd3 (23.2 K) lies on the static DFT hull.
items.author: Cristóbal Méndez, Justin Tahmassebpur, Tomás A. Arias

items.title: Graph representations of dislocation networks
items.summary: The mechanical response of a crystal is governed by the evolving network of dislocations it contains, yet quantitatively linking the `state of that network' to its yield stress remains challenging. Here we represent the dislocation networks obtained from discrete dislocation dynamic simulation as graphs, using five distinct graph representations, characterize each network through a compact set of topological properties, and predict the yield stress from these graph properties and the applied strain rate using a standard random forest model evaluated with strain rate stratified cross-validation. The model predicts the yield stress with $R^2\approx0.86-0.90$ across all box sizes and $R^2\approx0.91-0.94$ for larger box sizes, and this accuracy is consistent across all five representations, indicating that the topology-stress relationship is a robust feature of the graph properties rather than an artefact of any single graph representation.
items.author: Gaurav Lathiya, Markus Stricker

items.title: Sperm phospholipase C signaling via PLCζ1 and PLCδ4 is essential for Ca 2+ oscillations and fertility in mice
items.summary: by Neha Gupta, Lei Zhang, Hiroki Akizawa, Maria G. Gervasi, Darya A. Tourzani, Pablo E. Visconti, Ana Romarowski, Mariano Buffone, Wei Cui, Rafael A. Fissore Fertilization-induced calcium (Ca 2+ ) oscillations are essential for egg activation and embryonic development in mammals. The sperm-specific phospholipase C isoform, PLCζ1, is the primary trigger of these oscillations. Functional and clinical studies have linked mutations or reduced expression of PLCζ1 to male infertility. However, whether PLCζ1 alone accounts for Ca 2+ release at fertilization in all mammals remains uncertain. Male mice lacking Plcζ1 exhibit subfertility and reduced litter sizes; their sperm induce delayed, low-frequency Ca 2+ oscillations, indicating a compensatory mechanism.
items.author: Neha Gupta, Lei Zhang, Hiroki Akizawa et al.

items.title: Ten simple rules for a department chair
items.summary: by Lubomir Tomaska Department chairs occupy a pivotal position in the university. Teaching, research, graduate education, and much of the academic community's professional and administrative activity are organized at the departmental level. Yet, despite the importance of the position and the considerable challenges it entails, many scientists assume the role with little or no formal preparation for academic leadership. This paper is intended as a practical primer rather than a comprehensive guide to academic leadership. The proposed rules provide a framework that prospective and current department chairs can adapt to their own institutional circumstances, experience, and leadership style.
items.author: Lubomir Tomaska

items.title: PINN-based functional inference in size-structured population models: Application to fish oogenesis
items.summary: by Louis Fostier, Manon Lesage, Violette Thermes, Frédérique Clément, Romain Yvinec Early oogenesis in juvenile fish establishes the ovarian reserve, which conditions lifelong reproductive capacity. This process is regulated by local hormonal feedback mechanisms, mainly involving Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH). In this work, we develop a mechanistic size-structured population model describing an unstructured germ-cell compartment and a population of growing oocytes, with AMH feedback on the renewal of the precursor cells compartment. Using repeated cross-sectional observations of oocyte size distributions in fish ovaries, we formulate and solve a nonlinear inverse problem with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to infer three demographic functions: the size-dependent oocyte growth rate, the AMH-regulated net renewal rate of the precursor cells compartment, and the recruitment rate of new oocytes.
items.author: Louis Fostier, Manon Lesage, Violette Thermes et al.

items.title: kinGEMs: A robust and scalable framework for resource-constraint models through stochastic tuning of deep learning-predicted kinetic parameters
items.summary: by Rana A. Barghout, Lya Chiñas Serrano, Benjamin Sanchez-Lengeling, Radhakrishnan Mahadevan The construction of accurate enzyme-constrained genome-scale models (ecGEMs) remains a critical challenge in systems biology, limited by sparse kinetic data and the need for biologically meaningful representations. This work presents an integrated framework combining CPI-Pred, a deep learning model to predict kinetic parameters (kcat) from sequence and compound embeddings, with kinGEMs, a pipeline to incorporate these uncertainty-aware parameters into ecGEMs for metabolic optimization. By leveraging representations at multiple scales, the approach captures sequence, structure, and kinetic data to enhance model generalizability and accuracy. Rigorous benchmarking demonstrates the framework’s capability to predict growth rates and fluxes that are consistent with experimental observations and measured proteome fractions, reduce median flux variability by several folds, and yield better-constrained metabolic models by explicitly accounting for the uncertainty inherent in ML-predicted kinetic parameters.
items.author: Rana A. Barghout, Lya Chiñas Serrano, Benjamin Sanchez-Lengeling et al.

items.title: Sequence-based coevolutionary prediction of species-specific interactomes
items.summary: by Miguel Fernandez-Martin, Camila Pontes, Victoria Ruiz-Serra, Alfonso Valencia Evolutionarily conserved protein-protein interactions (PPIs) reveal fundamental biological processes. However, predicting protein function solely from these interactions provides an incomplete picture of biological systems. Computational methods for predicting PPIs often struggle due to limited functional annotations in databases, making it difficult to fully understand unique biological systems. This study introduces ContextMirror2.0 (CM2.0), a coevolution-based method designed to address these limitations. Coevolutionary approaches, unlike supervised machine learning methods, do not rely on labelled datasets, proving valuable in addressing the scarcity of data for species-specific PPIs. Around 40% of CM2.0’s top-1000 predicted PPIs for E.
items.author: Miguel Fernandez-Martin, Camila Pontes, Victoria Ruiz-Serra et al.

items.title: SwimmingIndividuals: A high-performance agent-based model for marine ecosystems
items.summary: by Matthew S. Woodstock, Jann Paul Mattern, Zhen Wu, Gregory L. Britten Because they are based on established theory, mechanistic models are essential for projecting ecological responses to novel conditions. Yet mechanistic agent-based model (ABM) applications have often been limited by computational constraints. This paper introduces SwimmingIndividuals , an open-source ABM framework that advances our ability to simulate physiological processes, animal movement, higher trophic level marine ecosystem dynamics, and fisheries removals at large ecological scales. The software's key contributions are a suite of mechanistic sub-models governing the full life cycle of each agent, including visual prey detection, adaptive behaviors such as diel vertical migration (DVM), a flexible bioenergetics engine with three taxon-specific metabolic architectures, and a spatial pathfinding algorithm for habitat-seeking movement.
items.author: Matthew S. Woodstock, Jann Paul Mattern, Zhen Wu et al.

items.title: Transcriptome- and methylome-wide association studies prioritized lung cancer genes in East Asian populations
items.summary: by Xingjie Hao, Minghan Qu, Yi Jiang, Cheng Wang, Ziwei Zhu, Pinpin Long, Chaolong Wang, Hongxia Ma, Shanshan Cheng The relationship between gene expression, DNA methylation, and lung cancer remains elusive in East Asian (EAS) populations. Transcriptome- and methylome-wide association studies (TWAS/MWAS) help uncover gene–trait associations by integrating multi-omics data, yet models trained mainly on European references limit cross-population generalizability. To address this, we developed EAS-specific gene expression and DNA methylation prediction models using whole-blood data from over 800 and 4,300 individuals, respectively. Applying these to lung cancer GWAS from Nanjing Medical University (13,327 cases; 13,328 controls) and Biobank Japan (4,444 cases; 489,012 controls), we identified 25 genes and 42 CpGs associated with lung cancer risk in the discovery stage, with seven genes and 32 CpGs replicated.
items.author: Xingjie Hao, Minghan Qu, Yi Jiang et al.

items.title: Yellow fever virus infection triggers the assembly of compositionally unique and specialised stress granules
items.summary: by Celia Jakob, Felix Streicher, Marta Lopez-Nieto, Lucy Eke, Aïssatou Aïcha Sow, Diane Lee, Jinjun Wu, J. Paul Taylor, Ana M. Matia-Gonzalez, Nolwenn Jouvenet, Nicolas Locker The phase separation of biomolecules into stress granules (SGs) allows the cell to tightly regulate translation activity in response to different stimuli, such as oxidative stress, starvation, or the recognition of non-cellular RNA. Recent reports suggest SGs induced during viral infection may act as a crossroad between the cellular stress response and the activation of the innate immune response. Here, we aimed to dissect the role of SGs in the context of yellow fever virus (YFV) infection.
items.author: Celia Jakob, Felix Streicher, Marta Lopez-Nieto et al.

items.title: Chandipura virus after recurrent outbreaks in India: Five questions that matter for preparedness

items.title: Suramin inspires next-generation broad-spectrum antiviral design targeting RdRps
items.summary: by Arwen Baer, Ge Yang, Fan Bu, Bin Liu Structural studies of diverse viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases reveal that the broad-spectrum antiviral Suramin binds distinct sites while repeatedly exploiting conserved RNA-interacting and electrostatic features. This Pearl highlights common vulnerabilities within viral RNA polymerases and discusses how structural studies provide a framework for future antiviral design.
items.author: Arwen Baer, Ge Yang, Fan Bu et al.

items.title: The underappreciated role for phase variation and quasi-clonality in microbial populations
items.summary: by Sophie Dyzenhaus, Scott D. Gray-Owen, Freeman Lan Phase variation is a well-established phenomenon in some bacteria, where it generates heritable phenotypic variants within a population. These states, while reversible, are stable across generations, giving rise to quasi-clonal populations even when starting from a single bacterium. Underlying mechanisms include variation in short homopolymeric or heteropolymeric sequence repeats, DNA inversions mediated by site-specific recombination, reversible insertions and deletions, and switching between alternative methylation states. Although phase variation occurs in diverse bacteria, its contribution to phenotypic heterogeneity remains overlooked and use of the term is often absent in describing this phenomenon.
items.author: Sophie Dyzenhaus, Scott D. Gray-Owen, Freeman Lan

items.title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on vitamin D status and physical performance in football players: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: by Jinfa Gu, Yu Zhang, Luhua Xiao Background/Objectives Low vitamin D status is frequently reported among athletes, but whether vitamin D supplementation improves physical performance in football players remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration, jump performance, sprint performance, aerobic capacity, and muscular performance in association football and futsal players. Methods PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026. Controlled intervention studies comparing vitamin D supplementation with control conditions were eligible. Standardized mean differences were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects meta-analyses.
items.author: Jinfa Gu, Yu Zhang, Luhua Xiao

items.title: Tranexamic acid for anemia in women of reproductive age: A systematic review of randomized trials
items.summary: by Sima Berendes, Katharine Ker, Hilary O. D. Critchley, Raoul Mansukhani, Ian Roberts Objective The global target to halve the prevalence of anemia by 2025 has not been met. New strategies are needed. This systematic review examined the effect of tranexamic acid on anemia, menstrual health and wellbeing in women of reproductive age. Methods We searched six databases from inception to 30 August 2025 and reference lists of seven related reviews. We included randomized trials comparing the effects of tranexamic acid with placebo or standard care on uterine bleeding. Eligible participants had normal menstrual bleeding or any type of non-pregnant abnormal uterine bleeding.
items.author: Sima Berendes, Katharine Ker, Hilary O. D. Critchley et al.

items.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and Chinese art teachers’ career exploration behavior: The roles of job substitution risks, job insecurity, and organizational AI readiness
items.summary: by Jia Li, Yun Gao The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in art education raises questions about teachers’ professional security and career development. Drawing primarily on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and, in a complementary manner, on Career Construction Theory (CCT), this cross-sectional study examined associations among AI adoption, perceived job substitution risk, job insecurity, career exploration behavior, and organizational AI readiness. Survey data from 381 Chinese art teachers were analyzed using Mplus 7.4. AI adoption was positively associated with career exploration behavior. Statistically significant indirect associations were observed through job substitution risk, job insecurity, and their hypothesized sequential combination.
items.author: Jia Li, Yun Gao

items.title: Estimation of aerobic and anaerobic performance using a novel intermittent reactive agility test – An exploratory correlation study
items.summary: by Bettina Karsten, Richard Latzel, Michael Kölling, Thorben Hülsdünker Separate tests are usually used to assess an athlete's ability to meet the aerobic and anaerobic demands of ball sports. These tests often compromise ecological validity by relying on linear runs and sprints rather than multidirectional reactive agility. This study investigated the correlations between a novel motor-cognitive reactive agility (RA) test and aerobic and anaerobic performance indices. Twenty-two trained participants (V˙O 2max : 56 ± 6.4 ml ∙ kg -1 ∙ min -1 ) performed a treadmill ramp test to determine maximum oxygen uptake (V˙O 2 max), a running-based anaerobic sprint test (RAST) to determine peak power output (PPO), average power putput (POAV), fatigue index (FI) and anaerobic capacity (AC) and a motor-cognitive RA test on the SKILLCOURT.
items.author: Bettina Karsten, Richard Latzel, Michael Kölling et al.

items.title: Pharmacological cGAS-STING pathway inhibition on neuroinflammation in animal models of traumatic brain injury: A systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
items.summary: by Myriam Lamamri, Stéphanie Sigaut, Hélène Cwerman-Thibault, Valérie Faivre, Juliette Van Steenwinckel, Vincent Degos, Pierre Gressens, Alice Jacquens Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of mortality and long-term neurological disability worldwide. Secondary injury mechanisms, particularly neuroinflammation, play a key role in determining neurological outcomes after the initial trauma. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway has recently been identified as a mediator of innate immune activation following brain injury. Activation of this pathway promotes microglial activation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to neuronal damage and impaired recovery. Pharmacological inhibition of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway has therefore emerged as a promising neuroprotective strategy in experimental TBI models.
items.author: Myriam Lamamri, Stéphanie Sigaut, Hélène Cwerman-Thibault et al.

items.title: Adaptive–based cascaded PI–PID controller for load frequency regulation with real time verification
items.summary: by Abdullah M. Alharbi, Mohamed A. Awad, Mahmoud A. Attia, S.F. Mekhamer, Ahmed H. EL-Ebiary In order to address Load Frequency Control (LFC) problems in single-area and interconnected two-area power systems, this work proposes a cascaded control scheme that combines PI–PID control with the Set-Membership Affine Projection Algorithm (SMAPA). The proposed approach is evaluated under various practical operating conditions, including step load disturbances, random load variations, wind power fluctuations, and parameter uncertainty. In addition, frequency-domain stability analysis is performed to further assess the robustness of the proposed controller, while real-time validation is conducted for the two-area system to demonstrate its practical effectiveness.
items.author: Abdullah M. Alharbi, Mohamed A. Awad, Mahmoud A. Attia et al.

items.title: Aligning entity of knowledge graph based on graph convolutional network with maximum translated similarity
items.summary: by Jianhui Zhou, Yun Gao, Xiangbing Zhao, Yanping Guo, Xulong Zhang Entity alignment is a pivotal technology for integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs, yet most embedding-based alignment methods destroy the inherent structural embedding information of knowledge graphs when unifying cross-graph embedding spaces, resulting in limited alignment accuracy and stability. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a novel model for entity alignment tasks, which named as Graph Convolutional Network with Maximum Translated Similarity (GCN-MTS). GCN-MTS innovatively leverages a maximum translated similarity mechanism to optimize the adjacency matrix, degree matrix and loss function. This core design effectively maintains the original relative embedding structure of cross-graph entities during embedding space unification, which is the key improvement over existing approaches.
items.author: Jianhui Zhou, Yun Gao, Xiangbing Zhao et al.

items.title: HIV/AIDS knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among adult residents of the United Arab Emirates: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Hiba Jawdat Barqawi, Kamel A. Samara, Abdul Rahman Sheiko, Mohamed Alhariri, Moustafa Saber Mashal, Amal Abu Helwa, Eman Abu-Gharbieh Background HIV-related stigma remains a significant barrier to prevention and treatment efforts in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. This study assessed HIV knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among United Arab Emirates (UAE) residents. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted across the UAE between January and March 2025. A total of 1,211 eligible adult residents were recruited through convenience sampling. Demographic analyses included all 1,211 participants, while HIV knowledge and stigma analyses included 1,171 participants with analyzable outcome data.
items.author: Hiba Jawdat Barqawi, Kamel A. Samara, Abdul Rahman Sheiko et al.

items.title: Harrowing experiences of vagina fistula victims in the Kpandai District of Ghana: A qualitative study
items.summary: by Eric Elorm Ahorsu, Joshua Adeti, Ernest Kemevor Selasie, Mohammed Ibn Shamsudeen, Cynthia Akos Okumasi, Benjamin Amedume, Justice Wiston Amstrong Jonathan Background Vaginal fistula (VF), particularly vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), remains a significant reproductive health challenge in many low-resource settings, including the Kpandai District of Ghana. Despite its profound physical and psychosocial impact, the lived experiences of affected women in rural districts remain under-documented. Aim This study explored the lived experiences of women diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula in the Kpandai District of Ghana, focusing on their physical, emotional, and social challenges, as well as coping strategies. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using in-depth interviews with ten women with clinically confirmed VVF.
items.author: Eric Elorm Ahorsu, Joshua Adeti, Ernest Kemevor Selasie et al.

items.title: Epidemiological surveillance of bacterial pathogens in cultured European sea bass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye
items.summary: by Pınar Çelik, Vyron Georgalas, İhsan Çelik Intensive aquaculture of European sea bass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye faces continuous production challenges from infectious diseases, yet comprehensive multi-year baseline data remain limited. This study presents a multi-year retrospective surveillance program (2020–2025) monitoring bacterial pathogens associated with 748 distinct cage-level disease outbreaks in fish across 19 discrete offshore commercial sea farms. To maintain industry confidentiality, diagnostic data from these separate facilities were fully aggregated and evaluated across three broad macro-regional surveillance zones. A total of 5,235 fish displaying clinical signs underwent diagnostic necropsy. Presumptive bacterial identification was conducted using phenotypic profiling through the API 20E system, and organ touch-imprint cytology.
items.author: Pınar Çelik, Vyron Georgalas, İhsan Çelik

items.title: Source apportionment and non-carcinogenic health risk assessment of selected heavy metals in the Turag river area of Gazipur District, Bangladesh
items.summary: by Juned Hussain Chowdhury, Md Jamil Hossain, Ryadul Alam, Ifteker Uddin Sakib, Wahida Ahmed, Naimur Rahman Sarker, Sangita Chakroborty, Md Mushfiqur Rahman Porosh, Md Shakhaoat Hossain, Badhan Saha, Mohammad Moniruzzaman, Ayesha Ahmed Introduction Rapid industrialization in Bangladesh, especially in Gazipur District, has raised concern over heavy metal contamination of soil and water and the associated health risks to nearby residents. This study compared the concentration, spatial distribution, probable sources, and non-carcinogenic health risk of five heavy metals (Hg, Ni, Mn, Zn, and Co) in soil and water in the Turag River areas in Gazipur District. Methods Soil and water samples were collected from 18 sites in the Turag River (including both industrial and non-industrial zones) and analyzed for five heavy metal concentrations (Hg, Ni, Mn, Zn, and Co) using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS).
items.author: Juned Hussain Chowdhury, Md Jamil Hossain, Ryadul Alam et al.

items.title: Finite-time robust motion control of intelligent vehicles based on neural approximation and disturbance estimation
items.summary: by Lijuan Zhang This paper addresses the inherent trade off between rapid convergence and high‑precision disturbance rejection in intelligent vehicle motion control under severe nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties, and time varying external perturbations. A composite finite‑time robust control strategy is proposed by synergistically integrating a nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) surface, radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN), and a finite time disturbance observer (FTDO). The NFTSM guarantees singularity free finite time convergence of the tracking errors. The RBFNN approximates the slowly varying unknown dynamics, while the FTDO compensates online for the neural approximation residual and fast varying disturbances in a cascaded “coarse to fine” manner.
items.author: Lijuan Zhang

items.title: Exploratory cluster analysis of noninvasive vascular measures reveals heterogeneous vascular profiles after stroke
items.summary: by Bria L. Bartsch, Amanda N. Engler, Sandra A. Billinger Vascular dysfunction is prevalent after stroke and contributes to elevated cardiovascular risk; however, the extent to which vascular heterogeneity exists in this population remains unclear. This study examined whether distinct multi-domain cluster-derived vascular profiles are present in individuals with chronic stroke and whether these profiles are associated with functional performance. Vascular structure and function were assessed using flow-mediated dilation, carotid intima-media thickness, pulse wave velocity, and augmentation index, with age included in vascular clustering to account for vascular aging. Unsupervised k-means clustering was applied to identify vascular profiles. Functional performance was assessed using gait speed and predicted peak oxygen consumption (VO 2peak ) derived from a submaximal exercise test.
items.author: Bria L. Bartsch, Amanda N. Engler, Sandra A. Billinger

items.title: A Kampo medicine, kamishoyosan, ameliorates menstruation-associated symptoms in patients with premenstrual syndrome: An exploratory open-label, randomized controlled trial
items.summary: by Jun Chikumi, Eri Sato, Ai Ikebuchi, Yohei Tokita, Mitsuto Fukushige, Mayu Yamamoto, Hiroshi Sunada, Yusuke Endo, Hisashi Noma, Tasuku Harada, Fuminori Taniguchi Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a psychological or physical symptom. We conducted an open-label, randomized, exploratory trial with the aim of evaluating the efficacy and safety of kamishoyosan (KSS) for PMS. KSS was administered orally during three menstrual cycles. The primary endpoint was the change in the premenstrual Menstrual Distress Questionnaire (MDQ) total score. The secondary endpoints included MDQ total and subscale scores, a daily symptom questionnaire, the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) Questionnaire, overall impressions, sleep status, and heart rate.

items.title: Antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar’s poultry sector: informality, knowledge gaps, and market constraints
items.summary: by Sophie Molia, Ilo Tsimok’Haja Ramahatafandry, Michel Rakotoharinome, Christian Lienhardt, Muriel Figuié, Alexandre Hobeika, Daouda Kassié Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is a major global public health threat, largely driven by the overuse and misuse of antibiotics. Tackling its animal health component is particularly difficult in low- and middle-income countries, where data and resources are limited. This qualitative study aims to explore antibiotic use (ABU) and its underlying drivers in poultry farms in Analamanga, Madagascar’s region with the highest poultry density. In April 2023, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 79 poultry farmers (13 backyard and 66 semi-intensive), 10 animal health professionals, and 10 agrovet shop sellers.
items.author: Sophie Molia, Ilo Tsimok’Haja Ramahatafandry, Michel Rakotoharinome et al.

items.title: Introduction of contraceptive implants as a family planning strategy in Honduras and Chiapas: Results from the Salud Mesoamerica Initiative (SMI)
items.summary: by Adrián Santoro, Natalia Basualdo, Federico Rolón, Lucía Bartolomeu, Camila Volij, Matt Simon, Brittany Hagedorn, Diego Ríos-Zertuche, Santiago Esteban, Adolfo Rubinstein Expanding access to a broad range of contraceptive methods is critical for reducing unintended pregnancies and improving reproductive health. This study evaluates the introduction of subdermal contraceptive implants in the selected areas of Honduras and Chiapas, Mexico, in the context of the Salud Mesoamérica Initiative, a results-based financing program focused on disadvantaged populations. Data were obtained from household surveys conducted between 2012 and 2022 among women aged 15–49 years in selected intervention and comparison municipalities in Chiapas, Mexico, and Honduras, using a two-stage sampling design.
items.author: Adrián Santoro, Natalia Basualdo, Federico Rolón et al.

items.title: A psychological perspective on peer tutoring in EFL collaborative writing in Chinese higher education contexts
items.summary: by Zefu Huang, Nalini Arumugam In Chinese higher learning institutions, students learning English as a foreign language (EFL) often demonstrate low writing self-efficacy (WSE) and poor writing competence. The present study examined the associations between the integration of peer tutoring with collaborative writing and students’ WSE and writing outcomes from a psychological perspective. A quasi-experiment was implemented for 11 weeks for 100 Chinese university students studying EFL. Changes in WSE were examined, and writing competence was assessed using tests. The results showed a notable rise in students’ WSE after the instructional intervention. The multiple linear regression analysis indicated that gains in WSE were positively associated with the writing outcome after controlling for pretest writing competence and group membership, explaining 20.2% of the total variance.
items.author: Zefu Huang, Nalini Arumugam

items.title: Whose morning, whose evening? Temporal asymmetries in intermedia agenda-setting between X and online news in Türkiye
items.summary: by Mehmet Ceylan, Ramazan Yılmaz, Rumeysa Erdoğan Bodur This study examines whether temporal ordering between X and online news varies across first-level issue and second-level attribute agendas in Türkiye’s polarized media environment. The analysis draws on 448,664 X posts and 10,357 articles from 19 mainstream online news outlets collected during the 31-day period preceding and including the 31 March 2024 Istanbul local election. Using 12-hour AM/PM windows, we conducted 122 cross-lagged panel analyses—62 same-day AM → PM and 60 overnight PM→next-day AM panels across the two agenda levels—comparing issue- and attribute-indicator frequency profiles. First-level issue agendas were strongly synchronized, with correlations often approaching or exceeding r = .90, whereas second-level attribute relationships were weaker and less consistent.

Aremu, Marguerite Adriaanse, Daphne van Dijk, Preyanka Pillay, Sam Africa, Erika Jones, Mashiko Setshedi, Adrian Brink, Wendy A. Burgers, Ntobeko A. B. Ntusi Background Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with poor control in low- and middle-income countries. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ) has been associated with hypertension through inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and immune pathways, but data from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resistant hypertension, are limited. Methods This cross-sectional observational study will enrol 200 adults aged ≥18 at a tertiary academic hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: 80 with resistant hypertension, 80 with non-resistant hypertension and 40 with normotension.

items.title: Visual outcomes and headache in intracranial hypertension following cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: A retrospective cohort study
items.summary: by Theresia Knoche, Ivo Grueninger, Charlotte Pietrock, Zohreh Jami, Leon Alexander Danyel Intracranial hypertension is a frequent complication of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVT), posing a risk for permanent visual impairment. However, long-term visual outcomes have not been systematically assessed using objective neuro-ophthalmic measures. We retrospectively evaluated consecutive adults presenting to a single-center tertiary intracranial hypertension clinic between 2019 and 2025 with intracranial hypertension following CVT. Visual outcomes were assessed using best-corrected visual acuity, automated perimetry, and optical coherence tomography measuring global peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Headache phenotype and medication overuse were documented. Nineteen patients (11 female; mean age 33.4 ± 12.1 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 3.4 ± 2.4 years after diagnosis of CVT-related intracranial hypertension.
items.author: Theresia Knoche, Ivo Grueninger, Charlotte Pietrock et al.

items.title: E-Service quality and customer satisfaction in online shopping: Implications for sustainable digital commerce
items.summary: by Mohammed AL Awadh The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified competition among online retailers, making e-service quality increasingly important for building customer trust, satisfaction, and sustainable customer–platform relationships. This study examines the relationships among e-service quality, customer trust, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty using a second-order Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework. The five SERVQUAL dimensions such as empathy, responsiveness, reliability, assurance, and tangibles were modeled as first-order constructs reflecting the higher-order construct of service quality. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 402 respondents with prior online-shopping experience. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and SEM were employed to assess the measurement and structural models.
items.author: Mohammed AL Awadh

items.title: Clinical and epidemiological characteristics of invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease in Ghana
items.summary: by Francis Opoku Agyapong, Michael Owusu, Michael Owusu-Ansah, Sampson Twumasi-Ankrah, Kennedy Gyau Boahen, Gifty Nkrumah, Ezekiel Bonwin Ackah, Rachel Laadi Sulla, Akua Serwaa Boafo, Nathaniel Nsiah-Poku, Portia Okyere Boakye, Anthony Enimil, Yaw Adu-Sarkodie, Ellis Owusu-Dabo, Florian Marks Background Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) disease remains a significant public health threat in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Although the disease is important, its clinical characteristics are not well described in literature. This study describes the clinico-epidemiological profile of iNTS disease in Ghana aiming to bridge important knowledge gaps and inform more effective management strategies. Methods The study spanned 8 years and utilized selected fever surveillance sites in Ghana.

items.title: Various aspects of upper-limb muscle strength and tennis performance: A comparative study of U12 and U14 female tennis players
items.summary: by Tomasz Waldziński, Aleksandra Durzyńska, Bartłomiej Niespodziński, Jan Mieszkowski, Ewa Waldzińska, Andrzej Kochanowicz This study investigated the relationship between muscle strength and tennis performance, assessed using the International Tennis Number (ITN) on-court test, operationalized as point-based outcomes (total points and subcomponent points), in young female tennis players aged under 12 (U12) and under 14 (U14). Thirty-three players underwent a comprehensive evaluation including ITN testing, general strength tests (handgrip strength, flexed arm hang, and tennis-ball throw), isometric upper-limb muscle strength, and sense of force assessment. Results demonstrated significantly higher ITN scores and muscle strength in the U14 group, with differences largely attributable to body size and training experience.

Klein, Abigail Shoben, Darren Mays Background Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are novel nicotine products and evidence on how features of ONP packaging affect product engagement, perceptions, use intentions, and behavior is limited. Moral-Munoz Background Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke. items.title: Deep learning optimisation for cardiology: Neural Architecture Search-driven arrhythmia classification with electrocardiograms
items.summary: by Erik Vanegas Müller, Arese Joe-Oshodi, Abhirup Banerjee, Mauricio Villarroel Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for roughly 50% of all cardiac deaths. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is widely used for diagnosing cardiac disease. However, the complexity of interpretation limits the ECG’s efficacy. Modern deep learning methods can assist clinicians in diagnosis. We applied Neural Architecture Search (NAS) to identify optimal deep learning architectures for classifying cardiac arrhythmias with ECGs. We applied the Differentiable Architecture Search strategy to an AutoFormer search and trained, validated, and tested the resulting model on the PhysioNet Challenge 2021 (PC21) dataset (n = 88,253 from three continents).

This study aims to investigate the role of the HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis in regulating retinal astrocyte senescence and endothelial function in DR. Methods Mouse retinal astrocytes were exposed to high glucose (30 mM) to mimic diabetic conditions. Senescence was evaluated by β-galactosidase staining. Signaling pathways were manipulated using HIF-1α inhibitor (PX-478), PPAR-γ inhibitor (T0070907), SIRT1 agonist (SRT2104), and autophagy inhibitor (3-MA).

items.title: A State-Variable Theory of Evolving Material Symmetry
items.summary: Material architecture can evolve during loading, yet its mechanically expressed symmetry depends on both the structural state and the constitutive coupling. We connect these quantities through one parent-invariant free energy with a symmetric traceless internal tensor $\mathbf Q$. Its stabilizer distinguishes isotropic, uniaxial, and biaxial states, and projected gradient kinetics satisfies the structural dissipation inequality. Parent invariance generally guarantees only symmetry inheritance. For an explicit two-coupling elastic potential, we derive a stiffness-contraction reconstruction of $\mathbf Q$ and prove equality of the structural and tangent rotational symmetries for every nonzero coupling pair. The associated acoustic tensor links residual symmetry to protected transverse degeneracies.

items.summary: We present the absolute calibration of a transmission grating spectrometer (TGS) with uncertainty estimates in the 5--400 nm range using synchrotron radiation at the BEAR beamline at Elettra light source in Trieste, Italy. Firstly, the spectral responsivity of a Si photodiode in the spectrometer was absolutely calibrated with respect to the absolutely-calibrated beamline photodiode. Subsequently, this photodiode was used to calibrate the transmittance of Zr and Al thin-film filters, along with bulk MgF$_2$ and UV-grade fused silica windows at their operating positions in the spectrometer to minimize mounting-induced uncertainties. Next, the quantum efficiency of the spectrometer's CCD camera was calibrated over the 5--400 nm range.

items.title: Disentangling Spin and Orbital Contributions in the Search for Altermagnetic Terahertz Conversion in RuO2
items.summary: Rutile RuO2 has emerged as a prominent candidate altermagnet, yet the microscopic origin of its reported charge-angular-momentum conversion remains unsettled. Recent theoretical and experimental advances have highlighted a potentially dominant role of orbital transport, raising a fundamental ambiguity between spin- and orbital-mediated conversion in RuO2. Here, we report the first experimental disentanglement of the spin- and orbital-to-charge conversion channels in RuO2 heterostructures using terahertz emission spectroscopy. We identify Fe as a predominantly spin-current injector, whereas Ni and permalloy predominantly inject orbital currents, revealing a substantial orbital contribution to ultrafast terahertz emission. Under controlled spin-current injection, we find no evidence for inverse altermagnetic spin-splitting effect.

items.title: Outcomes of Patients with Rare Cancers Treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors with and Without Lung and/or Liver Metastases (NCI/SWOG S1609).
items.summary: Introduction Limited prior retrospective data, primarily among patients with lung cancer, liver cancer, and melanoma, has indicated that liver metastases are associated with poorer outcomes with chemotherapy, targeted agents, and checkpoint inhibitor therapy. We used a unique clinical trial resource to evaluate whether liver and/or lung metastases were associated with outcomes among patients with rare tumors treated with combination anti-CTLA-4 (cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4) and anti-PD-1 (programmed cell death protein 1) therapy. Methods The basket trial, SWOG trial S1609 (NCT02834013, DART trial), treated 655 eligible patients without lung or liver primary cancers. Associations with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated with Cox regression models.
items.author: Wang Y, Othus M, Chae YK, Davies M, Dietrich E, Patel SP, Kurzrock R.

items.title: PIKfyve inhibition induces LRRK2 activation through phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate and CASM.
items.summary: LRRK2 is a Parkinson's disease-associated kinase that phosphorylates Rab GTPases. Hyperactivation of LRRK2, which is thought to cause Parkinson's disease, occurs on stressed endolysosomal membranes via conjugation of ATG8 to single membranes (CASM) and Rab, whereas the involvement of specific membrane lipids remained unclear. Here, we found that the inhibition of PIKfyve that metabolizes phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) induces hyperactivation of LRRK2 and that additional inhibition of the class III phosphoinositide 3-kinase that generates PI3P suppressed LRRK2 hyperactivation. Cellular PI3P levels were indeed elevated when LRRK2 was activated. CASM-induced activation of LRRK2, but not CASM itself, was suppressed by phosphoinositide 3-kinase inhibitors, whereas inhibition of CASM or Rab12/Rab29 suppressed LRRK2 activation induced by PIKfyve inhibitors.
items.author: Kuwahara T, Yoshii G, Sakurai M, Suenaga S, Nakanishi H, Jefferson M, Wileman T, Tomii K, Iwatsubo T.

items.title: Developmental elimination of electrical synapses by UNC-51/UNC-76-mediated vesicular transport.
items.summary: Neural circuit maturation requires precise elimination of transient synaptic connections, but how electrical synapses are eliminated remains unknown. Using Caenorhabditis elegans PLM mechanosensory neurons, we found that gap junctions form transiently during early development and are subsequently eliminated as the circuit matures. These transient electrical synapses drive high-frequency calcium oscillations; optogenetic ablation of early gap junctions abolishes calcium dynamics and disrupts chemical synapse formation, while restoring calcium activity independently of gap junction coupling substantially rescues this defect, directly linking electrical synapse-driven calcium dynamics to chemical synapse formation. Through forward genetic screening, we identified the conserved kinase UNC-51/ULK as essential for elimination.
items.author: Huang H, Yang Y, Xu Y, Jian Y, Qiu S, Zhao Z, Yan D, Meng L.
