items.title: Effect of extreme heat on fall risk in older adults in a rural state.
items.summary: Background Falls are common in older adults and may result in decreased functional ability, hospitalization, and death. Extreme temperature events, expected to worsen as a result of changing climates, have systemic impacts on the body, many of which overlap with the risk factors for falls in older adults. Our objective was to quantify the association between temperatures of 32°C (90°F) and greater and fall risk in older adults in a rural population. Methods We analyzed emergency medical services (EMS) patient care report data (2019-2023, n = 26,266) and hospital discharge data (emergency department visits (2011-2022, n = 96,658); hospitalizations (2011-2022, n = 31,407) on falls among adults aged 55 years and older at the ZIP Code level in Montana using case-crossover conditional logistic regression models.
items.author: Adam CE, Yang H, Graham J, Semmens EO, Knudson J, Fogaça B, Orr A, Landguth EL.

items.title: Associations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) with muscle mass and function in women in midlife.
items.summary: Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous chemicals that disrupt hormonal and inflammatory pathways and may thereby influence body composition. Reduced muscle mass increases risk of frailty, a condition disproportionately affecting women. Methods In the Project Viva cohort (N = 551), we assessed outcomes in midlife (2017-2024, mean age 50.7 years) including appendicular lean mass index (ALMI), a marker of muscle mass measured via dual X-ray absorptiometry, and plasma concentrations of PFAS at enrollment in pregnancy (1999-2002) and in midlife. We used covariate-adjusted linear regression of individual PFAS and the PFAS burden score and quantile g-computation (qgcomp) mixture models to examine PFAS-ALMI associations, and we explored effect modification by menopausal status, diet, and physical activity at midlife.
items.author: Rokoff LB, Rifas-Shiman SL, Lin PD, Cardenas A, Botelho JC, Calafat AM, Zota AR, James-Todd T, Gold DR, Fleisch AF, Oken E.

items.title: Spleen as an Ectopic Site for Human Stem Cell-derived Hepatocyte and Islet Transplantation in an Operational Immunodeficient Pig Model.
items.summary: Background Extensive efforts in cell transplantation have focused on identifying effective transplantation sites, including autologous and ectopic options. Intraportal transplantation of pancreatic islets into the liver has produced favorable outcomes. We examined whether the spleen, which possesses a sinusoidal vascular structure similar to that of the liver, could serve as an alternative transplantation site for human progenitor cell-derived hepatocyte- or islet-like cells, using the same clinically relevant transplantation procedure. Methods The operational immunodeficient pig (OIDP) model has been used for transplantation of human stem cell-derived cells. In accordance with the OIDP protocol, recipients underwent thymectomy and received tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisolone via a gastric tube, while the spleen was not removed.
items.author: Enosawa S, Noguchi H, Umezawa A, Miyamoto Y, Nasu M, Kin T, Kobayashi E.

items.title: Exposure to wildfire smoke and risk of mortality and hospitalization among hemodialysis patients in the Western United States: Effect modification by extreme heat events.
items.summary: Background Climate change is increasing the extent of wildfires and extreme heat events (EHEs) in the Western United States. Our objective was to estimate the risk of all-cause mortality and hospitalization among end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients after exposure to wildfire smoke, EHEs, and the combined occurrence of wildfire smoke and EHE. Methods We analyzed records of 55,223 adult ESKD patients who received hemodialysis treatment at Fresenius Kidney Care clinics in California, Oregon, and Washington during the warm months of 2010-2018. We quantified wildfire smoke plumes, wildfire-related particulate matter 2.5 (PM 2.5 ), and EHE exposure for each hemodialysis facility.
items.author: Song H, Sieck NE, Liang M, He H, Ellicott EA, Remigio RV, He X, Nguyen Q, Liang XZ, Raimann JG, Usvyat LA, Maddux FW, Kotanko P, Sapkota A.

items.title: Sodium Bicarbonate and Non-HLA Autoantibody or HLA Antibody Trajectories in Long-term Kidney Transplant Recipients With Metabolic Acidosis: A Post Hoc Analysis of the Preserve-Transplant Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.summary: Background Long-term kidney allograft loss remains a major challenge, driven in part by chronic allograft injury, microvascular inflammation, and antibody-mediated rejection. Beyond HLA donor-specific antibodies, non-HLA autoantibodies such as angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) and endothelin receptor type A (ETAR) antibodies may contribute. Metabolic acidosis, common after transplantation, has been linked to inflammatory activation, endothelial dysfunction, and upregulation of angiotensin II, aldosterone, and endothelin-1 pathways. Together, these findings raise the hypothesis that metabolic acidosis may contribute to chronic alloimmune and profibrotic injury by amplifying vasculopathy, antibody-mediated microvascular inflammation, and consequently long-term graft dysfunction. Methods This post hoc analysis used prospectively collected data and biobank samples from a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of oral sodium bicarbonate in stable long-term kidney transplant recipients with metabolic acidosis (Preserve-Transplant Study).
items.author: Ritter A, Nilsson J, West E, Kuhn C, Wagner CA, Schachtner T, Mohebbi N.

items.title: DQA1-Derived Indirect T Cell Epitope Load Associates With Immune Injury Markers in Pediatric Liver Transplant Recipients.
items.summary: Background Human leucocyte antigen molecular mismatch (MMM) may contribute to alloimmune risk after transplantation; however, its predictive value in pediatric liver transplantation (LT) remains incompletely defined. We hypothesized that higher MMM quantified by PIRCHE-T2 would be associated with the development of de novo donor-specific antibodies (dnDSA) and graft injury markers, including liver allograft fibrosis and T cell-mediated rejection (TCMR). Methods We retrospectively studied pediatric isolated LT recipients with available 2-field class II human leucocyte antigen typing for donor and recipient. MMM was calculated using PIRCHE-T2. Endpoints included dnDSA development, TCMR, and liver allograft fibrosis. Results One hundred and ninety children made up the study cohort.
items.author: Reddy D, Yazigi N, Khan K, Rumbo C, Gondolesi G, Matsumoto C, Kroemer A, Fishbein T, Li D, Ahn J, Bandstra S, Niemann M, Timofeeva O, Ekong UD.

items.title: California petroleum refinery retirements as a natural experiment to assess effects on adverse birth outcomes.
items.summary: Background Numerous studies have linked residential proximity to refineries with higher pollutant exposures and adverse health outcomes, but few have examined impacts on birth outcomes. Four petroleum refineries in California have ceased operations since 2010, providing a natural experiment to evaluate their perinatal health impacts. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of singleton births between 2008 and 2022. The study population included infants conceived within 3 years prior or after one of four retired California refineries in four regions based on air quality management district boundaries. We conducted a difference-in-differences analysis using logistic regression to evaluate whether refinery closures led to reduced odds of adverse birth outcomes in exposed versus unexposed communities.
items.author: Meng Q, Villanueva M, Shearston JA, Goin DE, Heath N, Archer H, Morello-Frosch R, Cushing LJ.

items.title: Immediate Robot-assisted Third Kidney Transplantation After Retroperitoneal Graftectomy: A Single-session Hybrid Approach.
items.author: Park S, Kwon HE, Kim JM, Ko Y, Jung JH, Kwon H, Kim YH, Shin S.

items.title: Associations between prenatal heatwave exposure and child development and behavior and the mediating role of maternal depression in Brazil.
items.summary: Background Heatwaves are becoming more frequent and intense under climate change. Although prenatal heat exposure has been linked to adverse birth outcomes, its implications for early-childhood development and behavior remain poorly understood in tropical low- and middle-income settings. We examined whether prenatal heatwave exposure is associated with infant development and behavior, and whether current maternal depression mediates this association. Methods We used data from the Brazilian Center for Early Child Development (CPAPI) birth cohort in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo state, Brazil, comprising 946 infants born between July 2023 and March 2024. We assessed development and behavior at 6-10 months using the Survey of Well-being of Young Children and derived prenatal heatwave exposure from climate reanalysis data linked to maternal residential addresses.
items.author: Kawaoka Komatsu B, Martins Linhares MB, Menezes-Filho N.

items.title: Alzheimer Disease Risk Variants at ABCA7 Tag Tandem Repeat Length.
items.summary: Background and objectives ATP-binding cassette subfamily A member 7 ( ABCA7 ) variants are a well-established genetic risk factor for Alzheimer disease (AD). This risk includes increased length of a variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) with a ∼25bp repeat motif in intron 18 of ABCA7 . We sought to examine VNTR length, exact internal sequence composition, and correlation with genome-wide association study (GWAS) single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in AD. Methods Three hundred and seven ABCA7 alleles based on long-read sequencing were evaluated from the 1000 Genomes Project. Short read sequences from 7,968 cases and 6,792 controls were evaluated from the AD Sequencing Project (ADSP).
items.author: Kaufman EJ, Smukowski SN, Gudsnuk K, Course MM, Valdmanis PN.

items.title: Immunogenicity of the 9-Valent Human Papillomavirus Vaccine in Occupationally-Exposed Adults.
items.summary: Objective HPV is the most common sexually transmitted infection and has a well-established role in the pathogenesis of recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). HPV DNA is detectable in surgical smoke, and case reports have linked occupational exposure to laryngeal papillomatosis in healthcare workers. In 2026 a joint European Laryngological Society/Union of European Phoniatricians Delphi consensus agreed that occupational exposure is plausible and that vaccination should be offered to workers at risk, but stronger recommendations were not issued due to absence of transmission and immunogenicity data. Immunogenicity data in adults over 26-particularly men-remain minimal in the literature.
items.author: Thurber CMS, Stone L, Derkay CS.

items.title: Preoperative Tympanometry and the Presence of Middle Ear Effusion at the Time of Tympanostomy Tube Placement.
items.summary: Objectives To evaluate the relationship between preoperative tympanometry and intraoperative middle ear effusion in children undergoing tympanostomy tube placement. Methods Retrospective cohort study of children undergoing tympanostomy tube placement at a tertiary academic medical center from January to April 2021. Preoperative tympanometry was categorized as Type A, B, or C per Jerger classification. The primary outcome was middle ear effusion visualized at myringotomy. Secondary outcomes included effusion resolution among Type B ears and effusion development among Type A and C ears. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were estimated using modified Poisson regression fit via generalized estimating equations, clustered by patient, with robust standard errors.
items.author: Prabhakar AR, Frelier M, Trautmann D, Johnson RF.

items.title: Researchers' perspectives on donor-level metadata collection and reporting for human tissue research.
items.summary: Introduction No widely adopted guidelines exist for collecting and reporting donor-level metadata in tissue-based research, which limits interpretability and reproducibility and may introduce bias. This study aimed to identify researchers' perspectives to inform ethical and appropriate metadata practices. Materials and methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 investigators from the Human BioMolecular Atlas Program. Thematic analysis using inductively derived codes identified metadata elements and perspectives on their collection and reporting. Results Participants identified 80 metadata variables across six domains: demographic, sociodemographic, medical history, personally identifying information, cause of death, and tissue/organ data. Participants predominantly supported collection and reporting of demographics and medical history, whereas views on cause of death and sociodemographic data were mixed.
items.author: Liu-Galvin R, Tran K, Khan M, Eadon MT, Sarder P, Levites Strekalova YA.

items.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
items.summary: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple probability peaks before recycling, suggesting the presence of alternative states. We derive state-specific distance restraints by fitting and separating these multi-peak distributions.
items.author: Li J, Zhu Z, Song C.

items.title: Helicobacter pylori , Betel Quid Chewing, and Endoscopic Pathology in Dyspeptic Patients: A Cross-Sectional Analytical Study.
items.summary: Background Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection and betel quid (BQ) chewing are both highly prevalent in South Asia and are independently implicated in upper gastrointestinal mucosal injury, yet their joint contribution to endoscopic pathology in dyspeptic patients is poorly characterised. We aimed to describe the exposure profile of dyspeptic patients with and without endoscopic pathology, quantify the individual and joint associations of H. pylori and BQ use with pathology and explore trends with BQ exposure. Methods In this cross-sectional analytical study, 211 consecutive dyspeptic patients attending a tertiary gastroenterology department were classified as having endoscopic pathology (Group A, n = 141) or a normal endoscopic examination (Group B, n = 70).
items.author: Ahmed MU, Ahmad I, Tanu S, Mithila MT, Haque ANMI, Athina RT, Bhowmik RC, Jahangir Alam M, Asaduzzaman M.

items.title: Massive thoracic recurrence of adrenocortical carcinoma.
items.author: Renda R, Lamartina L.

items.title: Serial metabolic profiling and liver transplantation in concurrent maple syrup urine disease and type 1 diabetes.
items.summary: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) and type 1 diabetes (T1D) require careful attention to dietary composition and predispose to ketoacidosis. The co-occurrence of these metabolic disorders therefore compounds these challenges. Here, we present a 29-year-old man with prenatally diagnosed MSUD and childhood-onset T1D who, despite extreme metabolic vulnerability, did well until his mid-20s, when he was admitted to the hospital 8 times for metabolic decompensation, with the latter 7 times occurring within a 12-month period. Most laboratory evaluations were suggestive of MSUD crisis rather than diabetic ketoacidosis. Ultimately, the patient underwent liver transplantation for definitive treatment of MSUD. The case illustrates the complexity of comanaging T1D with an inborn error of metabolism requiring dietary modification that challenges glycemic management.
items.author: Wang EY, DeCherney GS, Adams MC, Stiles AR, Williams M, Matson BC.

items.title: The elusive culprit: a renal neuroendocrine tumor unmasked by ectopic Cushing syndrome.
items.summary: The case provides insight into the diagnostics and management of ectopic Cushing syndrome caused by the ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion by a primary renal neuroendocrine tumor (RenNET), an exceptionally rare cause of endogenous hypercortisolism.
items.author: Denysova V, Yutkin V, Bel-Angе A, Atlan K, Solomonov E, Grozinsky-Glasberg S.

items.title: Neonatal compressive goiter as the initial presentation of thyroid hormone resistance with dual THRB and TSHR mutations.
items.summary: Resistance to thyroid hormones (RTH) is a rare disorder mostly caused by mutations in the thyroid hormone receptor β gene ( THRB ). It typically presents in late childhood or adulthood with elevated free thyroid hormone levels, inappropriately normal or high thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and goiter. We report a case of RTH associated with a compressive neonatal goiter. A preterm newborn presented with respiratory distress due to a large goiter (9.7 mL; normal, 30 pmol/L (>19.5 pg/mL; NR, 3.5-7.8 pmol/L [2.3-5.1 pg/mL]). Genetic testing and functional analyses identified a de novo heterozygous THRB nonsense mutation and an inherited heterozygous missense activating mutation in the TSHR gene.
items.author: Dubois S, Savagner F, Heneau A, Azar-Kolakez A, Al-Amir I, Carel JC.

items.title: Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy type 2 presenting as an acromegaly mimic with enteropathy.
items.summary: Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (PHO) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by digital clubbing, pachydermia, and periostosis that frequently mimics acromegaly. Autosomal recessive pathogenic variants in SLCO2A1 cause PHO type 2 (PHOAR2) and are uniquely associated with chronic enteropathy associated with SLCO2A1 (CEAS). We report a 39-year-old male evaluated for acromegaly due to progressive coarse facies, cutis verticis gyrata, and profound limb clubbing. Endocrine workup demonstrated a normal growth hormone (GH) suppression test (GH nadir 0.76 ng/mL [SI: 0.76 µg/L]; reference range, SLCO2A1 pathogenic variant (c.764G>A, p.Gly255Glu), confirming PHOAR2-CEAS syndrome. Etoricoxib (120 mg daily) provided partial symptomatic relief. This case illustrates that digital clubbing in a patient with acromegaloid features mandates SLCO2A1 genetic evaluation, avoiding unnecessary pituitary investigation.
items.author: Kumar S, Khatri SJ, Sreevatsa T, Kumar A, Singh SK, Kumar S.

items.title: Dose-related depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation during cabergoline therapy in an adolescent with macroprolactinoma.
items.summary: Cabergoline is the preferred medical treatment for prolactinomas in children and adolescents because of its efficacy in reducing prolactin concentrations and tumor size. Although dopamine agonists are generally well tolerated, neuropsychiatric adverse effects have been reported, with depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation less frequently described. We report a 15-year-old girl with macroprolactinoma who developed low mood, emotional dysregulation, crying spells, reduced appetite, sleep-wake disturbance, loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, and passive suicidal thoughts after cabergoline was increased to 1 mg twice weekly. She had no previous psychiatric history, major psychosocial stressor, manic symptoms, or psychotic features. Psychiatric assessment identified moderate depressive symptoms, with a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score of 11.
items.author: Malik S, Al Harrasi A, Al Kiyumi MI, Al Kiyumi MH.

items.title: Delayed recognition of primary thyroid lymphoma with progressive thyroid enlargement and cardiopulmonary symptoms.
items.summary: Primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL) is a rare thyroid malignancy that may present with respiratory symptoms overlapping with cardiopulmonary disease, contributing to delayed diagnosis. We report a 78-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, and prior lung cancer whose worsening dyspnea was repeatedly attributed to underlying cardiopulmonary conditions. She subsequently developed dysphonia and dysphagia with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass requiring tracheostomy for airway protection. Prior computed tomography imaging obtained during multiple evaluations for cardiopulmonary symptoms incidentally demonstrated subtle thyroid enlargement with progressive interval growth on retrospective review. Core biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and staging established stage IIIE disease.
items.author: Tovar YE, Elsayed AG, Pragani M, Romanoski PT, Kaur R, Jun JY.

items.title: Pediatric gigantism due to ectopic growth hormone releasing hormone secretion from a metastatic bronchial neuroendocrine tumor.
items.summary: Pediatric gigantism due to ectopic secretion of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) is exceptionally rare. Most pediatric reports have involved pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors in the context of multiple endocrine neoplasia 1 (MEN1). We describe a female patient diagnosed at 9 years of age with a typical bronchial neuroendocrine tumor and subsequently found to have diffuse hepatic and skeletal metastases, accelerated linear growth, and acromegalic features. Evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated plasma GHRH, growth hormone, and insulin-like growth factor 1, with diffuse pituitary hyperplasia on magnetic resonance imaging and no discrete pituitary adenoma. Genetic testing for MEN1 was negative. Management required repeated surgery, first-generation somatostatin analogs, dopamine agonist therapy, pegvisomant, pasireotide, and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with lutetium-177 DOTA-Tyr3-octreotate.
items.author: Vidal-Ostos De Lara F, Sanchis-Pascual D, Hernández-Rienda L, Del Olmo-García MI.

items.title: Novel compound heterozygous POLR3A variation: expanding 4H syndrome with progressive keratoconus.
items.summary: POLR3A -related leukodystrophy is a multisystem disorder classically defined by hypomyelination, hypodontia, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (4H syndrome). While neurological and endocrine features are well-defined, the ocular phenotypic spectrum remains incomplete. We present a 15.9-year-old female with a classic 4H phenotype and compound heterozygosity for 2 novel variants (NM_007055.4:c.2102G > T [p.(Gly701Val)] and NM_007055.4:c.2989C > T [p.(Pro997Ser)]). The patient exhibited advanced, rapidly progressive bilateral keratoconus, with a maximum keratometry ( K -max) reaching an extreme 75.9 diopter (D). K -max of 75.9 D (approximately 40-47 D in children and adolescents) represents extreme corneal ectasia. Longitudinal follow-up documented progressive ectasia, treated with penetrating keratoplasty in the left eye and corneal collagen cross-linking in the right eye.
items.author: Simsek E, Simsek T, Cilingir O, Atalay E.

items.title: Role of microglia in neuromyelitis optica (Review).
items.summary: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is an antibody‑mediated autoimmune disease of the central nervous system (CNS), typically characterized by optic neuritis and myelitis. Aquaporin‑4 antibodies initiate astrocyte injury, although the factors triggering their production are unclear. Subsequent interactions among astrocytes, microglia, complement and peripheral immune cells drive neuroinflammation, demyelination and axonal damage. Microglia amplify tissue injury through the release of inflammatory mediators and cytotoxic factors, while contributing to debris clearance and tissue repair. The present review examines the roles of microglia in NMOSD, with a focus on complement, cytokine and interferon signaling, lipid metabolism and metabolic reprogramming. It further discusses therapeutic strategies for modulating microglial activity and the challenges of translating experimental findings into clinical practice.
items.author: Zhang Y, Hong JB, Liu MW, Zhang LM.

items.title: Protein S‑palmitoylation in T cell‑mediated antitumor immunity: Context‑dependent mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities (Review).
items.summary: S‑palmitoylation is a critical post‑translational regulator of protein function; however, its role in T cell‑mediated antitumor immunity remains unclear. The present review summarizes emerging evidence that redefines T cell biology and its implications for antitumor immunity. The regulatory functions of S‑palmitoylation in T cell receptor signaling, activation, proliferation, differentiation, exhaustion and apoptosis are first outlined, highlighting the distinct roles of the zinc finger Asp‑His‑His‑Cystype family of palmitoyl acyltransferases and depalmitoylating enzymes in modulating the membrane localization, stability and signal transduction of key T cell signaling regulators. How S‑palmitoylation of immune checkpoints, such as programmed death‑ligand 1, and the components of antigen presentation shape the tumor immune microenvironment were further examined.
items.author: Wang S, Xu R, Jin S, Yu T, Qin M, Xu L, Wang X.

items.title: Fatty acid‑binding proteins at the inflammation‑cancer interface: Isoform‑specific metabolic‑immune mechanisms and therapeutic implications (Review).
items.summary: Fatty acid‑binding proteins (FABPs) comprise ten mammalian isoforms (FABP1‑FABP9 and FABP12), each a small intracellular lipid chaperone traditionally viewed as a mediator of fatty acid uptake, trafficking and metabolic partitioning. Evidence from metabolic disease, immunology and oncology indicates that selected FABP isoforms also regulate inflammatory signaling, immune‑cell metabolism and tumor‑stromal crosstalk. Prior reviews have mainly emphasized single isoforms of FABPs or single disease categories. The present narrative review organized FABP biology as a context‑specific evidence map across the inflammation‑cancer interface, in which each principal claim is reported together with the experimental system, with the outcome and limits of extrapolation described.
items.author: Hah YS, Ju YT, Lee SJ, Hwang J, Kwag SJ.

items.title: Roles of TRIM proteins in cardiovascular diseases: From pathogenesis to therapeutic targeting (Review).
items.summary: Cardiovascular diseases are driven by sustained mechanical stress, metabolic derangement, inflammation and oxidative injury, which progressively disrupt cellular homeostasis within the heart and vasculature. Although current therapeutic strategies have substantially improved clinical outcomes, most interventions primarily target downstream pathological manifestations rather than upstream regulatory mechanisms that determine stress adaptation and tissue remodeling. Tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins constitute a large family of E3 ubiquitin ligases characterized by a highly conserved RBCC domain architecture and diversified C‑terminal regions. By catalyzing distinct ubiquitin chain topologies and functioning as molecular scaffolds, TRIM proteins broadly regulate protein turnover, inflammatory signaling, metabolic adaptation and cell fate determination.
items.author: Wang F, Xing Z, Gao Y, Gai Y.

items.title: Harnessing the power of Scutellaria baicalensis : Advances in active compounds and their impact on skeletal system diseases (Review).
items.summary: Skeletal system diseases (SSDs) encompass a variety of conditions affecting bones, cartilage and joints, including osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and osteosarcoma. These diseases significantly impair physical function, rank among the leading causes of disability worldwide, and can even lead to mortality, affecting the lives of hundreds of millions of individuals. Scutellaria baicalensis , a widely used traditional Chinese medicinal herb, is rich in flavonoids, including baicalein, baicalin, wogonin, oroxylin A and wogonoside. Given the increasing prevalence of SSDs and their profound impact on quality of life, existing research highlights the promising therapeutic effects of Scutellaria baicalensis . The present review explores the therapeutic potential of Scutellaria baicalensis and its active compounds in combating SSDs.
items.author: Sun W, Wu Y, Chen L, Ni Y, Zhao C, Sun W, Cui Y, Yi Q.

items.title: Exploring Environmental Influences on Mono(2-Ethylhexyl) Phthalate (MEHP) Exposure in Common Bottlenose Dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in Sarasota Bay, FL, USA.
items.summary: Phthalates, endocrine-disrupting, persistent organic pollutants widely used in plastic manufacturing, can readily enter aquatic environments and contaminate estuaries. As apex predators, resident bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) provide critical insights into ecosystem health. Prior work documented phthalate exposure in the long-term resident bottlenose dolphin community of Sarasota Bay, Florida, with evidence of temporal and spatial variability, particularly for mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), a metabolite of the commonly used plasticizer di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP). We predicted that environmental factors, such as large-scale storm events, rainfall, and harmful algal blooms (HABs), may influence this variability. Urine samples collected from 138 free-ranging dolphins during 1993-2024 were screened for phthalate metabolites, reliable biomarkers of exposure.
items.author: Warden KB, Dziobak MK, Wilkinson KA, Wells RS, Sandifer PA, Vulava VM, Hart LB.

items.title: Routine foreskin pathology in adults: Low yield, high cost-Time to change practice?
items.summary: Objective This study aimed to determine the diagnostic yield for malignant lesions and cost-effectiveness of routine foreskin pathology in adults. Subjects/patients and methods A retrospective audit was conducted of all adult circumcisions (age ≥16) performed between January 2015 and February 2025 at a UK tertiary centre. Clinical and pathology records were reviewed to identify unexpected cancer diagnoses-defined as cases with no prior biopsy evidence or clinical suspicion. The number needed to screen (NNS) to detect one cancer was calculated, and pathology costs were estimated based on local processing costs and the pathologist workload score for each sample. Results There were 2503 adult circumcisions performed between 2015 and 2025, with 2.6% ( n = 66/2503) cancers detected on pathological assessment.
items.author: McLean KA, Gardner E, Kirkwood K, Shukla CJ, Laird A, Blackmur JP.

items.title: Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension Complicated by Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome: A Case Series of Two Patients.
items.summary: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. This report presents two cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension complicated by PRES, both clinically characterized by headache and visual disturbances, with characteristic neuroimaging findings. The clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of two patients are described. Following prompt multidisciplinary consultation and immediate interventions, including strict blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, infection prevention, and appropriate obstetric management, both patients achieved favorable clinical outcomes. No significant neurological abnormalities were observed at the 42-day postpartum follow-up.
items.author: Zhao X, Yan M, Long F, Mumdzjans A, Song R.

items.title: Use of a Multilayer-Structured Polyurethane Foam Protective Pad to Prevent Deformity and Promote Epithelialization in Buttock Pressure Ulcers: Two Adult Cases With Prolonged Bed Rest.
items.summary: Buttock pressure ulcers are highly susceptible to pressure, shear, moisture, and contamination, frequently resulting in delayed healing. Conventional dressings are often easily displaced in this region, reducing their intended effect. To prevent wound deformation and maintain a flat surface, a multilayer-structured polyurethane foam protective pad (ALLEVYN LIFE, Smith & Nephew), typically used for prevention, was applied alongside local treatment. Two male patients demonstrated the effectiveness of this adjunctive treatment. The first, a 65-year-old man with a chronic National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel Stage II pressure ulcer that had persisted for 2 months, achieved near-complete epithelialization by day 6 after hospital admission and pad application.
items.author: Mamada E, Tokoro S, Fujiyoshi-Ito A, Ogata Y, Tanaka K, Asaka E.

items.title: Symmetrical Peripheral Gangrene in a Child With Plasmodium falciparum Cerebral Malaria: A Rare but Serious Complication.
items.summary: Symmetrical peripheral gangrene is a rare, limb-threatening complication associated with severe infection and disseminated intravascular coagulation. We report a case of a 6-year-old girl with cerebral malaria who developed gangrene of all toes during treatment. Management included antimalarials, antibiotics, supportive care, debridement, and subsequent skin grafting after adequate wound granulation.

items.title: Clinically Suspected Tumefactive Demyelination Mimicking a Brain Tumor in a 10-Year-Old Boy: A Case Report.
items.summary: After cranial surgery, a 10-year-old boy developed hand weakness, numbness, and fatigue. MRI showed frontoparietal lesions; biopsy lacked documented demyelination. Symptoms and lesions reportedly improved after methylprednisolone. Tumefactive demyelination was suspected, but discordant laterality, unavailable antibody testing, and brief follow-up left the diagnosis unclassified.
items.author: Aman F, Ali A, Khan MF, Khan HN, Shah A, Erkin AS, Khan S, Sattar Y, Khalid AA.

items.title: Do Leaf Temperatures Determine Endophyte Composition and Richness in Florida Native Plant Species?
items.summary: Microbiomes play crucial roles in ecosystems, largely through their interactions with plants. Fungal endophytes occur in nearly all plant tissues and can influence host physiology, stress tolerance, and productivity. Although previous studies have examined how air temperature shapes foliar endophyte communities, endophytes may respond more strongly to leaf temperatures, which are often decoupled from ambient air temperatures. Consequently, changes in leaf temperature (e.g., due to global warming) may alter endophyte diversity and composition. In this study, we experimentally tested whether elevated leaf temperatures affect fungal endophyte richness and community composition in six native subtropical plant species from South Florida. Using in situ localized heating of individual branches, we increased leaf temperatures by 1°C-3°C over a 2-week period.
items.author: Tserej O, Hernandez DJ, Rawstern AH, Kiesewetter KN, Almeida BK, Afkhami ME, Feeley KJ.

items.title: Unified Phase Criterion for Band Crossings in One-Dimensional Topological Photonics.
items.summary: One-dimensional photonic crystals (1DPCs) provide a simple and versatile platform for exploring topological photonics. Topological effects in these layered systems have enabled a range of applications in robust light confinement, lasing, modulation, and disorder-tolerant optical devices. Among their underlying band features, band crossings are of particular interest because they represent critical degeneracies associated with topological phase transitions in periodic media. However, although band crossings in one-dimensional topological photonics have been extensively studied, a unified theoretical criterion for their occurrence remains unclear. In this work, a unified phase criterion for band crossings that applies to both TE and TM polarizations from normal to oblique incidence was derived based on transfer-matrix method and Bloch theory.
items.author: Song J, Liu H, Sun C, Qi P, Liu W.

items.title: Adaptive Genomic Variation Across Sub-Alpine Climates in a Keystone Forest Tree: Implications for Seed Sourcing for Restoration in a Changing Climate.
items.summary: A major challenge for ecological restoration is seed sourcing decisions that ensure that restored populations have the adaptive variation for current and future environments. This is increasingly important for alpine and sub-alpine communities where climate change is predicted to be rapid and drive shifts in selective pressures. Selecting source populations representing future climates is an evolutionary-based strategy for increasing adaptive capacity, but requires an understanding of population genetic structure, identification of putatively adaptive genomic variation and an assessment of how these change across the landscape. items.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
items.summary: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.
items.author: Yuanjie Ren, Margarita Davydova, Shankar Balasubramanian et al.

items.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
items.summary: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs.
items.author: Amy Wayland, Robert Reischke

items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs.
items.author: Aldana Al-Sulaiti, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Muhammad Bilal Akram Dastagir et al.

items.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
items.summary: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry.
items.author: Ke-Sean J. M. Peter, Ryan A. Kowalski, David A. Curie et al.

items.title: Testing the Spin of New Physics with Top Precision Measurements
items.summary: Precision measurements can reveal not only the presence of new physics, but also information about the dynamics that generated it. We study this question in top-pair production by comparing three top-philic scenarios: a colored scalar top partner, a colored vector-like fermion, and a spin-one $Z^\prime$ mediator. The first two contribute through loop corrections, while the $Z^\prime$ contributes at tree level. We show that the scalar and vector-like fermion scenarios match onto the same effective operator structure at low energies,making their distinction unfeasible using the EFT approach. However, near or above threshold their full loop amplitudes develop distinct momentum-dependent interference patterns.
items.author: André Lessa, Vinícius Rocca, Veronica Sanz

items.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
items.summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field.
items.author: Chenwei Lv

items.title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
items.summary: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss. For Fock-state boson sampling, Gaussian boson sampling with fixed uniform squeezing, and fermion sampling with magic inputs, we obtain polynomial-time sampling at inverse-polynomial total variation error, for any fixed nonzero overall loss rate, and with high probability over Haar-random interferometers. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth.
items.author: Armando Angrisani, Hela Mhiri

items.title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
items.summary: We numerically investigate the collision and fracture processes of ball milling based on a minimal model of a three-sphere geometry using discrete element method (DEM) simulations combined with Christensen-type and Weibull-type normalized fracture criteria. The outcome of the brittle target particle (ejected versus trapped, fractured versus intact) depends on the impact geometry and velocity. We develop a reduced three-sphere collision description in which trapping is governed by impact geometry and friction, while fracture inside the trapping regime is evaluated from DEM output using stress-based and contact-force-based normalized criteria. The trapping regime follows a closed-form geometric condition, while the critical conditions for fracture vary with impact angle, obliquity angle, impact velocity, and particle size ratio.

items.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
items.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations. The auxiliary prediction loss is jointly optimized with the diffusion objective, allowing quantum auxiliary supervision to influence the learned denoising model. Once trained, protein sequences are generated entirely through classical reverse diffusion. On the CATH benchmark, DiffSequence-Q achieved the highest secondary structure recovery among the four evaluated models for complete sequence generation.

items.title: Can the exposome help solve the alcohol and cancer mystery?
items.summary: by Vasilis Vasiliou, Arthur Stem, David C. Thompson Alcohol consumption is a preventable driver of many cancers, yet a central biological question remains unresolved: by what mechanisms does ethanol promote malignancy? We propose that alcohol in the context of the exposome (i.e., the network of chemical, biological, and social determinants that interact with ethanol across the life span) provides a unifying framework for understanding alcohol-related carcinogenesis. Viewed through the lens of the exposome, alcohol is not only as a direct carcinogen but also as a systemic amplifier of environmental risk acting across multiple levels of biological organization, from molecular damage to whole-body physiology.

items.title: Two parallel lateral hypothalamic GABAergic projections differentially modulate pain and anxiety in mice
items.summary: by Yi-Ling Sun, Yi-Ting Peng, Xue Zhang, Cui Yin, Cheng Xiao, Junping Chen, Chunyi Zhou The lateral hypothalamus (LH) is fundamentally involved in motivated behaviors, yet the precise functional segregation of its GABAergic projections in modulating pain and its affective dimensions remains poorly understood. Here, using male and female mice, we revealed that LH GABAergic neurons sent parallel projections to two pivotal pain and affect processing centers: the lateral parabrachial nucleus (LPB) and the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT). In vivo fiber photometry revealed that LH GABAergic terminals in both the PVT and LPB are robustly activated by noxious, aversive, and rewarding stimuli, indicating their roles in encoding salient and affective information.

items.title: Phylogenetic evidence that migratory behavior increases ungulate extinction rates
items.summary: by Joel O. Abraham, Kaedan O’Brien, Nathan S. Upham, Brett R. Jesmer, Faysal Bibi, J. Tyler Faith Widespread instances of migratory collapse have been documented within the past several decades, indicating that migration may be a fragile strategy in the Anthropocene. Yet the fragility of migration as a strategy for navigating seasonally variable resource availability may extend deeper into evolutionary time. We used phylogenetic imputation to infer the migratory habits of 51 ungulate species that went extinct during the late Quaternary and evaluated whether migration enhances extinction rates on macroevolutionary timescales. We found that ~80% (41 of 51) of recently extinct species were migratory, whereas only 46% (95 of 207) of extant ungulates are migratory.

items.title: TriTower-m6Am: A triple-tower heterogeneous deep learning architecture integrating semantic, sequential, and structural information for mRNA N6,2′-O-dimethyladenosine site prediction
items.summary: by Kaifeng Xiong, Jianhua Jia Background N 6 ,2′-O-dimethyladenosine (m6Am) is a cap-proximal mRNA modification deposited by PCIF1 (phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD)-interacting factor 1) at the first transcribed nucleotide of eukaryotic mRNAs. Knowing where m6Am sites sit would help explain how cells tune mRNA stability and translation, but current predictors typically depend on a single representation and do not jointly model multiple views of the same RNA sequence. Results We present TriTower-m6Am, combining semantic (RNA-FM, a pretrained RNA foundation model, with BellPooling), sequential (One-Hot BiLSTM, bidirectional long short-term memory), and structural (RGCN, a relational graph convolutional network, over the 41-nt window) representations of each RNA window.

items.title: A computational framework to model cartilage degeneration induced by mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation in post-traumatic osteoarthritis
items.summary: by Moustafa Hamada, Atte S. A. Eskelinen, Joonas P. Kosonen, Sanna Hakonen, Cristina Florea, Alan J. Grodzinsky, Rami K. Korhonen, Petri Tanska Knee joint injury is a major risk factor for post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), often associated with early cartilage degeneration. Mechanical overloading and cytokine-driven inflammation are key drivers of this process, yet the underlying mechanisms and their distinct temporal and spatial contributions to cartilage degradation remain unclear. Here, we present a mechanobiological finite element framework that simulates cartilage degradation through cell-mediated proteolytic activity triggered by injurious loading-driven mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation. The model reproduces experimentally observed depth-dependent loss of collagen and aggrecan, with mechanoinflammation inducing a transient response and cytokine-driven inflammation sustaining prolonged matrix degradation.
items.author: Moustafa Hamada, Atte S. A. Eskelinen, Joonas P. Kosonen et al.

items.title: Ten simple rules for a successful global health roundtable
items.summary: by Maria Gabriela Uribe Guajardo, Amanda Rush, Michelle Cunich, Kathleen Cravero, Carmen Huckel Schneider Qualitative approaches play a critical role in global health research by capturing the social, political, and contextual dimensions that shape health outcomes. While interviews and focus groups are widely used, these methods are often time‑limited and project‑specific. Global health roundtables offer a complementary approach, providing a flexible and long-term platform for engaging diverse stakeholders—including researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and community representatives—in collective dialogue, knowledge exchange, and collaboration. When designed well, roundtables can support co‑production of knowledge, address complex system‑level challenges, and generate insights with relevance beyond a single event.

items.title: Membrane tension and cell–nucleus mechanical coupling regulate confined cell migration
items.summary: by David Hernandez-Aristizabal, Anotida Madzvamuse, Rachele Allena Cell migration is a fundamental physiological process essential from embryogenesis to cancer metastasis. It is primarily governed by the coupled mechanics of the plasma membrane (PM) and the nucleus, together with cytoskeletal dynamics. Being the largest and stiffest organelle, the nucleus is considered a rate-limiting factor in confined migration. However, nuclear positioning varies across cell types and migration modes, and the forces orchestrating its mechanical coupling with the PM are not completely understood. In recent decades, mathematical modelling has gained relevance to support cell migration research, yet models face the fundamental challenge of balancing mechanistic detail with computational efficiency.

items.title: Social manipulations trigger shifts in group-level dominance patterns
items.summary: by Annemarie van der Marel, Xavier Francis, Claire L. O’Connell, Cesar O. Estien, Chelsea Carminito, V. Darby Moore, Elizabeth A. Hobson Within dominance hierarchies, individuals often direct aggression based on their own rank and the rank of others. When many group members make the same rank-informed aggression decisions, a broader group-level “dominance pattern” can emerge which further structures aggression within the framework of the dominance hierarchy. However, whether groups can change their group-level dominance patterns over time, and what factors might drive these changes, are not well understood. We investigated aggression dynamics by experimentally manipulating captive groups of monk parakeets ( Myiopsitta monachus ) using targeted rank-based removals and reintroductions of group members to induce social instability.

items.title: Nitroxoline treatment of Balamuthia mandrillaris triggers genomic crisis, transcriptional collapse, and incomplete encystment via copper and iron chelation
items.summary: by Kaitlin A. Marquis, Natasha Spottiswoode, Angela M. Detweiler, Norma Neff, Joseph L. DeRisi Balamuthia mandrillaris is a free-living amoeba that can infect the central nervous system to cause granulomatous amebic encephalitis (GAE), a fatal disease with mortality rates up to 90%. GAE is typically treated with a six-drug regimen with limited efficacy and significant toxicity. Our lab previously identified nitroxoline, a quinolone antibiotic, as a promising therapeutic complement to the existing regimen, and in 2021 nitroxoline was first successfully used to treat a human patient. In this study, we elucidate nitroxoline’s mechanism of action using a combination of genomics, transcriptomics, chemical complementation, growth assays, and electron microscopy.

Deletions within the hemagglutinin (HA) receptor-binding domain represent a notable, albeit rare, evolutionary trajectory. Here, we systematically characterized the multifaceted impact of a single-amino-acid deletion at residue 227 of HA (designated HA Δ227 ), a naturally occurring deletion within the 220-loop that overlaps a key antigenic epitope, using isogenic reverse genetics H9N2 viruses. Paradoxically, the HA Δ227 imposed a fitness cost and was associated with enhanced HA receptor-binding avidity, reduced apparent virion-associated NA activity, altered HA/NA functional balance, attenuated viral replication in vitro , and reduced respiratory shedding in vivo .

The antiviral innate immune response is highly regulated at the RNA level, especially through RNA modifications. Adenosine-to-Inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing modifies the mRNA sequence. Growing evidence shows that this type of RNA editing plays a key role in mediating cellular responses to viral infections and disease resistance. items.title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
items.summary: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $fσ_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $Λ$CDM within $2σ$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $Ω_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8σ$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$.

items.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
items.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields.

items.title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
items.summary: Quantum processors remain susceptible to crosstalk-induced effects despite the continuous evolution of their underlying hardware architectures. In this work, we experimentally investigate the effectiveness of crosstalk-induced attacks across six IBM superconducting quantum processors and one IQM processor. Our results demonstrate that such attacks can be launched across all the platforms, due to persistance of crosstalk, although their effectiveness varies significantly between devices. The probability of a measurement outcome flip in the victim qubits reaches a maximum value of $60\%$. Also, it is seen that processors sharing identical coupling graphs exhibit different vulnerability profiles, indicating that connectivity alone is insufficient to predict attack efficiency.

items.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
items.summary: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.

items.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
items.summary: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model.

items.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
items.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate.

items.title: Negative non-linear differential dissipation in mechanical quartz resonators
items.summary: We observe negative non-linear differential dissipation in a low-frequency (32.7 kHz) miniature quartz tuning fork, representing a high-Q piezoelectric resonator, at temperatures below 0.3 K. Similar drive-induced dissipation suppression has previously been reported in superconducting microwave resonators, and high-frequency MEMS devices, associated to coupling with tunneling two-level systems (TTLSs). In the case of low-frequency resonators, the equivalent temperature of the mechanical mode is orders of magnitude lower than the thermodynamic temperature of the device, implying that accessible TTLS states are largely saturated. We demonstrate that the observed temperature and drive dependence of the losses fit well within the framework of an interacting TTLS bath, indicating the presence of a channel for energy transfer between the mechanical mode and thermally activated TTLSs.

items.title: Saccadic suppression enhances saliency of ecologically relevant stimuli in the zebrafish optic tectum
items.summary: by Giulia Soto, Carina Thomas, Louis Funk, Tim C. Hladnik, Florian A. Dehmelt, Ziad M. Hafed, Aristides B. Arrenberg Saccadic suppression, a reduction in visual sensitivity around the time of rapid eye movements, is well-documented in primate psychophysics, but its mechanisms and functions remain debated. Here, we use zebrafish to trace the origins of saccadic suppression, and we demonstrate how saccadic suppression selectively enhances the visual salience of ecologically relevant stimuli. Saccadic suppression thus contributes to more than just compensation for rapid saccade-induced image shifts. We first established a behavioral correlate of saccadic suppression in larval zebrafish escape behavior. Then, using electrophysiology, we show that retinal ganglion cells jumpstart saccadic suppression in a spatial frequency-dependent manner.

items.title: Shapley fields reveal mosaic chemotopic organization in the mouse Olfactory bulb across diverse chemical feature sets
items.summary: by Nikola Milićević, Shawn D. Burton, Matt Wachowiak, Vladimir Itskov Neural representations in the olfactory bulb (OB) remain poorly understood compared to well-established coding principles in other sensory systems. This difficulty arises because a natural coordinate system for olfactory stimulus space has not yet been identified, complicating the characterization of neural receptive fields analogous to those in other sensory modalities. Moreover, the extent to which these tuning properties are spatially organized within the OB remains unclear. To advance our understanding of the olfactory coding, we introduce an interpretable method of Shapley fields, as an olfactory analog of retinotopic receptive fields.
items.author: Nikola Milićević, Shawn D. Burton, Matt Wachowiak et al.

items.title: Bayesian efficient coding
items.summary: by Il Memming Park, Jonathan W. Pillow The efficient coding hypothesis, which proposes that neurons are optimized to maximize information about the environment, has provided a guiding theoretical framework for sensory and systems neuroscience. More recently, a theory known as the Bayesian Brain hypothesis has focused on the brain’s ability to integrate sensory and prior sources of information in order to perform Bayesian inference. Although pieces of a connection between these two hypotheses have appeared in prior work, a general formulation that treats the optimality criterion as an arbitrary functional of the posterior distribution – and thereby admits both information-based and other objectives within a single framework – has remained largely implicit.

Gonzalez Rivera, Matteo D’Antonio Background Noncoding genetic variants underlie many complex traits, yet predicting their regulatory impact in cell type-specific contexts remains a major challenge. Transcription factor binding is a primary mechanism through which noncoding variants influence gene regulation, but the relationships among chromatin accessibility, variant frequency, and transcription factor binding are complex and nonlinear, limiting the performance of traditional linear models. items.title: Modular design of Salmonella Typhimurium OMV-based nanovaccines for tunable dual-form polysaccharide antigen delivery
items.summary: by Mengru Li, Kai Zhou, Meihong Lei, Huanhuan Cao, Xinyu Liu, Shan Li, Ruida Wu, Ming Yang, Xiaoping Bian, Longlong Cao, Qingke Kong Bacterial diseases are primarily managed with antibiotics, but vaccination is widely acknowledged as the most efficacious strategy for their prevention. Bacterial polysaccharides serve as key protective antigens in hosts and are therefore consistently prioritized as targets for bacterial vaccine development. Polysaccharide-conjugated vaccines have emerged as a promising and effective approach to combat multidrug-resistant bacteria. In order to construct a vaccine carrier capable of delivering bacterial polysaccharides while inducing robust immune response, this study utilized outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) derived from Salmonella Typhimurium as the vaccine carrier instead of the traditional adjuvant components to enhance the immunogenicity of polysaccharide vaccine.

items.title: A heat-induced HagF-HrcA regulatory loop promotes chlamydial fitness and infectious progeny yield under stress
items.summary: by Yehong Huang, Yuxuan Wang, Matthew Pan, Danny Wan, Lingling Wang, Joseph D. Fondell, Xiang Wu, Guangming Zhong, Huizhou Fan Bacterial survival under environmental stress requires precise regulation of protein homeostasis, yet how this is achieved in organisms with streamlined genomes remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify HagF as a previously unrecognized protein that antagonizes the conserved heat-inducible transcriptional repressor HrcA in Chlamydia . Using genetic and biochemical approaches, including overexpression and CRISPRi-mediated knockdown, we show that under non-stressed conditions, HrcA represses hagF along with its five known targets, including hrcA and four chaperone genes. Upon heat stress, HagF is induced and binds HrcA, attenuating its repressor activity.

items.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002
items.summary: by Hao Pang, Yuan Chen, Zeng Peng, Hao Xiao, Wenyuan Chen, Xiaowu Li, Ping Chen, Jing Zheng, Hongrong Liu Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa —a top-seven global pathogen—particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa . Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to the tail. Phage A1002 exhibits a distinctly elongated tail morphology distinct from other reported podophages.
items.author: Hao Pang, Yuan Chen, Zeng Peng et al.

items.title: An open-source eye-tracking system adaptable to diverse terrestrial vertebrates reveals state-dependent visual acquisition in lizards
items.summary: by Nimrod Leberstein, Tali Remenick, Milan Becker, Mark Shein-Idelson Gaze shifts are fundamental to visual exploration and processing, yet empirical knowledge is largely confined to a small number of model species, limiting our understanding of general principles of visual acquisition across animals. Here, we introduce a versatile, low-cost, and open-source framework design for eye-tracking in small, freely moving animals. Leveraging photogrammetry, 3D modeling, and 3D-printing, we produce headmounts adaptable to diverse head-eye geometries, as we demonstrate for lizards, turtles, and mice. Detailed recordings in Pogona vitticeps, a laterally eyed ectotherm with a high-acuity retina, reveal a rich oculomotor repertoire with kinematics closely resembling the saccadic main sequence in primates.
items.author: Nimrod Leberstein, Tali Remenick, Milan Becker et al.

items.title: The human hippocampus supports auditory coding and multisensory integration
items.summary: by Omri Raccah, Aryan Agarwal, Yannan Zhu, Nicholas B. Turk-Browne The hippocampus receives convergent input from multiple sensory systems, yet in humans it has been studied almost exclusively through vision. Here we examine how the hippocampus contributes to sensory processing beyond the visual modality and to the multisensory integration of visual information with these other modalities. Participants were exposed to multiple repetitions of short naturalistic movie clips, each presented in four formats: auditory-only, visual-only, congruent audiovisual, and incongruent audiovisual (audio and video from different movies). Using high-resolution fMRI, we measured univariate activation and multivariate representations across the longitudinal axis and subfields of the human hippocampus.
items.author: Omri Raccah, Aryan Agarwal, Yannan Zhu et al.

items.title: A deep genetic structure phylogenomically frames the closest algal relatives of land plants
items.summary: by Maaike J. Bierenbroodspot, Cäcilia F. Kunz, Elisa S. Goldbecker, Maike Lorenz, Iker Irisarri, Thomas Pröschold, Tatyana Darienko, Jan de Vries Discerning the nature of the last common ancestor of land plants (embryophytes) and algae allows to retrace the adaptations that ushered in the conquest of land by plants. For this, the closest streptophyte algal relatives of embryophytes hold key information. Albeit initially coming as a surprise due to their plain body plans, all major phylogenomic efforts have concluded that the Zygnematophyceae are the algal sisters to land plants. The Zygnematophyceae are the streptophyte algal class with the greatest species richness and while we now have ample genome information on a few select members of zygnematophytes, our understanding of the genomic divergence as well as genetic potential for key traits is limited by a lack of phylodiverse data that accounts for this diversity and integrates it into a phylogenomic framework.
items.author: Maaike J. Bierenbroodspot, Cäcilia F. Kunz, Elisa S. Goldbecker et al.

items.title: Infant presence and mother-infant conflict predict fetal loss in wild mandrills
items.summary: by Nikolaos Smit, Berta Roura-Torres, Axelle Delaunay, Alice Baniel, Elise Huchard, Marie J. E. Charpentier Female fitness depends on reproductive pace and offspring survival, both of which are determined by the ability to balance resource allocation between current and future reproduction. Using 11 years of data on 356 pregnancies (52 of which resulted in fetal loss) from 117 wild female mandrills, we show that females who conceive while still caring for a young infant experience a greater probability of fetal loss as well as increased mother-infant behavioral conflict in the form of maternal rejection. In addition, females whose infants throw more tantrums show a greater probability of fetal loss, consistent with observations from other species where living offspring can interfere in parental reproduction.
items.author: Nikolaos Smit, Berta Roura-Torres, Axelle Delaunay et al.

items.title: Folding without glutamine: Proteome-scale removal of a canonical amino acid
items.summary: by Alejandro Garciarrubio, Blanca Ramos-Cerrillo, Enrique Morett, Lorenzo Segovia All known life uses a canonical alphabet of 20 amino acids, yet which residues are structurally essential remains untested at proteome scale. Isoleucine was recently eliminated from ribosomal proteins in Escherichia coli , establishing that amino acid alphabet reduction is feasible. Here we ask whether an entire amino acid can be eliminated from a proteome, and develop a computational framework to identify the best target. Using two independent approaches — ProteinMPNN structure-based probabilities and multiple sequence alignment conservation — we define “keep-score” as the fraction of positions where the native residue is optimal.
items.author: Alejandro Garciarrubio, Blanca Ramos-Cerrillo, Enrique Morett et al.

items.title: The influence of ensemble size and composition on the performance of combined real-time COVID-19 forecasts
items.summary: by Friederike Becker, Katharine Sherratt, Nikos I. Bosse, Sebastian Funk During infectious disease outbreaks, short-term forecasts can play an important role for both decision makers and the general public. While previous research has shown that combining individual forecasts into an ensemble improves accuracy and consistency, practical guidance for organisers of multi-model prediction platforms on how to construct an ensemble has been scarce. In particular, it is not entirely clear how ensemble performance relates to the size of the underlying model pool, a relevant question when relying on voluntary contributions from modelling teams that face competing priorities. Furthermore, the exact composition of an ensemble forecast may influence its performance.
items.author: Friederike Becker, Katharine Sherratt, Nikos I. Bosse et al.

items.title: Global sensitivity analysis for stochastic models of infectious diseases: Re-emergence of yellow fever virus in the Americas as a case study
items.summary: by Nate Kornetzke, Helen J. Wearing Emerging infectious diseases are a persistent public health threat that challenge deterministic, mechanistic modeling approaches. Because outbreaks initially start with a low number of infected hosts, their dynamics are highly stochastic, making traditional deterministic methods, e.g., ordinary differential equations, unable to qualitatively or quantitatively capture the transmission dynamics. In place, stochastic models are used, such as Markov chain models, but these models present their own challenges. Often, to infer a quantity of interest with stochastic models, we need to sample the model’s distribution many times over, introducing an additional source of noise to our analysis.
items.author: Nate Kornetzke, Helen J. Wearing

items.title: Whole-proteome structure/function prediction in uropathogenic E. coli reveals previously missed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways
items.summary: by Chunxiang Peng, Henry Schreiber, Chengxin Zhang, Quancheng Liu, Scott Hultgren, Lydia Freddolino The rapid advancement of high-throughput sequencing technologies has vastly increased the number of known protein sequences, but the experimental characterization of their structures and functions lags behind. This gap in knowledge impedes our understanding of biological mechanisms of these proteins, hinders the interpretation of high-throughput experiments, and exposes a significant challenge in modern biology: deducing the structural and functional information of proteins based on their sequences. Most computational approaches rely on homology with well-annotated proteins, yet many proteins lack identifiable homologues, reducing the power of this approach.

items.title: A Plasmodium knowlesi A1-H.1 transcriptome time course focusing on the late asexual blood stages
items.summary: by Katlijn De Meulenaere, Dalia Díaz-Delgado, Pieter Monsieurs, Erin Sauve, Alfred Cortés, Ellen Knuepfer, Anna Rosanas-Urgell The zoonotic parasite Plasmodium knowlesi is closely related to Plasmodium vivax , the second leading cause of human malaria. P. knowlesi line A1-H.1 can be maintained in human erythrocytes and is an experimental model for P. vivax biology. We present the first transcriptome time course of the intraerythrocytic developmental cycle (IDC) of P. knowlesi A1-H.1 grown in human normocytes.
